> `quantity_complete`, the scanner resolver (`clock_in_blockers` /
> `complete_blockers`, so `POST /scanner/resolve-action` reports the same text), and the floor read
> payloads' `start_blocked_reason`. Every refusal happens before any write (no TimeEntry, no status
> flip, no audit row) and is a **409** with a plain-string `detail` — never a 400, because the crew
> station reads a clock-in 400 as "already clocked in":
>
> | Work order status | `detail` |
> |---|---|
> | `draft` | `This work order has not been released — release first. Work cannot start until a supervisor releases it.` |
> | `on_hold` | `This work order is on hold — work cannot start until a supervisor resumes it (Resume Work Order on the work order). Resuming or clearing an operation's hold does not lift it.` |
> | `complete` / `closed` / `cancelled` | `cannot start operation: work order is <status>` — the start verb's existing text, unchanged. Clock-in had no terminal rung before and now refuses with this one |
>
> - **Both start verbs also refuse an operation-level hold** with **409** `This operation is on hold —
>   lift it with Resume (kiosk) or Clear Hold (desk) first. Starting it does not lift a hold.` They used
>   to flip an ON_HOLD operation straight to IN_PROGRESS, silently clearing the hold and leaving its
>   blocker OPEN. Clock-in keeps its existing **400** `Operation is not ready to start` for an
>   operation-level hold.
> - **`PUT /shop-floor/operations/{id}/start` no longer lifts a DRAFT work order to IN_PROGRESS.** That
>   branch was a release with no Release verb and no record of who authorized it; the verb now lifts a
>   RELEASED work order only. The office twin `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/start` gained the
>   floor twin's **400**s (`Operation is already complete` / `Operation is already in progress`) — it
>   used to re-open a COMPLETE operation and re-stamp `actual_start` / `started_by` on a running one.
> - **Completing a READY operation starts it**, so both complete verbs refuse it **409** with the same
>   text on a draft or on-hold work order, before the quantity checks, any write and any inventory
>   effect (the office verb used to book stock on a held job this way). Completing an operation that is
>   already **IN_PROGRESS** is **not** gated, and neither are clock-out, production reporting,
>   operation resume or blocker resolve/dismiss: labor already running when a job is held must always
>   be closable, and the kiosk's finish flow completes an IN_PROGRESS operation after clocking out.
> - **The generic operation `PUT` is not a way around the gate.** `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}`
>   with `status: in_progress` is refused **409** with the table's text on a draft, on-hold or terminal
>   work order — without it, a hand-set IN_PROGRESS followed by the office complete verb (which accepts
>   an IN_PROGRESS operation with no work-order gate, by design) started *and* completed work, tied
>   material included, on a job nobody released or a supervisor stopped. `status: ready` on a **draft**
>   is refused **409** with the `draft` text too (it would put unreleased work on the dispatch board;
>   resume-to-DRAFT and a `PUT` back to draft demote exactly those rows). Both are raised before the
>   first field is written, and re-sending the operation's current status in an unrelated edit is not
>   a transition, so it still lands. Hand-setting READY on a held job's operation stays the supervisor override it was —
>   every start verb still refuses that operation until the work order resumes.
> - **Nor is a count.** Recorded good quantity on a not-started operation is what a reconciling read
>   treats as a start (it lifts a PENDING / READY operation carrying `quantity_complete > 0` to
>   IN_PROGRESS), so `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` refuses **409** with the table's `draft` /
>   `on_hold` text a `quantity_complete` **raise** on an operation that is — or that write leaves —
>   PENDING or READY, on a draft or on-hold work order, before any field is written — and before the
>   open-operation good-ceiling and labor-record 409s (see "Short count at completion"), whose
>   remedies (clock-out, Report production, the office Complete) that job keeps shut. And the read
>   itself no longer performs that lift on a draft or on-hold job: quantities still reconcile, the
>   operation stays PENDING / READY, and the first read after Release / Resume lifts it. Together they
>   close the "`PUT` a count, read, office-complete" path. Deliberately narrow: lowering a count,
>   scrap changes, and counts on an IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETE operation are unaffected, and so is a
>   terminal work order.
> - **A soft-deleted work order is 404** on clock-in, both start verbs, `POST /work-orders/{id}/start`,
>   `POST /work-orders/{id}/release` and the generic `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` (the whole verb:
>   no field of a deleted job's operation is editable through it) — and, since 2026-11-16, the header
>   `PUT /work-orders/{id}` too (restore is its own verb).
> - **A laser child does not inherit its assembly parent's draft or hold** — the gate reads the
>   operation's own work order. Hold the laser work order itself to stop its nests.
> - **List membership does not change.** Draft and held jobs stay on the kiosk queue, the crew station,
>   `/shop-floor/operations`, the dispatch board and the wallboard, carrying `start_blocked_reason`
>   (see Shop Floor) so the floor shows a "Not released" / "WO on hold" chip and a disabled start
>   instead of discovering the 409. A work-order hold does **not** move rows onto the kiosk `held`
>   list, which stays operation-level holds only.
>
> **`POST /work-orders/{id}/start`** is now **Admin / Manager / Supervisor** (it was open to any
> authenticated user) and accepts a **RELEASED** work order only: **409** with the `draft` / `on_hold`
> text above, **400** `Work order must be released to start` on any other status, **404** when missing
> or soft-deleted, **409** `This work order was modified concurrently. Refresh and retry.` on a stale
> version. It **no longer lifts a hold** — it used to accept ON_HOLD and move it to IN_PROGRESS.
>
> **Hold Work Order** is the existing `PUT /work-orders/{id}` with `{"status": "on_hold", "version"}` on a
> released or in-progress job (Work Order detail → **Hold Work Order**). On a **draft** it now refuses
> **409** `A draft work order has not been released, so there is nothing on the floor to hold. Leave it
> in draft until it is ready, then release it.`, before any write. That `PUT` is the only writer of a
> work-order ON_HOLD, so every hold placed from now on is on released work. Re-sending `on_hold` on a
> held job, ON_HOLD → DRAFT and ON_HOLD → CANCELLED stay allowed (a move to DRAFT now also takes the
> job's READY cards off the floor — see "Returning a job to draft" below). **Known gap, a follow-up:** the
> `PUT`'s blind DRAFT / ON_HOLD → RELEASED / IN_PROGRESS status writes are still accepted from the API
> (the MCP `update_work_order` tool refuses them), `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` has no
> draft / on-hold gate, and finishing the last running operation of a draft or held job **still
> completes the work order** — decided for this change: labor already running is always closable, so
> no completion verb refuses it; whether a job with no release record, or one on hold, may complete
> this way is the owner's call. The hold itself is recorded by the `PUT`'s best-effort `log_update`.
>
> **Returning a job to draft** is the same `PUT` with `{"status": "draft", "version"}` on a released,
> in-progress or held job. A draft leaves no cards on the dispatch board or the kiosk, and every
> promotion seam is forward-only (and never promotes a draft), so the `PUT` itself takes them off: every
> **un-worked** READY operation — laser nests included — goes back to PENDING through the same demotion
> core resume-to-DRAFT uses, one **required** ready → pending `STATUS_CHANGE` row each
> (`extra_data.transition = "work_order_returned_to_draft"`, `operation_number`, `sequence`), written
> after a flush so a concurrent clock-in surfaces as the usual **409**. When a row cannot be written the
> whole `PUT` rolls back, the work order's own status included: **503** `The audit record for taking
> this work order's operations off the floor could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry.` Worked
> operations (IN_PROGRESS, an `actual_start`, booked good/scrap quantity, any TimeEntry) are left as
> they are; re-sending `draft` on a draft is not a move and demotes nothing. The `->DRAFT` move itself
> is not refused (whether to refuse it while work is under way is an open product call).
>
> **Resume Work Order — `POST /work-orders/{id}/resume`** (Admin / Manager / Supervisor) is the one door
> that puts a held job back on the floor under the release-record rule below. (`PUT` ON_HOLD → DRAFT and
> ON_HOLD → CANCELLED also leave a hold, restrictively — neither puts work on the floor; the `PUT`'s
> blind ON_HOLD → RELEASED / IN_PROGRESS write is the known gap above.) It never releases a job — Release is the authorization step — so the
> target comes from the release record (`released_at` or `released_by`) and the operations' work
> evidence (the work order's `actual_start`, any COMPLETE operation, or any operation that is
> IN_PROGRESS, carries an `actual_start`, has booked good/scrap quantity, or has any TimeEntry):
>
> | Release record | Work evidence | Resumes to | `restore_basis` |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | yes | yes | `in_progress` | `release_record_with_work` |
> | yes | no | `released` | `release_record` |
> | no | — | `draft` | `no_release_record` |
>
> A **draft** result returns every un-worked READY operation — laser nests included — to PENDING, so a
> draft leaves no cards on the dispatch board or the kiosk, and nothing puts them back before Release:
> the promotion rule never promotes a draft, so finishing labor that was still running when the job was
> held (it stays closable, by rule) completes that operation without re-promoting its successors or the
> demoted nests. Release it with `POST /work-orders/{id}/release`. **Finishing the last running
> operation of a draft or held job completes the work order** — the always-closable-labor rule wins.
> Clock-out, the office complete verb and `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/complete` all record that
> work-order transition (`draft` / `on_hold` → `complete`) as a best-effort `STATUS_CHANGE` row
> (the floor close gained its row in the short-count change; before it, that verb wrote none on any
> work-order completion). Whether a job with no release record (or one on hold) may
> complete this way is an open owner follow-up beside `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete`'s missing
> draft / on-hold gate. A legacy hold with no stamp (an older laser package, an MRP
> auto-released or `PUT`-released job) therefore resumes to DRAFT: restrictive, visible, one Release
> click to fix. Operation-level holds are untouched (lift them with Resume / Clear Hold). Refusals:
> **400** `Work order is not on hold`, **404** `Work order not found` (missing, cross-tenant or
> soft-deleted), **409** on a concurrent write, and **503** `The audit record for resuming this work
> order could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry.` — the evidence is **required**: one
> `STATUS_CHANGE` row on the work order (`extra_data.transition = "work_order_hold_cleared"`,
> `restore_basis`, `operations_returned_to_pending`) plus one ready → pending `STATUS_CHANGE` row per
> demoted operation (`extra_data.transition = "work_order_resumed_to_draft"`, `operation_number`,
> `sequence`), written through `AuditService.log_required` and rolled back together with the status
> change when any row fails. The **200** body is `WorkOrderResumeResponse`
> `{work_order_id, message, status, restore_basis, operations_returned_to_pending}`, where `message` is
> display-ready (`Work order resumed — it is back in progress.` / `Work order resumed — it is released
> and back on the floor.` / `No release is on record for this work order, so it returned to DRAFT —
> release it to put it back on the floor.`). It broadcasts `work_order_resumed` on the work-order,
> dashboard and each affected work center's shop-floor channels. The MCP tool is
> `work_orders_resume_work_order`. A standing API token whose user holds Admin / Manager / Supervisor
> may call it (**owner decision 2026-11-07**: an agent may lift a work-order hold); the required rows
> it writes carry `extra_data.credential` naming the token, as every token write does (see
> [API tokens](#api-tokens-bots-and-mcp-clients)).
>
> **Before deploying this change**, run the two read-only queries in
> [`DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md` → Wave 2 rollout](DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md#wave-2-rollout): draft or held jobs
> that still carry READY / IN_PROGRESS operations or open labor become un-joinable at deploy, and held
> jobs with no release record will resume to DRAFT.
>
> **Completion contract (shared finalizer).** Operation completion rolls up into the work order
> through one shared finalizer, so all completion paths behave identically. The office
> `/work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` stores the requested good **total** as
> `clamp(max(existing, requested, recorded production evidence), 0, target)`: it never drops below
> the value already recorded or below durable production evidence, and never exceeds the operation
> target (nor the units that can still reach the operation — see "Short count at completion" below).
> The shop-floor `/shop-floor/operations/{id}/complete` records **no** good of its own: it closes at
> `clamp(max(existing, recorded production evidence), 0, target)`. While operations are open the work
> order's `quantity_complete` only moves forward. When **every** operation is COMPLETE it is **set**
> by one rule (`finished_quantity_at_all_complete`): `quantity_ordered` when no operation declared a
> short (the old snap, now clamped to the order), otherwise what came out of the last whole-order
> stage — or the sum of the line items when their targets add up to the order. A force-complete
> (`/work-orders/{id}/complete`) sets it to the quantity it books. On a
> **laser dispatch-pool WO** (`work_order_type='laser_cutting'`) the work-order rollup is the
> **sum** of per-nest progress rather than the sequential single-operation rule, and completing all
> nests does **not** snap the header to `quantity_ordered` — see "Pool WO header progress" under
> Laser Nests. Scrap
> is **opt-in on update**: `quantity_scrapped` is optional on both `/work-orders/{id}/complete` and
> `/work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` — omit it to leave previously-recorded scrap untouched. On
> `/work-orders/{id}/complete` an explicit value (including `0`) overwrites the work order's scrap; on
> `/work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` it is a **total that never lowers** (a value below what is
> recorded leaves the recorded scrap as it is). A scrap reason is **required** (else **422**) when
> `/work-orders/{id}/complete` writes scrap above **0**, or when `/work-orders/operations/{id}/complete`
> raises the recorded total — free-text `scrap_reason` or a structured `scrap_reason_code_id`, on
> both verbs — see "Scrap reason is required when scrap is reported" below. Completing an
> **on-hold** operation is rejected with **409 Conflict**
> (`{"detail": "Operation is on hold and cannot be completed"}`);
> `/work-orders/{id}/complete` likewise returns **409** if any open operation is on hold
> (`"…is on hold; resolve the hold first"`) — resolve the hold before completing. Completing a
> **READY** operation of a **draft** or **on-hold** work order is refused **409** on both operation
> completion verbs (completing it would start it — see "Draft and on-hold work orders refuse every
> start" above); an IN_PROGRESS operation stays completable, under the short-count rules below. A
> work order that reaches `complete` always carries both an `actual_start` and an `actual_end`.
> Successful completion responses carry a `quality_exceptions` array (default `[]`) listing any
> unsatisfied **quality gates** — see "Quality gates on completion are warn-and-record" under Shop
> Floor; these warn, they do **not** block the completion.
>
> **Short count at completion (owner ruling 1, 2026-11-05).** A short count at operation completion
> is reported as **scrap with a reason**, or the operation **stays open** — it is never closed at the
> counted quantity. Every short close is an explicit Complete by a named person; nothing closes a
> short on its own. The arithmetic has one implementation,
> `work_order_state_service.OperationAccounting` (built by `operation_accounting` /
> `stage_accounting`), which every verb, read model and seam below calls:
>
> | Figure | Meaning |
> |---|---|
> | `target` | The operation's target (`operation_target_quantity` — what `quantity_ordered` means on every operation payload) |
> | `ceiling` | `target` − the shorts declared upstream in this operation's chain — the **most good the server accepts** here (clock-out, `/production` and the office verb refuse **400** above it) |
> | `received` | `ceiling` − soft feed credit from a short component chain — the units that actually reached the operation |
> | `unaccounted` | `received` − good − scrap — what a close must still account for |
> | `closing_short` | `received` − good — the short a close declares (covered by scrap) |
>
> - **Two completion rules, deliberately different.** The implicit auto-complete paths — a clock-out,
>   and reconcile-on-read — complete an operation only on a **full good count** of the units that
>   **can** reach it: `good ≥ ceiling`, the HARD figure (`OperationAccounting.is_full_count`). Soft
>   component feed never lowers it, so an assembly stage is never closed out from under the crew at the
>   feed-reduced count (a completed stage could never record replenished units afterwards); and a count
>   **above** a ceiling that is below the target is never auto-completed — it is an error to correct.
>   Scrap never counts there, so an operator who scrapped two and is re-running replacements is never
>   closed out from under them, and a GET never closes a short. The explicit close verbs —
>   `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/complete` and `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` —
>   close when good **+ scrap** cover every received unit (`unaccounted = 0`), so a stage short only by
>   soft feed is closed by a person's explicit Complete. An operation whose target is 0 is no longer
>   auto-completed by a clock-out.
> - **A short is declared, never inferred.** A close that closes short writes
>   `work_order_operations.quantity_short_declared` = `received − good` (migration `117`; `null` on
>   every other close and on every pre-117 row). Only the two explicit close verbs write it, it is on
>   no request schema, and nothing re-derives it from the counts later — so a later correction cannot
>   change what the next stage was credited with, and existing data reads exactly as before.
> - **Credit flows along chains, by sequence.** The operations of one component part
>   (`component_part_id`) form a chain that is always credited. The work order's whole-order
>   operations (no component, target = `quantity_ordered`) form the main chain, credited **only on a
>   sequential work order** (`sequential_operations = true`). Laser dispatch-pool nests and line
>   items are singletons and never receive credit. A short declared upstream lowers each later
>   operation's `ceiling`; a component chain's loss reaches the main chain as **soft** feed credit
>   (`ceil(lost ÷ qty_per)`), which lowers `received` but never the `ceiling`, so an assembly built from
>   replenished components can still record its full count. A main stage whose operations are all
>   COMPLETE passes on what it actually made when that is more than the feed predicted (it was
>   replenished), and the feed loss before it stops counting for the stages after it.
> - **On a pooled work order the main chain gets no credit** (owner decision): its same-target
>   operations cannot be told apart from line items. A later stage there must **not** record scrap for
>   units an earlier stage already declared lost — that records the same loss twice and consumes the
>   later stage's tied material for runs that never happened (invariant 6, never reversed). The floor
>   close's 409 says so when it applies (the read models carry the figure as
>   `upstream_short_uncredited`), and the remedy is to have a supervisor turn on **Sequential
>   operations** (`PUT /work-orders/{id}` `sequential_operations: true`) **before** the later stage
>   closes — that credits it. Lowering `quantity_ordered` does not help there: the upstream stage has
>   already accounted for the full order.
> - **A sequencing flip cannot re-interpret a declared short.** Credit is read at the work order's
>   current setting, so `PUT /work-orders/{id}` refuses **409**: turning sequencing **off** while a
>   COMPLETE whole-order stage that has later stages carries a declaration (it would withdraw the credit
>   they closed on or are owed); turning it **on** once a later whole-order stage has already
>   COMPLETED after the declaring one (that close already covered the loss itself), or when a later
>   stage already holds more good than the credit would let reach it. With nothing declared — every
>   flip before this rule — nothing changes.
> - **An operation left open short holds the routing.** Later operations at other work centers stay
>   PENDING behind it on any work order, and on a sequential one every later operation does. Pieces
>   never started are **never** scrap (scrap consumes material, invariant 6): leave the operation
>   open and have a supervisor lower `quantity_ordered` (floored, below) or a nest's `planned_runs`.
>   Whole-order targets the new-work-order wizard restated as `component_quantity` (no component
>   part, value = the old order) move with a `quantity_ordered` change, one audit row each — otherwise
>   they would keep demanding the old count.
> - **The all-complete header** is `finished_quantity_at_all_complete` — see "Completion contract"
>   above. A work order that closed 8 good + 2 scrapped at its last stage books 8, and its
>   finished-goods receipt is 8. With parallel final stages (one sequence) the lowest binds, each
>   capped at its own ceiling. A routing made only of component operations books the order less the
>   worst chain's declared loss in finished units (`ceil(declared × ordered ÷ target)` summed along the
>   chain) — never 0.
> - **No stage may hold more good than can reach it.** Every write that raises good is capped at the
>   `ceiling` (clock-out, `/production`, the office verb, and the generic operation `PUT`), the floor
>   close refuses **409** to close an operation whose recorded good is above it, the reconcile never
>   completes one, and a close that **declares** a short is refused **409** when a later stage of its
>   chain (or, for a component chain, the assembly it feeds) already records more good than the
>   declaration lets reach it. A **0-piece** clock-out always closes the entry, whatever the stored
>   count (an open TimeEntry is never trapped); only a clock-out that adds good is judged.
>
> **The office verb — `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete`** (Admin / Manager / Supervisor /
> Quality). Query parameters: `quantity_complete` (required, the absolute good **total**),
> `quantity_scrapped` (optional absolute scrap **total that never lowers** — omit it to leave the
> floor's scrap untouched), `scrap_reason` / `scrap_reason_code_id` (required only when the scrap
> total rises; written only then, never cleared), `quantity_override_reason`, and
> `acknowledge_open_entries` (default `false`). Every check runs before the first write, in this
> order: **400** non-finite quantity; **404**; **409** terminal work order; **400** predecessors
> incomplete; **400** bad quantity / missing target; **400** already complete; **409** operation on
> hold (**400** other non-startable status); **409** a READY operation under a draft / on-hold work
> order; **400** negative scrap; **403** an API token raising the scrap total (owner decision
> 2026-11-07 — see "API tokens may not declare scrap" below); **404** / **422** unknown / inactive
> scrap code; **422** a scrap rise with no reason; **400** good above the `ceiling`; **409** a scrap
> rise submitted with a
> `quantity_complete` below the good the floor has since recorded (a stale screen — the scrap would
> cover units that are now good); **403** an API token recording good above the floor's labor
> evidence; **422** good above the floor's labor evidence with no `quantity_override_reason` — only
> when the operation carries any TimeEntry, so desk cleanup of never-clocked work stays reason-free
> (the owner's office-exempt asymmetry). Then the decision:
> - **Not accounted, nothing changed** (same good, no scrap rise) → **200**
>   `{"message": "No change — Op N left open", "is_fully_complete": false, …}` that writes **nothing**
>   — not even the auto-start.
> - **Not accounted otherwise** → **200** `"Progress updated"`, the operation stays open.
> - **Accounted and short** (`closing_short > 0`) → **403** for an API token; **409** naming anyone
>   still clocked in (the caller included) unless `acknowledge_open_entries=true`, which clocks them
>   out with their quantities untouched (pieces they never reported are not counted) and lists them in
>   `closed_time_entries`; **409** when one of those open entries is **approved** (approval is the
>   immutability boundary — unapprove it, or have them clock out, first); **409** on a serialized work
>   order whose per-serial step records are missing; **409** when a later stage already records more
>   good than the declaration would let reach it. A **full-count** office close never auto-closes
>   anyone.
> - Then, whenever the call closes the operation, **409** `STEPS_INCOMPLETE` as before.
>
> The response is `{message, is_fully_complete, operation: {id, status, quantity_complete,
> quantity_scrapped, upstream_quantity_short, quantity_unaccounted, quantity_short_declared},
> closed_time_entries, quality_exceptions}`. Every call that writes records **one** quantity audit row
> (`UPDATE`, `work_order_operation`; old/new `quantity_complete`, `quantity_scrapped`, `scrap_reason`,
> `scrap_reason_code_id`, `quantity_short_declared`; `extra_data` `changes`, `target`, `received`,
> `upstream_quantity_short`, `unaccounted_after`, `closed_short`, `asserted_above_recorded`,
> `recorded`, `override_reason`, `acknowledged_open_entries`), followed on a close by the
> `STATUS_CHANGE` row, whose `extra_data` now carries `target` / `received` /
> `upstream_quantity_short`. The quantity row is **required** evidence (`log_required`) whenever scrap
> rose, the close was short or good exceeded the floor's evidence: when it cannot be written nothing
> is saved and the answer is **503** `The completion audit could not be saved; nothing was changed.
> Please retry.`
>
> **Force-complete — `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete`** (Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality) is
> held to the rule at the **work-order** grain. After its existing checks (cancelled **409**; an API
> token sending a `quantity_scrapped` above the header's recorded scrap **403**, right after the
> number checks — owner decision 2026-11-07; the scrap-reason **422**; an open operation on hold
> **409**) and before any write, one grouped,
> tenant-scoped TimeEntry read feeds `work_order_completion_bounds`: `deliverable` (the most the
> floor's recorded good supports at the binding operation), `physical_max` (the most that can exist
> once declared shorts are out) and `floor_loss` (units the floor already accounted as lost). It
> refuses, in order: **403** an API token completing below the order or above `deliverable` (first, so
> a token is never sent to add a reason it would then be refused for); **409** `quantity_complete`
> above `deliverable` without a non-blank `quantity_override_reason` (naming the binding operation);
> **400**, with a reason, above `physical_max`; **400**, reason or not, when `quantity_complete` plus
> the floor's HARD loss (`hard_loss`: declared shorts and scrap covering a shortfall, never soft feed)
> exceeds the order — those units can never also be finished; **409** when
> `quantity_ordered − quantity_complete` is not covered by `max(floor_loss, work-order scrap)` (the
> `quantity_scrapped` sent, else the stored value). The header is then **set** to `quantity_complete` for every
> work-order type — never `max()`'d with the header before the loop, which on a routing whose first
> stage completed at the full order re-inflated the finished-goods receipt past a declared short (two
> stages, op 10 at 10, op 20 at 8 + 2: the header and the FG receipt are 8, not 10). Open operations
> are still closed without invented per-operation counts and without a declared short. The quantity
> audit row carries `extra_data` `deliverable`, `physical_max`, `floor_loss`, `binding_operation_id`,
> `binding_operation`, `override_reason`, `asserted_above_recorded`, and is **required** evidence
> (**503**, nothing saved) whenever the booked quantity is below the order or an override was used.
> The response shape is unchanged. An unreported work order booked at its full order passes the
> bounds exactly as before.
>
> **Correcting a completed operation.**
> - **`PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}`** refuses **409** a change to `quantity_complete` or
>   `status`, or a LOWERING of `quantity_scrapped`, on a COMPLETE operation, after the version check
>   and before any write. Scrap found after the close may be **added** (with `scrap_reason`) into
>   what is still **unaccounted** — units that reached the operation and are recorded neither good nor
>   scrapped: zero on an accounted close, positive on a legacy short close — and the reason text
>   corrected; neither can make the operation short, and a COMPLETE operation has no other door for it
>   (the clock-out refuses pieces there). Both are written as **required** audit evidence
>   (`extra_data.transition = "completed_operation_scrap_correction"`, **503** with nothing saved when
>   it cannot be). A rise past the unaccounted remainder is refused **409** before any write: it would
>   count a piece the close already counted good as scrap too, and the whole-work-order consumption
>   reconcile would deplete its tied material a second time (consumption never auto-reverses). The
>   409's remedy depends on the work order. On a **live** one, pieces counted good and later found bad
>   go through reduce-production with `reopen_operation`, then a re-close with the scrap — an operation
>   nobody ever clocked in to included (see the next bullet). On a **COMPLETE / CLOSED / CANCELLED**
>   work order reduce-production refuses every correction, so the 409 says so and names the record
>   that still exists: a nonconformance (NCR) against the finished work or its lot, not a change to
>   the operation. Re-sending the stored values (compared numerically) and editing any other field are
>   still accepted.
>
>   This bounds the **after-close** door only, and it does not settle the model. While an operation is
>   open, scrap past what reached it is still accepted on every door — clock-out, `/production`, this
>   `PUT` and the office close (only the floor close bounds the scrap it declares at the close) — as
>   replacement runs that consumed material (see `docs/KIOSK.md` → the COMPLETE overlay), so a reopen
>   followed by a re-close can still record good + scrap above what reached the operation. Whether
>   open-operation scrap should be bounded the same way, and where scrap from extra runs nobody
>   recorded before the close goes once the operation is complete (the clock-out refuses pieces
>   there and this `PUT` bounds them), are **open owner questions**; nothing here decides them. On an **open** operation it refuses **409** raising `quantity_complete` above the
>   `ceiling`, or above the floor's labor record when anyone ever clocked in (that assertion goes
>   through the office Complete's `quantity_override_reason`). Those two run after the start gate: on
>   a draft or on-hold work order a raise on a PENDING / READY operation is the start gate's 409
>   ("release first" / "Resume Work Order") instead (see "Draft and on-hold work orders refuse every
>   start").
> - **`POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/reduce-production`** (the office twin, body
>   `ProductionReductionRequest`) also corrects an operation **nobody ever clocked in to** (no
>   `TimeEntry` at all, open, closed or approved — the office's labor-less close): there is no
>   evidence to walk, so it lowers the good count the office entered directly, up to that count
>   (**400** `Only {n} good piece(s) are recorded on Op N, which nobody clocked in to; the correction
>   cannot exceed them.` above it), with every rule below unchanged; the audit row carries
>   `extra_data.no_labor_recorded = true`, both facts are re-checked under the row locks (**409**
>   `This operation was modified concurrently. Refresh and retry.`), and an operation with any labor
>   keeps the evidence bound byte-for-byte. It gains `reopen_operation` (default `false`). When lowering a
>   COMPLETE operation's count would leave it short, the correction is refused **409** before any
>   write unless `reopen_operation: true` is sent. Then the operation returns to **IN_PROGRESS**
>   (`actual_end`, `completed_by` and `quantity_short_declared` cleared, `current_operation_id`
>   re-pointed) and every un-worked READY operation it now blocks returns to PENDING through the one
>   demotion core (scope `blocked_by`). The reopen is refused **409** while a later operation of the
>   same chain is COMPLETE — correct that one first. The reopen's `STATUS_CHANGE` row
>   (`extra_data.transition = "reopened_by_correction"`, the reason, the accounting and the demoted
>   ids) and one ready → pending row per demoted operation
>   (`extra_data.transition = "predecessor_reopened"`) are **required** evidence: **503**
>   `The correction audit could not be saved; nothing was changed. Please retry.` rolls the whole
>   correction back. The reopen is also judged on the accounting (`accounting_change_strands`), so it
>   is refused **409** when clearing the declaration would leave a COMPLETE operation in **another**
>   chain short (a component chain's declaration feeds the assembly chain). A correction that scrap
>   still covers leaves the operation COMPLETE; when it raises the short the operation now closes with,
>   the declaration is **re-stamped** (required audit row,
>   `extra_data.transition = "short_redeclared_by_correction"`) so the later stages are credited with
>   the real loss — refused **409** when a later stage already holds more good than that lets through.
>   Consumed material is never auto-returned — use the material return verb. The
>   operator's `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/reduce-production` refuses `reopen_operation: true`
>   with **422** `reopen_operation is an office correction`. **Neither verb takes a standing API
>   token** (**403**, right after the 404 / scope 409s, before any lock, eligibility read or write,
>   and again under the row locks in the shared core) — see "API tokens may not declare scrap or make
>   count judgments" below.
> - **`PUT /work-orders/{id}`** refuses **409** lowering `quantity_ordered` below the largest good +
>   scrap any whole-order operation has already recorded, after the status / draft / due-date checks
>   and before the sequencing check and any write. Laser nests and line items set no floor. It also
>   refuses **409** RAISING it once any whole-order or component operation has COMPLETED (that stage
>   would become a completed operation that is short — open a new work order for the extra units).
>
> **API tokens may not declare scrap or make count judgments.** The refusals below (three texts)
> apply to a standing per-user API token (`app.core.credentials.is_api_token_credential`) whatever
> its user's role, and are raised before any write and before any audit row. This block says where
> each sits on its route; the policy list across all credential rules — the AI ones included, and the
> judgment writes deliberately left open to a token — is
> [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).
>
> - **Scrap — owner decision 2026-11-07.** A standing API token may not declare scrap, anywhere: only
>   a person (kiosk, crew badge, desk) does, because a scrap count is quality evidence someone has to
>   have seen. A request that would **raise** a recorded scrap quantity — an operation's, a time
>   entry's or the work-order header's `quantity_scrapped` — is refused **403** `Scrap must be
>   reported by a person (at the kiosk, with a crew badge, or signed in at a desk), not an API token:
>   a scrap count is quality evidence someone has to have seen. Record good pieces only, or leave the
>   work open for that person.` (`operation_action_gates.API_TOKEN_SCRAP`, one predicate
>   `api_token_declares_scrap` for every route). Where it sits on each route:
>
>   | Route | Refused when | Ahead of / behind |
>   |---|---|---|
>   | `POST /shop-floor/clock-out/{id}` | `quantity_scrapped > 0` | After the 404, the already-clocked-out 400, the non-finite 400 and the negative 400; before source / scrap-code resolution, the row locks, the completed-operation 409 and the ceiling 400. The time entry stays open |
>   | `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/production` (with or without `open_ncr`) | `quantity_scrapped_delta > 0` | After the not-found / not-in-progress / not-clocked-in / bad-number / both-zero checks; before scrap-code resolution, the row locks and the ceiling checks — no NCR, no production receipt, no audit row. An idempotent replay still returns its saved result first |
>   | `POST /hank/tasks`, `POST /hank/tasks/{id}/execute` (kind `report_production`) | `quantity_scrapped_delta > 0` | In the preview, so at preparation (no task row, no audit row) and again at execution (the task stays `awaiting_review`); after the 404 / not-in-progress / not-clocked-in checks, before the scrap-code check |
>   | `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/complete` | declared `quantity_scrapped` delta `> 0` | Right after the scrap NaN / negative 400s (the work-order start rung and the state / labor / source checks still answer first); before the scrap-reason 422, scrap-code 404 / 422 and every quantity / accounting 409 |
>   | `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` | `quantity_scrapped` above the operation's stored scrap | Right after the negative-scrap 400; before scrap-code 404 / 422, the reason 422, the ceiling 400, the stale-scrap 409 and the override checks. Re-sending the recorded scrap is no rise |
>   | `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` | `quantity_scrapped` above the header's recorded scrap (it overwrites the header) | Right after the non-finite / negative 400s; before the scrap-reason 422, the scrap-code checks, the exceeds-ordered 400, the held 409 and the short / above-recorded 403. Omitting it, or sending the recorded value with the recorded reason and code, is not a declaration; the already-COMPLETE no-op and the CANCELLED 409 still come first |
>   | `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` | `quantity_scrapped` above the stored scrap, on an open or a COMPLETE operation | Right after the stale-version 409; any other count change keeps the count-judgment text below |
>   | `PUT /work-orders/{id}` | `quantity_scrapped` above the header's recorded scrap | Right after the stale-version 409; before the status / due-date / `quantity_ordered` / sequencing refusals. Re-sending the recorded value, or omitting it, works (the `update_work_order` MCP tool calls this route); any other change to `quantity_complete` / `quantity_scrapped` gets the count-judgment text below |
>
>   **Any** positive amount counts, however small: the predicate applies no tolerance (it does not
>   use the `1e-9` quantity epsilon the count comparisons use), because every writer behind it
>   stores scrap, its reason and an NCR at `> 0` — a token's `quantity_scrapped_delta: 5e-10` with
>   `open_ncr: true` is **403** with no NCR, and on the office close a sub-epsilon rise (which that
>   verb would not have written) is **403** too rather than a silent full-count close. On
>   `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` the rise is judged on the raw value, not through the
>   epsilon-compared list of changed counts. A delta that is not a finite number counts as a
>   declaration (the predicate fails closed); every route also refuses a non-finite quantity for
>   everyone first — clock-out now included (**400** `Quantity must be a valid number`, where a
>   person's NaN used to commit and then 500) — so the predicate's branch is a backstop. `null`, an
>   exact zero and a lowering never count. A request that declares no new scrap —
>   a good-only production report or clock-out, a full-count close, re-sending the recorded scrap
>   exactly as read (float noise included: `0.30000000000000004` back is a zero delta) — is
>   byte-identical to before, unless it writes or changes a scrap reason (next bullet).
> - **Scrap reasons — this PR's extension of the same decision.** Re-categorizing scrap a person
>   declared is the same quality evidence (the scrap Pareto groups by `scrap_reason_code_id`), so a
>   token request that would **write or change** a `scrap_reason` / `scrap_reason_code_id` is refused
>   with the same **403** text, even with no new scrap: `POST /shop-floor/clock-out/{id}` (it writes a
>   sent reason or code onto the caller's own time entry even at `quantity_scrapped: 0`; refused
>   right after the scrap check, before the code is resolved, so an unknown code is **403** too),
>   `PUT /work-orders/{id}` (its setattr), `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` re-sending the recorded
>   `quantity_scrapped` with a different reason or code — or with none over a recorded one, which
>   would erase it — and `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` (formerly the count-judgment text).
>   Judged on what the write would store against what is stored: sending no reason, or the stored
>   one, is no change. `/production`, the Hank task and both close verbs write a reason only with new
>   scrap, which the rule above already refuses.
> - **Short close — the same decision.** The question was about closing work short by reporting the
>   missing pieces as scrap, and the answer leaves a token only the full-count close. A short close
>   by either operation verb whose scrap is already on record (the request declares none), and a
>   force-complete below the order, are refused **403** `Closing work short must be done by a person
>   signed in to the app, not an API token.`
> - **The other count judgments — this PR's extension of the same rule** (the owner was asked about
>   scrap, not these). **403** `Recording more good than the floor counted, editing an operation's
>   counts, or lowering the order after work was recorded must be done by a person signed in to the
>   app, not an API token.` on: good above the floor's record (office verb and force-complete,
>   override reason or not); any change through `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` to
>   `quantity_complete` or a `quantity_scrapped` that is not a rise; any change through
>   `PUT /work-orders/{id}` to the header's `quantity_complete` or `quantity_scrapped`, in either
>   direction (a rise is the scrap text) — the header is what the FG receipt and every report read;
>   **every** correction through `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/reduce-production` or
>   `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/reduce-production` — a reopen erases a person's close and
>   walks other operators' labor down, a plain lowering is the count edit the operation PUT refuses,
>   and a re-stamp that would set a declared short gets the short-close text instead
>   (`production_reduction_service.api_token_reduction_refusal`); lowering `quantity_ordered`
>   once any operation has recorded good, scrap, a start or any labor; lowering a laser nest's
>   `planned_runs` through `PATCH /laser-nests/{id}` once that nest's operation has — its runs are
>   the operation's target and the laser work order's order is derived from them, so the next read
>   could otherwise complete the nest and the job at what was recorded; and re-importing a nest
>   package (`POST /work-orders/{id}/laser-nest-packages/import`, either import shape) when any
>   operation the import would delete has, or the laser work order's header already carries good or
>   scrap — the import replaces every nest operation and zeroes the header counts, erasing a person's
>   good, scrap and any declared short (that refusal has its own text, below, so the caller is told
>   which action was refused). All three read one per-operation rule,
>   `operation_action_gates.operation_has_recorded_work` (good, scrap, a start — IN_PROGRESS /
>   COMPLETE status or a stamped `actual_start` — or any `TimeEntry`). The re-import is refused
>   before the upload is unpacked and again under the import's lock before the first write, the
>   second read taken from the database rather than the rows the first one loaded; a person's
>   re-import, a token's import onto a job with no worked nest operation and zero header counts, and
>   the standalone import (which wipes nothing) are unchanged.
>
> A crew-station badge token is a person and passes all three (it cannot reach `/work-orders` or
> `/hank` at all). An interactive JWT — including one an MCP client carries — is the person's own
> session and is not refused: current behavior, not part of the 2026-11-07 decision, which covered
> standing API tokens only. `tests/api/test_api_token_scrap_refusal.py` enumerates every scrap
> writer three ways (ORM writes, request schemas, MCP tools), so a new one fails CI until it is
> guarded or listed as exempt with a reason.
>
> **Cost and actual hours on the work-order read** (P1.3 / P1.4, 2026-11-13). The two
> single-work-order reads — `GET /work-orders/{id}` and `GET /work-orders/by-number/{wo_number}` —
> carry two cost figures, on two different bases. Every other route that returns a
> `WorkOrderResponse` (create, `PUT`, release, duplicate, template use, nest imports) leaves both
> `null`.
>
> - **`job_cost_actuals`** — the work order's `JobCost` by element, or `null` when it has none.
>   **Nothing creates a `JobCost` automatically** (the completion sync only updates an existing
>   one), so expect `null` on most jobs. Fields: `job_cost_id`, `status` (`in_progress` /
>   `completed` / `reviewed`), `actual_material_cost`, `actual_labor_cost`, `actual_burden_cost`
>   (the JobCost's `actual_overhead_cost`: OVERHEAD **plus OTHER** entries),
>   `actual_subcontract_cost` (SUBCONTRACT entries), `actual_total_cost` (all five types) and
>   `updated_at`. These are the JobCost's own totals of its cost entries: labor is rebuilt from
>   closed time entries at the work-center rate (`POST /job-costs/{id}/calculate`, or the
>   completion sync when `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED` is on); material, burden and subcontract come
>   **only** from manually added entries. Read with its own `company_id` scope — a legacy row of
>   another company holding this work order's id on the global `job_costs.work_order_id` key is
>   never disclosed. Plain numbers, which may be negative (a manual entry can be).
> - **`issued_material_cost`** — net `ISSUE` minus `RETURN` cost from the inventory ledger, over
>   all three work-order reference shapes (`work_order_ledger_filter`): the material leg of
>   `actual_cost`. Present whether or not a JobCost exists and whatever
>   `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED` says. It is **not** `job_cost_actuals.actual_material_cost`, which
>   counts manual MATERIAL entries only; a job can show real issued material here and `0` there.
>
> **Where actual hours come from.** An operation's `actual_setup_hours` / `actual_run_hours` are
> never copied from routing standards (`setup_time_hours` / `run_time_hours` are the estimate
> only), and no API writes them by hand. Every non-zero value is a sum of time-entry
> `duration_hours`, which is the **server's wall clock** from clock-in to clock-out. `SETUP`
> entries credit setup hours; every other type — `RUN`, `REWORK`, `INSPECTION`, `DOWNTIME`,
> `BREAK` — credits run hours. Clock-out credits the operation at once. Some paths close entries
> **without** crediting it: an operation hold (`PUT /shop-floor/operations/{id}/hold`, and the
> process-sheet OOT quality hold) always, and the auto clock-out when an operation or work order
> completes while `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED` is off. A paper back-entry (`source` `backfill`)
> records the clerk's keying session, not the labor. So each operation on the two reads above
> also carries, derived at read time from the same batched time-entry read (never stored):
>
> | Field | Meaning |
> |---|---|
> | `hours_source` | `time_entries` — closed time entries measured hours on this operation (a closed zero-duration entry with no stored hours also reads `time_entries`: it is still a measurement). `manual` — stored hours with no time-entry hours behind them (legacy or out-of-band data; no API writes them). `none` — nothing recorded; an open entry counts for nothing until clock-out. `standard` is **reserved and never returned**. |
> | `recorded_setup_hours` / `recorded_run_hours` | The measured sums of **closed** entries, split as clock-out splits them. They can be **higher** than `actual_setup_hours` / `actual_run_hours` after a hold or a flag-off auto clock-out. |
> | `hours_include_backfill` | `true` when any closed entry behind those sums is a paper back-entry or an import, whose duration is keying time. |
>
> All four are `null` on responses not built through `_enrich_work_order_operations`. A foreign
> company's entry on a colliding operation id never counts.
>
> **Read models.** `WorkOrderOperationResponse` (every response built through
> `_enrich_work_order_operations` — `GET /work-orders/{id}`, by-number, create, duplicate, both
> nest-package imports, template use) carries `quantity_short_declared` (the column) and, computed in
> memory, `upstream_quantity_short`, `quantity_good_ceiling`, `quantity_unaccounted`,
> `upstream_short_uncredited` (a pooled work order's earlier declared short, not credited),
> `has_labor_evidence` and `quantity_recorded_good` (the floor's evidence-floored good — the office
> modal asks for `quantity_override_reason` exactly when the server will) — all `null` outside that
> enrichment. `WorkOrderResponse` there carries `quantity_deliverable` and
> `quantity_accounted_loss` — the same bounds the force-complete enforces, from one grouped TimeEntry
> read per work order. `quantity_ordered` keeps meaning the target; a client derives
> `received = quantity_ordered − upstream_quantity_short`. The floor reads carry the same per-operation
> keys — see Shop Floor → "Short-count figures on floor reads".
>

> `Op N` is the operation's label, never doubled on a legacy `Op 10` value):

>
> **Not changed:** the scanner's `complete_blockers` stay state-only (so `legal_actions` may list
> `complete` for an operation whose close would be refused short); the material consumption formula
> (it now reads honest counts); laser nest `PATCH` **lowering** `planned_runs` by a person (below
> completed runs is still allowed — RAISING it on a COMPLETE nest, or on a COMPLETE / CLOSED /
> CANCELLED laser work order, is now refused **409** before any write, because the nest's planned runs
> are its operation's target and a completed operation is never short; a standing API token lowering
> it on a worked nest is **403**, above); and the floor-requires-labor / office-exempt
> asymmetry. **Before deploying**, see
> [`DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md` → Wave 2 rollout](DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md#wave-2-rollout) (migration `117`).
>
> **Completion signals.** When a work order reaches **COMPLETE** (operation/WO completion paths) or
> **CLOSED** (shipment close), the system fires a uniform signal set: an internal `WO_COMPLETED`
> notification to the tenant's recipients (supervisors, managers, and the WO creator) and an outbound
> `work_order.completed` / `work_order.closed` **webhook** to the company's registered endpoints — see
> [Webhooks](#webhooks). Both are dispatched asynchronously **after commit** and best-effort: a signal
> failure never fails the completion, and nothing fires for a rolled-back completion.
>
> **Parent/child laser-nest completion rollup (G1).** When the **last** laser-cutting child work order
> (`WorkOrderType.LASER_CUTTING`, linked by `parent_work_order_id`) of a parent reaches a terminal
> status, the system records a `child_work_orders_complete` operational event **and** a tamper-evident
> `audit_log` row (action **`CHILD_WORK_ORDERS_COMPLETE`**) attributed to the parent. This is a
> **signal only** — it does **not** auto-complete the parent or mutate its route (parent and child WOs
> are not operation-coupled); it surfaces "all children done, ready to advance" so a human completes
> the parent. It fires from every completion path including reconcile-on-read (tagged
> `source = "reconcile_on_read"` there) and is tenant-scoped and best-effort. **No API request/response
> shape change.**
>
> **Idempotent completion.** `/work-orders/{id}/complete` (and shipment `/{id}/ship`) are idempotent:
> re-invoking on an already-terminal work order/shipment returns the current state
> (`{"already_completed": true}` / `{"already_shipped": true}`) and fires no second audit row, event,
> notification, or webhook.
>
> **Terminal-state lock (a finished/cancelled WO can't be resurrected).** The terminal statuses are
> **COMPLETE**, **CLOSED**, and **CANCELLED**. The idempotent no-op above applies only to a WO that has
> already completed (COMPLETE/CLOSED); a **CANCELLED** WO was deliberately taken out of production and is
> not silently completed:
> - `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` on a **CANCELLED** WO returns **409 Conflict**
>   (`{"detail": "cannot complete a cancelled work order"}`).
> - `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` (and the shop-floor equivalent) against an operation
>   whose parent WO is in **any** terminal status returns **409 Conflict**
>   (`{"detail": "cannot complete operation: work order is <status>"}`) before any mutation — so
>   finalizing the last operation of a cancelled/closed WO can't drive it to COMPLETE.
> - `PUT /work-orders/{id}` that moves a **terminal** WO back to a **non-terminal** status returns
>   **409 Conflict** (`{"detail": "cannot move work order out of terminal status '<current>' to '<target>'"}`).
>   (This is a targeted guard on the one dangerous transition, not a full state machine.)
> - `PUT /work-orders/{id}` that sets `status` to **COMPLETE** or **CLOSED** from any status **other
>   than** COMPLETE/CLOSED returns **409 Conflict** — a blind status write would mark the job finished
>   while permanently bypassing every completion effect (FG receipt, tied-material consumption,
>   backflush, cost rollup), and nothing ever heals it because the completion verbs and the reconcile
>   refuse terminal WOs afterwards. The detail points at `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete`. The
>   exemption is deliberately COMPLETE/CLOSED only, **not** all terminal statuses: **COMPLETE → CLOSED**
>   is an archival move between two states whose completion chain already ran (still a 200), and a
>   resend of the WO's current status is idempotent — but **CANCELLED → COMPLETE/CLOSED** is refused
>   with its own detail (`"cannot mark a cancelled work order '<target>': its completion effect chain
>   never ran and never will. A cancelled work order stays cancelled."`) rather than pointing at
>   `POST /complete`, which also (correctly) refuses cancelled WOs.
> - `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` that sets `status` to **COMPLETE** on an operation that is not
>   already COMPLETE returns **409 Conflict** — it would be a fifth completion path outside the four
>   wired handlers (no `finalize_operation_completion`, no operation-scoped tied-material consumption,
>   no completion audit shape). The detail points at `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete`.
> - **Reconcile-on-read leaves terminal WOs untouched** — operation evidence read on any GET will not
>   reopen a terminal WO to IN_PROGRESS or resurrect a CANCELLED WO to COMPLETE.
>
> Resurrecting a terminal WO would re-fire finished-goods receipt / backflush / cost rollup and write a
> spurious COMPLETE row onto the tamper-evident audit chain; the lock prevents that.
>
> **Completion writes finished goods to inventory.** When a work order reaches **COMPLETE** (any
> completion path, including reconcile-on-read), the system **always** performs a finished-goods
> RECEIVE: it assigns the work order a lot number if it has none (`LOT-<work_order_number>`),
> creates or increments an inventory item for the work order's part at warehouse **`MAIN`** /
> location **`FINISHED-GOODS`** for the completed quantity, and writes a positive `RECEIVE`
> `InventoryTransaction` (`reference_type='work_order'`) at the part's `standard_cost`. The receipt is
> **audited** (`GET /audit/`) and **idempotent** — at most one finished-goods receipt per work order
> (DB-enforced), so a re-completion or a reconcile re-read never double-receives. Receipts are lot-only
> (no serial is assigned; the system has no part-serialization flag yet). A fully-scrapped work order
> (zero completed quantity) receives nothing, and a **laser nest-dispatch WO**
> (`work_order_type='laser_cutting'` — the shared `is_laser_dispatch_work_order` predicate) **never
> receives FG at all**: it is a dispatch pool whose `quantity_complete` counts pooled nest **runs**, and
> a parented laser child carries the **parent assembly's** `part_id`, so receiving here would mint
> phantom finished goods of the parent part (5 nests × 8 runs = 40 phantom units) that the parent's own
> completion later books for real. Part-less standalone nest WOs are the same shape with no part at all.
> The skip covers both and is logged at debug (expected behavior, not an error). The receipt's lot is
> reconstructable end-to-end via [Traceability](#traceability).
>
> **Component backflush is opt-in per part (default off) — and as of PR 4.5 the flag is SETTABLE.** If
> the finished part has `backflush_components = true` (see [Part Schema](#part-schema)), completion
> **auto-consumes** the part's BOM components: one negative `ISSUE` `InventoryTransaction` per
> component, decrementing source stock and carrying the consumed lot for genealogy — each **audited**
> and **reconciled to target** per component (`reference_type='work_order_backflush'`). When the flag is
> **false** (the default, and every part's state until somebody changes it) completion moves no
> components, so a shop that issues material manually is never double-consumed. A **laser
> nest-dispatch WO** (`work_order_type='laser_cutting'`, same predicate as the FG-receipt skip above)
> never runs this leg even when its part is armed: a parented child's `part_id` is the parent's part
> and its `quantity_complete` counts nest runs, so exploding the parent's BOM against those numbers
> would consume the parent's components on the wrong demand basis while the parent's own completion
> runs the real backflush. Only the BOM leg is gated — the nest's **material ties** are its actual
> consumption mechanism and post unchanged.
>
> **Read the previous sentence's scope bound literally.** Until PR 4.5 the flag had no writer anywhere
> in the application, and the sentences below described what the leg *would* do rather than observable
> behavior. That is no longer true in principle — `PUT /parts/{id}` and `PUT /materials/{id}` can now
> turn it on, behind the refusal gate described under [Part Schema](#part-schema) — but it remains true
> in practice **until the first part actually opts in**: the column's `server_default` is `false` and no
> production work order has yet reached this leg. Treat the behavior described here as **unproven in
> production**, not as observed.
>
> A backflush shortage (insufficient stock, after the shared FIFO policy has walked every consumable lot
> and skipped the segregated ones) **does not fail the completion** — the remainder is drawn negative and
> the shortfall is recorded as a tamper-evident `BACKFLUSH_SHORTAGE` audit row plus a
> `backflush_shortage` warning event (notification catalog `material.backflush_shortage` since PR 4.4).
>
> **A dry run is available before any of this happens**, and it writes nothing:
> `GET /work-orders/{id}/backflush-preview` (below) resolves the same demand through the same issue loop
> and the same lot policy, so the preview and the outcome cannot name different heats.
>
> **How component demand is resolved** (hardened while still dark; see
> `docs/MATERIAL_CONSUMPTION_PLAN.md` → "The BOM/routing backflush leg"):
> - **Basis is `quantity_complete + quantity_scrapped`**, each BOM line extended by its `scrap_factor`
>   — the same basis the per-run tie engine uses, so one shop cannot report two different consumptions
>   for the same physical event depending on whether the material was tied. A **fully-scrapped** work
>   order therefore backflushes (it previously backflushed nothing).
> - **Alternate, optional and `reference` BOM lines are skipped.** An alternate group is an OR, not an
>   AND; optional lines have nothing on the work order recording which units got them; `reference`
>   lines are documentation and tooling. This matches `mrp_service`, so planning and consumption state
>   the same demand for one BOM. (There is still **no substitution logic** — alternates are inert
>   columns, not a feature.)
> - **Multi-level BOMs:** a `phantom` sub-assembly explodes into its children; a `make` sub-assembly is
>   issued as a stocked unit and its children are **not** (they were consumed when it was built).
> - **Routing precedence is per part, not all-or-nothing.** An operation's `component_part_id` states
>   *that component's* demand; the BOM supplies every part the routing does not name. Previously one
>   stray `component_part_id` disabled the entire BOM explosion for the work order. An operation naming
>   the work order's **own** part is refused (it would ISSUE the part the FG receipt just RECEIVEd).
> - **Suppression runs in two layers**, so tied material is never issued twice: an OPEN operation-scoped
>   tie owns its part's demand (even before it consumes), **and** the signed ledger net suppresses any
>   part the ledger already shows consumed against this work order's operations — recorded as a
>   tamper-evident **`BACKFLUSH_DOUBLE_ISSUE_BLOCKED`** audit row rather than silently. A **fully
>   returned** tie nets to zero and is deliberately allowed to re-issue: the material physically came
>   back, so the BOM's demand is genuinely unmet again.
> - **A blocking diagnostic REFUSES the demand it describes, and the refusal is recorded** (PR 4.5).
>   The opt-in gate is a one-time check and everything it reads stays editable afterwards by anyone
>   with `boms:edit`, so a BOM edited after a part was armed would otherwise move material against a
>   figure the resolver has itself judged wrong — previously with no log line, no audit row and no
>   event, leaving only an ordinary-looking ledger row. Each blocking diagnostic now drops **that
>   component's** demand when it names a `component_part_id`, or the **whole leg** when it names none
>   (the demand is then incomplete in a way no component owns — four codes today: `deleted_active_bom`,
>   `bom_depth_exceeded`, `missing_component_part`, and the foreign-component branch of
>   `foreign_component_part`, which carries no identity by design), and writes one
>   **`BACKFLUSH_DEMAND_REFUSED`** audit row carrying the code, the operator sentence, the BOM line or
>   operation it names, and the quantity that did **not** move. Under-issuing is the recoverable
>   direction — the material is still on the shelf; over-issuing writes it into an as-built record
>   that never contained it. `GET /work-orders/{id}/backflush-preview` reports the same refusal as
>   `suppression_reason: "blocking_diagnostic"`, so the dry run and the outcome agree.
>   **`refused_quantity` is attributed once per refused SCOPE, not once per row.** One BOM line can
>   raise several blocking diagnostics and two lines can name one component, so the first row naming a
>   given component carries the quantity and every later one carries `0` (the structural tier likewise
>   charges its whole-leg total to the first structural row). Summing `refused_quantity` over
>   `BACKFLUSH_DEMAND_REFUSED` therefore gives the real quantity that did not move — the rows still
>   number one per diagnostic, because each names a different thing to fix. The same rows that carry
>   the quantity emit the `material.backflush_demand_refused` notification, so one refused component
>   notifies once rather than once per condition it violates.
>
> **Completion also consumes tied material (material allocations).** A work order can optionally be
> **tied** to stock material via `…/material-allocations` (see "Material ties" below). Consumption is
> **never a separate endpoint** — authority to complete the work is what authorizes the movement — and
> it always joins the completing handler's transaction, so it is atomic with the status change. **An
> untied work order is untouched** — no ledger row, no audit row, no event (asserted by test).
>
> **Consumption fires when an OPERATION completes, and again (as a reconcile) when the WORK ORDER
> completes.** Two seams, deliberately different in scope:
> - **Operation completion** — `apply_operation_completion_inventory_effects`, called by the four
>   operation-completion handlers (`POST /shop-floor/clock-out/{time_entry_id}` when it closes the
>   operation, `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/complete`, `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete`,
>   and the per-operation leg of `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete`) right after the operation is
>   flipped `COMPLETE`. It reconciles **that operation's ties only**. A laser child work order carries
>   **one operation per nest**, so completing nest 1 of 3 now deducts **nest 1's sheet**. Scope is one
>   operation on purpose: a still-`IN_PROGRESS` operation can still be walked back by **either**
>   reduce-production verb — including the operator's own self-service one — so consuming against one
>   would let an operator strand material with no supervisor in the loop. (A **COMPLETE** operation is
>   now correctable through the **office** verb, which is safe precisely because the reasoned material
>   return exists to hand the material back; the operator verb still refuses. See "Over-count
>   correction … (supervisor/office)" above.) Every call site
>   is inside its handler's non-terminal branch, so a finished/cancelled job never consumes.
> - **Work-order completion** — `apply_completion_inventory_effects`, unchanged, on all five of its
>   existing call sites (kiosk clock-out, shop-floor and office operation complete, force-complete,
>   reconcile-on-read). It reconciles **every** open tie on the work order and is now the **self-heal**:
>   whatever an operation-level post missed still flushes here, and whatever already posted computes
>   `delta = 0` and writes nothing. The FG receipt and the BOM backflush stay here and did **not** move
>   to operation completion (per-operation they would double-receive a multi-operation job and collide
>   with `uq_wo_inventory_issue`).
>
> **Reporting production is still NOT a consumption trigger.** A partial production report on an open
> operation — `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/production`, an office
> `POST /work-orders/operations/{id}/complete` that saves progress, or a clock-out that does not close
> the operation — moves **no stock**. Keying 3 of 6 runs on an unfinished nest
> deducts nothing; the sheets move when that operation closes. Client copy built on these numbers must
> say "deducts when this operation completes", never "deducting now".
>
> **Force-complete is a no-op for consumption in practice.** `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` calls
> the seam for symmetry, but it never writes `operation.quantity_complete`, so `target` is 0 and the
> sum-delta is non-positive: a force-completed operation's tie posts nothing unless the operation
> already carried produced quantity from an earlier report. (Since ruling 1 it does **set** the
> work-order header to the quantity it books, so the finished-goods receipt and the BOM backflush
> basis follow that figure — see "Short count at completion".) See
> `docs/MATERIAL_CONSUMPTION_PLAN.md` → "Residual gaps of the operation-completion trigger".
>
> The two tie shapes behave differently:
> - **Operation-scoped** ties (`work_order_operation_id` set — the laser-nest case) are reconciled
>   **per operation** as a **sum-delta**: `target = qty_per_run × (operation
>   quantity_complete + quantity_scrapped)`, and a negative `ISSUE` is posted for
>   `target − qty_consumed` whenever that delta is positive. Because the target is recomputed from
>   live operation state, the operation-completion post, a replay, and the work-order reconcile all
>   converge instead of double-issuing — the later caller simply sees `delta = 0`
>   (see `docs/MATERIAL_CONSUMPTION_PLAN.md` → "Capability vs. wiring"). These rows
>   carry **`reference_type='work_order_operation'`** with `reference_id` = the **operation** id
>   (and `reference_number` = the work-order number) — deliberately outside the
>   `uq_wo_inventory_receipt` / `uq_wo_inventory_issue` idempotency predicates, which key on
>   `reference_type='work_order'`.
> - **Work-order-scoped** ties (no operation) are drained by the work-order-completion backflush, **as
>   their own leg**, and reconciled to `qty_planned` against that tie's signed ledger net (ISSUE −
>   RETURN, keyed on `allocation_id`). Their rows carry **`reference_type='work_order_backflush'`**
>   with `reference_id` = the **work order**, also outside the `uq_wo_inventory_*` predicates. Unlike
>   the BOM leg this is **not** gated on `backflush_components` — an explicit tie is itself the opt-in.
>   The drain advances the tie's `qty_consumed` to that ledger net (never to `qty_planned` regardless
>   of what posted) and **audits** the advance (`work_order_material_allocation` UPDATE,
>   `extra_data.reference_type = "work_order_backflush"`), exactly as the per-run engine audits its own.
>   Tie material **before** the work order completes.
>
>   > **Changed in PR 4.4 — the previous contract is stated so a stale integration is not read as a
>   > regression.** Through PR 4 a work-order-scoped tie was *summed per part* with any BOM demand and
>   > drained as **one** `ISSUE` row under `reference_type='work_order'`, because
>   > `uq_wo_inventory_issue` permitted exactly one row per (work order, part). It is now **two
>   > separately-attributed rows** — the tie row carries `allocation_id`, the BOM row has it NULL — and
>   > the tie leg posts **first**, so a shortage lands on the derived side and the tie's lot pin gets
>   > first claim on stock. **The total issued for a part carrying both demands is unchanged.** The
>   > unpinned draw also spills across lots now, so one logical draw can be N rows naming N lots.
>   > A `POST` of a work-order-scoped tie on a part carrying a **legacy** (pre-4.4) `work_order`-shaped
>   > `ISSUE` on the same work order is still refused **409** — see the error table below — but that
>   > refusal is now a legacy-only fence and is **unreachable** in practice.
>
> **Tied material counts as work-order material cost.** `WorkOrder.actual_cost`, the work-order
> read's `issued_material_cost` and the analytics cost variance sum `abs(total_cost)` over the work
> order's `ISSUE` rows (less `RETURN` credits) under **all three** reference shapes (`work_order`,
> `work_order_backflush` and `work_order_operation`) — one shared predicate
> (`work_order_ledger_filter`), so the stored rollup and the analytics leg cannot drift. A nest that
> burned six $80 sheets contributes $480. **A `JobCost` does not**: its sync on completion only
> rebuilds labor from time entries, and its `actual_material_cost` is the total of manually added
> MATERIAL entries. (This paragraph said "the synced `JobCost`" did until 2026-11-13; it never
> did.)
>
> **Scrap consumes**, and posts as `ISSUE` (not `SCRAP`): lot genealogy filters on `ISSUE`, so a
> `SCRAP` row would erase audited scrap material from the as-built record. The good/scrap split is
> recorded in the transaction `notes`.
>
> **Consumption never auto-reverses.** A negative delta (e.g. after an over-count walk-back) is a
> **no-op**, never an automatic `RETURN` — the material was already cut. Reversal is a separate,
> explicit, reasoned verb: `POST …/material-allocations/{allocation_id}/return`, shipped in PR 3 and
> documented under **Material ties** below. (This paragraph said the verb *"does not exist yet"* for
> three PRs after it shipped; corrected 2026-07-27.)
>
> **A shortage never fails the completion.** Insufficient stock drives the source lot negative,
> writes a tamper-evident **`ALLOCATION_SHORTAGE`** audit row, and emits a
> `material_allocation_shortage` warning event. It is the allocation twin of `BACKFLUSH_SHORTAGE` /
> `backflush_shortage` and is deliberately kept distinct from it in the audit trail. **Both are now in
> the notification catalog** — `material.allocation_shortage` and, since PR 4.4,
> `material.backflush_shortage` (both Purchasing / warning, in-app + email to the Purchasing and
> Inventory departments); the backflush event had been emitted with no catalog row since Batch 6 and
> therefore notified nobody. The **rolled-back** case — where the draw raised and the savepoint undid
> it, so no stock moved at all — is separately keyed as `material.allocation_consumption_failed` /
> `material.backflush_failed`, so "stock went negative" and "stock never moved" are distinguishable
> without opening the audit log. PR 4.5 adds a third backflush key,
> **`material.backflush_demand_refused`** (same category / severity / channels / recipients), for the
> case where no draw was attempted at all because a blocking diagnostic condemned the demand — see the
> completion-time refusal above. It is emitted **once per refused scope**, not once per diagnostic.
> See [docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md](NOTIFICATIONS.md).
>
> **`GET /work-orders/{id}/backflush-preview` — the dry run (PR 4.5).** Returns, for this work order,
> what a completion would draw out of stock: one `BackflushPreviewLine` per component, each carrying
> `required_quantity`, `already_issued`, the `delta_quantity` that would actually post, the ordered
> `lots` the draw would hit, `shortfall` / `would_go_negative`, and — where the shared policy passed over
> segregated stock — `held_quantity_skipped` / `held_lot_numbers`. Three fields answer questions the
> first cut of this endpoint could not: each lot carries **`is_shortfall`** (the writer posts the unmet
> remainder as a SECOND issue against the last lot it drew, driving that lot negative and putting *its*
> number on the as-built record — so a line may legitimately list one `inventory_item_id` twice);
> **`shortfall_creates_placeholder`** says the part has no stock row at all, so the completion would
> mint a lot-less placeholder row instead; and **`pinned_lot_is_held`** says a tie's pinned lot has gone
> on hold / quarantine / rejected *since* it was pinned and the completion will consume it anyway
> (recording `HELD_MATERIAL_CONSUMED`) — the one warning the `held_*` fields structurally cannot carry,
> because a pinned draw is never short. Response-level `blockers` /
> `advisories` are the demand resolver's diagnostics for **this** work order, including the routing
> conditions the part-level readiness check cannot see. Any authenticated tenant user; a cross-tenant or
> unknown id is **404**.
> - **It models the ISSUE LOOP, not just the demand resolver** — both legs in the real order
>   (work-order-scoped ties first, so a tie's lot pin gets first claim), the legacy
>   `('work_order', ISSUE)` fence, the reconcile-to-target delta, and the actual lot pick through the
>   same `consumable_source_items` + `plan_stock_draw` the writer uses. Preview and outcome therefore
>   cannot disagree about which heat gets consumed — which is exactly the failure a preview built on its
>   own predicate would produce silently.
> - **Pure read. It writes NOTHING** — no ledger row, no `audit_log` row (in particular no
>   `BACKFLUSH_DOUBLE_ISSUE_BLOCKED`, which the suppression layer used to write from inside the
>   resolver), no operational event, nothing to commit. That is **structural**, not careful: the
>   resolution layer takes no `AuditService` at all and the recording layer is a separate function only
>   the completion path calls. Same rule as the per-allocation consumption read on this router — a poll
>   is not an actor and records no reason.
> - **Lines appear whether or not the part has opted in** (each carries `requires_opt_in`, and the
>   response carries the part's current `backflush_components`), because the operator reading it is
>   deciding whether to opt in.
> - **`suppression_reason` values:** `converged` (the ledger already holds the whole target — the
>   healthy steady state), `already_issued` (a legacy pre-4.4 one-shot row fences this work order out
>   for that part, permanently), `ledger_consumed` (a tie already drew it), `open_operation_tie` (an
>   open operation-scoped tie owns the demand; the material still moves, on the per-run engine), and
>   `blocking_diagnostic` (a blocking diagnostic stands, so the completion refuses that component and
>   records `BACKFLUSH_DEMAND_REFUSED` instead of issuing it).
> - **`basis` is `quantity_complete + operation scrap`.** A work order that has produced nothing has a
>   basis of 0 and therefore **no BOM lines at all**. That is the resolver's real behavior, not a preview
>   artifact — and it is why part-level readiness runs at a synthetic basis of 1.0 instead.
>
> **Labor-hour + cost rollup on completion is opt-in (global flag `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED`,
> default OFF).** When the flag is **on**, a work order reaching **COMPLETE** (any path, including
> reconcile-on-read) rolls op/WO `actual_hours` monotonic-up from time-entry evidence, computes
> `actual_cost` = **labor + issued material + overhead** (labor at `WorkCenter.hourly_rate`, falling
> back to `DEFAULT_LABOR_RATE`; overhead at `DEFAULT_OVERHEAD_RATE` — see
> [Environment Variables](ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md)), syncs any linked `JobCost` to status `COMPLETED`,
> and writes one **audited** rollup row — all atomic with the completion, best-effort (a cost-side
> error never fails the completion). Hours sum across **all operators'** time entries on an operation
> (multiple operators are summed, not deduped). When the flag is **off** (the default), completion does
> **not** auto-populate `actual_cost` / `actual_hours` and touches no `JobCost`; the on-demand
> `POST /job-costs/{id}/calculate` is then the only way to materialize cost actuals. The
> `no_labor_recorded` quality exception (above) fires regardless of this flag.
>
> **Scrap reason is required when scrap is reported (AS9100D defect traceability).** The same rule
> the shop floor enforces (see "Scrap reason is required when scrap is reported" under Shop Floor) now
