> and `PUT /shop-floor/operations/{id}/start` evaluate the operator against the operation's work
> center and **record** (never block) any unsatisfied qualification gate — the clock-in / start still
> **succeeds** (these are operator-facing; the gate only records). Clock-in is open to **any
> authenticated user**; the start verb is Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Operator / Quality since
> P0.4 (2026-11-13), a role gate, not a qualification one. Each unsatisfied gate writes a tamper-evident `audit_log` row (action
> **`OPERATOR_QUALIFICATION_EXCEPTION`**) plus a warning operational event, and is surfaced on a
> `qualification_exceptions` array on the response — on the clock-in `TimeEntryResponse` and on the
> start-operation response body. The gates are:
> - `operator_not_skill_qualified` (severity `medium`): no active `SkillMatrix` entry at
>   `skill_level >= 2` ("Basic", a module constant `MIN_SKILL_LEVEL`) for the operation's work center.
> - `operator_certification_missing_or_expired` (severity `high`): where the work center declares a
>   `required_certification_type`, the operator holds no current (active / expiring-soon)
>   `OperatorCertification` of that type. When the work center has no required cert type (the common
>   case) this leg is skipped.
>
> Each entry is `{ "code", "message", "reference_type", "reference_id", "severity" }`; the field
> defaults to `[]`, so an all-clear clock-in / start is shape-compatible with the pre-G5-B response.
> The gate is **tenant-scoped** — every skill/cert/work-center lookup filters the active company.
>
> **Operator-certifications router is fully tenant-scoped (as of 2026-06-09).** Beyond the gate above,
> the operator-certifications read/by-id endpoints now filter the active `company_id`:
> - **Skill matrix:** the read endpoints under `GET /operator-certifications/skill-matrix/…` —
>   `check/{user_id}/{work_center_id}`, `user/{user_id}`, `work-center/{work_center_id}`, and the list —
>   the `POST .../skill-matrix/` writer, and `PUT .../skill-matrix/{entry_id}` (`update_skill_entry`)
>   all filter `SkillMatrix.company_id`. The model's unique constraint is now tenant-qualified too —
>   `(company_id, user_id, work_center_id)` via migration `045_skillmatrix_company_unique`.
> - **Certifications / training:** `GET /operator-certifications/certifications/dashboard` (its cert
>   counts, compliance rate, operators-with/without-certs — `User` now `company_id`-scoped — and
>   training-hours-this-month aggregates), `GET .../certifications/expiring`,
>   `GET .../certifications/user/{user_id}`, `GET .../certifications/{cert_id}`,
>   `GET .../training/user/{user_id}`, and `PUT .../training/{training_id}` (`update_training`) all
>   filter the active company; a cross-tenant id now returns **404** before any read/mutation.
>
> These remain open to **any authenticated user** — the tenant-scoping fix added company scoping, not an RBAC change.
>
> **Operator-certifications WRITE endpoints are now role-gated, audited, and FK-validated (2026-06-09).**
> The seven write endpoints on this router are no longer open to any authenticated user (they had no
> RBAC rows before):
> - **Certifications + training:** `POST/PUT/DELETE /operator-certifications/certifications/{…}` and
>   `POST/PUT /operator-certifications/training/{…}` → `require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER, QUALITY])`.
> - **Skill matrix:** `POST /operator-certifications/skill-matrix/` and
>   `PUT /operator-certifications/skill-matrix/{entry_id}` → `require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR])`.
>
> Any other authenticated role gets **403**. Each write writes a tamper-evident `audit_log` row
> (resource types `operator_certification` / `training_record` / `skill_matrix`; create/update/delete —
> `GET /audit/`). On the create endpoints (and `update_training`'s re-pointed `work_center_id`), a
> `user_id` / `work_center_id` that does not belong to the active company is rejected with **422**
> (`"… does not reference a … in your company"`) before insert — a cross-tenant FK-injection guard. The
> read endpoints listed above are unchanged (any authenticated user, tenant-scoped). See
> `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Operator Certifications & Training / Skill Matrix.

#### Inspection Schema

`POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/inspection` signs off an operation's in-process inspection. It sets
`inspection_complete = True` (clearing the `inspection_incomplete` gate above) and is the **only**
writer of that flag: `PUT /work-orders/operations/{id}` refuses the field (below). It is
**tenant-scoped** and role-gated to **Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality** (there is no separate
Inspector role). In the app the control is the **Sign off** button beside the "Inspection required"
chip on Work Order Detail operation rows and on the Shop Floor (`/shop-floor/operations`) operation
cards, offered to those four roles only where `requires_inspection` is true and the inspection is not
yet signed.

Both fields are optional; `{}` is a valid sign-off:

```json
{
  "inspection_type": "final",
  "notes": "All critical characteristics within tolerance"
}
```

`inspection_type` is free text (≤ 100 characters; the app offers `in_process` / `first_article` /
`final`). When it is omitted the operation keeps the type it already has — a routing inspection point
stamps `final` — so the app sends it only when the signer picks a different one. `notes` is ≤ 2000
characters. Over-length fields are **422** and sign nothing.

Refusals, in the order they are checked, each before anything is written:

- **403** for a crew-station badge token (`scope="kiosk"`), of any role: the kiosk path fence denies
  `/shop-floor/operations/{id}/inspection`, as it does labor approval (see Authentication → Path fence).
- **403** (role gate) for Operator / Shipping / Viewer.
- **403** for any standing API token, whatever its role or scope, before the operation is read (so a
  token cannot probe whether an id exists): `An inspection is signed off by a person signed in to the
  app, not an API token: recording that an inspection was performed is a person's judgment.`
  (`API_TOKEN_INSPECTION_SIGN_OFF`; see
  [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes)).
- **404** `Operation not found` for a missing or other-company operation, and for one whose work order
  is soft-deleted.
- **503** `The audit record for this inspection sign-off could not be saved; nothing was signed off.
  Retry.` — the `MARK_OPERATION_INSPECTED` audit row is **required** evidence, written in the same
  transaction (old / new `inspection_complete` and `inspection_type`, plus `extra_data`
  `{work_order_id, work_order_number, notes}`); if it cannot be written the flag is not saved.

On success it also emits the `operation_inspected` operational event and a shop-floor websocket
broadcast `{event: "operation_inspected", work_order_id, operation_id}`, and bumps the operation's
`version` (a later operation `PUT` carrying the pre-sign-off version gets the usual **409**). The
**200** body:

```json
{
  "message": "Operation inspection recorded",
  "operation_id": 412,
  "work_order_id": 87,
  "requires_inspection": true,
  "inspection_complete": true,
  "inspection_type": "final",
  "signed_off_by_id": 15,
  "signed_off_by_name": "Dana Reyes",
  "signed_off_at": "2026-11-23T15:04:05.123456Z"
}
```

`signed_off_by_*` / `signed_off_at` describe **this** sign-off and come from the audit row it just
wrote. The operation has no inspected-by / inspected-at column, so no operation read carries them; the
app shows who signed and when only in the session that signed, and the audit log is the lasting record.

Signing an operation that is already signed is accepted and writes a further audit row (old
`inspection_complete: true`); nothing clears the flag. The verb also accepts an operation that is not
an inspection point (`requires_inspection: false`) and any operation or work-order status; the app
offers it on neither a signed operation nor a non-inspection-point one (nor, on Work Order Detail, on a
cancelled laser nest's operation).

#### Time-entry approval

`POST /shop-floor/time-entries/{id}/approve` and `POST /shop-floor/time-entries/{id}/unapprove`
let a supervisor sign off on shop-floor labor (G5-A). Approve sets `approved` (timestamp) +
`approved_by` (the approver); unapprove clears both. Both:

> - are **role-gated to Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality** — any other role is **403**;
> - **forbid self-approval**: a user cannot approve or unapprove their **own** TimeEntry (segregation
>   of duties for the labor-cost gate) — **403** (`"You cannot approve or unapprove your own time
>   entry"`), even if the caller holds an approver role;
> - are **tenant-scoped**: an id belonging to another company returns **404** before any mutation;
> - are **idempotent** (approving an already-approved entry, or unapproving an already-unapproved one,
>   is a no-op that returns the current state with **no second audit row**);
> - respect the TimeEntry's optimistic-lock `version` column — a concurrent stale write returns
>   **409 Conflict** (`"This time entry was modified concurrently. Refresh and retry."`);
> - write **one** tamper-evident `audit_log` row (action `time_entry_approve` / `time_entry_unapprove`).
>
> Both return the updated `TimeEntryResponse` (now carrying `approved` / `approved_by`; these also
> surface on `GET /shop-floor/my-active-job`). Approval is what the opt-in
> `REQUIRE_APPROVED_LABOR_FOR_COST` flag keys on: when that flag is **on**, only approved TimeEntries
> feed the labor-cost legs (job costing, completion cost rollup, and the analytics OEE/labor leg).
> When the flag is **off** (the default), approval is recorded but does not affect costing. See
> `docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md`.

#### Clock Out Schema

`POST /shop-floor/clock-out/{time_entry_id}` body (`ClockOut`):

```json
{
  "quantity_produced": 50,
  "quantity_scrapped": 2,
  "scrap_reason": "Drill bit broke",
  "scrap_reason_code_id": 3,
  "notes": "Replaced drill bit, resumed operation"
}
```

> When `quantity_scrapped` > 0 a reason is **required** — either `scrap_reason_code_id` (a
> predefined code from `GET /quality/scrap-reason-codes`) or a non-blank free-text `scrap_reason`;
> neither present returns **422**. Both stay optional when no scrap is reported. See "A scrap reason
> is required when scrap is reported" and "Structured scrap reason CODE" under the shop-floor notes
> above. A quantity that is not a finite number (`NaN`, `Infinity`) is refused **400** `Quantity must
> be a valid number` for everyone, before the negative check and any write (it used to close the entry,
> commit NaN and then 500). A standing API token sending `quantity_scrapped > 0` is refused **403**
> (owner decision 2026-11-07 — only a person declares scrap) before any lock or write, and the entry
> stays open; so is one sending a `scrap_reason` / `scrap_reason_code_id` that would change the one on
> its time entry, even with no scrap (this PR's extension — re-categorizing scrap is the same
> judgment). Its zero-scrap clock-out without a reason is unchanged.
>
> The response (`TimeEntryResponse`) carries **`operation_status`** — the operation's status after
> this clock-out (`"complete"` when the clock-out itself completed it at a full good count; `null` on
> clock-in). A clock-out completes the operation only when good covers every unit that reached it;
> scrap never counts. On an already-COMPLETE operation a clock-out carrying pieces is **409** and a
> 0-piece clock-out is labor-only (see "Clock-out under the same rule" above).

#### Complete Operation Schema

`POST /shop-floor/operations/{operation_id}/complete` body (`OperationCompleteRequest`,
`extra="forbid"`). A full-count close needs no fields beyond the channel:

```json
{ "source": "kiosk" }
```

A short close that declares the lost pieces (the operation recorded 8 good of 10 received):

```json
{
  "quantity_scrapped": 2,
  "scrap_reason_code_id": 3,
  "scrap_reason": "Cracked at the bend",
  "acknowledge_open_entries": true,
  "source": "kiosk"
}
```

Response **200** (always a close):

```json
{
  "message": "Operation completed",
  "operation": {
    "id": 812, "status": "complete", "quantity_complete": 8, "quantity_scrapped": 2,
    "upstream_quantity_short": 0, "quantity_short_declared": 2,
    "actual_start": "2026-11-07T14:02:11Z", "actual_end": "2026-11-07T16:40:03Z"
  },
  "work_order": { "id": 301, "status": "complete", "quantity_complete": 8 },
  "is_fully_complete": true,
  "quality_exceptions": [],
  "closed_time_entries": [{ "time_entry_id": 4471, "user_id": 12, "operator_name": "Bob K." }],
  "next_operation": null
}
```

> `quantity_complete` is **deprecated** — an expectation check that is never stored (**409** above the
> recorded good). `quantity_scrapped` is an **additive** delta, not a total. Refusals and texts:
> "Floor completion contract" above and Work Orders → "Short count at completion".

#### Over-count correction Schema

`POST /shop-floor/operations/{operation_id}/reduce-production` body (`ProductionReductionRequest` —
the **same body** is shared by the office twin
`POST /work-orders/operations/{operation_id}/reduce-production`) — walk back an over-reported good
count on the caller's own **unapproved** labor (open clock-in first, then their own earlier
unapproved sessions; **not** scrap; see "Over-count correction" under the shop-floor notes above):

```json
{
  "quantity_delta": 3,
  "reason": "double-scanned the tray",
  "source": "kiosk",
  "notes": "recount was 47, not 50"
}
```

Response **200** (`operation` stays in progress; `active_time_entry.clock_out` is `null` for the
caller's still-open entry; `reduced_time_entries[]` is the per-entry paper trail of the walk, in
walk order — open entry first, then the caller's closed unapproved sessions newest-first):

```json
{
  "message": "Production quantity corrected",
  "operation": {
    "id": 812,
    "status": "in_progress",
    "quantity_complete": 47,
    "quantity_scrapped": 2,
    "quantity_ordered": 50
  },
  "active_time_entry": {
    "id": 4471,
    "quantity_produced": 0,
    "quantity_scrapped": 2,
    "clock_out": null
  },
  "reduced_time_entries": [
    {
      "time_entry_id": 4471,
      "entry_type": "run",
      "quantity_produced_before": 1,
      "quantity_produced_after": 0
    },
    {
      "time_entry_id": 4460,
      "entry_type": "run",
      "quantity_produced_before": 12,
      "quantity_produced_after": 10
    }
  ]
}
```

(The example walks a delta of 3: the open clock-in's 1 piece is exhausted first, then 2 come off
the caller's most recent closed unapproved session.)

> `quantity_delta` must be `> 0`; `reason` is **required** and non-blank (a correction reason, not a
> scrap reason). The delta may not exceed the caller's own **unapproved** recorded evidence on the
> operation (**400** — approved labor is excluded and needs a supervisor), and the endpoint refuses
> with **409** once the operation/WO is complete. `reopen_operation` (default `false`) is
> **office-only**: this verb refuses `true` with **422** `reopen_operation is an office correction`. See the full guardrail / error-code contract in
> "Over-count correction" under the shop-floor notes above.
>
> The **office twin** `POST /work-orders/operations/{operation_id}/reduce-production` (Admin /
> Manager / Supervisor; see "Over-count correction … (supervisor/office)" under Work Orders) returns
> the same shape except `active_time_entry` is replaced by
> `work_order {"id", "quantity_complete"}` (the recomputed rollup) — there is no caller clock-in on
> that path — and its `reduced_time_entries[]` may span **multiple operators'** unapproved entries.
> On a COMPLETE operation it requires `reopen_operation: true` whenever the lowered count would leave
> the operation short; `operation.status` then reads `in_progress` (see Work Orders → "Correcting a
> completed operation").

### Scanner (QR / barcode)

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| POST | `/scanner/resolve-action` | Resolve a scanned traveler/badge code into a typed action context (A0.4) | Yes |
| POST | `/scanner/lookup` | Look up a scanned barcode: supplier part number → internal part number → work order number | Yes |
| GET | `/scanner/mappings` | List supplier part-number mappings | Yes |
| POST | `/scanner/mappings` | Create a supplier part-number mapping — **404** on a soft-deleted `vendor_id` (see note) | Yes |
| DELETE | `/scanner/mappings/{mapping_id}` | Deactivate a supplier part-number mapping | Yes |

> **`POST /scanner/resolve-action` (A0.4 QR traveler / badge scan plumbing).** Every scan surface
> (kiosk, wedge scanner, phone) posts the raw scanned text and gets back a **discriminated union**
> keyed on `kind` — `operation` | `work_order` | `employee` | `unknown`. Request body:
> `{ "code": "<raw scanned text>", "work_center_id": <optional station work center id> }` (`code`
> 1–255 chars, whitespace stripped; `work_center_id` only drives the `work_center_match` flag on
> operation scans — it never widens access). Open to **any authenticated user** — it mirrors the
> read-broad shop-floor reads. Code formats (prefix/scheme matching is case-insensitive):
> - `OP:{operation_id}` — a traveler routing-step code → `kind: "operation"`.
> - `WO:{work_order_number}` — a work-order code → `kind: "work_order"` (exact match, with a
>   case-insensitive exact fallback). Still accepted, though current travelers print URL QRs
>   (below) rather than bare `WO:` codes.
> - **URL-shaped codes** (`http://` / `https://`) — what the printed traveler QRs now encode, so a
>   phone camera opens the app while a wedge gun types the same text into this endpoint. Two URL
>   forms resolve; the **host is deliberately not validated** (travelers may be printed against any
>   deployment origin — the URL carries no tenant authority; tenancy comes from the authenticated
>   caller, same as every other code shape):
>   - a `scan` query param (the per-operation traveler QR, e.g.
>     `{origin}/shop-floor/operations?scan=OP%3A123`) — URL-decoded **one level only** and
>     re-resolved as `OP:` / `WO:` / badge; a `scan` value that is itself a URL is a structured
>     miss.
>   - a `/work-orders/{id}` path (the traveler header QR; trailing slash allowed) — resolves the
>     work order by integer primary key → the same `kind: "work_order"` shape as `WO:{number}`.
>
>   Every result — hit or miss — echoes the **original scanned URL** in `code`, so operators see
>   exactly what was scanned.
> - anything else — probed as an employee badge id (exact match on an **active** user's
>   `employee_id`) → `kind: "employee"`.
> - no match / malformed → `kind: "unknown"` with `{ code, reason }`, returned with **HTTP 200** —
>   a structured miss, not an error, because wedge scanners hit unknown codes constantly.
>
> **`kind: "operation"`** carries an operation summary (sequence, status, WO number/status, part,
> work center, quantities, plus `work_center_match` — true/false when the request named a station,
> `null` otherwise), `legal_actions` — the subset of
> `clock_in | report_production | complete | hold | resume` the **calling user** could perform
> right now — and `blockers`, a map of action → human-readable reasons, present only for actions
> **not** in `legal_actions`. The gating is derived from the same predicates the live shop-floor
> write endpoints enforce (`app/services/operation_action_gates.py`, extracted from those
> handlers, which now call the same helpers), and it **mirrors the live endpoints' gating
> verbatim — clients should treat blocker text as display-ready** (a kiosk showing a resolver
> blocker and a kiosk showing the endpoint's 400 show the same message). The summary also carries
> `upstream_quantity_short` and `quantity_unaccounted` (owner ruling 1), figured on the
> evidence-floored good. They are informational: `complete` in `legal_actions` stays a **state**
> check, so it can be listed for an operation whose close the endpoint would still refuse **409**
> because units are unaccounted (see Work Orders → "Short count at completion").
>
> **Routing-staleness warning is a documented proxy.** `warning: "routing_revision_changed"` (with
> the accompanying `routing_revision_check` object) flags that the part's current **released**
> routing was released after the work order's release/creation baseline — i.e. any traveler
> printed from this WO predates the routing now in force. This is **timestamp inference, not an
> exact check**: work orders do not snapshot the routing revision their operations were generated
> from, and traveler prints are not recorded server-side. `routing_revision_check` carries the
> current released routing's `current_released_revision`, the boolean
> `released_routing_changed_after_wo_creation` (`null` when either side lacks a usable timestamp),
> the `checked_against` baseline (WO `released_at`, else `created_at`), and a `note` restating the
> proxy semantics. An exact check requires a WO-level routing snapshot (pending; not in the data
> model today).
>
> **`kind: "work_order"`** returns the WO summary plus its operation list (id / sequence /
> operation number / name / status) and `current_operation_id` — the first non-complete operation
> by sequence (computed, not the stale column).
>
> **`kind: "employee"` is a lookup ONLY** — `{ employee_id, first_name, last_initial }`, no
> tokens, no session, **no auth side effects**. Badge **login** stays exclusively on
> `POST /auth/employee-login`.
>
> **Read-only / zero-write.** Resolving a scan writes **no audit rows** and emits **no operational
> events** — it has GET semantics in a POST body (POST keeps raw scanner text out of URLs and
> access logs). **Tenant-scoped:** every lookup filters the active company; a code that exists in
> another tenant — and a soft-deleted work order (or an operation whose WO is soft-deleted) —
> resolves to `kind: "unknown"` exactly like a code that exists nowhere.

> **Supplier part-number mappings and soft-deleted vendors.** A mapping is a **live routing rule**
> ("this barcode means this part, from this supplier"), not a historical record, and nothing
> deactivates it when its vendor is removed — so `POST /scanner/mappings` now refuses a soft-deleted
> `vendor_id` (**404** "Vendor not found"). Mappings that already point at one are deliberately
> **kept**: the part half is what resolves the scan at the dock, and dropping the row would break
> barcode lookup over a vendor bookkeeping change. Only the supplier name is withheld —
> **`vendor_name` reads `null`** for a mapping whose vendor is soft-deleted, on both
> `POST /scanner/lookup` and `GET /scanner/mappings`. The field is `Optional[str]` and has always
> been `null` for a mapping with no vendor at all, so the response *shape* is unchanged.

### Quality

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/quality/inspections/` | List inspections | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/inspections/` | Create inspection | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/inspections/{id}` | Get inspection by ID | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/inspections/{id}/approve` | Approve inspection | Quality |
| GET | `/quality/scrap-reason-codes` | List scrap reason codes (active only by default; `category` / `include_inactive` filters) | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/scrap-reason-codes` | Create a scrap reason code | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| PUT | `/quality/scrap-reason-codes/{reason_code_id}` | Update a scrap reason code (deactivate via `is_active: false`) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| GET | `/quality/ncr` | List live NCRs, newest first (`status` / `part_id` filters) | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/ncr` | File an NCR; `part_id` / `work_order_id`, when given, must be live records of the active company (**404** otherwise). See "NCR / CAR writes" | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}` | Get a live NCR | Yes |
| PUT | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}` | Edit, disposition (the server stamps who decided it), record the action taken and the customer concession, close, reopen, assign, or link a CAR. See "NCR / CAR writes" and "NCR disposition evidence" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/reverification` | Record the re-verification of reworked or repaired product; body `{ "result": "conforming" or "nonconforming", "notes": "<non-blank>" }`. Server-stamped, re-recordable. **409** on a CLOSED NCR or unless it is dispositioned `rework` / `repair`, **403** for a standing API token. See "NCR disposition evidence" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| DELETE | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}` | **Void** an NCR (soft-delete + status → `void`); body `{ "reason": "<non-blank>" }`. Guarded, see note | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/restore` | Restore a voided NCR — reopens it to `open` | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/create-car` | Raise a CAR from the NCR and link it, prefilled with the NCR's part and PO number; **409** naming the CAR when one that is not void is already linked | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| GET | `/quality/car` | List CARs, void ones included (`status` filter) | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/car` | Open a CAR, including the CAR form fields. See "CAR form fields" | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/car/{car_id}` | Get a CAR | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/car/{car_id}/pdf` | The printable CAR (PDF, `inline`) in the layout of Werco's controlled CAR form. Writes nothing. See "Printable CAR" | Yes |
| PUT | `/quality/car/{car_id}` | Edit, verify, close, reopen, or assign a CAR. See "NCR / CAR writes" and "CAR corrective-action evidence" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/car/{car_id}/quality-approval` | Record the form's Quality Manager approval; no body. Server-stamped, once. **409** on a VOID or already-approved CAR, **403** for a standing API token. See "Quality Manager approval" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/car/{car_id}/effectiveness` | Record the effectiveness verification of the corrective action; body `{ "result": "effective" or "not_effective", "evidence": "<non-blank>" }`. Server-stamped, re-recordable, only while the CAR is in `verification` (**409** otherwise); `not_effective` returns it to `corrective_action`. **403** for a standing API token. See "CAR corrective-action evidence" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/car/{car_id}/void` | **Void** a CAR; body `{ "reason": "<non-blank>" }`; returns the CAR with `status: "void"`. See note | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/car/{car_id}/restore` | Restore a voided CAR — reopens it to `open`; **409** when the CAR is not void. See note | Admin / Manager / Quality |

> **Scrap reason codes (Lean Phase 1).** The tenant's structured scrap vocabulary, referenced by the
> optional `scrap_reason_code_id` accepted on the three scrap write paths —
> `POST /shop-floor/clock-out/{id}`, `POST /shop-floor/operations/{id}/production`, and
> `POST /work-orders/{id}/complete` (see those sections). Shape:
> `{id, code, name, category, description, is_active, display_order}`; `category` is one of
> `material | machine | tooling | operator | setup | programming | engineering | supplier | handling |
> other`. `code` is unique **per tenant** — a duplicate returns **400** (`"Scrap reason code already
> exists"`). Reads are open to any authenticated user (the kiosk/desktop scrap pickers); writes are
> role-gated to **Admin / Manager / Quality** and write tamper-evident `audit_log` rows (resource type
> `scrap_reason_code`). There is deliberately **no DELETE endpoint** — historical scrap rows reference
> these ids (traceability), so retirement is `is_active: false`, never a row removal.

> **NCR void + restore (`NonConformanceReport` now `SoftDeleteMixin`).** Voiding is the quality-record
> form of a soft delete: `DELETE /quality/ncr/{ncr_id}` marks the NCR `is_deleted` **and** moves it to
> `VOID` status (the status already existed), retaining it for AS9100D traceability and the
> tamper-evident audit trail while dropping it from all live reads (which now filter
> `is_deleted == false`). The request **requires a non-blank JSON body `{ "reason": "..." }`**
> (whitespace-only → **422**); gate **Admin / Manager / Quality**. **Guardrail:** the void is **refused
> with 400** while the NCR still **actively gates a work order** — an `OPEN`/`ACKNOWLEDGED`
> `WorkOrderBlocker` references it — resolve the blocker first; a re-void returns **400** ("already
> voided"). `POST /quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/restore` clears the soft-delete and reopens the NCR to
> **`OPEN`** (the pre-void status is not preserved — a safe reset). An NCR voided while CLOSED comes
> back OPEN without its closure: restore clears `closed_date` / `closed_by`, as a reopen does. Both
> actions are **required-audited** (see "NCR / CAR writes" below): the void writes a `STATUS_CHANGE`
> row (→ `void`, reason in the description and `extra_data.reason`) **and** a `DELETE` row
> (`soft_delete=true`, reason in `extra_data`); restore writes a `RESTORE` row (old/new `is_deleted`
> and `status`, plus `closed_date` / `closed_by` when it cleared them). Another company's `ncr_id` is
> **404** with nothing changed.

> **NCR / CAR writes (`services/quality_record_service.py`).** Every NCR and CAR write behind
> `/quality/ncr` and `/quality/car` — create, `PUT` (including disposition, closure, reopen and CAR
> verification), `create-car`, NCR void / restore, CAR void / restore, the CAR quality-approval
> verb, the NCR re-verification verb and the CAR effectiveness verb — commits together with a
> **required** `audit_log` row in one transaction.
> If that row cannot be written, the change is rolled back and the route answers **503**
> (`"Unable to save audit record"`), the same posture as FAI and job costing. The `ncr_*` / `car_*`
> operational events are still emitted, but as notification / timeline telemetry, not as the audit
> record. NCRs and CARs created elsewhere do not go through this service yet. The receiving
> rejection, the shop-floor scrap → NCR, the process-sheet out-of-tolerance → NCR and the AI action
> applier write their creation row best-effort. The customer-complaint `create-ncr` / `create-car`
> verbs are required-audited in their own service (`services/customer_complaint_service.py`; see
> **Customer Complaints & RMA**).
>
> - **One audit row per request** (resource type `ncr` / `car`), holding every changed field old → new
>   plus `extra_data.changes` in the `log_update` diff shape. The action is `STATUS_CHANGE` when
>   `status` moved and `UPDATE` otherwise; `extra_data` flags `closure`, `reopen`,
>   `disposition_change` (NCR) and `verification` (CAR). Create writes a `CREATE` row with the new
>   record. `create-car` writes a CAR `CREATE` row (`extra_data.ncr_id` / `ncr_number`) **and** an NCR
>   `UPDATE` row recording the `car_required` / `car_id` link. The quality approval writes one
>   `APPROVE` row (old/new `quality_approved_by` / `quality_approved_at`,
>   `extra_data.quality_approval = true`). A disposition change carries the server's
>   `dispositioned_by` / `dispositioned_at` stamp, and any re-verification it cleared, on its row;
>   a CAR `PUT` changing `root_cause` or `corrective_action` likewise carries any effectiveness
>   verification it cleared.
>   The NCR re-verification writes one `UPDATE` row (old/new `reverification_result` /
>   `reverification_notes` / `reverified_by` / `reverified_at`, `extra_data.reverification = true`).
>   The CAR effectiveness verification writes one row, `STATUS_CHANGE` when a `not_effective`
>   result moved the status and `UPDATE` otherwise (old/new `effectiveness_check` /
>   `effectiveness_result` / `effectiveness_verified_by` / `effectiveness_verified_at`, plus
>   `status` when it moved; `extra_data.effectiveness_verification = true`).
> - **Only real changes are written.** Each requested value is compared with the stored one (`""`
>   equals `null`, a decimal equals the stored number, enums compare by value), and unchanged fields
>   are dropped. A `PUT` that changes nothing writes no audit row, emits no event and returns **200**,
>   so re-saving the detail screen's full payload is safe. The `changed_fields` on
>   `ncr_updated` / `car_updated` lists only the fields that actually changed.
> - **References are tenant-validated before anything is written** (**404**, nothing changed). On
>   create, `part_id` must be a live part and `work_order_id` a live (not soft-deleted) work order of
>   the active company (`"Part not found"` / `"Work order not found"`; a soft-deleted work order used
>   to be accepted). On `PUT`, `assigned_to` must be an **active** user of the company
>   (`"Assigned user not found"`) and an NCR's `car_id` one of its CARs (`"CAR not found"`; a void CAR
>   is **409**). A CAR's form references (`part_id`, `customer_id`, `vendor_id`) are checked the same
>   way, with one exception for vendors; see "CAR form fields" below.
> - **Reads never expand another tenant's part.** NCR list / get and every NCR write response load
>   `part` only when it belongs to the active company, so a legacy row whose `part_id` names another
>   tenant's part shows `part: null`. A same-company soft-deleted part is still named (historical
>   record).
> - **CLOSED and VOID are final.** A `PUT` to a CLOSED NCR or CAR is **409** unless its **only**
>   change is moving `status` to an open state. That is the reopen: it clears `closed_date` /
>   `closed_by`, and the audit row keeps the cleared values. A CAR reopened straight to
>   `verification` also records its verifier on the same row (`extra_data` carries both `reopen` and
>   `verification`). A reopen combined with a content edit is **409**; reopen first, then edit in a
>   second save. The reopen captures **no reason** yet: the audit row records who and when, not why.
>   A VOID CAR (or a legacy NCR in `void` status that is not soft-deleted) refuses every change with
>   **409**; a voided NCR is soft-deleted, so its `PUT` is **404**. `status: "void"` through `PUT` is
>   **422**; use the void verbs.
> - **Other `PUT` refusals.** An explicit `null` on NCR `status` / `disposition` / `car_required` /
>   `quantity_rejected` / `estimated_cost` / `actual_cost` or CAR `status` / `priority` is **422**
>   (`"<field> cannot be null"`). Closing an NCR or a CAR requires its evidence (**422**
>   `"Closure requires …"` naming everything missing); see "NCR disposition evidence" and "CAR
>   corrective-action evidence" below for the exact lists. A CAR `initiation_reason` of
>   `other` with a blank `initiation_reason_other` is **422** (create too). An `expected_updated_at`
>   that no longer matches the record is **409** (`"This record changed since you opened it. …"`). That
>   is the only conflict check: the required `version` field is **ignored** (NCRs and CARs carry no
>   version column), so a client that omits `expected_updated_at` gets last-writer-wins on the fields
>   it changes.
> - **`create-car` is idempotent.** It locks the NCR first. When the NCR already links a CAR that is
>   not void, it answers **409** (`"NCR … already has corrective action CAR-… (id N). Open that CAR
>   instead of creating another."`) rather than minting a second CAR and relinking. Once the linked
>   CAR is voided, a fresh one may be raised and the link moves to it. It is allowed on a CLOSED NCR,
>   because it changes only `car_required` / `car_id`. The new CAR is prefilled with the NCR's
>   `part_id` (only when that part belongs to the company; a soft-deleted one is still carried, as the
>   record it inherits), its `po_number` as `vendor_po_number`, and today's Central date as
>   `submitted_date`.

> **NCR disposition evidence (migration `127_ncr_car_records`, AS9100D 8.7).** An NCR records what
> was done with the nonconforming product, the customer's concession where one is needed, who
> decided the disposition, and the re-verification of corrected product. Every new column is
> nullable; an NCR filed before `127` reads `null` in each (nothing was backfilled).
>
> | Field | Type | Written by | Rule |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `action_taken` | text ≤ 4000 | `PUT` | What was physically done to the nonconforming product. Required to close |
> | `concession_reference` | text ≤ 100 | `PUT` | The customer's deviation / waiver / concession number. Required to close a `use_as_is` or `repair` disposition. **Not by a standing API token** |
> | `concession_authorized_by` | text ≤ 255 | `PUT` | Who at the customer authorized it (a name, not a user: the authorizer is outside the company). **Not by a standing API token** |
> | `concession_date` | date | `PUT` | When the customer authorized it. Later than today (Central) is **422** (`"The concession date cannot be in the future."`); an unchanged date is not re-checked. **Not by a standing API token** |
> | `dispositioned_by`, `dispositioned_at` | user id, UTC datetime | the server | Who decided the disposition, and when. Never accepted in a body |
> | `reverification_result` | `conforming` or `nonconforming` (DB CHECK `ck_ncrs_reverification_result`) | `POST /quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/reverification` | |
> | `reverification_notes` | text ≤ 4000 | the same verb | What was re-inspected or re-tested, against which requirement |
> | `reverified_by`, `reverified_at` | user id, UTC datetime | the server | Stamped by the re-verification verb. Never accepted in a body |
>
> `NCRResponse` adds every field above plus `dispositioned_by_name` and `reverified_by_name`, on
> every NCR route, list included. The names resolve tenant-scoped: a stamped user outside the company
> is named only when it is a superuser or Platform Admin who acted in this company's context, as on
> the CAR.
>
> - **The disposition stamp.** A `PUT` that changes `disposition` to anything but `pending` stamps
>   `dispositioned_by` (the caller) and `dispositioned_at` (now, UTC); changing it back to `pending`
>   clears both. Re-sending the stored disposition stamps nothing. The stamp rides on that request's
>   one audit row, old → new.
> - **A disposition change clears the re-verification.** A re-verification vouches for the
>   correction of one disposition (a rework verified conforming says nothing about a later repair),
>   so changing `disposition` sets `reverification_result`, `reverification_notes`, `reverified_by`
>   and `reverified_at` back to `null`. The cleared values stay on the same audit row, old → new.
> - **A standing API token may not change the judgment.** A token `PUT` that changes `disposition`
>   or any `concession_*` field (clearing included) is **403** (`"A standing API token cannot record
>   an NCR's disposition or customer concession. A person signed in to the app must record it."`),
>   before any write. Re-sending the stored values beside another edit is not a change and is not
>   refused, and `action_taken` is open to a token. See
>   [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).
> - **Closing (`status: "closed"`) needs its evidence.** Request validation runs first, unchanged:
>   the closing body itself must carry a `disposition` other than `pending` and a `root_cause` of at
>   least 20 characters (**422**). The service then judges the record as it would be saved (a value
>   this request changes, else the stored one) and refuses **422** `"Closure requires …"`, naming
>   everything missing in this order: `a disposition`, `action taken`, `a customer concession
>   reference (use-as-is and repair)`, `a conforming re-verification (rework and repair)`.
>
>   | Disposition | Required to close, beyond root cause |
>   |---|---|
>   | `scrap`, `return_to_vendor` | `action_taken` |
>   | `use_as_is` | `action_taken` and `concession_reference` |
>   | `rework` | `action_taken` and a stored `conforming` re-verification |
>   | `repair` | `action_taken`, `concession_reference` and a stored `conforming` re-verification |
>
>   The concession may be entered in the closing request itself. The re-verification cannot: only
>   its own verb writes it, so the gate reads the stored result. A `nonconforming` result does not
>   satisfy it, and a closing request that also changes the disposition clears it, so it cannot
>   close a `rework` / `repair` NCR. An NCR closed before `127` keeps its closure; reopened, it
>   meets this gate to close again.
>
> **Re-verification (`POST /quality/ncr/{ncr_id}/reverification`, MCP tool
> `record_ncr_reverification`).** Body `NCRReverificationRequest`
> `{ "result": "conforming" or "nonconforming", "notes": "..." }`. `notes` is required and trimmed,
> at most 4000 characters; blank or whitespace-only is **422**, and so is an unknown key. The server
> stamps `reverified_by` (the caller) and `reverified_at` (UTC). Neither is ever taken from a body,
> and no `PUT` body carries a `reverification_*` or `reverified_*` field. Gate **Admin / Manager /
> Quality**. Returns the NCR (`NCRResponse`).
>
> - **403** for a standing API token (`"A standing API token cannot record an NCR's re-verification.
>   A person signed in to the app must record it."`), before the NCR is read.
> - **409** on a CLOSED NCR (`"NCR … is closed; reopen it to record a re-verification."`; reopen
>   with a status-only `PUT` first) and on a legacy `void`-status row. A voided NCR is
>   soft-deleted, so it is **404**.
> - **409** unless the stored disposition is `rework` or `repair` (`"Re-verification applies to
>   rework and repair dispositions; NCR … is dispositioned <value>."`). Save a disposition change
>   before recording: the verb reads the stored disposition.
> - **Re-recordable.** A later re-verification replaces the earlier one (result, notes, who, when),
>   and the audit row keeps what it replaced. Only a `conforming` result lets a `rework` / `repair`
>   NCR close.
> - The NCR row is locked first, so concurrent re-verifications serialize. The required `UPDATE`
>   audit row commits with the stamp, or neither is saved (**503**). It emits `ncr_updated`
>   best-effort; the status does not move, so no `ncr.closed` notification fires.
> - The NCR detail screen shows who decided the disposition and when, the action-taken and
>   concession fields, and a **Re-verification** panel on a `rework` / `repair` NCR (or one still
>   carrying a recorded re-verification). **Record re-verification** shows for `quality:approve`
>   holders on an NCR that is not closed, is disabled while edits are unsaved, waits for the server, and shows a
>   refusal verbatim.

> **CAR form fields (migration `122_car_form_quote_rev`).** A CAR carries the fields of Werco's
> controlled form, "AS9100 PROCESS - Corrective Action Report". `POST /quality/car` and
> `PUT /quality/car/{car_id}` accept them (`CARFormFields`); all are optional and nullable, and a
> CAR raised before `122` reads `null` in every one (nothing was backfilled).
>
> | Field | Type | Rule |
> |---|---|---|
> | `initiation_reason` | one of `management_review`, `nonconformance_trend`, `customer_feedback`, `internal_audit`, `production_problems`, `external_audit`, `continuous_improvement`, `other` | One value per CAR (the form's eight boxes). `other` requires a non-blank `initiation_reason_other` (**422**). Held by the DB CHECK `ck_cars_initiation_reason`. Distinct from `car_type` |
> | `initiation_reason_other` | text ≤ 255 | The "Other ____" text. A `PUT` that moves `initiation_reason` off `other` without sending this field clears it (recorded old → `null` on the audit row) |
> | `rma_number` | text ≤ 50 | Free text: a Werco RMA, a customer's, or a paper back-entry |
> | `submitted_date` | date | "Date Submitted". Defaults to today in Central at create; a past date back-enters a paper CAR; a date after today (Central) is **422**. Due-date validation is unchanged |
> | `part_id` | id | A **live** part of the active company (**404** `"Part not found"`) |
> | `customer_id` | id | A **live** customer of the active company (**404** `"Customer not found"`). Its name is snapshotted into `customer_name`, which is never accepted in a request: re-taken when `customer_id` changes, cleared when it is cleared |
> | `vendor_id` | id | A vendor of the active company (**404** `"Vendor not found"`). **Inactive and soft-deleted vendors are accepted**: a supplier CAR can be the record of that supplier's removal (invariant 3's records exception, AS9100D 8.4) |
> | `vendor_po_number` | text ≤ 100 | "P.O number (if C/A applies to a vendor)" |
> | `cost_labor`, `cost_material`, `cost_outside_services`, `cost_shipping` | decimal, ≥ 0, at most 12 digits with 2 decimal places (**422** otherwise) | Blank is not zero: each stays `null` until entered |
> | `management_action` | text ≤ 2000 | |
> | `vendor_approval_name`, `vendor_approval_title`, `vendor_approval_date` | text ≤ 255, date | Vendor management approval. The date cannot be after today (Central) (**422**). **A standing API token may not fill or change these** (see below) |
> | `customer_approval_name`, `customer_approval_date` | text ≤ 255, date | Customer approval. The date cannot be after today (Central) (**422**). **A standing API token may not fill or change these** (see below) |
>
> - **The sign-off boxes are a person's entry.** A standing API token is refused with **403**
>   (`"A standing API token cannot record or change a CAR's vendor or customer approval. A person
>   signed in to the app must record it."`), before any write, when a create fills any vendor or
>   customer approval field or an update changes (or clears) one. Leaving them blank, or re-sending
>   the stored value beside another edit, is not refused. See
>   [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).
> - **Only a changed reference is checked.** On `PUT` a part, customer or vendor the CAR already
>   names is never re-validated, so a CAR keeps naming a part or customer retired after it was raised.
>   A new selection must pass the rules above.
> - **`CARResponse` adds** every field above plus `cost_total` (the sum of the entered buckets,
>   computed on read and never stored; `null` when none is entered), `part_number` / `part_name` /
>   `part_current_revision` (the part's revision **today**, read from the part; the CAR records no
>   revision of its own, and the detail screen labels it "current Rev"), `customer_name`,
>   `vendor_name`, `containment_due` / `corrective_due`, the `initiated_by` / `assigned_to` /
>   `verified_by` / `closed_by` ids with a `*_name` beside each, and `quality_approved_by` /
>   `quality_approved_by_name` / `quality_approved_at`. Part and vendor names are read without an
>   `is_deleted` filter (historical record), but always tenant-scoped, so a legacy row pointing at
>   another company's record shows no name rather than theirs. A server-stamped user
>   (`initiated_by`, `verified_by`, `closed_by`, `quality_approved_by`, and since `127`
>   `effectiveness_verified_by`) outside the company is
>   named only when it is a superuser or Platform Admin who acted in this company's context; an
>   ordinary user of another company is never named. Every CAR route, list included,
>   returns this shape.
> - **Escalations prefill the form.** `POST /quality/ncr/{id}/create-car`: see the bullet above.
>   `POST /complaints/complaints/{id}/create-car`: see **Customer Complaints & RMA**.
> - A CLOSED CAR still refuses every `PUT` except a status-only reopen, form fields included.
> - **Export control (AI-external tokens).** The CAR's own `part_id`, `customer_id` and
>   `customer_name` snapshot place it, alongside the NCRs and complaints that reference it: a CAR is
>   served in full to an AI-external API token only when every one of those links clears, so
>   setting a controlled customer on a CAR raised from a cleared NCR withholds it from the next
>   request on. Inside a withheld CAR the form's text (reason, RMA #, vendor PO, management action,
>   approval names and titles, and since `127` the two reviews and the effectiveness evidence) is
>   `"[export-controlled]"`; the cost buckets and `cost_total` stay
>   true. `GET /quality/car/{car_id}/pdf` is a file and is refused to every read-only token. See
>   [EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md → Linkage map](EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md#linkage-map).
>
> **Quality Manager approval (`POST /quality/car/{car_id}/quality-approval`).** Records the form's
> Quality Manager approval. No body: the server stamps `quality_approved_by` (the caller) and
> `quality_approved_at` (UTC; the printed date is its Central date). Neither is ever taken from a
> request body: a CAR's `POST` and `PUT` have no field for them. Gate **Admin / Manager / Quality**.
>
> - **Once.** An already-approved CAR is **409** (`"CAR … already has its quality approval; it is
>   recorded once."`), so the record keeps naming the first approver. A VOID CAR is **409**.
> - **A standing API token is refused** with **403** (`"A standing API token cannot record a CAR's
>   quality approval. A person signed in to the app must record it."`), before any write: the stamp
>   names a person. See
>   [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).
> - **It neither gates closure nor freezes the CAR.** It is allowed in every status except VOID, CLOSED
>   included. The existing closure evidence rules are unchanged, and the other fields stay editable
>   under the usual `PUT` rules.
> - The CAR row is locked first, so two concurrent approvals serialize and the second gets the
>   **409**. The required `APPROVE` audit row commits with the stamp, or neither is saved (**503**).
>   It emits `car_updated` with `changed_fields: ["quality_approved_at", "quality_approved_by"]`.
> - The CAR detail screen's **Record quality approval** button shows for `quality:approve` holders on
>   an unapproved, non-void CAR, is disabled while edits are unsaved, waits for the server, and
>   shows a refusal verbatim.
>
> **CAR corrective-action evidence (migration `127_ncr_car_records`, AS9100D 10.2).** A CAR records
> the human-factors and similar-nonconformity reviews behind its corrective action, when the
> follow-up effectiveness check is due, and the effectiveness verification itself. Every new column
> is nullable; a CAR raised before `127` reads `null` in each (nothing was backfilled).
>
> | Field | Type | Written by | Rule |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `human_factors_review` | text ≤ 4000 | `POST` / `PUT` (`CARFormFields`) | Human factors considered in the cause (fatigue, training, procedure clarity, workload, environment, communication). Required to close a corrective CAR |
> | `similar_nonconformities_review` | text ≤ 4000 | `POST` / `PUT` | Where else this nonconformity exists or could occur. Required to close a corrective CAR |
> | `effectiveness_due` | date | `POST` / `PUT` | When the follow-up effectiveness check is due. Recorded only: nothing gates or notifies on it |
> | `effectiveness_check` (existing column) | text ≤ 4000 (was 2000) | `PUT`, while no result is recorded; then only the effectiveness verb (its `evidence`) | Now "the evidence reviewed for effectiveness". Locked while a result is recorded (below) |
> | `effectiveness_result` | `effective` or `not_effective` (DB CHECK `ck_cars_effectiveness_result`) | `POST /quality/car/{car_id}/effectiveness` | Cleared by a `PUT` that changes `root_cause` or `corrective_action` (below) |
> | `effectiveness_verified_by`, `effectiveness_verified_at` | user id, UTC datetime | the server | Stamped by the effectiveness verb. Never accepted in a body. Cleared with the result |
>
> `CARResponse` adds the six new columns plus `effectiveness_verified_by_name`, resolved like the
> other stamped users above.
>
> - **Closing a corrective CAR needs the 10.2 evidence.** For `car_type` `corrective`, or `null`
>   (which has always meant corrective), closing (`status: "closed"`) requires, beyond root cause,
>   corrective action, verification method and verification results: a non-blank
>   `human_factors_review`, a non-blank `similar_nonconformities_review`, and a **stored**
>   `effective` effectiveness result. It is judged on the record as it would be saved: the two
>   reviews may be entered in the closing request, the result only through its verb. **422**
>   `"Closure requires …"` names everything missing, in this order: `root cause`, `corrective
>   action`, `verification method`, `verification results`, `human factors review`, `similar
>   nonconformities review`, `an effective effectiveness verification`. `preventive` and
>   `improvement` CARs keep the original four. Since a result is recorded only in `verification`, a
>   corrective CAR passes through `verification` before it can close. A CAR closed before `127` keeps
>   its closure; reopened, it meets this gate to close again.
> - **`effectiveness_check` is locked while a result is recorded.** The evidence a recorded
>   verification reviewed is part of that record, so a `PUT` that changes `effectiveness_check` on a
>   CAR carrying an `effectiveness_result` is **409** (`"CAR … has a recorded effectiveness
>   verification; record a new one with the effectiveness action to change its evidence."`).
>   Re-sending it unchanged is not a change. It changes by recording a new verification, which
>   re-stamps who reviewed it and when, or in a request that clears the result (next bullet).
> - **Changing what was reviewed clears the effectiveness verification.** A verification vouches
>   for the cause and action it reviewed, and no more. So a `PUT` that changes `root_cause` or
>   `corrective_action` on a CAR carrying a recorded verification sets `effectiveness_result`,
>   `effectiveness_verified_by` and `effectiveness_verified_at` back to `null`, `not_effective`
>   results included. The cleared values stay on that request's audit row, old → new. The evidence
>   text (`effectiveness_check`) stays, unlocked: the same request may change it without the
>   **409**, and so may any later `PUT` until a new result is recorded. A close in the same request
>   is judged as already cleared, so a corrective CAR gets the **422** naming `an effective
>   effectiveness verification`. The status does not move, and a status-only reopen of a CLOSED CAR
>   changes neither field, so it clears nothing. This is the CAR twin of the NCR rule that a
>   disposition change clears the re-verification.
>
> **Effectiveness verification (`POST /quality/car/{car_id}/effectiveness`, MCP tool
> `record_car_effectiveness`).** Body `CAREffectivenessRequest`
> `{ "result": "effective" or "not_effective", "evidence": "..." }`. `evidence` (what was reviewed to
> judge it) is required and trimmed, at most 4000 characters; blank or whitespace-only is **422**,
> and so is an unknown key. It is stored as `effectiveness_check`. The server stamps
> `effectiveness_verified_by` (the caller) and `effectiveness_verified_at` (UTC); no `POST` or `PUT`
> body carries `effectiveness_result` or either stamp. Gate **Admin / Manager / Quality**. Returns
> the CAR (`CARResponse`).
>
> - **403** for a standing API token (`"A standing API token cannot record a CAR's effectiveness
>   verification. A person signed in to the app must record it."`), before the CAR is read.
> - **409** unless the CAR is in `verification` (`"Record effectiveness once CAR … is in
>   Verification; it is <status>."`), VOID and CLOSED included.
> - **`not_effective` returns the CAR to `corrective_action`**, on the same audit row
>   (`STATUS_CHANGE`, described as the verification finding it not effective and returning it from
>   `verification` to `corrective_action`): the action did not work, so the work is not done. The
>   stored result stays `not_effective`, which keeps a corrective CAR from closing, until a new
>   verification replaces it (or a revised `root_cause` / `corrective_action` clears it, above);
>   move the CAR back to `verification` (a `PUT`, which records the verifier as before) and record
>   one. `effective` leaves the status alone.
> - **Re-recordable.** A later verification replaces result, evidence, who and when, and the audit
>   row keeps what it replaced.
> - The CAR row is locked first, so concurrent verifications serialize. The required audit row
>   commits with the stamp, or neither is saved (**503**). It emits `car_updated` best-effort
>   (severity `medium` for `not_effective`, `info` otherwise).
> - The CAR detail screen has the two review fields and the due date, and an **Effectiveness
>   verification** panel showing the result, evidence, verifier and date. **Record effectiveness**
>   shows for `quality:approve` holders while the CAR is in Verification, is disabled while edits
>   are unsaved, waits for the server, and shows a refusal verbatim; the evidence field is read-only
>   once a result is recorded.
>
> **For the Quality Manager: which AS9100D clause each new record serves.** These are records, not
> new approvals; who recorded each stamped one is on the record and on its audit row.
>
> | AS9100D clause | Record | What it holds |
> |---|---|---|
> | 8.7.1 (concession) | NCR `concession_reference`, `concession_authorized_by`, `concession_date` | The customer's concession for releasing use-as-is or repaired product: its number, who at the customer authorized it, and when. Required to close a use-as-is or repair NCR |
> | 8.7.1 (re-verification after correction) | NCR re-verification: `reverification_result`, `reverification_notes`, `reverified_by`, `reverified_at` | That corrected (reworked or repaired) product was re-verified against the requirement, what was checked, the result, by whom and when. A conforming result is required to close a rework or repair NCR |
> | 8.7.2 (action taken, who decided) | NCR `action_taken`; `dispositioned_by`, `dispositioned_at` | What was done with the nonconforming product, and the authority who decided the disposition (server-stamped, never typed) |
> | 10.2.1 (human factors, similar nonconformities) | CAR `human_factors_review`, `similar_nonconformities_review` | The review of human factors in the cause, and of whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur. Both required to close a corrective CAR |
> | 10.2.2 (effectiveness evidence and result) | CAR `effectiveness_check`, `effectiveness_result`, `effectiveness_verified_by`, `effectiveness_verified_at`, `effectiveness_due` | The evidence reviewed, the result (effective / not effective), who judged it and when, and when the check was due. An effective result is required to close a corrective CAR; a not-effective one sends the CAR back to corrective action. Changing the root cause or corrective action clears the result, so it always speaks to the action as it stands |
>
> **Printable CAR (`GET /quality/car/{car_id}/pdf`).** Returns the CAR as a PDF in the layout of the
> controlled form (`services/car_pdf_service.py`), served `inline` as `<car_number>.pdf`. It has the
> same read access as `GET /quality/car/{car_id}`; another company's CAR is **404**. The header is the
> active company's own name, address and phone from its Company record. The grid then follows the
> form: initiated by / RMA # / CAR number; date submitted / date due; part / vendor PO and vendor /
> customer; the eight reason boxes (ASCII `[X]` / `[ ]`); problem, root cause and corrective action
> (with containment and preventive action); the four costs and their total; vendor management
> approval; management action; customer approval and Quality Manager approval. Nothing is truncated:
> long text continues on the next page, and every page has a footer with the CAR number and page
> number. Every value is escaped at the reportlab sink. It writes nothing and records no audit row
> (one record, not a bulk export). The CAR detail screen's **Print CAR** button opens it in a preview.
>
> Since `127` the grid also carries the AS9100D 10.2 evidence the paper form has no room for, as
> boxes of its own: a **Human Factors Review** and a **Similar Nonconformities Review** after the
> corrective action, and, after the management action and just above the approvals, an
> **Effectiveness Verification** row (result printed `Effective` / `Not effective`, verified by, and
> the Central date of the UTC stamp) followed by **Evidence Reviewed for Effectiveness**. An empty
> box prints blank, leaving room to write in. **The printed CAR now has boxes Werco's controlled CAR
> form does not, so Quality should bump the controlled form's revision** to match what the ERP
> prints.

> **CAR void + restore (`POST /quality/car/{car_id}/void`, `POST /quality/car/{car_id}/restore`).**
> Void retires a duplicate CAR or one raised in error. Body `CARVoidRequest` `{ "reason": "..." }`:
> required and trimmed; blank or whitespace-only is **422**. Gate **Admin / Manager / Quality** for
> both verbs. An already-void CAR is **409**. A CLOSED CAR is **409** too, so a completed corrective
> action is never voided in one step, but this is not a control against the same roles: they can
> reopen it with a status-only `PUT` (no reason captured yet) and then void it. Both steps are
> required-audited, so the reopen is on the record either way. `VOID` is the CAR's tombstone
> (`CorrectiveActionRequest` has no `SoftDeleteMixin`): the CAR stays in `GET /quality/car` and
> `GET /quality/car/{car_id}` with `status: "void"`, drops out of the `open_cars` count on
> `GET /quality/summary`, and refuses every `PUT` until restored. The reason is stored only on the
> `STATUS_CHANGE` audit row (`extra_data.reason`), since `cars` has no reason column. A linked NCR
> keeps its `car_id` until a new CAR is raised from it.
>
> Restore takes no body and reopens the CAR to **`open`**; the pre-void status is not preserved, the
> same safe reset as the NCR restore. A CAR that is not void is **409** (`"CAR … is not void"`). It
> writes a required `RESTORE` audit row (old/new `status`, plus `closed_date` / `closed_by` when a
> legacy void row still carried a closure and restore cleared it). The CAR is not relinked: an NCR
> that raised a fresh CAR after the void keeps pointing at the fresh one. Both verbs emit
> `car_updated`. The Quality page has no Void or Restore CAR action yet; the routes are reachable
> through the API and MCP.

#### First article inspections (FAI)

FAI reads remain available to every authenticated user in the active tenant. Authoring requires
**Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality**; a final disposition requires **Admin / Manager /
Quality**. Platform Admin/superuser role overrides retain the same tenant and record-state checks.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/quality/fai` | List tenant inspections | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/fai/log` | The FAI log of record, newest first: one `FAILogRow` per inspection. Filters `start_date` / `end_date` (inclusive Central dates), `status`, `customer` (≤ 255), `part_id`, `work_order_id`, `search` (≤ 255); `limit` 1–500 (default 100), `offset`. See "FAI log of record" | Yes |
| GET | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}` | Read an inspection and its tenant-owned characteristics | Yes |
| POST | `/quality/fai` | Create an inspection for an undeleted tenant part and optional undeleted tenant work order that builds that part (its own part, or a component of one of its operations; **422** otherwise). An omitted or blank `part_revision` records the part's current revision | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| PUT | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}` | Edit an unfinished inspection; setting `passed`, `failed`, or `conditional` requires approval authority and a person (**403** for a standing API token) | Authoring roles; Admin / Manager / Quality for final disposition |
| POST | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}/customer-approval` | Record the customer's approval of a PASSED or CONDITIONAL inspection; optional body `{ "customer_approval_date": "<date, optional>" }`. Once. **403** for a standing API token. See "Customer approval" | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}/characteristics` | Add a characteristic with the parent's company context | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| PUT | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}/characteristics/{char_id}` | Record/correct an unfinished characteristic | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| DELETE | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}/characteristics/{char_id}` | Remove an unfinished characteristic and retain its prior contents in the audit trail | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| POST | `/quality/fai/{fai_id}/prefill-from-steps` | Fill missing values from matching conforming process-step records | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |

Every writer locks and resolves the same tenant-owned FAI before changing it. A characteristic
must belong to both that FAI and company; unknown/foreign parents, children, inspectors, or
referenced records return **404**. A forbidden authoring/approval role returns **403**, without
changing the inspection. A standing API token setting a final status is refused **403** (`"A
standing API token cannot record an FAI's final disposition. A person signed in to the app must
record it."`) before the row lock and any write; it may still make the non-final edits its role
allows. Finalization records the actual actor in `approved_by` and the completion
date (today on the Central calendar, not the server host's date). `inspection_date` records an
inspection that happened, so a future one is **422** (`"The inspection date cannot be in the
future."`), before the row lock. A final disposition is **409** while the stored inspection date
is in the future (a value written before that bound existed), naming the date: correct it first,
or in the same request. Otherwise the disposition would freeze a date no customer approval could
satisfy (the approval may not predate the inspection and may not be in the future). A final status (`passed`,
`failed`, `conditional`) **or any existing `completed_date`** makes all header, characteristic, and
prefill writes return **409**: corrections require a new inspection. The customer approval is the one
write allowed after that (see below). The legacy `version` request field is not an optimistic-lock
guarantee for the FAI model.

Create refuses (**422**, nothing written) a `work_order_id` whose job does not build the part: the
log of record names the linked job's number, customer and PO, so an FAI of one part linked to
another part's job would put that job's customer on this first article. A job builds the part when
it is the job's own part or a `component_part_id` of one of its operations (a component FAI inside
an assembly job); a part-less job (a standalone laser-nest work order) is not judged.

Create stamps the revision inspected: `part_revision` is trimmed and upper-cased before its
`^[A-Z0-9]+$` check, and when it is omitted or blank the part's current revision is recorded, so the
FAI keeps naming the inspected revision after the part revs up. `reason` is bounded at 50 characters
and a characteristic's `specification` at 255, the widths of their columns. A longer value is a
**422** with nothing written (it used to reach PostgreSQL and fail as a **500**).

`FAIResponse` now also carries `customer_approval_date`, `updated_at`, `inspector_id` /
`inspector_name`, `approved_by` / `approved_by_name`, and, read from the linked work order,
`work_order_number`, `customer_name` (the work order's customer, else the part's) and `customer_po`,
plus `part_current_revision` (the part's revision today, which can differ from `part_revision`).
Names are resolved in batched tenant-scoped reads. `approved_by_name` also resolves a superuser or
Platform Admin who dispositioned in this company's context, because the server stamped that id.
A since-deleted work order or part is still named (historical record).

**Customer approval (`POST /quality/fai/{fai_id}/customer-approval`).** Records that the customer
accepted the first article. A customer approval normally arrives after the final disposition, which
froze the evidence, so it has its own verb. It writes only `customer_approved = true` and
`customer_approval_date`. Gate **Admin / Manager / Quality**. Optional body
`FAICustomerApprovalRequest` (unknown keys are **422**; no body records today):

- `customer_approval_date` defaults to today (Central). A past date back-enters an approval received
  earlier, but not one before the FAI's `inspection_date` when it has one (**422**); a future date
  is **422**. The lower bound is not applied when the stored `inspection_date` is itself after today:
  that is a typo the final disposition froze, and no date could satisfy both rules.
- Only a **PASSED** or **CONDITIONAL** inspection can carry it. One with no final disposition yet is
  **409** ("Record FAI …'s final disposition (Passed or Conditional) before its customer
  approval."). A **FAILED** one is **409** too: a failure is answered by a new inspection.
- **Once.** An FAI that already has its customer approval is **409**.
- **A standing API token is refused** with **403** (`"A standing API token cannot record an FAI's
  customer approval. A person signed in to the app must record it."`), before any write. See
  [RBAC → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).
- The FAI row is locked first (the same lock every FAI writer takes). The required `APPROVE` audit row
  commits with the approval, or neither is saved (**503**). It emits `fai_updated` with an unchanged
  `status`, so the `fai.completed` notification does not fire a second time.

**FAI log of record (`GET /quality/fai/log`, `GET /exports/fai/export`).** The ERP's FAI module is
the company's FAI log of record. The spreadsheet log it replaces (form QF 7.5-3.4) is a **frozen
archive**: by owner decision its 274 legacy rows (2016-03-14 to 2024-05-24) were **not imported**,
and the ERP is authoritative going forward, so new first articles are logged only here. The log is a
read of existing FAI records; no new column or migration backs it.

Each `FAILogRow` starts with what the paper log carried: `fai_number` (FAI Report #), `log_date`,
`part_number`, `part_name` (product description), `customer`, `job_number` and `is_complete` (true
once the FAI has its final disposition). It adds `fai_id`, `part_id`, `part_revision` (inspected),
`part_current_revision`, `customer_po`, `work_order_id`, `serial_number`, `status`, `fai_type`,
`reason`, the characteristic counts, `inspection_date`, `completed_date`,
`customer_approval_required`, `customer_approved`, `customer_approval_date` and `created_at`.

- `log_date` is the completion date, else the inspection date, else the Central day the FAI was
  created. `start_date` / `end_date` filter on it, inclusive.
- `customer`, job # and customer PO come from the linked work order; `customer` falls back to the
  part's customer. The `customer` filter matches that displayed value, and `search` matches FAI #,
  serial number, part number or name, job # and customer PO. Both are case-insensitive substring
  matches.
- **Historical record.** The part and work order are joined without an `is_deleted` filter, so a line
  keeps naming a since-deleted part or job. Both joins are tenant-scoped, so a legacy row pointing at
  another company's record shows blanks rather than its labels.
- Paging is offset-based with a ceiling of 500. Ask for one row more than a page to learn whether
  another page exists (the FAI tab's **Log** view does).
- **AI-external API tokens** may read the log (it is on the AI-external allowlist). Each row is
  judged like the FAI it names (by `fai_id`, `part_id` and `work_order_id`): a row of an
  export-controlled or unlinkable FAI keeps its ids, `fai_number`, `job_number`, `status`, dates,
  booleans and counts, and every other value is `"[export-controlled]"`. The `customer` and `search`
  filters match withheld text, so they are refused **403** to such a token; the date range,
  `status`, `part_id`, `work_order_id`, `limit` and `offset` are allowed. The export is a file and
  stays refused to every read-only token. See
  [EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md](EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md#5-the-ai-external-allowlist).

The export, `GET /exports/fai/export`, takes the same filters plus `format` (`csv` / `xlsx`, sheet
"FAI Log") and `columns`, and is gated **Admin / Manager** and audited like every `/exports/*`
route (see [Spreadsheet Exports](#spreadsheet-exports-csv--xlsx)). Its default columns are the
paper log's seven in its order (`fai_number`, `log_date`, `part_number`, `part_name`, `customer`,
`job_number`, `is_complete`, written as `X` or blank), then `part_revision`, `customer_po`, `status`,
`fai_type`, `reason`, `serial_number`, `inspection_date`, `completed_date`,
`customer_approval_required`, `customer_approved` and `customer_approval_date`. The **Export log
(xlsx)** button on the Log view is shown only to Admin / Manager.

Create numbers each inspection `FAI-YYYYMMDD-NNN` from a per-company sequence under a per-company
lock. `fai_number` is unique per company (migration `116`). Before `116` it was globally unique, so
a second company's first FAI of the day returned **500**.

Prefill preserves existing measurement values/devices and never sets `is_conforming`; ambiguous
labels and specification mismatches remain unmatched for the inspector to resolve. A conformance
value of `null` is unrecorded, not failed. Characteristic counts, evidence changes and required audit
rows commit together; failed audit persistence returns **503** (`"Unable to save audit record"`)
and rolls them back. Historical part labels remain visible for same-company soft-deleted parts;
foreign related records are not expanded.

### Calibration (gauges and calibration records)

`app/api/endpoints/calibration.py`, mounted at `/calibration`. This is the gauge register behind the
process-sheet gauge check (`docs/KIOSK.md` → Gauge capture): a `requires_gauge` measurement accepts a
gauge only while it is `active` **and** its `next_calibration_date` is today or later, so what sets
those two fields is what the check is worth.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/calibration/equipment` | List gauges (`status` filter, incl. `due_soon`; `include_inactive`) | Yes |
| GET | `/calibration/equipment/due-soon` | Gauges due within `days` (`1 … 365`, default 30) | Yes |
| GET | `/calibration/equipment/{id}` | Gauge plus its calibration records | Yes |
| GET | `/calibration/equipment/{id}/history` | Calibration records, newest first | Yes |
| POST | `/calibration/equipment` | Register a gauge (it has no due date until its first passing calibration) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| PUT | `/calibration/equipment/{id}` | Edit a gauge; `status` may only take it **out** of service (see below) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/calibration/equipment/{id}/calibrate` | Record a calibration; the `result` decides the gauge's state (see below) | Admin / Manager / Quality |

> ⚠️ **`POST .../calibrate` returned 500 on every call, and its logic would have certified a failed
> gauge.** `CalibrationRecord` carries `TenantMixin`'s NOT NULL `company_id` and the handler never set
> it, so no calibration could be recorded. Behind the insert, every record — whatever its `result` —
> set the gauge `active` and advanced `next_calibration_date` by the interval, so a recorded **fail**
> would have put the gauge straight past the gauge check. The record now takes `company_id` from the
> tenant-scoped gauge, and the result decides the outcome:
>
> | `result` | Gauge `status` | `last_calibration_date` / `next_calibration_date` | Record `due_date` |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `pass`, `adjusted` | `active` | calibration date / calibration date + `calibration_interval_days` | calibration date + interval |
> | `fail` | `out_of_service` | unchanged — a failed calibration never extends certification | calibration date (due now) |
>
> `result` is **required** — omitting it is **422** with nothing written. (It used to default to
> `pass`, and a default never reaches the validator, so a request that named no outcome — an API or
> MCP caller leaving the field out — certified the gauge.) It is trimmed and matched
> case-insensitively (`" Fail "` is `fail`); any other word is **422** with nothing written, so an
> unrecognised or missing result is never read as either outcome. `adjusted` means the gauge was
> brought back into tolerance and certified as-left.
>
> **`calibration_date` cannot be in the future** — **422** with nothing written. The bound is the
> later of the server's local and UTC dates, so the Central "today" the Calibration page sends is
> never refused. Unbounded, a future-dated pass (a year typo on a certificate) certified the gauge a
> year too long and, as the newest record on file, outranked a genuine `fail` recorded today —
> leaving the failed gauge `active` and passing the gauge check.
>
> **A record is always filed, but it moves the gauge only when it is the newest on file and the
> gauge is not `retired`.** A record dated before the latest calibration already on file (a backdated
> certificate) is history: entering an old pass cannot re-certify a gauge that has failed since.
> Same-day records apply in entry order, so a fail entered after a same-day pass takes the gauge out
> of service. The response model is `CalibrationRecordedResponse` — the record fields plus
> `equipment_status` and `applied_to_equipment` (`false` when the record was filed as history only),
> so a caller can tell "filed" from "filed and the gauge moved".
>
> **A pass cannot lift a hand pull it predates.** Taking a gauge out of service with `PUT` (it was
> dropped, it is suspect) writes no calibration record, so "newest on file" alone would let a stale
> certificate — dated after the last record but *before* the pull — re-certify the gauge someone had
> just quarantined. While a gauge is `out_of_service`, a `pass` / `adjusted` record applies only if
> its `calibration_date` is **on or after** the Central date of the newest hand pull in the current
> out-of-service episode; otherwise it is filed as history (`applied_to_equipment: false`). The pull
> date comes from the gauge's `equipment` `STATUS_CHANGE` audit rows (no new column): rows written by
> a failed calibration are skipped, since a fail is already ordered by its own record date, and a pull
> that a later passing calibration resolved does not count. A gauge that is out of service with no
> status evidence explaining it (set before this router was audited) uses its `updated_at` instead —
> never earlier than the real pull, so it can only refuse more. Date granularity means a certificate
> dated the same day as the pull is accepted.
>
> **Writes are serialized per gauge.** `calibrate` and `PUT` row-lock the gauge
> (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE OF equipment` on Postgres) before deciding anything, so two calibrations
> posted together are ordered rather than both reading the same "newest on file".
>
> **The evidence is fail-closed.** The record, its `CREATE` audit row (resource type `calibration`:
> result, dates, certificate, performer, provider, as-found / as-left, `applied_to_equipment`) and,
> when the status moved, an `equipment` `STATUS_CHANGE` row commit in one transaction through
> `AuditService.log_required`. If either audit write fails nothing is saved and the call returns
> **503** (`"Unable to save audit record. No changes were committed."`). This is the AS9100D 7.1.5.2
> calibration record.

> **`PUT /calibration/equipment/{id}` can take a gauge out of service but never put one back.**
