> `status` accepts `out_of_service` or `retired`. Setting `active`, `due` or `overdue` is **409**,
> naming `POST /calibration/equipment/{id}/calibrate`: a gauge returns to `active` only through a
> passing calibration record, and `due` / `overdue` are derived from dates. (A newly registered gauge
> is stored `active` with no due date; the gauge check refuses it until its first passing calibration
> sets one.) Re-sending the gauge's current
> status is a no-op, not a refusal. A retired gauge comes back only by `PUT` → `out_of_service` and
> then a passing calibration. Before this change `PUT` was a blind `setattr` over the body, so any
> authenticated user could set `active` on an out-of-calibration gauge, and an unknown status word was
> a **500** (now **422**). Fields are applied from an explicit allowlist (`name`, `description`,
> `equipment_type`, `location`, `assigned_to`, `calibration_interval_days`, `calibration_provider`,
> `is_active`, `notes`, plus `status`); `calibration_interval_days` is bounded `1…3650` on create and
> update; an explicit `null` on `name`, `calibration_interval_days`, `is_active` or `status` is
> **422**. `PUT` writes a `log_update` row (self-suppressed when nothing changed) plus, when the status
> moved, a `STATUS_CHANGE` row that is **required evidence**: a hand pull starts the AS9100D 7.1.5.2
> suspect-product window and is what a later backdated pass is measured against, so it is written
> through `AuditService.log_required` and, if it cannot be saved, the whole edit rolls back with
> **503**. A field-only edit is not gated on it. `POST /calibration/equipment` writes a `log_create`.
> `is_active: false` hides a gauge from the lists but does **not** affect the gauge check, which reads
> `status` and the due date only — take a gauge out of use with `status`, not `is_active`.

> **Tenancy.** `GET .../{id}/history` resolved the gauge by bare id, and the record query behind
> `GET .../{id}` was not company-filtered. Both now resolve the gauge in the active company and read
> only that company's records; a foreign gauge is a flat **404** with the same body as an absent id
> (`"Equipment not found"`), and `PUT` / `calibrate` against one write nothing. The list also keeps a
> stored `retired` status as `retired`; it used to be recomputed from dates into `active` / `due` /
> `overdue`, which only `out_of_service` was exempt from.

> **`equipment_id` codes are unique per company.** `equipment.equipment_id` — like `tools.tool_id`
> and `downtime_reason_codes.code` — is unique on `(company_id, …)` since migration `116`; before
> that all three were unique install-wide, so a code another tenant used was refused, which told the
> caller that *some* tenant used it. Another company's identical code is now accepted. A code the
> company already uses is **400** `"Equipment ID already exists"`, and so is a concurrent create that
> races past the duplicate check and hits the per-company constraint (never a 500).

### Job costing

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/job-costs/` | List tenant job costs (`status`, `work_order_id`; `date_from` / `date_to` filter `created_at` by inclusive calendar date in the company time zone — see [Timestamps](#timestamps); a reversed range is **422**) | Yes |
| GET | `/job-costs/summary` | Summarize tenant costs | Yes |
| GET | `/job-costs/{id}` | Read one job cost | Yes |
| GET | `/job-costs/{id}/entries` | Read its tenant-owned entries | Yes |
| GET | `/job-costs/{id}/variance-report` | Read its variance report | Yes |
| POST | `/job-costs/` | Create for an undeleted tenant work order | Admin / Manager |
| PUT | `/job-costs/{id}` | Update estimates/status | Admin / Manager |
| POST | `/job-costs/{id}/entries` | Add a manual cost entry (`entry_type` `material` / `labor` / `overhead` / `other` / `subcontract`) | Admin / Manager |
| DELETE | `/job-costs/{id}/entries/{entry_id}` | Remove a cost entry, retaining its prior contents in the audit trail | Admin / Manager |
| POST | `/job-costs/{id}/calculate` | Regenerate TimeEntry labor entries and recompute totals, preserving other entries. Each regenerated labor entry's `entry_date` is the **production day** its time entry is attributed to (see [Production calendar & shifts](#production-calendar--shifts)); before 2026-11-13 it was the UTC date of the clock-in | Admin / Manager |

All reads and writes resolve the job cost through a work order in the active company; writes
require it to be undeleted, while reads preserve historical costs after work-order soft deletion.
Explicit foreign/missing parent and entry ids return **404**; a submitted operation reference must belong to
that work order and company. Manual entries may omit the operation. Relationship expansion never
reveals foreign ordinary users, parts, or entries: legacy foreign entries are omitted and invalid
operation/user references are rendered `null`. Same-company historical part labels and legitimate
platform-actor attribution remain readable. A second job cost for an already-costed work order
returns **400**; a conflicting legacy row outside the tenant returns **409** without exposing it.
Explicit `null` estimates/status and invalid enum values return **422**.

**Cost elements (2026-11-13, migration 121).** A job cost totals its entries by type:
`actual_material_cost` (MATERIAL), `actual_labor_cost` (LABOR), `actual_overhead_cost`
(OVERHEAD **and** OTHER — its stored meaning, unchanged), and `actual_subcontract_cost`
(SUBCONTRACT: outside processing such as plating or heat treat). `actual_total_cost` is all five
types; subcontract is never folded into overhead. There is no subcontract **estimate**, so
subcontract reaches `total_variance` but no per-element variance; the variance report lists a
`subcontract` line (estimated `0`) so its lines add up to the total. Subcontract entries are
manual: no purchase-order line or receipt carries a work-order link, so nothing posts one
automatically. The work-order read reports these totals as `job_cost_actuals` (burden =
`actual_overhead_cost`) — see Work Orders → "Cost and actual hours on the work-order read".

Every manual write requires **Admin / Manager**, including recalculation (**403** otherwise).
Cost entries, parent totals, and required audit rows commit atomically; audit failure returns
**503** (`"Unable to save audit record"`) and leaves all unchanged. Delete/recalculation audit
evidence retains the removed/rebuilt entry contents and before/after totals; calculation preserves
non-TimeEntry cost entries. These routes add no
new financial approval workflow; automatic work-order completion keeps its existing business path.

### Documents

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/documents/` | List the tenant documents the caller may open; optional `access_level` filter (`standard` / `restricted` / `export_controlled`, anything else **422**) | Yes |
| GET | `/documents/types/list` | List document types | Yes |
| GET | `/documents/access-review` | Documents whose part's customer is export-controlled but whose level is not `export_controlled`, plus a count of documents with no part link | Admin / Quality |
| GET | `/documents/{id}` | Read document metadata | Yes |
| GET | `/documents/{id}/revisions` | Read retained revision history | Yes |
| GET | `/documents/{id}/download` | Download the tenant document | Yes |
| POST | `/documents/upload` | Multipart manual upload/revision, published as released; optional `access_level` form field | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/documents/{id}/attach-work-order` | Body `{"work_order_id": id}`; attach an unlinked PDF. Raises it (and its revisions) to `export_controlled` when the work order's customer is export-controlled | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/documents/{id}/access-level` | Body `{"access_level", "reason"}`; change who may open the document and every revision in its history. Refuses any API token **403**; not an MCP tool | Admin / Quality |
| DELETE | `/documents/{id}` | Delete a document only when no retention reference protects it | Admin / Manager |

Every read and write above is limited to the documents the caller may open: see
[Restricted and export-controlled documents](#restricted-and-export-controlled-documents-as9100d-7531)
below.

`part_id` is optional on `POST /documents/upload`. The Documents page's **Upload Document**
dialog requires a part only for the part-specific types `drawing`, `inspection_plan` and `fai`
(so they can be found by part number); for every other type, such as a procedure, form or
specification, **No part (company-wide document)** is a valid choice. Whatever is chosen carries
to every later revision, because a revision must keep its predecessor's part link.

Deletion also refuses documents referenced by a same-company Hank intake result
or sharing its retained source storage reference. This preserves the reviewed
PDF, completed intake receipt and source-page recovery together with existing
receipt-certificate and revision-history retention.

Deletion also refuses (**409**) a document that a same-company QMS standard or QMS clause
evidence link names through its `document_id`. Both columns are plain foreign keys with no
`ON DELETE`, so on Postgres the unguarded delete failed at flush, after the document row lock and
the audit-chain lock were taken: a **500**, or a deadlock (40P01, answered **409** or **503**
depending on where the delete lost) against an evidence edit holding the referencing row, and
neither said why. The check runs before the audit write and
before any change, so a refusal writes nothing and keeps the bytes. The message depends on the link:

- **A live link** (the standard, or the evidence with its clause and standard, not removed):
  *"This document is linked to QMS standard AS9100D"* or *"…linked as QMS evidence on AS9100D
  clause 7.5.3"*, plus *"and N other QMS links"* when there are more, then *"Unlink it first by
  setting document_id to null on that QMS standard or evidence link."* That means
  `PUT /qms-standards/{standard_id}` or `PUT /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` with
  `{"document_id": null}` (both audited). The QMS Standards page picks a document only when it links
  new evidence (the Link Evidence dialog's optional **Linked Document** field); it cannot change or
  clear the document on an existing standard or evidence link, so this is an API / MCP step.
- **Any removed link** (a soft-deleted standard, clause or evidence link, including evidence
  under a removed clause or standard), reported ahead of any live link: *"This document is named by a removed QMS standard, clause or
  evidence link, which keeps the record of what was assessed. It must remain available and cannot be
  deleted."* A removed QMS row still records which document a clause was assessed against, and
  clearing its link would rewrite that record, so the document is retained the way a voided
  receipt's certificate is. Removing an evidence link (`DELETE /qms-standards/evidence/{id}`)
  therefore does **not** release its document; clear `document_id` first if the document is meant
  to go. The same goes for removing a clause or standard: clear its evidence links' `document_id`
  first, because once the clause or standard is removed, the evidence `PUT` answers **404** for
  the links under it. There is no restore for a removed QMS standard, clause or evidence link, so a
  document still linked when its QMS row is removed stays permanently.

The standard and evidence `PUT`s flush their change before writing the audit row, so a new
`document_id` takes its lock on the document row before the global audit-chain lock, the order
the delete takes them in. A link made concurrently with a delete either commits first, and the
delete sees it and refuses, or waits for the delete and then fails its own foreign-key check.

Only the active company's QMS rows are read. A link from another company's QMS row is not
named, since that would disclose the other tenant's record; on Postgres that delete still fails at
the foreign key until the link is cleared. Since 2026-11-17 (#348) the QMS create / update routes
refuse another company's document (see QMS Standards → *A linked document must be your
company's*), so such a link can only be one written before that check existed, when they accepted
any existing document id.

Every other table with a foreign key to `documents.id` is checked the same way: before the audit
write and before any change, so a refusal (**409**) writes nothing and keeps the bytes. None of these
columns has an `ON DELETE` either, so each used to fail at flush on Postgres with a **500** that gave
no reason. The records below keep their document for as long as they exist, removed or voided
included, and there is no verb that lets go of it:

| Referencing column | Refusal says | Kept after |
|---|---|---|
| `shipments.label_document_id` / `bol_document_id` | *"This document is the carrier label (or bill of lading) for shipment SHP-…"* | the label is voided or the shipment is removed |
| `po_receipts.label_document_id` | *"This document is the receiving label for receipt RCV-…"* | the receipt is voided |
| `operation_step_records.attachment_document_id` | *"This document is evidence captured at a process-sheet step on work order WO-…"* | the step record is superseded |
| `document_files.document_id` | *"This document is held by a governed file record…"* (retention policy / legal hold) | — |

A receipt reprint stores a new label document and points the receipt at it, so only the label the
receipt currently names is protected by this check; an earlier print is no longer referenced.

A **laser nest's PDF** (`laser_nests.document_id`) is a reference drawing with its own audited
release: *"This document is the PDF attached to laser nest CNC-… on work order WO-… [and N other
laser nests]. Detach it from the nest first (Detach on the work order's laser nest row)."* That is
`DELETE /laser-nests/{id}/document` (Admin / Manager / Supervisor), once per nest; a duplicated work
order copies the reference, so one PDF can sit on several nests. Two cases keep the PDF instead, with
no mention of Detach:

- **A nest whose operation has recorded work** (good, scrap, a start or labor: the
  `operation_has_recorded_work` predicate): *"This document is the PDF of laser nest CNC-… on work
  order WO-…, which has recorded work, so it is the record of what was cut."* The PDF is the layout
  the sheet was cut from. Known gap: Detach itself is not gated on recorded work, so the API still
  lets a person detach such a PDF and then delete it.
- **A removed nest** (*"…the PDF of a removed laser nest, which keeps it so that restoring the nest
  brings its drawing back"*): `POST /laser-nests/{id}/restore` brings the nest back with it, and
  Detach answers **404** for a removed nest. Removing a nest therefore does not release its PDF;
  detach it first.

An **engineering change order's affected documents** (`engineering_change_orders.affected_documents`)
are a JSON id list, not a foreign key, so here Postgres would *not* stop the delete. Before this
check the document was deleted and `GET /eco/eco/affected-items/{id}` silently dropped it from the
change record (AS9100D 8.5.6). ECOs have no delete verb, so the reference lasts. The check depends
on the ECO's status:

- **No approver has decided yet** (draft, submitted): *"This document is listed as affected by
  engineering change ECO-… (PUT /eco/eco/41). Take it out of that change's affected_documents
  first, while no approver has decided on it yet."* Every such ECO is named with its own edit
  path (*"engineering changes ECO-… (PUT /eco/eco/41), ECO-… (PUT /eco/eco/43) and …"*), because
  the Engineering Changes page has no document field and the ECO list can't be searched by
  document. The edit is `PUT /eco/eco/{id}` with the list minus this id (Admin / Manager,
  audited), an API / MCP step.
- **Under review, approved or later, rejected or cancelled**: *"This document is listed as affected
  by engineering change ECO-… (under review), which keeps the record of what the change covered.
  It must remain available and cannot be deleted."* Under review means at least one approver has
  already signed the scope, so editing it would leave sign-offs on a scope those people never saw.
  From approval on the list is the authorized change scope, and a rejected or cancelled change
  records what was decided. Known gap: `PUT /eco/eco/{id}` still accepts edits to an under-review,
  approved or in-implementation ECO (it refuses only completed, rejected and cancelled ones), so the
  API still lets a person take the document off such an ECO and then delete it.

The id is matched exactly: the text column is only narrowed by substring, then each candidate's
JSON is parsed, so an ECO listing document 12 never blocks deleting document 1. A string id
(`"12"`) counts; a value that is not a JSON list is skipped, as the affected-items read skips it.
Because there is no foreign key, ECO create and update lock each document they name (`FOR KEY
SHARE`, the lock a foreign key takes) before their audit row. A list written at the same time as a
delete is therefore either seen by the delete, or fails its own validation with **422** once the
delete commits. (This relies on Postgres's default READ COMMITTED isolation, which the app does not
change.)

**Order of reasons.** Every reason that keeps the document for good is reported before any
instruction: the retained records above, then a removed QMS link, then a worked or removed nest,
then an ECO under review, approved or closed. Only when every blocker can be released does the refusal give
instructions, and then it gives the QMS unlink, the nest Detach and the ECO edit together in one
message. Nobody is sent to unlink or detach
something (an audited change, and on the floor a nest losing its drawing) only to be refused
again. The nest attach verb
(`POST /laser-nests/{id}/attach-document`) flushes the link before its audit row, like the QMS
`PUT`s, so it takes its lock on the document row before the audit-chain lock. Every other writer of
these columns creates the document in the same transaction or already flushes first. Only the active
company's rows are read; no writer accepts another company's document, and a row of another company
is never named.

Manual upload is a release action: the persisted Document stores `status="released"`, the actual
`released_by` actor, and UTC `released_at`. Returned metadata exposes the released status;
the audit details retain release actor/time, which are not fields of `DocumentResponse`.
Upload/release and PDF attachment require **Admin /
Manager / Quality** (**403** otherwise); deletion retains its **Admin / Manager** gate.
Generated receipt/shipping artifacts continue to use their owning business-route permissions.
Document and related-record lookups use the active tenant (**404** for foreign/missing ids).
New part/work-order links require undeleted rows. A revision may retain a same-company deleted
part/work order only when its links exactly match the validated, locked predecessor. Vendor
links and historical part labels may retain same-company soft-deleted records for traceability.

A revision upload supplies `previous_revision_id`, a new nonblank `revision` (1–20 characters,
not an ancestor's label ignoring case), and nonblank `revision_notes`. It must retain the previous
type and part/work-order/vendor links (**422** for an invalid revision), and must extend the latest
revision (**409** if a newer one exists). Prior files remain available. PDF attachment may link an
unlinked document without revision history; attaching to the same work order is a no-op, while
rebinding an existing work-order link or revision history returns **409**. A non-PDF is **400**.

Deleting any member of a revision chain, or a certificate referenced by a receipt **including a
voided receipt**, returns **409** and preserves both row and bytes. Allowed metadata mutations
and required audit rows commit together; audit failure returns **503** (`"Unable to save audit
record"`) and rolls back the mutation. Upload failure removes only the new uploaded object;
deletion removes bytes only after the audited metadata transaction commits. Storage cleanup
failure is logged and may leave an orphan, without removing a prior revision or a live document's
file. Manual upload audit evidence includes the file hash and release metadata.

#### Restricted and export-controlled documents (AS9100D 7.5.3.1)

Migration `131_document_access` gives every document an `access_level` and every user an
export authorization. The rule is one module, `app/services/document_access.py`: a SQL clause for
queries, a Python twin for a document already loaded through a relationship, and
`visible_document_or_404` for by-id lookups. A parity test holds the clause and its twin together
over every role, export flag, level and company.

| `access_level` | Who may open it |
|---|---|
| `standard` (the default) | Anyone who could read documents before migration 131 |
| `restricted` | Admin, Manager, Quality and Supervisor, plus a superuser and a Platform Admin |
| `export_controlled` | **Only** a user whose `export_authorized` is true, and only in that user's **own** company. No role bypasses it: not Admin, not a superuser, not a Platform Admin |

The levels are not a ladder. An export-authorized Operator opens `standard` and
`export_controlled` documents but not `restricted` ones, and an Admin who is not export-authorized
opens `standard` and `restricted` ones but not `export_controlled` ones.

- **Export authorization is per company.** It is granted by a company's Admin for that company's
  documents and counts only while the user is working in their own company (`users.company_id`).
  A platform account authorized in its home company that switches into another tenant opens no
  `export_controlled` document there.
- An API token and a crew-station badge (kiosk operator) token act as the user they are bound to,
  with that user's role and flag.
- Two callers see `standard` only, whoever they are: a crew-station tablet's own station token
  (no person behind it), and an **AI-external** API token, on every path (see
  [EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md](EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md#documents-of-a-controlled-customer-migration-131)).
- **Reads bound for an AI model never include `export_controlled`,** for anyone, export-authorized
  or not: copilot document search, Hank's job documents (readiness, knowledge, the shipping
  packet), and everything Hank chat reads (below). With the company's AI egress on, those results
  go to Anthropic, and an export authorization lets a person open a document, not send it to an
  outside model.

After the migration every document is `standard` and nobody is export-authorized, so nothing
changes until Quality flags documents.

**404, before any other check.** A document the caller may not open is the same **404** as one
that does not exist or belongs to another company (where a route answers a missing id with a 422,
it is that same 422), and that check comes first, so no later 400 / 409 / 422 says anything about
it. The exceptions are listed under *Known residuals* below. In detail:

- `GET /documents/` lists only what the caller may open (the filter is in the query, so a page is a
  page of openable documents). `GET /documents/{id}` and `GET /documents/{id}/download` are
  **404** `Document not found`.
- `GET /documents/{id}/revisions` is **404** when the caller may not open the document asked for.
  The history is traced through every revision, but a revision the caller may not open is left out
  of the answer.
- `POST /documents/{id}/attach-work-order` and `DELETE /documents/{id}` are **404** first, before
  the PDF, revision-history and retention checks. A revision upload whose `previous_revision_id`
  names a document the uploader may not open is **404** `Previous document revision not found`.
- Laser nests: `GET /laser-nests/{id}/document` answers **404** `No document attached` for a PDF the
  caller may not open, the same as a nest with none, and `POST /laser-nests/{id}/attach-document` is
  **404** `Document not found` before the PDF check. Every nest response (`PATCH`, attach, detach,
  restore, the manual nest add, the `laser_nest` object on the kiosk queue, `my-active-job`,
  `/shop-floor/operations` and `/shop-floor/operations/{id}`, and the work-order responses
  `GET /work-orders/{id}`, by number, create, duplicate, template use, nest import, `PUT
  /work-orders/{id}`, release, and the operation `POST` / `PUT`) reports a PDF the caller may not
  open as no PDF: `document_id` and `document_file_name` null, `has_document` false. The stored link
  is untouched.
- Kiosk: `GET /shop-floor/operations/{id}/documents` picks the newest released drawing the caller
  may open that no later revision supersedes, and nulls the nest's `document_id` / `file_name` when
  the caller may not open the nest PDF. `GET /shop-floor/documents/{id}/inline` is **404** first. See
  Shop Floor → "Kiosk doc viewer".
- Process sheets: a step record's `attachment_document_id` reads null in `GET
  /shop-floor/operations/{id}/steps` when the caller may not open that document, and capturing or
  superseding a record with an `attachment_document_id` the operator may not open is **404**
  `Attachment document not found`.
- QMS: a `document_id` the caller may not open is **404** `Document not found` on standard and
  evidence create / update. An update that re-sends the link the row already holds is not
  re-checked, so a form that echoes an unchanged link does not lock its author out of the row. The
  live document-control auto-evidence read (`GET .../auto-evidence`) counts, and names examples
  from, only the documents the asking person may open. Auto-link, which stores its evidence, counts
  `standard` documents only, whoever runs it, and its stored description says so, so a stored count
  never depends on who clicked.
- Engineering changes: an `affected_documents` id the caller may not open is refused with the
  **same 422** as an id that does not exist. On `PUT /eco/eco/{id}`, ids the ECO already lists are
  not re-checked. `GET /eco/eco/affected-items/{id}` leaves out documents the caller may not open.
- Hank and the AI copilot read only the documents the asking person may open. What goes to the
  model also treats every `export_controlled` document as missing (above): copilot document
  search, the work order's documents in readiness, knowledge and the shipping packet, and Hank
  chat's reads. In chat, the attach-document preview is **404** `Document not found`, a saved Hank
  task or intake file that names such a document is left out of saved work and is **404** when read
  (`Hank task not found` / `Intake file not found`), the intake-file chat tools answer the same
  **404**, and a handoff read leaves the document out of `document_references`.
- Outside chat, the ordinary rule applies: a person's own `POST /hank/tasks` (the attach preview is
  **404** first for a document they may not open, and opens an `export_controlled` one they are
  authorized for), handoff responses (a document the reader may not open is left out of
  `document_references`; the ids stay in `document_ids`, and a handoff naming a document the
  sender may not open is the same 422 as a missing one), and document watches (the baseline and
  every check).
- The audit log is redacted when it is read (below).
- Ids that only point at a document are not checked against the rule: a receipt's certificate and
  receiving label, a shipment's carrier label and bill of lading. The file is gated where its bytes
  are served (`GET /documents/{id}/download`).

**The audit log, redacted at read time.** `GET /audit/` returns a row about a document the reader
may not open with `old_values` / `new_values` replaced by
`{"redacted": "document not available to you"}`, `description` "Document change (restricted)" and
`resource_identifier` "Restricted document". Three kinds of row are judged:

- a `document` row, by the document its `resource_id` names (a `document` row with no resource id
  is redacted);
- a `hank_intake_file` row (a filing's plan carries the title, description and reviewed fields, its
  result the document number), by the document its intake file was filed as and any document its
  own values name;
- a `hank_task` row (an attach task carries the document's number and title), by the documents its
  task names and any document its own values name.

A Hank row's values name a document through a `document_id` key or a `{"type": "document", "id":
…}` reference, at any depth. Pointer keys such as `certificate_document_id` are not followed. A row
naming any document the reader may not open is redacted. A deleted document is judged by its last
recorded level, read from its own audit trail (every document audit row written since migration 131
carries `access_level`; a document deleted before 131 was `standard`).

Listing without a `search` still returns the redacted rows. With a `search`, the filter runs in the
database **before** `offset` / `limit`, and a row the reader would see redacted matches only on what
the reader can see: the actor's name and the redaction markers, never the stored text. Nothing reveals that hidden text matched. Pages are filled in the database, so they are full in
practice; the one exception is a Hank row redacted only because of a document id inside its own
values (not its source record), which the route drops after the page is read, so such a page can
come back one or two rows short. `GET /audit/integrity/record/{sequence_number}`
hides the identifier the same way. The stored rows are never changed, and the hash chain verifies
over them as before.

**Upload level and the raise rule.** `POST /documents/upload` takes an optional `access_level`
form field (`standard`, `restricted` or `export_controlled`; blank means `standard`, anything else
**422**). The server only ever raises it, never lowers it:

- a revision is stored at least at its predecessor's level;
- a document whose linked part's **or** linked work order's customer resolves as export-controlled
  is stored `export_controlled`. "Export-controlled" is the same finding that redacts an
  AI-external connector (`export_control_service.build_controlled_index`): the record's free-text
  `customer_name` resolves to a customer with a controlling contract or handling instruction. A
  vendor link raises nothing, and neither does a part or work order whose customer name is blank
  or matches no customer.

**A revision history moves together.** A revision stored above its history's level lifts every
earlier revision to that level (never lowers one), with one required `ACCESS_LEVEL_CHANGE` audit row
per lifted revision (reason "Raised with new revision …", `chain_change.trigger` `new_revision`).
The upload locks the whole chain before it judges the predecessor.

**Chain locking.** Every writer that changes a chain's level (the access-level verb, a revision
upload's lift, an attach that raises) locks the revision chain in id order, then walks the chain
again and locks any revision it did not see the first time (one committed while it waited), until a
walk finds nothing new. After 5 walks that keep finding new revisions it gives up with **409** `The
revision history changed while this change was being made; retry.` and nothing is saved.

The response (`DocumentUploadResponse`) is the document plus `access_level_requested`,
`access_level_raised`, `access_level_raised_because` (a list in order of `predecessor_revision` and
`export_controlled_customer`) and `access_level_lifted_document_ids` (the earlier revisions this
upload lifted). When the level was raised, the upload's `CREATE` audit row also carries
`access_level_requested` and `access_level_raised_because`, and `access_level_lifted_document_ids`
when it lifted any. The uploaded document is returned even when the stored level is one the
uploader cannot open.

**Hank intake filing applies the same raise rule** to the document it files against a part or work
order (requested level `standard`, no predecessor). When it raises one, the filing's audit row
carries `access_level_raised_because` and the receipt warns that only export-authorized users can
open the document.

**Attaching to a work order applies it too.** `POST /documents/{id}/attach-work-order` and the Hank
`attach_document` task (on execute) raise the document and its revision chain to
`export_controlled` when the work order's customer resolves as export-controlled, so the attach
and an upload carrying that `work_order_id` end at the same level. Each raised revision gets a
required `ACCESS_LEVEL_CHANGE` row (reason `work order customer is export-controlled`,
`chain_change.trigger` `work_order_link`). The attach response shows the new `access_level`, even
when the caller may no longer open the document.

**Changing a level: `POST /documents/{id}/access-level`** (Admin / Quality). Body
`{"access_level": "...", "reason": "..."}`; the reason is required (1–2000 characters, not blank).

The level belongs to the document's **whole revision history**: every earlier and later revision
moves with the one addressed. The **Change access** dialog says so before anything is saved
("Applies to all N revisions of this document…").

- Any API token, whatever its role or scope, is refused **403** before anything is read. The route
  is not an MCP tool, so a person's own JWT cannot reach it through an agent either.
- The caller must be able to open the addressed document now (**404** otherwise), so lowering an
  `export_controlled` document takes an Admin or Quality user who is export-authorized. The chain
  is then locked (see *Chain locking* above; **409** after 5 walks).
- **409** `Some revisions of this document are not available to you, so its access level cannot be
  lowered. …` when the change would lower any revision and the caller cannot open every revision.
- **409** `The document is already at that access level` when no revision changes.
- One required `ACCESS_LEVEL_CHANGE` audit row **per changed revision**, each with the old and new
  level, the reason, `authorized_user_count` and a `chain_change` marker (`trigger`
  `access_level_change`, the addressed document id, `chain_size`), all in the same transaction
  (**503**, nothing saved, if any cannot be written).
- The response is the addressed document plus `previous_access_level` (its own former level),
  `changed_document_ids` (every revision that changed), `chain_size` (1 for a document with no
  revisions) and `authorized_user_count`: the company's own active export-authorized users.
  `export_controlled` with `authorized_user_count` 0 means nobody can open the document until an
  Admin authorizes someone; the UI warns.

Every document audit row (upload, attach, delete, Hank intake filing, and each `ACCESS_LEVEL_CHANGE`)
records `access_level` among the document's values; that is what the audit-log redaction reads for
a deleted document.

**Access review: `GET /documents/access-review`** (Admin / Quality; pure read, a tool for an agent
whose user holds the role). It returns `documents`: every document the caller may open whose
linked part's customer resolves as export-controlled and whose level is still `standard` or
`restricted`, each with `document_id`, `document_number`, `revision`, `title`, `document_type`,
`access_level`, `part_id`, `part_number`, `customer_id`, `customer_name` and `classification`
(`itar_export_controlled` or `cui`). Also `document_count`, and `unlinked_document_count`: documents
below `export_controlled` with no part link, which the server cannot judge. A document linked to a
part whose customer name is blank or matches no customer is neither listed nor counted. Fix a row
with `POST /documents/{id}/access-level`.

**Known residuals.**

- **The access review judges by part only.** Unlike the raise rule, it does not read the work
  order: a document linked to a work order and no part is counted in `unlinked_document_count`,
  even when the work order's customer is export-controlled. New uploads and attaches to such a work
  order are raised automatically; this matters for documents linked before the customer was
  marked.
- **Legacy chains with mixed levels.** A revision upload's own checks read the whole chain. In a
  history whose revisions already carry different levels, uploading against a predecessor the
  uploader may open can still answer **409** `A newer revision exists` for a later revision the
  uploader may not open (and the **422** duplicate-label check walks every ancestor). Since levels
  move chain-wide, a chain stays uniform once one access-level change has been applied to it.
- The other writers of `documents` store `standard`: receiving certificates and labels, carrier
  labels and bills of lading, laser-nest drawings and process-sheet step evidence. A person raises
  one with `POST /documents/{id}/access-level`.
- The crew station reads its queue with the tablet's own station token, which sees `standard`
  only, so a `restricted` or `export_controlled` nest PDF has no **View nest / drawing** button
  there, even for an export-authorized operator (see
  [KIOSK.md → Drawing / nest viewer](KIOSK.md#drawing--nest-viewer)).

> **For the Quality Manager (AS9100D 7.5.3.1, ITAR / EAR handling).**
>
> - **The three levels.** `standard`: anyone signed in who can read documents. `restricted`:
>   Admin, Manager, Quality and Supervisor. `export_controlled`: only people an Admin of this
>   company has marked export-authorized on the Users page; being an Admin does not count, and a
>   platform account's authorization from another company does not count here. Deactivating a
>   user revokes their authorization, and reactivating them does not bring it back.
> - **Order matters.** First have an Admin grant export authorization to the people who must open
>   ITAR / EAR drawings, including the operators who run those jobs (Users → **Export-authorized** →
>   **Grant**, with a reason). A document flagged `export_controlled` while nobody is authorized
>   cannot be opened by anyone, you included.
> - **Run the access review.** Documents → **Access review** lists every document whose part
>   belongs to an export-controlled customer but is not yet `export_controlled`. Open each row and
>   use **Change access**, with a reason. The review judges by part only, and counts the documents
>   with no part link (work-order-only documents among them); it cannot judge those, so look
>   through them yourself (the Documents list's access-level filter, set to **Standard**, helps).
> - **Flag documents.** On upload, choose the access level; the server raises it to
>   `export_controlled` when the linked part's or work order's customer is export-controlled, and
>   Hank filing and attaching a document to such a work order do the same. A level belongs to the whole revision history: **Change access**
>   sets every revision at once, a new revision filed above its history lifts the earlier ones,
>   and a revision never drops below the one it replaces. You can lower a level only if you can
>   open every revision. Every change is in the Audit Log as `ACCESS_LEVEL_CHANGE`, one row per
>   revision, with your reason. A reader who may not open a document sees its audit rows, and the
>   Hank intake and task rows that name it, redacted.
> - **AI.** Hank and the AI copilot never send an `export_controlled` document's details to the
>   model, even for an authorized user; in Hank chat such a document, and saved Hank work that
>   names it, reads as missing.
> - **What is not covered.** Certificates, receiving and shipping labels, bills of lading,
>   laser-nest drawings and step photos are stored `standard`; raise them by hand when they carry
>   controlled data. Parts and work orders link to customers by name only (`customer_name`), so a
>   record with a blank or misspelled customer name is never judged: neither the raise rule nor the
>   review sees it. Keep customer names exact. The customer's own export-control marking is an
>   Admin's job (Customers → **Export control**). On the floor, an operator sees only what they
>   may open, and a crew station shows only `standard` nest PDFs (KIOSK.md).

### QMS Standards & Audit Readiness

Standards/clause/evidence management for AS9100D, ISO 9001, CMMC and similar quality systems, all
under `/qms-standards`. Every endpoint is **tenant-scoped to the caller's active company**
(`get_current_company_id`). Reads (list / get / detail) are available to **any authenticated user**
in the tenant, while writes are **role-gated** — the read-broad / write-restricted model documented
in `RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md`.

**Standards**

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/qms-standards/` | List standards with compliance-summary counts (`active_only` filter) | Yes |
| POST | `/qms-standards/` | Create standard | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}/upload-pdf` | AI clause extraction from an uploaded PDF | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| GET | `/qms-standards/audit-readiness` | Audit-readiness dashboard summary across active standards | Yes |
| GET | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}` | Get standard with all clauses and evidence | Yes |
| PUT | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}` | Update standard | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| DELETE | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}` | Delete standard and all its clauses/evidence | Admin |

> **A document a standard or evidence link names cannot be deleted.** `DELETE /documents/{id}`
> answers **409** while a standard's or an evidence link's `document_id` points at it, and removed
> standards, clauses and evidence links keep it too. To release a document, set `document_id` to
> `null` on the standard or evidence link first; removing the link does not. See
> [Documents](#documents).

**Clauses**

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses` | List clauses for a standard (flat list) | Yes |
| POST | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses` | Add a clause | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| POST | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses/bulk` | Bulk-import clauses (e.g. from a parsed document) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| PUT | `/qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}` | Update clause, incl. compliance-status assessment | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| DELETE | `/qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}` | Delete a clause and its evidence links | Admin / Manager |

> **A parent clause must be a live clause of your company in the same standard:** the three routes
> that take a `parent_clause_id` in the body (`POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses`, `POST
> /qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses/bulk` and `PUT /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}`) check it
> before they write anything. An id that does not exist, another company's clause, a deleted clause
> and a clause of another standard all get the same **404 `Parent clause not found`**, with nothing
> saved and no audit entry, so the answer says nothing about other companies' clauses. The bulk
> import is all-or-nothing: one bad parent refuses every clause in the request (clauses in the same
> request cannot name each other; they have no id yet). On a `PUT`, the clause itself (**422** `A
> clause cannot be its own parent clause`) or any of its own sub-clauses at any depth (**422** `A
> clause cannot be placed under one of its own sub-clauses`) is refused, so no new cycle can be
> stored. The descendant check follows stored links through deleted clauses too, and re-parenting is
> serialized per company (a Postgres advisory lock), so two opposite moves sent at the same moment
> cannot both pass. `parent_clause_id: null` still clears the parent, and a `PUT` that does not send
> `parent_clause_id` is not judged on the value already stored. Every response that carries a clause
> tree renders `clauses`, `sub_clauses` and their evidence from your own company's live rows only
> (`GET /qms-standards/{standard_id}`, `GET /qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses`, and the `PUT
> /qms-standards/{standard_id}` and `PUT /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}` responses), so a link
> written before this check existed no longer shows another company's clause.
> Before this, any existing clause id, another company's included, was accepted, while a
> nonexistent one failed with a 500, and a self- or descendant parent stored a cycle that made every
> read of that standard fail with a 500. To clear such a stored link, `PUT {"parent_clause_id":
> null}` on the child clause.

> **Compliance notes and the last-assessed stamp:** `PUT /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}` sets
> `last_assessed_date` (now) and `last_assessed_by` (the caller) only when the body carries
> `compliance_status`. A body without it, such as one that sends `compliance_notes` alone, leaves
> the status and both stamp fields as they were, and writes an audit `UPDATE` entry (when a value
> changed) but no status-change entry. `compliance_notes` is at most 5,000 characters (**422** over
> it), and `null` clears it.
>
> **On the QMS Standards page**, an expanded clause shows a **Notes** block: the stored
> `compliance_notes` with their line breaks kept, or *No notes yet.* when there are none, and an
> **Edit notes** button (**Add notes** when there are none) that opens a notes dialog. The dialog
> counts characters against the 5,000-character cap and shows an inline error over it; **Save
> notes** is enabled only when the text differs from what is stored and is within the cap. Saving
> sends `PUT /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}` with `compliance_notes` only, never the status, so
> it does not change the clause's compliance status or its last-assessed stamp. Text that is empty
> or only whitespace is sent as `null`, clearing the notes; any other text is sent as typed. The
> save is not optimistic: after the server accepts the write the page reloads the standard, and only
> then does the dialog close, so reopening it always starts from the saved notes. A refusal (the route is Admin / Manager / Quality, so another role
> gets **403**) is shown inside the dialog, which stays open with what was typed. Cancel, the close
> button and Escape ask before discarding changed text, a click outside the dialog does not close
> it, and nothing closes it while a save is in flight.

**Auto-evidence discovery**

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/auto-evidence` | Discover live ERP/MES evidence for a single clause (read-only, nothing persisted) | Yes |
| POST | `/qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link` | Auto-discover and persist evidence links for all clauses in a standard | Admin / Manager / Quality |

**Evidence links**

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| POST | `/qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/evidence` | Link evidence to a clause. The audit `CREATE` row is required evidence: **503** and nothing linked if it cannot be written (see below) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| PUT | `/qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` | Update evidence, incl. verification. The audit `UPDATE` row is required evidence: **503** and nothing saved if it cannot be written (see below) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| DELETE | `/qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` | Remove an evidence link. The audit `DELETE` row is required evidence: **503** and the link stays if it cannot be written (see below) | Admin / Manager / Quality |

> **A linked document must be your company's:** the four routes that take a `document_id` in the
> body (`POST /qms-standards/`, `PUT /qms-standards/{standard_id}`, `POST
> /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/evidence` and `PUT /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}`)
> check it against the active company's documents before they write anything. An id that does not
> exist and an id that belongs to another company both get the same **404 `Document not found`**,
> with nothing saved and no audit entry, so the answer says nothing about other companies'
> documents. `document_id: null` on a `PUT` still clears the link, and a `PUT` that does not send
> `document_id` is not judged on the value already stored (the QMS Standards page's Verify sends
> `is_verified` only). The document's control status (draft, obsolete, ...) is not checked. Before
> this, a nonexistent id failed with a 500, while any existing id, another company's included, was
> accepted and linked.
>
> **On the QMS Standards page**, the Link Evidence dialog has an optional **Linked Document** field:
> a searchable list of the active company's documents (from `GET /documents/`, fetched each time
> the dialog opens), each shown by title with its document number and revision. It offers only the
> current revision of each document (a row that a later revision names in `previous_revision_id`
> is left out) and no shipping or receiving paperwork (`receiving_label`, `shipping_label`,
> `bill_of_lading`). Choosing a document fills the title with "*title*, Rev *revision*" while the
> title is empty or still the picker's own wording: choosing another document replaces it, clearing
> the document clears it, and a typed or edited title is never changed. If a reloaded list no
> longer offers the chosen document (a newer revision superseded it, or it was removed), the choice
> is dropped with a notice rather than sent. The page sends `document_id` only on
> `POST /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/evidence`, and only when a document is chosen; evidence
> can still be linked without one. A refusal such as the **404** above
> is shown inside the dialog, which stays open with what was typed; closing a dialog with input asks
> before discarding it. Every evidence row that carries a
> `document_id`, including links written through the API or MCP, shows an **Open document** link to
> `/documents?document=<id>`, which opens that document's preview on the Documents page. The page
> does not edit or clear an existing link's `document_id`.

> **PDF clause extraction:** `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/upload-pdf` requires a text-based
> PDF (≤ 20 MB, else **413** before any work; scanned/image-only PDFs are rejected) and a
> configured `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — it returns **500** if the key is missing. Claude extracts the
> numbered clauses and persists them against the standard.
>
> The text layer is read in the resource-limited reader process, with the QMS limits listed in
> [Document Text Extraction Limits](#document-text-extraction-limits): 2,000 pages, 2,000,000
> characters, 90 seconds. That read can refuse the upload with a **400** in two ways, both before
> the AI call, so nothing is saved:
> - `"Failed to read PDF: …"` when nothing could be read at all. Since 2026-11-09 the rest of the
>   detail is a plain sentence, for example "The PDF could not be read. It may be damaged or not a
>   PDF." or "Reading the PDF took longer than 90 seconds, so its text was not read.". It used to be
>   the parser's exception text.
> - (new 2026-11-09) `"Only part of this PDF could be read: … Split it into smaller PDFs and upload each one."` when
>   the read stopped part-way **and** the text it got is shorter than the 100,000 characters the AI
>   is sent. This response has no place for a warning, so the upload is refused rather than saving a
>   clause list that silently misses the unread pages. If a partial read already covers the first
>   100,000 characters, the upload goes ahead unchanged, because the AI never reads past that point.
>   When the read stopped because a page could not be parsed (rather than at a limit), the advice
>   ends `"The PDF may be damaged. Save or export it again as a new PDF and upload that copy."`
>   instead, since splitting the file would not get past a damaged page. Before 2026-11-09 such a
>   PDF was refused whatever was read before the damaged page, with the parser's exception text.

> **An evidence rule that fails is reported as not assessed, never dropped.** Each evidence rule a
> clause matches runs its query in its own savepoint. A rule whose query raises is rolled back to that
> savepoint, logged with its traceback, and listed in the `auto-evidence` response as a placeholder
> row: that rule's `evidence_type` / `title` / `module_reference`, `description` *"Evidence could not
> be computed from live records"*, `health_status` `not_computed`, `examples` `[]` and
> `suggested_compliance` `not_assessed` (its `total_count` / `recent_count` of 0 are placeholders, not
> measurements). `not_computed` is reserved for this placeholder and no evidence query returns it, so a
> client can tell it from `no_data` — a query that ran and found no records, with the same zero counts.
> Don't report a `not_computed` row's counts: the QMS Standards page shows it as *Not computed* with its
> `health_detail`, never as "0 records". The clause therefore cannot roll up to `compliant`: a finding from a rule that did
> compute (`non_compliant`, then `partial`) still decides the clause, and otherwise a clause with a
> failed rule is `not_assessed` — even when every other row is compliant, so a query failure is never
> presented as a compliance gap. The rules after it still run. The rule used to be silently dropped: a clause matching calibration and
> maintenance whose maintenance query failed showed `compliant` from calibration alone, and on
> PostgreSQL the aborted transaction failed, and dropped, every later rule too. The response shape is
> unchanged.
>
> `auto-link` persists **nothing** for a failed rule: no evidence link is created, and an existing
> auto-linked one keeps the `live_count`, description and `last_refreshed` of the last run that
> computed it. The failed rule still counts toward its clause's `compliance_summary` bucket, and a
> clause whose matched rules all failed counts under `clauses_without_evidence`. The `auto-link`
> response adds `total_evidence_failed` (int, default `0`: rule evaluations that failed this run). When
> N > 0 the audit row's description gains *", N not computed (left unchanged)"* and its `extra_data`
> carries `evidence_not_computed`, one `{clause_id, clause_number, rule_id}` per skipped rule, which is
> what explains the older `last_refreshed` on those links. The QMS Standards page shows that count on
> the auto-link result card (*Evidence Not Computed*) and as a warning toast, saying the links were
> left as last refreshed.

> **Auto-evidence supplier counts now exclude removed suppliers — expect the number to drop.** The
> *Supplier Management & Evaluation* evidence row (`GET /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/auto-evidence`,
> and what `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link` persists) counted **soft-deleted** vendors in
> its `total_count` / "N suppliers" figure while the "(M active)" half excluded them — inventing an
> approval gap, in an artifact meant for a registrar. Both halves now filter `is_deleted`.
>
> **"Approved" now means approved on the Approved Supplier List — expect that number to drop too.**
> The same row used to report its *active* vendor count as the approved count, overstating it by
> every active vendor that is Conditional, Disqualified or not on the ASL. The description now reads
> *"N suppliers (M active), K approved on the ASL, S performance scorecards"*, where K counts live,
> active vendors whose `approval_status` is Approved or Approved - Customer Directed (migration
> `123`; see Purchasing → *Approved Supplier List on the vendor record*). Until the ASL is loaded, K is
> 0. The "no performance scorecards" warning still quotes the active count.

> **The Audit Trail evidence row reports a paused hash chain, and missing triggers, instead of
> claiming them.** The *Audit Trail (Audit Log & Hash-Chain Status)* row — titled *Audit Trail
> (Immutable Hash-Chain Log)* until this change — used to say "integrity hash chain active" and
> suggest `compliant` whenever the company had any audit entries — even with the chain paused
> (`AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN_ENABLED=false`; see
> [Pausing the hash chain](AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_RUNBOOK.md#pausing-the-hash-chain-audit_hash_chain_enabled)),
> when new entries carry the `LEGACY_CHAIN_PAUSED` placeholder and can never be verified. It now reads
> three things on every call: the setting; how many of the company's entries carry that placeholder,
> over its **whole history** (a paused span never becomes verifiable by ageing; the last-12-months
> figure is shown alongside); and, on PostgreSQL, whether the `tr_audit_log_no_update` /
> `tr_audit_log_no_delete` triggers exist and fire (`pg_trigger`, enabled `O`/`A`).
>
> | Chain now | Paused entries (any age) | `health_status` / `suggested_compliance` | `description` says |
> |-----------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------|
> | on | 0 | `healthy` / `compliant` | `…, SHA-256 integrity chain` |
> | on | K > 0 | `warning` / `partial` | `…; SHA-256 integrity chain enabled, but K entries were written while it was paused (J in last 12 months)` |
> | paused | K ≥ 0 (the company has entries) | `warning` / `partial` | `…; SHA-256 integrity chain paused (K entries written without it, J in last 12 months)` — or `(no entries written without it yet)` |
> | either | no entries at all | `no_data` / `not_assessed` | unchanged when on; `…; SHA-256 integrity chain paused` when paused |
>
> Once the company has at least one audit entry, the trigger check can cap the row too. If it finds
> either trigger missing or disabled, the row is `warning` / `partial` whatever the chain state, and
> `description` ends `; database UPDATE/DELETE triggers missing or disabled`. A failed catalog read
> **on PostgreSQL** (it runs in its own savepoint, so a failure cannot abort the request) caps the row
> the same way, with `description` ending `; database UPDATE/DELETE trigger status could not be
> checked`; off PostgreSQL (dev/test SQLite) there is no catalog to read, so the status is reported as
> unchecked without capping. `health_detail` then ends with the trigger finding: "Database triggers
> refuse UPDATE and DELETE statements on audit entries." when both are in force, "The database triggers
> that refuse UPDATE and DELETE statements on audit entries are missing or disabled." when not, and
> "Database UPDATE/DELETE trigger status could not be checked." when the read failed or there is no
> catalog to read.
>
> With **no** audit entries the trigger state never caps the row: it stays `no_data` /
> `not_assessed` and `description` carries no trigger suffix. While the chain is on, `health_detail` is
> just "No audit log entries found"; while it is paused, it adds that entries written now will not be
> hash-chained, followed by the trigger finding.
>
> When the warning comes from the chain — paused now, or paused entries on record — `health_detail`
> also says the paused entries carry no integrity hash and can never be cryptographically verified,
> with the split `K of N (J in the last 12 months)` (K can be 0 while the chain is paused, until one of
> the company's entries is written without it). A warning from the triggers alone keeps the healthy
> chain text and adds the trigger finding. The healthy text says the chain is **enabled**, not
> verified: this row does not check chain integrity. `GET /audit/integrity/verify` and
> `/audit/integrity/verify-recent` do (platform-admin only, like the `/audit/integrity/status`
> statistics), and `GET /audit/integrity/record/{sequence_number}` verifies one of the company's own
> entries for a tenant Admin (see [Audit Log](#audit-log)).
>
> For a company with audit entries, a clause backed by this row therefore never gets a suggested
> roll-up (`overall_suggested_compliance`, auto-link's `compliance_summary`) of `compliant` once the
> company has any paused entry, while the chain is paused, or while the triggers are missing, disabled
> or (on PostgreSQL) unreadable: `partial` at best. Nor does a company with no audit entries, whose
> `not_assessed` row never rolls up `compliant`. That is a suggestion only: neither endpoint writes the
> clause's `compliance_status`. Of the fields that change, auto-link
> (`POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link`) stores only `description` (`health_status`,
> `health_detail` and `suggested_compliance` are computed per call and never persisted), so stored
> evidence picks up the new wording on the next auto-link run in which the audit rule computes for its
> clause (a run where it fails leaves the stored link unchanged; see `evidence_not_computed`). That
> rule no longer matches a 9.2 / 9.3 clause (unless its text says "audit trail" or "audit log"), so
> such a clause's stored link never picks it up: the next run retires the link or keeps it for review
> unrefreshed (see *Auto-link retires its own stale links* below). The QMS page's
> linked-evidence list shows each stored link's `description` under its title. For an auto-linked row
> that is the text written by the last auto-link run in which its rule computed, dated by the row's
> "Refreshed" stamp; an edit through `PUT /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` replaces it without
> moving that stamp, until the next auto-link run in which the rule computes overwrites it (a run where
> it fails leaves the stored link unchanged; see `evidence_not_computed`). A link whose rule no longer
> matches its clause (a 9.2 / 9.3 clause's audit-trail link, say) is not refreshed while that stays
> true: auto-link retires it, or keeps it for review exactly as it stands (a kept link is refreshed
> again only if the clause is later re-worded so its rule matches). An auto-linked description
> is always shown in full, never clamped, because the paused-chain and trigger disclosures sit at the
> end of the text. A manual description is clamped to three lines behind **Show more** only while it
> needs more than three lines on screen, so clamped text always has that control. `health_status`,
> `health_detail` and `suggested_compliance` are not stored: the live auto-evidence preview
> (**Auto-Discover**) shows each row's `health_detail` and its `health_status` as a coloured dot (a
> failed rule's row also reads *Not computed*), and only the clause-level roll-up of
> `suggested_compliance` (`overall_suggested_compliance`). The title was renamed because "Immutable
> Hash-Chain" was untrue for every paused entry, and until the list showed `description` the title was
> the one claim it showed; the title now names what the row reports and asserts nothing. Existing
> auto-linked evidence picks up the new title on the next auto-link run in which the audit rule
> computes for its clause (a run where it fails leaves the stored link unchanged; see
> `evidence_not_computed`), matched by rule id; no migration. On a 9.2 / 9.3 clause, which that rule
> no longer matches, a stored link keeps whatever title it had at its last refresh (or a person has
> since given it) until auto-link retires it or, if it is kept for review, a person removes it (see
> *What operators see* below). The row's `title`, `module_reference` and `evidence_type` do not
> change with the chain or trigger state.

> **The PM evidence row now judges the PM schedules, not just maintenance work orders — expect the
> verdict to drop.** The *Preventive Maintenance & Infrastructure* row (clauses matched on maintenance
> / infrastructure keywords, e.g. 7.1.3) counted every `MaintenanceSchedule`, active or not, and took
> "overdue" from maintenance work orders alone. A shop holding thirty PM schedules that had never been
> performed (first due date still ahead, no maintenance work orders) read **healthy / compliant** —
> and kept reading it with every schedule deactivated. Now only **active** schedules count (the same
> set `GET /maintenance/schedules` lists by default), "today" is the company's local date
> (America/Chicago unless the company sets another zone), and the first matching rung decides:
>
> | # | Condition | `health_status` / `suggested_compliance` |
> |---|---|---|
> | 1 | No active schedule and no maintenance work order | `no_data` / `not_assessed` |
> | 2 | An active schedule's `next_due_date` is before today, or a `scheduled` / `overdue` maintenance work order is past its `due_date` | `critical` / `non_compliant` |
> | 3 | No active schedule, but maintenance work orders exist (no PM plan) | `warning` / `partial` |
> | 4 | No active schedule has performance evidence | `warning` / `not_assessed` |
> | 5 | Some active schedules never performed, or some with no next due date | `warning` / `partial` |
> | 6 | Every active schedule current, dated and performed at least once | `healthy` / `compliant` |
>
> *Performance evidence* is a `last_completed_date` on the schedule, or a **completed** maintenance
> work order of the same company linked to it; completing a schedule-linked maintenance work order
> (`POST /maintenance/work-orders/{id}/complete`) is what clears "never performed". An overdue
> maintenance work order used to give `warning` / `partial`; it now gives `critical` /
> `non_compliant`, the calibration row's verdict for an overdue gauge. The response shape is
> unchanged: `total_count` is still the maintenance work-order count (the figure auto-link stores as
> the evidence's live count), and `recent_count` is now the **active** schedule count (it was every
> schedule). The description reads *"N active PM schedules (X past due, Y never performed), M
> maintenance WOs (C completed, O overdue)"*. Because `overall_suggested_compliance` is `partial`
> whenever a clause's rows disagree, a clause whose other rows are all `compliant` now rolls up to
> `partial`, not `compliant`, while this row is `not_assessed`. A shop that loaded its PM schedules
> before performing any PM will see the row at `not_assessed` until the first schedule-linked
> maintenance work order is completed — intended: a false "compliant" in front of a registrar is worse
> than "not assessed". Auto-link persists the counts and description as evidence; it never sets a
> clause's `compliance_status`.

> **Deletes are soft (records retained):** the three `DELETE` endpoints above return **204** but
> do not physically remove rows — the standard / clause / evidence is marked deleted and disappears
> from all reads (including the nested clauses/evidence on `GET /qms-standards/{standard_id}`), while
> the record is retained for AS9100D traceability. Every QMS create / update / delete route — plus
> a status-change entry when a clause's `compliance_status` changes — writes to the tamper-evident
> audit trail (`GET /api/v1/audit/`), with three routes audited at the summary level rather than per
> record: `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses/bulk` and `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/upload-pdf`
> each write one entry on the standard for all the clauses they add; and
> `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link` writes no entry for the evidence links it creates or
> refreshes, just the run's one best-effort summary entry on the standard (`Auto-linked evidence: N
> created, M updated…`), while each link it retires gets a **required** `DELETE` entry (see *Auto-link
> retires its own stale links* below). An evidence `PUT` that changes nothing writes no entry.

> **A clause of a removed standard is removed with it.** Removing a standard marks only the
> standard row deleted; its clauses keep their own flag. Every route that takes a clause id treats
> a clause whose standard is removed (or is not your company's) as removed: `PUT` and `DELETE
> /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}`, `GET /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/auto-evidence` and
> `POST /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/evidence` answer **404 `Clause not found`**, the same as
> for a removed clause, and write nothing. `GET /qms-standards/{standard_id}/clauses` answers **404
> `QMS standard not found`** for a removed standard, as `GET /qms-standards/{standard_id}` does; a
> missing id or another company's gets the same 404 (it used to be an empty list). Before this,
> all of them still answered for a removed standard's clauses: a `PUT` could change a clause's
> `compliance_status` on a standard that had left the record, the list still showed its clauses
> and their evidence links, and adding evidence created a link no screen would show. Nor does such a
> clause render as a sub-clause of a live standard's clause (a cross-standard `parent_clause_id`
> could be written before the parent check above existed): the standard and clause-list reads, and
> both `PUT` responses, leave it and its evidence out. The standard is checked when the request
> reads the clause; a removal that commits between that read and the request's own commit is not
> seen.

> **Evidence under a removed clause or standard is frozen.** Removing a standard or a clause marks
> only that row deleted; the evidence links under it keep their own flag but disappear with their
> parent from every QMS read. `PUT` and `DELETE /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` treat such a
> link as removed: **404 `Evidence not found`** (the same answer as for a removed link, judged after
> the row lock) and nothing is written. Before this, both accepted it, so an API caller could edit,
> verify or clear the `document_id` of a link that had left the record, and a cleared link let its
> document be deleted. The clause and standard are checked when the request reads them; a removal
> that commits between that read and the request's own commit is not seen.

> **Editing or removing an evidence link locks it first:** `PUT` and `DELETE
> /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` lock the evidence row before they read it, and write the
> change before the audit entry. So a Verify or Remove that runs at the same time as auto-link (or
> as another person's edit) waits for the other write to finish and is then judged against the row
> as it stands. If the link was removed while the request waited (auto-link retired it, or someone
> else removed it), the answer is **404 `Evidence not found`** and nothing is written. Before this,
> a Verify could mark a link that auto-link had just retired as verified and still answer 200, and
> a Verify or Remove racing auto-link could fail with the app-wide 409. A 404 here means the link
> is gone; if it should still exist, link it again. The `UPDATE` audit entry's `changes` now also
> lists the row's new `updated_at`.

> **Linking, editing (incl. Verify) and removing an evidence link are required audit evidence:**
> `POST /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/evidence`, `PUT /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}`
> and `DELETE /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` write their audit entry in the same
> transaction as the change, and the change is saved only if the entry is. A Verify is a quality
> judgment and the evidence row keeps only the latest one (`verified_by` / `verified_date` are
> overwritten by the next Verify), so the audit entries are its only history. If the entry cannot
> be written the change is rolled back and the answer is **503**:
>
> - `POST`: `"The audit record for linking this evidence could not be saved; the evidence was not linked. Retry."`
> - `PUT`: `"The audit record for this evidence change could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry."`
> - `DELETE`: `"The audit record for removing this evidence could not be saved; the evidence was not removed. Retry."`
>
> Nothing was saved, so retrying the same request is safe (a retried `POST` links the evidence
> once). An audit write that loses a PostgreSQL lock race (deadlock / serialization failure) also
> answers this 503 rather than the app-wide 409; either way nothing was saved. Before this, an audit write that failed without a database error (a retry-exhausted
> sequence collision, a value the audit row could not serialize) was skipped and the route still
> answered 201 / 200 / 204 with the change saved. Unchanged: a `PUT` that changes nothing (an empty
> body, or values equal to the stored ones) writes no entry and answers 200; the `CREATE` entry
> carries the row as created in `new_values`; the `UPDATE` entry carries the full before / after
> row in `old_values` / `new_values` and the field-level diff in `extra_data.changes`; the `DELETE`
> entry carries the row as it stood before the removal in `old_values` and
> `extra_data.soft_delete: true`. Auto-link (`POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link`) keeps
> its own audit rules and is not changed by this; those rules include required evidence too, since
> each link it retires gets a required `DELETE` entry (see *Auto-link retires its own stale links*
> below).
>
> Each entry's `resource_identifier` is the evidence title cut to 255 characters (the audit
> column's length; a title may be 500), and its `description` keeps the whole title. Before the
> cut, linking evidence whose title was longer than 255 characters failed with a 500 on PostgreSQL
> (the uncut identifier failed the audit INSERT).

> **Internal audit and management review are not assessed from the ERP — expect the suggested
> compliance for those clauses to drop.** Auto-evidence picks rules for a clause by keywords in its
> title and description. The *Audit Trail (Audit Log & Hash-Chain Status)* row (the ERP's own
> change log) used to match "internal audit", "audit program" and "management review" as well as "audit
> trail" and "audit log". Change-log entries exist on any working system, so AS9100D / ISO 9001
> 9.2 *Internal audit* and 9.3 *Management review* rolled up `compliant` with no evidence that an
> audit was run or a review held. The change-log row now matches only "audit trail" and "audit
> log". "internal audit", "audit program" (which also matches "audit programme") and "management
> review" go to a separate rule, `internal_audit_review`. So do a few common paraphrases a company
> quality manual uses: "internal quality audit", "audits at planned intervals" / "audit at planned
> intervals", "top management shall review" and "review by top management". These are kept
> specific on purpose: a bare "quality audit" or "audit plan" would also hit supplier-audit clauses.
> The rule's row is always the same: `title` *Internal Audit & Management Review (Not Assessed
> Automatically)*, `evidence_type` `other`, `total_count` and `recent_count` `0`, `health_status`
> `no_data`, `suggested_compliance` `not_assessed`. The zeros mean the ERP has no internal-audit,
> audit-program or management-review record type to count. The row says only that auto-evidence
> cannot assess the clause, not that the ERP holds nothing about audits: a person may have linked
> an audit report or review minutes to the clause, and the description asks for exactly that. NCRs
> with `source` `internal_audit` and CARs with `initiation_reason` `internal_audit` or
> `management_review` are deliberately not counted: they show a finding was raised, not that the
> program ran.
>
> `GET /qms-standards/clauses/{clause_id}/auto-evidence` lists the row like any other; internal
> `_`-prefixed keys are stripped from every row. The roll-up rule is unchanged: on its own the row
> gives `overall_suggested_compliance` `not_assessed`, and beside other rows the clause rolls up
> `partial` (or `non_compliant` when another row is), never `compliant`.

> **Auto-link retires its own stale links — expect 9.2 / 9.3 clauses to lose the change-log link.**
> An auto-linked evidence row exists only because a rule matched its clause. Each run of
> `POST /qms-standards/{standard_id}/auto-link` now goes through every clause of the standard and
> soft-deletes its auto-linked (`is_auto_linked` true) evidence rows whose rule (`auto_link_query`)
> no longer matches the clause's text, unless a person reviewed them (below). Each retired row gets
> one audit `DELETE` row: `resource_type` `qms_clause_evidence`, `extra_data.soft_delete` `true`,
> `extra_data.retired_by` `auto_link`, plus `rule_id`, `clause_id`, `clause_number` and
> `evidence_id`, with the pre-delete row in `old_values`. That row is **required**: it is the only
> record that auto-link, not the person who clicked it, removed the link. If it cannot be written,
> the whole run rolls back and answers **503** (*The audit record for retiring stale auto-linked
> evidence could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry.*). A retry is safe.
>
> - A row a person reviewed is never retired: verified (`is_verified` true), or carrying a document
>   (`document_id`) or non-blank `verification_notes`, which auto-link never writes. It is kept and
>   listed, with `reason` `verified` or `annotated`, in the response's `evidence_kept_reviewed` and
>   in the run's summary audit row.
> - Manually linked rows (`is_auto_linked` false) are never touched.
> - A rule is "matched" by its keywords, not by producing a row this run. A rule whose query failed
>   this run still counts as matched, so its stored row stays.
> - The *Internal Audit & Management Review* row is never persisted. A clause whose only row is that
>   one counts in `clauses_without_evidence`, not `clauses_with_evidence`. Its `not_assessed` still
>   counts in `compliance_summary`.
>
> The response gains `total_evidence_retired` (`0` when nothing was retired) and
> `evidence_kept_reviewed` (empty when nothing was kept); see the schema below. The run's summary
> audit row (`resource_type` `qms_standard`) carries `extra_data.evidence_retired` (a list of
> `{evidence_id, clause_id, clause_number, rule_id}`) and `extra_data.evidence_kept_reviewed` (the
> same, plus `reason`), each only when non-empty. Candidate rows are locked (`FOR UPDATE`) for the
> run, so a second run on the same standard never retires a row twice, and a **Verify** committed
> before the run reached the row is honored. A Verify or Remove that reaches a row while the run
> holds it waits for the run to finish; if the run retired that row, the answer is **404 `Evidence
> not found`** and nothing is written (see "Editing or removing an evidence link locks it first"
> above). The QMS Standards page's auto-link result dialog shows `total_evidence_retired` as *Stale
> Links Retired* (only when the API sends it), lists each `evidence_kept_reviewed` link under *Kept
> for Review* with its clause number, reason and rule, and raises a warning toast when any were kept.
>
> **What operators see:** a 9.2 or 9.3 clause already linked to the audit-trail row loses that link
> on the next **Auto-Link Evidence** run, unless someone verified or annotated it. That link keeps
> whatever title and description it had at its last refresh, because the audit rule no longer matches
> those clauses and no later run refreshes it there: the new title if an auto-link run refreshed it
> after the rename above but before the rule stopped matching, the old *Audit Trail (Immutable
> Hash-Chain Log)* otherwise (an edit a person made since through
> `PUT /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}` stands). Such a link is kept and listed in
> `evidence_kept_reviewed`: review it and, if it is wrong, remove it by hand
> (`DELETE /qms-standards/evidence/{evidence_id}`). Retirement never changes a clause's
> `compliance_status`, so a clause someone already set to `compliant` keeps that status until a
> person reassesses it. Retired rows drop out of `total_evidence_links` and `unverified_evidence` on
> `GET /qms-standards/audit-readiness`.

#### Audit-Readiness Summary Schema (`GET /qms-standards/audit-readiness`)

```json
{
  "total_standards": 2,
  "total_clauses": 142,
  "compliant": 120,
  "partial": 8,
```
