warnings[]}`. A pure read for the Create PO screen: `refused` is `true` (and `refusal` carries the
exact 409 text) when the vendor is Disqualified. Part ids not found in the active company, or
soft-deleted, are ignored. **404** for a vendor that is not this company's or is soft-deleted. Any
authenticated user.

**Purchase-order warnings — advisory, never a refusal.** Each warning is `{code, message, part_id,
part_number}` (`part_*` set on the per-part codes only):

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `vendor_not_on_asl` | The vendor has no ASL status — including a vendor approved by the checkbox (*"{name} is marked approved but is not on the Approved Supplier List."*): that checkbox is the approval that bypasses the controlled list, so it does not silence the warning |
| `vendor_conditional` | Status Conditional |
| `vendor_disqualified` | Status Disqualified (the check and the PO reads report it; every create refuses it, below) |
| `reevaluation_overdue` | Approved / Conditional / Customer Directed with `reevaluation_due` before today (Central) |
| `scope_not_approved` | A line's part has a `supply_scope` the vendor's `approved_scopes` does not include |
| `scope_unverified` | A line's part has no `supply_scope`, its `part_type` hints at a scope (`hardware` → Hardware; `raw_material` → any Raw Material scope; `consumable` → Adhesives, Paint / Powders or Welding Materials) and the vendor holds none of them. `purchased`, `manufactured` and `assembly` give no hint |

The per-part scope checks run only for a vendor on the ASL that is not Disqualified and not
Customer Directed (a customer-directed source's scope is the customer's direction, not Werco's
approval).

The warnings are returned as `supplier_approval_warnings` on the `POResponse` from `POST
/purchasing/purchase-orders`, `GET /purchasing/purchase-orders/{po_id}`, `PUT
/purchasing/purchase-orders/{po_id}` and `PUT .../supplier-confirmation`, and on the `POUploadResponse`
from `POST /po-upload/create-from-upload`. They are computed when the response is built, from the
vendor's **current** ASL entry and the lines' parts — never stored on the PO, so they change when the
ASL does. The PO detail view shows a `vendor_disqualified` entry red, as the stop on sending,
approving or adding lines to that order (below), never among the amber advisories. The list read (`GET /purchasing/purchase-orders`) does not carry them. To an **AI-external API token** a
warning is part of its purchase order: inside an order withheld for export control, each warning
(code, message and part number) is withheld with it, while a cleared order's warnings are served in
full. The vendor's own ASL fields and `GET /purchasing/vendors/reevaluation-due` are vendor reference
data and are served in full (that list is on the AI-external allowlist), with the residual text pass
removing any controlled part number typed into `approval_notes`. `POST
/purchasing/supplier-approval-check` is a `POST`, so no read-only or AI-external token reaches it. The create **audit
row** records the warnings shown at creation in `extra_data.supplier_approval_warnings` (only when
there are any) on every create through `create_purchase_order_command` (this route, the Hank
purchase-order task and the AI action applier's draft PO), on the PO-upload create, and on the doors
that build their POs directly — the MRP review draft (`POST /mrp/actions/{action_id}/supply-draft`), the
MRP purchase batch, the MRP auto-PO job (its `CREATE_PO` row's `extra_data`) and the open-PO Excel
loader — so a decision to buy anyway is part of the evidence.

**Disqualified is the one hard gate (owner decision 2026-11-13).** No purchase order can be raised to a
vendor that is Disqualified on the ASL: **409** *"{Vendor} is Disqualified on the Approved Supplier
List; a purchase order cannot be raised to it."*, raised before anything is written, at every door
that creates a PO:

- `POST /purchasing/purchase-orders`, the Hank purchase-order task and the AI action applier's draft
  PO — all through `create_purchase_order_command`. Hank also refuses at **prepare**, so it never
  offers a plan the gate would refuse.
- `POST /po-upload/create-from-upload`, before any part is created.
- `POST /mrp/actions/{action_id}/supply-draft` (purchase) and `POST /mrp/purchase-batch/drafts`. The
  MRP supply review's supplier list, and the MRP auto-PO vendor picker (`AUTO_DRAFT` only, never scheduled),
  never offer or choose a Disqualified vendor. The picker does not **re-route** either: a part whose
  only supplier on record (supplier-part mapping or purchase history) is Disqualified is not handed to
  another vendor. The auto-PO pass writes no purchase order for it and records the reason on the MRP action (*"{Vendor} is Disqualified
  on the Approved Supplier List and is the only supplier this part is sourced from …; MRP does not pick
  another supplier for it. Choose one on the MRP supply review."*). There is no "first active vendor"
  fallback any more (removed 2026-11-23): a part with no sourcing at all gets no draft either, and its
  action records *"This part has no supplier-part mapping and no purchase history, so MRP does not pick a
  supplier for it. Choose one on the MRP supply review."*
- The open-PO Excel loader (`POST /purchasing/purchase-orders/import`), as that purchase order's row
  error with the same text.

**An existing PO cannot move toward issue either.** A PO raised before its vendor was Disqualified (an
MRP AUTO_DRAFT pass, a buyer's draft) is refused **409** *"{Vendor} is Disqualified on the Approved
Supplier List; purchase order {PO} {cannot be sent | cannot be approved | cannot be submitted for
approval | cannot have lines added or changed | cannot be emailed}. Cancel it, or record a new approval
decision for the supplier first."* on `POST .../send`, a `PUT` to `approved` / `pending_approval`, a
`PUT` carrying `lines`, `POST .../lines`, and the document-delivery preview / send of the PO email.
Cancelling or closing it, editing its other fields, receiving what was already ordered and
`POST .../restore` (undoing a mistaken delete of a record) stay open.

**No same-name twin of a Disqualified supplier (lead decision L1, 2026-11-15).** A new vendor row
carries no ASL status, so a twin would take the orders the Disqualified record refuses. Every door
that **creates** a vendor therefore refuses a name that normalizes — by the ASL import's own rule
(casefold, whitespace collapsed, en / em dashes read as `-`, spaces beside `-` and `.` removed;
`supplier_approval_service.vendor_name_key`) — to a **live** (not soft-deleted) vendor whose
`approval_status` is `disqualified`, switched off or not: **409** *"{Vendor} is Disqualified on the
Approved Supplier List; a new vendor record cannot be created under that name. Re-evaluate the
existing vendor instead."*, naming the existing vendor, before anything is written:

- `POST /purchasing/vendors`;
- `POST /po-upload/create-from-upload` with `create_vendor` (no vendor and no purchase order);
- `POST /purchasing/vendors/import-csv`, and the Import Center vendor batch that runs it, as that
  row's error with the same text (dry run included; the other rows are unaffected).

Hank, the AI action applier and the open-PO loader never create vendors. Not refused: renaming an
existing vendor, restoring a deleted one, and a name that differs in a word.

Conditional, overdue and out-of-scope purchases are allowed with their warnings. The Purchasing
**Create PO** vendor picker offers vendors with `is_approved = true` **plus Conditional vendors**
(labelled *(Conditional)*; their `is_approved` derives `false`, and Conditional is a warning, not a
gate), never a Disqualified one; the form shows the warnings for the chosen vendor and lines, from
`POST /purchasing/supplier-approval-check`.

**ASL import — `POST /purchasing/vendors/asl-import/preview` then `/commit`.** An **update-only**
load of the ASL onto **existing** vendors. It never creates a vendor: production already holds every
supplier on the list, so creating rows would duplicate them. It is its own preview / commit pair (like
the routing import), not an Import Center batch; Import Center's **Approved Supplier List** card links
to Supplier Scorecards → Approved Supplier List → **Import ASL**.

- **Who:** Admin / Manager / Quality; an API token is refused **403** with the approval verb's text,
  and neither route is an MCP tool.
- **File:** the QL 7.4 workbook as-is, the `approved-supplier-list` template, or a CSV (shared
  parser, 10 MB cap). An `.xlsx` with a sheet named **Approved Supplier List** (any case) is read from
  that sheet, else the first sheet. The header row is the first of the first 10 non-blank rows that
  contains both `supplier_name` and `status` (normalized), so the form's title block is skipped; a
  file with no such row is **400**. Form number, revision and rev date are read from the title block
  when it labels them, and returned as `document`.
- **Columns:** `supplier_name` and `status` are required columns, and SUPPLIER NAME is required on
  every row. Optional: `supplier_address`,
  `approved_scope_of_supply`, `approved_date`, `approval_basis`, `re_evaluation_due_date`,
  `performance_evaluation_date`, `notes`, and `vendor_code` (also read as `code` / `supplier_code`).
  Several scopes or bases in one cell are separated by `;`, `,` or a line break.
- **Matching** (a controlled list must never bind a row to the wrong supplier): a filled `vendor_code`
  matches by code, case-insensitively — and the row's SUPPLIER NAME must then normalize to that
  vendor's name too, or it is a row error (a mistyped code never lands one supplier's approval on
  another's record; rename the vendor first if its name has changed); otherwise the **exact** normalized
  name (case, repeated spaces, en/em dashes and spaces next to `-` or `.` ignored — *"Cinder- Forge"* =
  *"Cinder-Forge"*, *"R.T.Hollis"* = *"R.T. Hollis"*). Nothing fuzzier. **Row errors:** a blank SUPPLIER
  NAME; no match; a code whose vendor's name differs from SUPPLIER NAME; a code matching two live
  vendors whose codes differ only in case; a name matching more than one live vendor (add
  `vendor_code`); a match that is soft-deleted (the error names `POST
  /api/v1/purchasing/vendors/{id}/restore`); two rows binding the same vendor; an unknown status,
  scope or basis label; an unreadable date; a blank STATUS on a vendor that is on the ASL (below).
- **Values:** a blank STATUS on a vendor not on the ASL leaves it off, with a warning. On a vendor that
  **is** on the ASL it is a **row error**: an import never takes a supplier off the list (from
  Disqualified that would lift the one hard PO refusal) — **Update approval** does, with a reason.
  Every other blank cell leaves the vendor's value unchanged; a blank date never clears one. APPROVED
  DATE overwrites `approval_date`. NOTES go to `approval_notes` (first 4000 characters), never to the
  vendor's `notes`. The address and the name are compared only, and a difference is a warning; the
  import never writes either. A Disqualified row and an inactive vendor also carry a warning.
- **Response** (both routes): `{filename, source_hash, plan_hash, document{form_number, revision, rev_date},
  committed, summary{total_rows, matched_rows, update_count, unchanged_count, error_count,
  warning_count, not_on_asl_count}, rows[{row, supplier_name, vendor_id, vendor_code, vendor_name,
  match_by, outcome, changes, warnings[], error}]}`. `outcome` is `update`, `unchanged` or `error`;
  `changes` maps each changed field to `{old, new}` (dates as ISO text). The preview takes no
  `AuditService` and writes nothing.
- **Commit:** `expected_source_hash` (64 characters) must be the preview's `source_hash` — **409**
  *"This file is not the one that was previewed. Preview it again, then commit."* otherwise. Every
  probe re-runs under row locks on the company's vendors. **All-or-nothing:** any row error is **409**
  with `detail = {message, errors[{row, supplier_name, error}]}` and nothing written. Then
  `expected_plan_hash` (64 characters) must be the preview's `plan_hash` — a digest of every row's
  match, outcome and changes — or **409** *"The vendors changed after this file was previewed, so the
  import would no longer write what the preview showed. Preview it again, then commit."*: a decision
  recorded after the preview (Quality disqualifying a vendor the preview showed unchanged) is never
  silently written over. Only changed
  vendors are written, each with a **required** audit row (`vendor` UPDATE, changed fields only,
  `extra_data.source = "asl_import"` plus the form identity, filename, source hash, row number,
  supplier name and match method), and one `vendor_asl_import` IMPORT summary row. If an audit row
  cannot be written nothing is saved (**503**). Re-running the same sheet changes nothing and writes
  no audit row. File-level problems are **400**.

**Part `supply_scope`.** A part can carry the ASL scope its purchases fall under (`parts.supply_scope`,
also migration `123`). It drives the `scope_not_approved` warning only. It is settable through `PUT
/parts/{id}`, `PUT /materials/{id}` and the materials import — see [Part Schema](#part-schema).

**Legacy `approved_supplier_list` table.** The `/supplier-scorecards/approved-suppliers` routes and
their rows are unchanged for people (next section), except that the two **write** routes refuse an
**API token** (**403**, the approval verb's text) and are not MCP tools — an agent's "approved" entry
there would contradict the vendor's own status. Nothing reads them for the ASL any more: the Supplier
Scorecards page's **Approved Supplier List** tab is built on the vendor fields above, and the
scorecard dashboard's `reviews_due` counts vendor re-evaluations (due within 30 days of the Central
day). The tab reads **every live vendor, switched-off ones included** (`GET
/purchasing/vendors?active_only=false`, and the re-evaluation list with `include_inactive=true`),
marking those *Inactive*: the ASL import and **Update approval** both write to them, and a
Disqualified supplier is often also switched off. The QMS auto-evidence supplier
card's "approved" count now means approved **on the ASL** (see QMS Standards).

#### Quality flow-down on the purchase order

AS9100D 8.4.3 requires the shop to communicate its quality requirements to its suppliers. Since
migration `128_po_flowdown`, every purchase order can print a **supplier quality requirements
block**: a heading, the controlled document it cites, a standard paragraph, and the clauses (short
codes such as `Q1`) chosen for that order. The company's settings live in `po_flowdown_profiles`
(one row per company), its clause catalog in `po_quality_clauses`, and each PO carries its own
clause choice (`quality_clause_codes`) and, once it leaves draft, the frozen block
(`flowdown_snapshot`). The block is built by one pure function,
`app/services/po_flowdown_service.py::build_flowdown_block`, for both the live and the frozen case.

> **For the Quality Manager.** Set this up in **Quality → PO Flow-down** (`/quality?tab=flowdown`).
> The same settings also appear in **Purchasing → Quality flow-down**; both tabs show for Admin,
> Manager and Quality, and a Quality user reaches only the Quality one by default (no
> `purchasing:view`; see `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Purchasing).
>
> - **Flow-down profile.** Tick *Print the flow-down block on purchase orders*. *Document
>   reference* is where your supplier quality requirements document and its current revision go
>   (for example `SQR-100 Rev C`); *Standard flow-down text* is the paragraph every PO carries
>   (blank lines start new paragraphs). *Heading* defaults to "Supplier Quality Requirements".
> - **Quality clauses.** *Add clause* once per Q-code: *Code* (for example `Q1`, unique in the
>   company ignoring case, fixed once saved), *Title*, *Clause text*, and *Pre-check on new purchase
>   orders* for clauses that apply to every order. Lower *Sort order* prints first. A clause is
>   never deleted: *Retire* it to stop offering and printing it.
> - **What the buyer does.** Create PO and a draft's PO detail show the active clauses as a
>   checklist, defaults pre-checked; the buyer changes it while the PO is a draft. Once the PO has
>   left draft, its detail shows the block frozen onto it (heading, reference and the clauses
>   actually printed), never the stored choice: a clause retired before issue was not printed.
> - **What the supplier sees.** On the printed and the emailed PO, after the totals and before the
>   notes: the heading, "Reference: {document reference}", the standard text, then one entry per
>   selected clause ("Q1 — title" and its text). It is exactly what was frozen when the PO left
>   draft, so a later edit to the settings or a clause never changes a PO already issued.
> - **Turn it on before issuing purchase orders.** A PO issued while the block is off freezes "no
>   block", and turning the block on later does not add one to it; POs issued before this feature
>   print none either.
> - **The text is entered in the app, never in the repository.** The settings and clauses are
>   company data. The repository is public: the real wording of your supplier quality requirements
>   document and its clauses must not be put in code, test fixtures or these docs. Every example
>   here (`SQR-100`, `Q1`) is invented.

**`GET /purchasing/flowdown-profile`** — any authenticated user. Returns `{id, enabled, heading,
document_reference, body, version, updated_by, updated_at}`. A company that never saved the settings
gets the unsaved default: `enabled` false, `heading` "Supplier Quality Requirements",
`document_reference` / `body` null, `id` null, `version` 0.

**`PUT /purchasing/flowdown-profile`** — Admin / Manager / Quality.

- **Body, a full replacement:** `enabled` (required), `heading` (1–255 chars; omitted = "Supplier
  Quality Requirements"), `document_reference` (≤ 100 chars, for example `SQR-100 Rev C`), `body`
  (≤ 20,000 chars) and `version` (required, ≥ 0). An omitted or blank `document_reference` / `body`
  is stored as null, so a client must send every field it means to keep.
- **Version compare-and-swap:** `version` must be the stored version, 0 before the first save (which
  creates the row at version 1). Anything else is **409** *"The quality flow-down settings were
  changed by someone else since you loaded them. Reload them and save again."* and nothing changes;
  so is a concurrent first save.
- **Audit:** one **required** `po_flowdown_profile` row (CREATE on the first save, then UPDATE with
  old and new values and versions). If it cannot be written nothing is saved: **503**. A save that
  changes nothing returns the row with no version bump and no audit row.
- **Effect:** every DRAFT purchase order prints the new settings at once; no PO that has left draft
  changes.

**`GET /purchasing/quality-clauses`** — any authenticated user. The catalog in print order
(`sort_order`, then `code`), each `{id, code, title, body, default_selected, is_active, sort_order,
created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at}`. Retired clauses (`is_active` false) are included
only with `include_inactive=true`.

**`POST /purchasing/quality-clauses`** — Admin / Manager / Quality. Body: `code` (required, 1–20
characters after trimming), `title` (required, 1–255), `body` (≤ 20,000; blank = null),
`default_selected` (default false), `is_active` (default true), `sort_order` (0–1,000,000, default
0). A `code` already used in the company **ignoring case** is **409** *"A quality clause with code
'{code}' already exists. Codes are unique (ignoring case); edit that clause."* A retired clause
still owns its code: reactivate it rather than re-adding it. One **required** `po_quality_clause`
CREATE audit row (**503**, nothing saved, when it cannot be written).

**`PUT /purchasing/quality-clauses/{clause_id}`** — Admin / Manager / Quality. Only the fields sent
change: `title`, `body` (null clears it), `default_selected`, `is_active` (false retires the
clause, true reactivates it) and `sort_order`. An explicit `null` for `title`, `default_selected`,
`is_active` or `sort_order` is **422**. **`code` is immutable:** the body may carry it only when it
equals the stored code (after trimming, case included), which is accepted as an echo; any other
value is **409** *"A quality clause's code cannot be changed once it exists. Retire this clause
(is_active false) and add a new one under the new code."* **404** for a clause outside the active
company. A change writes one **required** UPDATE audit row (**503**); an edit that changes nothing
writes none. There is no `DELETE`.

**The PO's clause choice: `quality_clause_codes`.** Accepted on `POST /purchasing/purchase-orders`
(`POCreate`, through `create_purchase_order_command`) and `PUT /purchasing/purchase-orders/{po_id}`
(`POUpdate`).

- **Meaning.** `null` (or omitted on create) = the catalog's **active default-selected** clauses,
  resolved when the block is built. A list, `[]` included, is the buyer's choice; `[]` prints the
  block with no clauses. Every PO-creating door that names no codes stores `null`: MRP drafts and
  the auto-PO job, PO upload, the open-PO loader, and a Hank or AI-applier draft that names none.
- **Validation (422).** At most 200 codes, each 1–20 characters after trimming. Duplicates are
  dropped, first-seen order kept. Every code must name an **active** clause of the company, matched
  exactly as stored (case-sensitive); otherwise **422** *"Unknown or retired quality clause code(s):
  {codes}. Use the codes of active clauses from GET /purchasing/quality-clauses."* A code whose
  clause is later retired stays on the PO but no longer prints.
- **Frozen once the PO leaves draft (409).** On `PUT`, changing the value on a PO whose status is
  anything but `draft` (`pending_approval` and `approved` included) is **409** *"PO {po_number} has
  been issued; its quality flow-down is frozen."* Re-sending the stored value unchanged is a no-op
  on **any** status and is never re-validated, so an echoed record carrying a since-retired code
  does not 422. "Unchanged" is judged as a **set** after trimming and de-duplication: the same codes
  in another order are unchanged and the stored order is kept (clauses print in catalog order
  anyway). `null` and a list, even `[]`, are always different. On a draft, an explicit `null` returns the PO to the catalog defaults. The check runs
  before the lines or any other field is written, so a refusal leaves the PO untouched. It reads the
  status before the request's own `status` change, so one `PUT` can set the clauses and move a draft
  out of `draft`; the block then freezes with the new choice.
- **Audit.** The create's CREATE row and the `PUT`'s UPDATE row carry the column like any other;
  a changed choice is also listed in the `purchase_order_updated` event's `changed_fields`.
- **Response.** `POResponse` (create, `GET .../{po_id}`, `PUT`, `PUT .../supplier-confirmation`)
  carries `quality_clause_codes` (the stored value, raw: `null` = catalog defaults) and
  `flowdown_frozen` (true once the status is not `draft`; derived, never accepted from a request)
  and `flowdown_snapshot`: the block frozen when the PO left draft, exactly as stored, which is what
  the supplier was sent (`{"enabled": false}` when the flow-down was off at issue). It is `null` on
  a draft, including one moved back to draft (whose stored snapshot is stale until it re-freezes),
  and on a PO issued before migration `128`. It can differ from `quality_clause_codes`, because the
  freeze drops a clause retired before issue, so the PO detail of an issued PO shows the snapshot,
  never the stored codes. The list read (`GET /purchasing/purchase-orders`) carries none of the
  three.

**The freeze: one listener, every door.** `flowdown_snapshot` is written only by the
`before_insert` / `before_update` mapper listeners on `PurchaseOrder` in
`app/models/purchasing.py`: when a PO is inserted with a status other than `draft`, or its status
moves from `draft` to anything else. Every door that takes a PO out of draft (`POST .../send`, a
status `PUT` to `pending_approval` / `approved` / `cancelled`, an accepted document-delivery send,
the reviewed-import path, the MRP auto-PO job, PO upload, the open-PO loader) flushes through that
mapper, so none carries a freeze call of its own. The listener computes the block from the
company's current settings, its active clauses and the PO's `quality_clause_codes`, with Core
selects on the flush connection scoped to the PO's company. A disabled or missing profile freezes
`{"enabled": false}`. A PO moved back to `draft` (allowed from `pending_approval` / `approved`) prints
live again and re-freezes when it next leaves draft. Nothing back-fills a snapshot. `POST
.../send` takes the PO's row lock before it judges the status (`_live_po_or_404(..., lock=True)`),
so a concurrent `PUT` of the clause choice lands wholly before or after the send and the frozen
block always matches the stored codes.

**The issue is in the audit chain as a digest.** The `purchase_order` STATUS_CHANGE row written
when a PO leaves `draft` through `POST .../send`, through an accepted document-delivery send, or
through the reviewed-import flip (`create_purchase_order_command` with `ready_for_receiving`)
carries `extra_data.flowdown_snapshot_sha256`: the SHA-256 (hex) of
`json.dumps(snapshot, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))` encoded as UTF-8, computed by
`po_flowdown_service.flowdown_snapshot_sha256` (`null` if there is no snapshot). The block itself
is not copied into the audit row. To prove what a PO was issued with, hash its `flowdown_snapshot`
the same way and compare it with that row, whose integrity the tamper-evident chain covers. A send
from `approved` carries no digest: that PO froze when it left draft, through the status `PUT`,
whose `purchase_order` UPDATE row records the changed columns, `flowdown_snapshot` among them.

**What prints: `PurchaseOrderPrintData.quality_flowdown`.** `GET
/print/purchase-orders/{po_id}/print-data` (any authenticated user) carries the block, or `null`
for none:

| PO | `quality_flowdown` |
|---|---|
| `draft` | The **live** block from today's settings and active catalog and the PO's choice; `null` while the flow-down is disabled |
| Left draft, with a snapshot | The **snapshot** frozen when it left draft; `null` when that snapshot is `{"enabled": false}` |
| Left draft, no snapshot (issued before migration `128`) | `null`: no block, and none is ever back-filled, because the supplier was never sent one |

The block is `{enabled: true, heading, document_reference, body, clauses: [{code, title, body}]}`,
clauses in `sort_order` then `code` order, only active ones that are selected (or default-selected
when the choice is `null`). The browser print (`PrintPurchaseOrder`) renders it after the totals and
before the notes as React text: heading, *Reference: …*, the body split into paragraphs on blank
lines, then each clause as "code — title" with its text.

**The emailed PDF.** The purchase-order email (`POST /document-deliveries/preview`, then `POST
/document-deliveries/{id}/send`) attaches `build_purchase_order_document`, rendered from the same
print data, so it carries the same block in the same place. Every value goes through `pdf_escape`
at the reportlab sink: clause text is stored verbatim and routinely contains `<`, `>` and `&`. The
delivery fingerprint covers the print data's `quality_flowdown`, so editing the settings or a
clause after previewing a draft PO's email makes the send **409** *"The document changed after this
PDF was prepared. Create a fresh preview before sending."* The fingerprint deliberately ignores the
`flowdown_snapshot` column: the accepted send's own move to `sent` writes it, and counting it would
turn an identical PDF into a new send. That move freezes the block the email carried.

**Credentials and agents.** The three writes are role-gated only: an **API token** is not refused,
unlike the Approved Supplier List writes above. Owner decision 2026-11-20: a full API token of an
Admin, Manager or Quality user may save the settings and edit clauses; read-only and AI-external
tokens are refused by their own gates (the read-only gate, and for an AI-external token also the AI-egress gate); the write is attributed to the token's bound user with
`extra_data.credential`. All five routes are
MCP tools (`get_po_flowdown_profile`, `update_po_flowdown_profile`, `list_po_quality_clauses`,
`create_po_quality_clause`, `update_po_quality_clause`); the two reads are in the read-only listing
and none is on the AI-external allowlist. See `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Purchasing.

### Supplier Scorecards, Audits & Approved Supplier List

`app/api/endpoints/supplier_scorecards.py`, mounted at `/supplier-scorecards`.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/dashboard` | Avg score, below-threshold, audits/reviews due, top & worst performer | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/ranking` | Vendors ranked by latest overall score | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/vendor/{vendor_id}/history` | One vendor's scorecards over time (a soft-deleted vendor's history still reads — see note) | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/` | List scorecards (`skip`/`limit` 1…5000) | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/{id}` | Scorecard detail | Yes |
| POST | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/` | Create scorecard | Admin / Manager |
| PUT | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/{id}` | Update scorecard | Admin / Manager |
| POST | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/calculate/{vendor_id}` | Auto-calculate from PO / receipt / NCR data | Admin / Manager |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-audits/due-soon` | Audits due within `days` (1…365, default 30) | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-audits/` | List supplier audits | Yes |
| POST | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-audits/` | Create supplier audit | Admin / Manager |
| PUT | `/supplier-scorecards/supplier-audits/{id}` | Update supplier audit | Admin / Manager |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/approved-suppliers/` | List **legacy** ASL entries | Yes |
| GET | `/supplier-scorecards/approved-suppliers/{id}` | **Legacy** ASL entry detail | Yes |
| POST | `/supplier-scorecards/approved-suppliers/` | Create a **legacy** ASL entry — **409** on a soft-deleted vendor (see note). Not an MCP tool | Admin / Manager; **403** for an API token |
| PUT | `/supplier-scorecards/approved-suppliers/{id}` | Update a **legacy** ASL entry — **409** on `approval_status` / `approved_date` / `certifications_verified` while the vendor is soft-deleted (see note). Not an MCP tool | Admin / Manager; **403** for an API token |

> **The Approved Supplier List now lives on the vendor record** (migration `123`; see Purchasing →
> *Approved Supplier List on the vendor record*). The four `approved-suppliers` routes above and the
> `approved_supplier_list` table behind them are unchanged and kept as read-only history in practice:
> the Supplier Scorecards page no longer reads or writes them, and `GET
> .../supplier-scorecards/dashboard` → `reviews_due` now counts vendors whose ASL re-evaluation is
> overdue or due within 30 days (Approved / Conditional / Customer Directed, live and active) instead
> of legacy rows' `next_review_date`. The notes below describe those legacy routes.

> ⚠️ **`POST .../calculate/{vendor_id}` was returning 500 in production, for two reasons.** The
> `SupplierScorecard` insert omitted `TenantMixin`'s NOT NULL `company_id` — but the handler never
> reached it, because `calculate_overall()` runs on the in-memory object *before* the flush, where
> the four weight **column** defaults are still `None` (`float * None`). `POST
> /supplier-scorecards/` never hit that, because `ScorecardCreate` carries the same values as
> **schema** defaults. Both are fixed, and the weights used in the arithmetic are now stated
> explicitly so they are the weights that get stored.
>
> **`PUT .../supplier-scorecards/{id}` was the second call site of the same crash.** Every numeric
> field on `ScorecardUpdate` is `Optional`, and `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` **keeps** an
> explicitly-sent `null`, so `{"quality_weight": null}` reached `calculate_overall` and 500'd. An
> explicit `null` on any numeric field is now refused at parse time with a **422** naming the field;
> *omitting* the field is unchanged (leaves the stored value), and nullable text fields
> (`notes`, `action_items`) may still be nulled.

> **Fifteen of sixteen handlers were reaching outside the caller's tenant.** Three of them were
> **cross-tenant writes** — `PUT` on scorecard, supplier audit and ASL entry each resolved their row
> by bare id (the scorecard handler even took a `company_id` dependency and never used it), so
> guessing an integer was enough to rewrite another company's AS9100D supplier evaluation, fail
> their audit, or set their approved supplier to `removed`. The reads (dashboard, ranking, both
> lists, due-soon, both detail reads) took no company argument at all, and the three creates stamped
> `company_id` correctly but resolved `vendor_id` with no predicate — and every serializer renders
> `vendor.name` / `vendor.code` straight back, so a create doubled as a read of the foreign
> supplier. All are scoped; a foreign `vendor_id`, scorecard, audit or ASL id answers a flat **404**
> with the same detail a genuinely missing id gets.
>
> **Expect the dashboard and ranking numbers to drop on a multi-company install** — they were
> summing every tenant.

> **`vendor_name` / `vendor_code` read as `null` for a legacy cross-tenant row.** Same shape as
> maintenance above: the create guards stop new mis-tenanted rows but do nothing about rows written
> before them, and the `vendor` relationship (plus the `joinedload` on it) carries no predicate.
> The serializers now null both fields when the vendor's `company_id` differs; `vendor_id` stays
> visible so the row can be corrected. Audit-row identifiers fall back to `vendor #{id}` in the same
> case, so recording an update can never become the thing that discloses the foreign supplier's
> code. See the pre-deploy detection SQL in `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Supplier Scorecards.

> **Soft-deleted vendors: only the *approval* refuses; every record still writes and reads.** This
> router draws one line, and it is records-vs-permissions rather than reads-vs-writes:
>
> - **Approved Supplier List — refused (409).** The ASL is not a history of who the shop bought
>   from, it is the AS9100D 8.4 statement of who the shop is **permitted** to buy from right now, so
>   a removed supplier must not appear on it. Both doors are closed: `POST /approved-suppliers/`
>   resolves through `_live_vendor_for_approval`, and `PUT /approved-suppliers/{asl_id}` — which
>   resolves by ASL id and never re-reads `vendor_id` — refuses the three fields that *constitute* an
>   approval (`approval_status`, `approved_date`, `certifications_verified`) when the vendor is
>   deleted. The refusal is **per field, not per row**: `notes`, `scope` and the review cadence stay
>   editable, so an entry whose vendor is gone does not freeze with nothing able to unfreeze it. (That
>   clause used to read *"no restore screen to unfreeze it"* — the per-field carve-out was designed
>   around the absence of one. The carve-out stays, on its own merits: an ASL row should not freeze
>   solid just because a restore is a step away.)
>   **There is now a restore screen** (Purchasing → Vendors → **Deleted**), and it changes nothing
>   about this refusal except who can clear it without an API call. Restoring the vendor lifts the
>   **409** — but it re-approves nothing: restore puts back the vendor's *pre-delete* `is_active`, so a
>   supplier that was deactivated before it was deleted comes back **inactive**, and the ASL entry's
>   `approval_status` is whatever it was left at. Re-approving is still a deliberate, separately
>   audited act on both records. See Purchasing → *Restoring a vendor returns the record, not the
>   approval*.
> - **Scorecards and supplier audits — still allowed, on purpose.** `POST /supplier-scorecards/`,
>   `POST .../calculate/{vendor_id}`, `POST /supplier-audits/` and `PUT /supplier-audits/{id}`
>   resolve through the tenancy-only `_vendor_in_company` and deliberately accept a soft-deleted
>   vendor. Removing a supplier is very often the *outcome* of the audit finding or the closing
>   scorecard, and AS9100D 8.4 expects that record — gating these would make the evaluation that
>   documents the removal the one evaluation that can never be filed. `calculate` is the clearest
>   case: every input it reads is historical and bounded by an explicit `period_start`/`period_end`,
>   so it writes a truthful account of a period during which the vendor *was* a supplier.
> - **Reads — unchanged.** `GET .../vendor/{vendor_id}/history` still returns a removed supplier's
>   scorecards, and the lists, details and ranking deliberately keep rendering a deleted vendor's
>   `vendor_name` / `vendor_code` / `vendor_id` (`_same_tenant_vendor` tests tenancy, not soft
>   delete). 404-ing the by-vendor history while `GET /supplier-scorecards/supplier-scorecards/
>   ?vendor_id=` returns the very same rows would be a contradiction, not a protection.
>
> The accepted, known cost is that these pages are where a deleted vendor's id is still visible in
> the UI — which is exactly why the ASL **update** verb has to re-check rather than trusting that
> nobody can obtain the ids.

> **The ASL duplicate check stays install-wide on purpose.** `ApprovedSupplierList.vendor_id`
> carries a *global* unique constraint, so the check must mirror the constraint exactly or a miss
> becomes an `IntegrityError` 500 instead of the **400** "Vendor already has an ASL entry". It is
> unreachable across tenants now that the vendor is scoped first — a vendor belongs to exactly one
> company. ⚠️ One consequence worth knowing: a **legacy** ASL row owned by company B against
> company A's vendor permanently consumes that vendor's single global slot, and company A can
> neither see nor edit it. The detection SQL above finds these; correcting them is a data task.

> **Every state change writes a tamper-evident `audit_log` row** (invariant 2 — the router
> previously wrote none at all). Resource types: `supplier_scorecard` (`CREATE` on both the manual
> and the auto-calculate path — the latter carries `period_start` / `period_end` / `auto: true` in
> `extra_data` — and `UPDATE`), `supplier_audit` (`CREATE` / `UPDATE`) and `approved_supplier`
> (`CREATE` / `UPDATE`). Rows are logged **before** the terminal commit so they commit atomically
> with the change.

> ⚠️ **Known frontend gap, not fixed here:** `apiClient.calculateSupplierScorecard` (`api.ts`) posts
> `calculate/{vendorId}` with **no body** while the handler requires `period_start` / `period_end`,
> so any UI call would 422 before reaching the handler — and nothing in `SupplierScorecards.tsx`
> calls it today.

### PO Upload (AI document extraction)

Upload a vendor PO or quote document, AI-extract its data for human review, then create the PO
from the reviewed result (`app/api/endpoints/po_upload.py`, mounted at `/po-upload`). Extraction
runs through the shared `run_llm_task` pipeline (prompt `po_extraction` 1.0.0,
`feature="po_upload"`, one tenant-scoped `ai_usage_events` row per call — telemetry, not audit)
and is covered by the per-company `allow_ai_egress` kill switch (see **Company (self-service)**
below).

All endpoints are stateless and **per-document** — there is no batch endpoint. The Upload PO
page's multi-file batch mode is pure client-side orchestration: one `upload-po` / `upload-quote`
call per file (at most 2 concurrent) and one `create-from-upload` call per reviewed document.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| POST | `/po-upload/upload-po` | Upload a PO document (`.pdf`/`.doc`/`.docx`, 10 MB cap; over it **413** before any work — this was a **400** before 2026-11-09) — AI-extracts data for review before commit | Yes |
| POST | `/po-upload/upload-quote` | Upload a vendor quote document (same types and 10 MB / **413** cap) — AI-extracts data to build a PO | Yes |
| POST | `/po-upload/upload-invoice` | Legacy alias of `upload-quote` (same extraction behavior) | Yes |
| POST | `/po-upload/create-from-upload` | Create the PO from the reviewed extraction — can create the vendor and missing parts. Part-number matching is **case-insensitive** and ignores surrounding whitespace: the same number repeated across lines / `create_parts` creates the part **once** (stored as the first occurrence's stripped form) and attaches every matching line to it; an active part already holding the number is reused, and a line with no `part_id` resolves by part number to an existing active part even when it isn't in `create_parts`. **400** if `line_items` is empty, the PO number already exists, a supplied `vendor_id` / line `part_id` doesn't exist in the active company **or is soft-deleted**, a line's part number matches no active part and isn't in `create_parts`, or a new part's number belongs to a **soft-deleted** part (restore it via `POST /parts/{id}/restore` or use a different number). **409** when the vendor is Disqualified on the Approved Supplier List, checked before any part is created; otherwise the response's `supplier_approval_warnings` lists the advisory ASL warnings, which the create audit row also records (see Purchasing → *Approved Supplier List on the vendor record*) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/po-upload/pdf/{path}` | Serve the uploaded source document for preview (`s3://` refs and local paths) | Yes |
| GET | `/po-upload/search-parts` | Part typeahead for extraction-review matching. `q` matches **part number, name, description, and customer part number** — every whitespace-separated term must appear, then results are ranked by similar-word score so a query like `raw material` surfaces `A36 Raw Material Sheet`. `limit` **1–50**, default 10 | Yes |
| GET | `/po-upload/search-vendors` | Vendor typeahead for extraction-review matching (`q`, `limit` **1–50**, default 10) — active, **non-soft-deleted** vendors only | Yes |

> **A partly read PDF is flagged in `validation_issues` (2026-11-09).** When the extractor read only
> part of an uploaded PDF (see [Document Text Extraction Limits](#document-text-extraction-limits)), each
> gap becomes an entry such as
> `{"field": "document_content", "severity": "warning", "code": "OCR_PARTIAL", "message": "Only the first 30 of 120 scanned pages were read."}`.
> `code` is `OCR_PARTIAL` when scanned pages were skipped or cut short, and `TEXT_PARTIAL` when the
> text layer was cut short. On a normal extraction these entries come before the field checks; only
> the "PO number already exists" warning is listed ahead of them. The two low-confidence responses
> (no usable text, and an AI extraction error) list them after their `error` entry. Today these are
> the only `validation_issues` entries that carry a `code`; every other entry has just `field`,
> `severity` and `message`.

### Receiving & Inspection

Canonical material-receiving and incoming-inspection endpoints, all under `/receiving`.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/receiving/open-pos` | List POs available for receiving (sent/partial); each PO carries `order_date` / `required_date` / `expected_date` plus its open lines | Yes |
| GET | `/receiving/po/{po_id}` | Get full PO detail for receiving | Yes |
| POST | `/receiving/receive` | Receive material against a PO line (`lot_number` optional — auto-assigned when blank, see below). Optional `ownership` / `owner_customer_id` / `owner_vendor_id` for customer- or supplier-owned material, recorded on the receipt and carried to stock on dock-to-stock, inspection accept or a cleared hold (see [Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property)); each `/receiving/deliveries` line takes the same | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| POST | `/receiving/deliveries` | Atomically receive multiple lines with a stable request ID; identical retry returns the durable receipt, changed payload is refused. Certificate document IDs are validated against the PO line — every line's before the first line is received, so a bad certificate on any line is refused **422** `Delivery line N: …` with nothing posted. At that point the delivery takes its locks in the order a single receipt does (the receipt-number lock, the PO row, then the certificates in ascending id order), before it inserts anything and before the first audit row takes the audit-chain lock, so it holds no document lock that a document writer (row first, chain lock second) could deadlock against | Admin / Manager / Supervisor, plus receiving view/create permission |
| POST | `/receiving/certificates` | Upload a real PDF/PNG/JPEG (20 MB maximum), bound to `po_line_id`; optional `receipt_id` attaches it to an existing receipt. Linked certificate bytes cannot be deleted through the document endpoint | Admin / Manager / Supervisor, plus receiving view/create permission |
| GET | `/receiving/inspection-queue` | List receipts pending inspection (`days_back` optional, bounded 1–3650; **no date cutoff by default** — pending receipts never age out, so the list matches the `/stats` `pending_inspection` count) | Yes |
| GET | `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}` | Get receipt detail | Yes |
| PATCH | `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}` | Correct a mis-keyed receipt in place (new total `quantity_received` + optional traceability fields; required `reason`) — reconciles PO line / PO status / inventory. Guarded, see note | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| POST | `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/void` | Void (soft-delete) a receipt with full reversal of PO line / status / inventory; required `reason`. Terminal — no restore. Guarded, see note | Admin / Manager |
| POST | `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/clear-inspection` | **Clear an inspection hold placed by mistake** — non-destructive: keeps the receipt and its lot / heat / cert exactly as keyed, re-classifies it as dock-to-stock, posts the material into inventory, and drops it off the queue; required `reason`. PO line / PO status untouched. Guarded, see note | Admin / Manager / Quality / Supervisor |
| POST | `/receiving/inspect/{receipt_id}` | Complete inspection (accept/reject, auto-NCR on rejection) | Admin / Manager / Quality / Supervisor |
| GET | `/receiving/history` | Receiving history with inspection results (`days` **1–365**, default 30) | Yes |
| GET | `/receiving/stats` | Receiving statistics for dashboard (`days` **1–365**, default 30) | Yes |
| GET | `/receiving/locations` | Receivable inventory locations | Yes |
| POST | `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/print-label` | Manually (re)print the 4×6 thermal receiving label | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/receiving/print-profile` | Get the company ProxyBox print profile (key masked; **404** until created) | Admin |
| PUT | `/receiving/print-profile` | Create / update the print profile, incl. the `allow_print_egress` kill switch | Admin, signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |

> **Lot number (`lot_number`).** Optional on `POST /receiving/receive` (max 50 chars): when
> blank or omitted the server auto-assigns the receipt number (unique, company-scoped) as the
> lot, so `POReceipt.lot_number` is still always stored non-null and AS9100D lot traceability
> is preserved — supply the vendor's lot number when it is known. The receipt audit row and
> the inventory RECEIVE transaction both carry the effective (supplied or auto-assigned) lot.
>
> **Incoming-inspection default (`requires_inspection`).** On `POST /receiving/receive` the
> field defaults to **`false`** when omitted: the receipt is auto-accepted (dock-to-stock) and
> lands directly in inventory with **`inspection_status = not_required`**. No incoming
> inspection is performed on this path, so `inspection_method`, `inspected_by`, and
> `inspected_at` stay **null** — the record must not assert an inspection that never happened
> (AS9100D records integrity); the receiver and receipt time are still captured by `received_by`
> / `received_at`. Pass `true` to hold the lot in the inspection queue until
> `POST /receiving/inspect/{receipt_id}`, where it resolves to `passed` / `failed` / `partial`
> with a real inspector, method, and timestamp. The part master's `Part.requires_inspection`
> flag is **not** applied automatically — it is exposed on the `/receiving/open-pos` and
> `/receiving/po/{po_id}` line payloads, and the Receiving UI renders it as an amber advisory
> hint next to its "Requires Inspection" checkbox (which always starts unchecked) so the
> receiver can opt in deliberately.
>
> **What the receive form carries between lines (UI behaviour).** Receiving one delivery
> usually means receiving several PO lines back to back, so the Receiving page keeps the
> **shipment-level** fields filled as the receiver moves from line to line — packing slip #,
> carrier, tracking #, and location are identical for every line off one truck. The
> **material-level** fields are blanked for each newly selected line and never carry over:
> `lot_number`, `heat_number`, `cert_number`, `serial_numbers`, the CoC-attached flag, the
> line notes, `requires_inspection`, and the over-receipt approval. Lot, heat and cert are
> issued together per heat lot by the mill, so carrying a cert past the lot and heat it
> belongs to would record a certificate against material it does not cover; and the two
> checkboxes are approvals, whose whole meaning is that somebody ticked them for **this**
> receipt. The over-receipt checkbox is additionally *hidden* whenever the quantity fits the
> line, so a value carried over there would be invisible as well as unearned. This is a UI
> default only — the API accepts whatever the caller sends on every field.
>
> A receipt's **`inspection_status`** (returned by `/receiving/history` and
> `/receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}`) is one of: **`not_required`** (dock-to-stock — accepted
> without inspection; no inspector/method/time — set either by receiving with the flag off, or by
> `POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/clear-inspection` waiving a hold placed by mistake),
> `pending` (awaiting inspection in the queue),
> `passed`, `failed`, or `partial` (recorded by `/receiving/inspect/{receipt_id}`). The History
> view badges `not_required` as a neutral **"Not Required"**, visually distinct from a green
> **"Passed"** (which means a real incoming inspection passed). Vendor acceptance-rate analytics
> count `not_required` as **accepted** (dock-to-stock material enters stock without rejection),
> so acceptance rates are unaffected. Receipts auto-accepted before this change keep their
> prior values (they may still read `passed` / `visual`) — historical quality records are
> corrected forward, not rewritten.

> **Correcting or voiding a receipt (`POReceipt` now `SoftDeleteMixin`).** A mis-keyed receipt is
> fixed with **`PATCH /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}`** (correct in place) or reversed entirely with
> **`POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/void`** (soft-delete). Both **require a non-blank `reason`**
> (recorded on the tamper-evident `audit_log`) and are **fully audited**; live reads now filter
> `is_deleted == false`. If the receipt itself is correct and only the **"requires inspection" box was
> ticked by mistake**, neither of these is the right verb — see
> **`POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/clear-inspection`** in the note below, which keeps the
> receipt exactly as keyed.
>
> - **Correct** — body: `quantity_received` (the **new TOTAL** received, **> 0** — not a delta) plus
>   optional `lot_number` / `heat_number` / `cert_number` / `serial_numbers` / `notes`, and the
>   required `reason`. Gate **Admin / Manager / Supervisor** (the receive-tier — the same roles that
>   `POST /receiving/receive` and post inventory adjustments). Response: the updated `ReceiptResponse`.
>   A changed `heat_number` / `cert_number` is stored trimmed (blank → NULL) and, on a dock-to-stock
>   or cleared-hold receipt, carried onto the stock row it placed under the rule in
>   [Heat number and mill cert on stock rows](#heat-number-and-mill-cert-on-stock-rows).
> - **Void** — body: `reason` only. Gate **Admin / Manager** (tighter — void is delete authority).
>   **Terminal: there is no restore** — to redo, re-receive.
>
> **What gets reconciled (both paths).** All refusal guards run **before any mutation**, so a refusal
> never leaves the receipt half-reconciled:
> - **PO line** — `quantity_received` is rolled to match (a void drops it to 0); the line's `is_closed`
>   is recomputed, so a void can **reopen** a previously-closed line.
> - **PO status** — recomputed from all lines: `received` (all closed) → `partial` (any received) →
>   back to **`sent`** when nothing is left received (the pre-receipt open state). A status move is
>   itself audited (`log_status_change`).
> - **Inventory (dock-to-stock receipts only)** — a **signed compensating `InventoryTransaction`
>   `ADJUST`** is appended (`reason_code` `RECEIPT_CORRECTION` / `RECEIPT_VOID`) to move on-hand by the
>   delta. **AS9100D records integrity: the historical `RECEIVE` transaction is never mutated or
>   deleted** — reversal is always a new, signed compensating row (like a manual inventory adjustment).
>   `PENDING_INSPECTION` receipts placed no stock, so nothing is adjusted there. The stock row adjusted
>   is the exact one the receipt placed, found through its `RECEIVE` ledger row (migration `129`; see
>   [Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property)); a legacy receipt
>   with no ledger link falls back to part / location / lot only when exactly one row matches, else
>   **409**.
>
> **State model — allowed only before inspection / while unconsumed.** A receipt is correctable/voidable
> only while it is **`pending`** (awaiting inspection) or **`not_required`** (dock-to-stock accepted).
> Refusals (all with actionable `detail`):
> - already **inspected** (`passed` / `failed` / `partial`) → **409** — handle via NCR / inventory
>   adjustment, not here.
> - **lot change after stock was placed** (dock-to-stock) → **400** — void and re-receive instead.
> - received stock for the lot **already allocated or consumed** (would drive `quantity_available`
>   negative) → **409** — make an inventory adjustment instead.
> - the reversal would drive the PO line's received total **negative** → **409**.
> - the receipt's PO line no longer exists (orphaned) → **400** (never a 500).
> - a cross-tenant / missing / already-voided receipt → **404**.

> **Clearing an inspection hold placed by mistake (`POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/clear-inspection`).**
> The third post-receipt verb, and the **non-destructive** one. Receiving ticks "Requires Inspection"
> on a line that never needed it; the lot then sits in the inspection queue with no honest way out —
> before this endpoint the **only** exit was `void`, which un-receives the material entirely and forces
> the whole receipt to be re-keyed. This verb is the missing *"the box was checked by mistake"*
> alternative: it re-classifies the receipt as the dock-to-stock receipt it should have been.
>
> - **Body** — `{ "reason": "<why the hold is being cleared>" }` (`ReceiptClearInspectionRequest`).
>   Required, **1–500 chars**, and **non-blank after trimming** (whitespace-only → **422**); the value
>   is stored stripped. Same validator as `ReceiptVoidRequest`. Waiving an AS9100D inspection hold must
>   always carry a stated justification.
> - **Response** — **200** with the updated `ReceiptResponse` (the same schema `PATCH .../{id}` returns).
> - **Gate** — **Admin / Manager / Quality / Supervisor**, i.e. **exactly the role list on
>   `POST /receiving/inspect/{receipt_id}`**, and the match is deliberate. An earlier draft excluded
>   Supervisor on a segregation-of-duties argument (the receive tier that ticks the box should not
>   waive it alone); the owner overruled it, because excluding Supervisor closed the **honest** exit
>   while leaving the **dishonest** one open. A supervisor with a mis-ticked receipt and no manager on
>   site did not leave it on the queue — they pushed it through **Inspect → Visual → Pass**, which
>   writes a named inspector and a timestamp for an inspection that never happened. That is a
>   *fabricated* quality record, and exactly the AS9100D records-integrity defect PR #127 fixed in
>   code, only performed by a human. Widening the gate is therefore a **records-integrity
>   improvement, not a convenience concession**: whoever can decide a lot *passes* can decide it never
>   needed inspecting, and between the two records that tier can already produce, the reasoned,
>   attributed, hash-chained waiver is the strictly more truthful one. Keep the two lists in lockstep
>   — if one moves, the other moves, or the dishonest exit reopens. **Void** stays tighter
>   (Admin / Manager) because that is *delete* authority, a different question.
>   See [docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md) → Receiving.
>
> **What it does** (mirrors the dock-to-stock leg of `POST /receiving/receive`; all guards run
> **before any mutation**, so a refusal leaves the receipt untouched):
> - `requires_inspection` → **`false`**, `status` → **`accepted`**, `inspection_status` →
>   **`not_required`**, `quantity_accepted` → `quantity_received`.
> - **`inspection_method` / `inspected_by` / `inspected_at` stay `null`**, and `inspection_status` is
>   `not_required` and **never `passed`** — no incoming inspection happened, so the record must not
>   assert one (the same AS9100D records-integrity rule as the dock-to-stock receive path, above).
> - The material is posted into inventory with **exactly the key `POST /receiving/receive` uses**
>   (part, `location.code` or the `RECV-01` default, receipt lot; unit cost from the PO line, supplier
>   from the PO vendor, reference = the receipt number), so a later **Correct** or **Void** re-finds
>   that same `InventoryItem` row to reverse it. A `RECEIVE` `InventoryTransaction`
>   (`reference_type="po_receipt"`) is appended, with its own audit rows.
> - The receipt leaves the inspection queue as a consequence of the status move — `/receiving/inspection-queue`
>   selects `status = pending_inspection` only. There is **no separate dismissal**.
> - **The PO line and PO status are deliberately NOT touched** — `po_line.quantity_received`,
>   `po_line.is_closed` and `po.status` were all advanced when the receipt was created (a
>   `pending_inspection` receipt already counts as *received*; only the inventory posting waits on
>   inspection). No quantity is moving, so this verb does **not** run the correct/void reconciler.
> - **The receipt stays correctable and voidable afterwards.** Clearing leaves it at
>   `inspection_status = not_required`, which is inside the correct/void state model above (only
>   `passed` / `failed` / `partial` are refused). And because `requires_inspection` flipped to
>   `false`, the correct/void reconciler now correctly sees the stock as **placed** and reverses it —
>   that flag is the reconciler's `inventory_placed` discriminator, so flipping it in the same breath
>   as the posting is what keeps a later Correct or Void from stranding the material on hand.
> - **The waiver is stamped on the receipt itself**, not only in `audit_log`: a machine-composed line
>   is **appended** to `receipt.notes` — `[YYYY-MM-DD] Inspection hold cleared by <user> (no incoming
>   inspection performed): <reason>` — preserving whatever receiving typed. It is **not** written to
>   `inspection_notes`, which would imply inspection activity. This exists because a cleared receipt is
>   otherwise byte-indistinguishable from one that was dock-to-stock from the first keystroke, and
>   `GET /audit/` is **Admin/Manager only** — Quality and Supervisor, two of the four roles authorized
>   to waive, could not read their own decision back.
> - The `RECEIVE` ledger row carries `reason_code="INSPECTION_HOLD_CLEARED"` and a note naming the
>   reason, so **Warehouse → Inventory → Stock Movements** (the app's only rendering of
>   `inventory_transactions`) shows *why* the material entered stock. Mirrors the
>   `RECEIPT_VOID` / `RECEIPT_CORRECTION` stamping the correct/void reconciler already does.
> - Audited as a **status change** on `receipt` (`pending_inspection` → `accepted`) with the reason in
>   both the description and `extra_data` (alongside `part_requires_inspection`, the part master's
>   advisory flag at the time of the waiver — recorded, never enforced, since it defaults true on
>   essentially every part). Emits the operational event **`receipt_inspection_cleared`**
>   (`source_module="purchasing"`, `entity_type="po_receipt"`, severity `medium`, payload
>   `receipt_number` / `po_id` / `po_number` / `po_line_id` / `part_id` / `quantity_received` /
>   `reason` / `part_requires_inspection`), which fans out the catalog entry
>   **`receipt.inspection_cleared`** — in-app to **Manager + Quality**, exactly like `receipt.voided`
>   and `receipt.corrected`. Waiving a hold is the most quality-relevant of the three post-receipt
>   verbs, so it is deliberately not the silent one.
> - **The status guard is read under a row lock** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the receipt). `POReceipt`
>   has no `version` column, and `inventory_items` has no unique constraint on
>   (company, part, location, lot) — unlocked, two concurrent clears would both pass the guard and
>   both post, doubling the lot's on-hand with only half of it reversible by a later Correct/Void.
>
> **Errors:**
> - **404** `"Receipt not found"` — missing, cross-tenant, or already-voided (soft-deleted).
> - **409** `"Receipt is not pending inspection"` — any other status. This is **also the replay
>   guard**: a second call finds the receipt already `accepted` and refuses, so stock can never be
>   posted twice. It subsumes the already-inspected case (an inspected receipt is `accepted` or
>   `rejected`), which is why this verb does not reuse the correct/void loader — that loader's
>   "already been inspected" 409 would be the wrong message here, and an already-*cleared* receipt
>   would slip past it entirely.
> - **400** `"Receipt's PO line no longer exists, so the inspection hold cannot be cleared here.
>   Contact an administrator to repair the receipt record."` — orphaned `po_line`, or a `po_line`
>   whose `purchase_order` is gone: there is no part / unit price / vendor context to post inventory
>   with. Never a 500. (Such rows are deliberately still surfaced by `/receiving/inspection-queue`
>   with `null` context fields so they can be found.)
>
> **Which of the three post-receipt verbs to reach for:**
>
> | Situation | Verb | Effect on the receipt | Effect on inventory | Gate |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | Quantity / lot / heat / cert was **keyed wrong** | `PATCH /receiving/receipt/{id}` (**Correct**) | Edited in place, kept | Signed compensating `ADJUST` for the delta (dock-to-stock only) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
> | The receipt **should not exist** (wrong PO line, wrong part, never arrived) | `POST /receiving/receipt/{id}/void` (**Void**) | Soft-deleted, **terminal — re-key to redo** | Full reversal via signed compensating `ADJUST` | Admin / Manager |
> | The receipt is **right**; only the **"requires inspection" box was a mis-click** | `POST /receiving/receipt/{id}/clear-inspection` (**Clear hold**) | Kept **exactly as keyed**, re-classified dock-to-stock | Material **posted in** (it never was) | Admin / Manager / Quality / Supervisor |
>
> A receipt genuinely needing inspection is still resolved by `POST /receiving/inspect/{receipt_id}`,
> which records a real inspector, method, and timestamp. Clearing the hold is **not** an inspection
> outcome and must not be used as a shortcut for one.
>
> **Ordering matters, and the UI says so:** while a receipt sits at `pending_inspection` its **lot
> number is still correctable in place**. Clearing the hold posts the stock, which flips
> `requires_inspection` to `false` — and `PATCH /receiving/receipt/{id}` then refuses a lot change
> ("Lot number cannot be changed after stock has been received into inventory"). So fix a mis-keyed
> lot **before** clearing the hold; afterwards the only route is void + re-key.
>
> **This is still not a two-person control, and must not be described as one.** Every role that can
> clear a hold can also place one (Admin / Manager / Supervisor hold `/receive`) or resolve it by
> inspection, so anyone can waive a hold they set themselves. What the endpoint guarantees is
> *attribution*, not separation: a non-blank reason, a named user, a tamper-evident `audit_log` status
> change, a stamp on `receipt.notes` and on the ledger row, and a notification to Manager + Quality.
> The control here is that the waiver is **visible and truthful**, never that a second person
> authorised it.

> **Deleting an open PO from the Receiving page (`DELETE /purchasing/purchase-orders/{po_id}`).**
> Each card in the Receive tab's open-PO list (`GET /receiving/open-pos`) carries a delete control,
> wired to the **existing Purchasing endpoint** — there is no receiving-specific verb, and nothing
> about the endpoint's behaviour changed. It is surfaced here because the dock is where a duplicate,
> cancelled or wrong-vendor PO is actually noticed, and until now the receiver had to leave for the
> Purchasing page to get rid of it.
>
> - **Gate — Admin / Manager** (`require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER])`): the same tier as receipt **void**,
>   and deliberately **tighter than the receiving role set** — receive / correct / clear-hold all
>   include Supervisor, this does not. A Supervisor sees no delete control and the card renders
>   exactly as it did before.
> - **Soft delete** (compliance invariant #3): the PO is marked `is_deleted` / `deleted_at` /
>   `deleted_by`, drops out of `/receiving/open-pos` and every Purchasing list, and is **restorable**
>   by Admin / Manager via `POST /purchasing/purchase-orders/{po_id}/restore`. Both directions write a
>   tamper-evident `audit_log` row (`log_delete` with `soft_delete=true`; `log_update` with
>   `action="restore"`). Nothing is destroyed.
>   **The restore is now reachable from a screen** — Purchasing → Purchase Orders → **Deleted**
>   (`GET /purchasing/purchase-orders?deleted_only=true`, documented under Purchasing above), which
>   is the only read that can see a soft-deleted PO. That view is open to anyone who can read POs;
>   the **Restore** button on its rows is Admin / Manager, mirroring `require_role` on the verb.
>   **The receiving confirm dialog says exactly that** ("This is reversible: an admin or manager can
>   restore it from Purchasing → Purchase Orders → Deleted"), and `Receiving.deletePO.test.tsx` pins
>   both halves of that wording — the promise *and* the "an admin or manager", not "you" — so the
>   copy cannot drift back either way. Naming the destination is the load-bearing part: this copy
>   previously said there was **no restore button in the app** and to treat the delete as one-way,
>   which was true only while nothing called `restorePurchaseOrder`. A reversal nobody can find is
>   not a reversal, and a promise with no route is how that copy became false in the first place.
>   *Vendor* deletes now have a screen of their own too, built to the same shape — Purchasing →
>   **Vendors** → **Deleted** (`GET /purchasing/vendors?deleted_only=true`); see the Purchasing note
>   above. One difference worth knowing before you promise anything: a **vendor** restore puts back
>   the `is_active` it had when it was deleted, so a supplier that had been switched off comes back
>   switched off.
> - **Refused 400 once any line has received material** (`quantity_received > 0`) —
>   *"Cannot delete purchase order &lt;po&gt;: it has received material. Void the receipt(s) first,
>   then delete."* **This is the refusal a warehouse user will actually hit**, and from *this* surface
>   it means a **partially** received PO: `/receiving/open-pos` lists `sent` / `partial` only, so a
>   fully-received PO has already left the list and its delete control with it. The sequence is worth
>   stating:
>
>   1. **Void every receipt** logged against the PO — `POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/void`
>      (Admin / Manager, required `reason`). A void reconciles the receipt down to zero, which is
>      what walks `po_line.quantity_received` back down, reopens `po_line.is_closed`, and rolls
>      `po.status` back to `sent` once nothing on the PO is left received — so a fully-voided PO
>      reappears in the open-PO list, where the delete control is.
>   2. With **no** line left at `quantity_received > 0`, the delete is accepted.
>
>   Two limits make step 1 unavailable for real deliveries, which is the point: **void is terminal**
>   (there is no receipt restore — to redo, re-receive) and it is **refused 409 once the receipt has
>   been inspected** (`passed` / `failed` / `partial`). So a PO whose material genuinely arrived and
>   was inspected **cannot be cleared for deletion this way, and should not be** — that receipt is the
>   quality record of a real delivery. Close or cancel the PO instead. Voiding truthful receipts
>   purely to make a PO deletable destroys traceability for material that is physically on the shelf.
>
>   **Which is why the receiving UI does not offer the control on a `partial` card at all.** The
>   endpoint's guard is unchanged and still authoritative, but on *this* surface `po.status ==
>   "partial"` is a perfect predictor of the 400 — the list carries `sent` / `partial` only, and the
>   backend sets `partial` on exactly the `quantity_received > 0` condition the delete refuses on.
>   So `Receiving.tsx` renders the trash icon only when `canDeletePO && po.status !== 'partial'`: a
>   button that can only ever fail is worse than no button, and here the failure hands back advice
>   ("void the receipt(s) first") that is *correct for a bogus receipt and destructive for a real
>   delivery*. The 400 stays reachable for the race (a PO that goes `partial` between list load and
>   confirm), and the confirm dialog carries the counter-guidance the server's `detail` cannot:
>   *"If the material genuinely arrived, do NOT void its receipt: close or cancel the PO in
>   Purchasing instead."* From Purchasing, which lists every status, the control is role-gated only
>   and the 400 is the normal teacher.
> - A **double delete** returns **400** (*"Purchase order &lt;po&gt; is already deleted"*); a missing
>   or cross-tenant PO returns **404**.
>
> This is **not** a fourth post-receipt verb: Correct / Void / Clear-hold fix something already
> received, while this removes a PO that should not be received against at all. See
> Purchasing → *Vendor / PO soft-delete + restore* for the endpoint's own note.

> **Thermal receiving-label printing (ProxyBox / WHTP203e).** A 4×6 PDF (part / rev /
> qty / lot / Code128, CRITICAL banner for critical parts) is rendered, stored as a
> `Document` (`RECEIVING_LABEL`, linked via `POReceipt.label_document_id`), and sent to
> a ProxyBox Zero bridge. See [docs/THERMAL_LABEL_PRINTING.md](THERMAL_LABEL_PRINTING.md).
>
> - **`POST /receiving/receipt/{receipt_id}/print-label`** — body (optional)
>   `{ "copies": <1–20> }` overrides the profile default. Response:
>   `{ receipt_id, receipt_number, label_document_id, printed, message }`. Errors:
>   **409** when `allow_print_egress` is OFF / the profile is incomplete, **404** for a
>   missing or cross-tenant receipt, **502** on a ProxyBox / printer failure (the label
>   `Document` is still persisted, so a later reprint works). Same role gate as
>   `POST /receiving/receive` (Admin / Manager / Supervisor).
> - **`PUT /receiving/print-profile`** — fields: `proxybox_base_url` (full base incl.
>   `/api/v1`), `proxybox_target`, `api_key` (**write-only**, Fernet-encrypted at rest,
>   never returned — sending it rotates the stored key), `default_paper_size`,
>   `default_copies` (1–20), `auto_print_on_receipt`, `allow_print_egress`, `is_active`.
>   Omitted fields are left unchanged. Read responses expose only `api_key_last4` /
>   `has_api_key`; secrets never appear in audit / event payloads. Flipping
>   `allow_print_egress` (default OFF) is recorded as a **status change** on the
>   tamper-evident audit trail. The route is the switch's only writer, so the **whole**
>   route refuses any API token **403** before reading or writing anything, and it is not an
>   MCP tool — see [Egress kill switches are a person's judgment](#egress-kill-switches-are-a-persons-judgment).
>
> Auto-print on receipt is a separate, best-effort ARQ job enqueued by
> `POST /receiving/receive` after commit; it no-ops unless the profile is active with
> **both** `auto_print_on_receipt` and `allow_print_egress` ON.

### Consumables

Consumables reuse `PartType.CONSUMABLE` and existing inventory. The employee
checkout register adds immutable attribution to each issue; it is not a separate
stock balance. See [Consumables setup and operation](CONSUMABLES.md).

| Method | Endpoint | Behavior | Server access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/consumables/metadata` | `can_manage`, `can_export`, and a minimal employee list (`id`, `name`, `department`, `is_active`). Includes active employees and inactive historical recipients for filtering. | Authenticated, active company |
| GET | `/consumables/stock` | `{items, total}` by consumable/location/lot, with on-hand, available quantity, unit, reorder threshold, low-stock and checkout eligibility. Filters `q`, `low_stock`; `skip` ≥ 0, `limit` 1–250 (default 100). Items without stock remain visible. The reorder judgment (the `low_stock` filter, `part_quantity_on_hand`, `is_low_stock`) counts the company's own active stock only; customer- and supplier-owned rows, supplier consignment stock for example, are still listed (see [Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property)). | Authenticated, active company |
| POST | `/consumables/checkouts` | Record one employee issue atomically; returns 201 and the saved receipt. | Admin, Manager, Supervisor |
| GET | `/consumables/checkouts` | `{items, total}`, ordered `issued_at DESC, id DESC`; filters `q`, `employee_id`, `part_id`, `date_from`, `date_to`; `skip` ≥ 0, `limit` 1–250 (default 100). | Authenticated, active company |
| GET | `/consumables/checkouts/export.csv` | Same history filters, all matching rows up to 10,000; 422 if exceeded. CSV includes Central timestamp and `CC-` checkout reference. Audited export. | Admin, Manager |

Checkout request:

```json
{
  "inventory_item_id": 123,
  "employee_id": 45,
  "quantity": 3,
  "notes": "Replacement grinding discs",
  "request_id": "8af26f41-30e6-45c1-9d1a-3ea9e29a53a8"
}
```

`employee_id` in commands/filters is the user's numeric primary key. Quantity
must be finite, greater than zero and at most 1,000,000,000; `each` must be a whole
number. Serialized stock is not supported by this workflow and is refused with
**409**. `notes` is optional, maximum 2,000 characters. `request_id` is a UUID.
Unknown request fields, including client-supplied issuer/time/company, are refused.

The response includes the immutable part number/name, unit, location/lot,
employee name/department, issuer name, quantity, notes and server UTC
`issued_at`. `replayed=true` identifies recovery of the same actor/payload under
the same company/request ID; recovery does not issue again. Conflicting reuse
returns **409**. Stock eligibility is revalidated under locks; inactive, deleted
or non-consumable parts, foreign references and inactive recipients cannot be
selected. Held, expired, nonpickable, allocated and reserved stock is protected.
Open unpinned work-order ties on the part are covered by **company-owned** stock
only (migration `129`), because automatic consumption never draws a customer's or
supplier's lot: that part-level reservation caps checkouts from company rows, while a
customer- or supplier-owned row is capped by its own free quantity (pins withheld).
An unavailable or insufficient quantity returns **409**. Required audit failure
returns **503** and rolls back stock, attribution and ledger effects together.

The issue writes a negative `InventoryTransaction` of type `ISSUE`, with
`reference_type="consumable_checkout"` and `reference_number="CC-<six-digit id>"`.
It is separate from work-order material issues and does not allocate job cost.
Dates filter complete inclusive **America/Chicago** calendar days; timestamps
are stored/returned in UTC and displayed/exported in Central time. `q` is at most
200 characters. An inverted date range returns **422**.

There is no checkout update/delete, return, void, historical-paper import or
backdating endpoint. Existing inventory adjustments can correct stock with a
checkout reference and reason; they do not rewrite employee usage attribution.
Badge/login credentials are not returned in metadata, receipts, history or CSV,
and cannot be searched through this feature. Migration `112_consumable_checkouts`
adds the immutable register and private PostgreSQL access controls. No new
environment variables are required.

### Inventory

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/inventory/` | List inventory items (`part_id`, `warehouse`, `location_code`, `has_quantity` — `has_quantity` filters **nonzero**, not positive, so driven-negative lots stay visible; see note below — and `ownership`, `owner_customer_id`, `owner_vendor_id`). Each row carries `ownership`, the owner id and `owner_name` (see [Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property)). Bounded: `limit` **1–10000, default 10000**, `offset` ≥ 0 | Yes |
| GET | `/inventory/summary` | On-hand summary by part, with per-location breakdown (every active row with **nonzero** on-hand, negatives included). `total_on_hand` is physical stock whoever owns it; `owned_by_others_on_hand` is the customer- and supplier-owned part of it, and each location entry carries its row's `ownership`. Bounded with the identical `limit`/`offset` as `/inventory/` — see note below | Yes |
| GET | `/inventory/low-stock` | Live parts with a reorder point above zero whose on-hand is at or below it -- the one low-stock rule (`low_stock_service`), shared with the `stock.low` alert, the operations inbox and the AI inventory sensor. Sorted critical first (on hand at or below safety stock), then by largest shortage, then part number. Each row also carries `out_of_stock` (a part with no stock row at all is listed at 0 on hand). `quantity_on_hand` is the **company's own** on-hand, summed per part over active rows in any status; customer- and supplier-owned stock is not counted, so a part whose only stock is owned reads 0 and is listed (see [Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property)) | Yes |
| GET | `/inventory/locations` | List warehouse locations / bins | Yes |
| POST | `/inventory/locations` | Create a location | Admin / Manager |
| GET | `/inventory/transactions` | Inventory transaction (ledger) history, newest first.
