> **Three consumption sources are read, and all three must be.** Genealogy resolves ISSUE rows under
> **`reference_type='work_order'`** (LEGACY pre-PR-4.4 one-shot BOM / work-order-scoped-tie rows,
> `reference_id` = the work order — nothing writes this shape any more), **`work_order_backflush`**
> (PR 4.4: the reconciling component leg — BOM/routing demand and work-order-scoped ties,
> `reference_id` = the work order) **and** **`reference_type='work_order_operation'`** (per-run
> consumption of material tied to
> an operation, `reference_id` = the **operation**, mapped back to its work order here). All three collapse
> into the same per-`(work order, component part, lot)` lines, so a nest that consumed sheets and a
> BOM that backflushed hardware read identically. Historical rows are **not** migrated — they
> truthfully carry `work_order` only. **Expect more lines per component than before PR 4.4**: the
> reconciling leg spills across lots, so one logical draw of 25 over lots of 10/10/10 is three lines
> naming three heats. That is the intended as-built record — the single summed row it replaced could
> not express which heats went into the part. Consequently `consumed_components` is non-empty when the
> producing part had `backflush_components = true` **or** the work order carried material ties (see
> Work Orders → "Material ties"); it stays empty for purchased/raw lots and for untied work on a part
> that never opted into backflush. In practice **material ties are still the only source with production
> mileage**: PR 4.5 made `backflush_components` settable (see [Part Schema](#part-schema)), but the
> column defaults to `false` and no work order has yet reached the BOM/routing leg. The claim here used
> to be structural ("nothing writes the flag"); it is now merely factual, and it stops being true the
> first time a part opts in. All three `work_order`-family reference types are also what the lot
> and serial traces use to collect `work_orders_used`.

### Shipping

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/shipping/` | List shipments | Yes |
| POST | `/shipping/` | Create shipment | Yes |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/ship` | Mark as shipped (decrements FG, closes WO, auto-issues CoC when required) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/coc` | Issue / generate the Certificate of Conformance (idempotent) | Admin / Manager / Quality |
| GET | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/coc` | Get CoC metadata (404 if none issued) | Yes |
| GET | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/coc/pdf` | Download the rendered CoC PDF (`application/pdf`) | Yes |

#### Carrier integration (rate / label / freight / pickup / tracking)

Multi-carrier endpoints on the shipping router. All carrier round-trips that transmit customer data
are gated by the per-company `allow_carrier_egress` kill switch (default **OFF**) — when disabled the
service makes **no** external call and returns **409**. Write actions are RBAC-gated to
`Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping`; reads are open to any authenticated tenant user. Money is
`Decimal`/`Numeric(12,2)` throughout. See
[docs/SHIPPING_CARRIER_INTEGRATION.md](SHIPPING_CARRIER_INTEGRATION.md).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| POST | `/shipping/validate-address` | Validate / normalize a postal address via the carrier (egress-gated). Optional `?carrier_account_id=` | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/rate-shop` | Rate-shop the shipment and persist the quotes (egress-gated). Body: `parcels` / `pallets` / optional `ship_from` / `ship_to` / `carrier_account_id` | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| GET | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/rates` | List the persisted rate quotes (read-only, no egress) | Yes |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/buy-label` | Purchase a parcel label (egress-gated, **idempotent**, audited). Body: `rate_id` (+ optional `carrier_account_id`) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/buy-bol` | Purchase an LTL Bill of Lading (egress-gated, idempotent, audited). **Returns 501 on EasyPost** (freight is unimplemented — see note) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/schedule-pickup` | Schedule a carrier pickup for a purchased shipment (egress-gated). Body: `pickup_date` / `window_start` / `window_end` | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/void-label` | Void a purchased label (egress-gated, idempotent, audited as CANCEL) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| POST | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/refund` | Request a refund for a purchased label (alias of void; same money-moving CANCEL) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping |
| GET | `/shipping/{shipment_id}/tracking` | Stored tracking status + event history (read-only, not egress-gated) | Yes |

> **Egress kill switch (409).** `validate-address`, `rate-shop`, `buy-label`, `buy-bol`,
> `schedule-pickup`, and `void`/`refund` are blocked with **HTTP 409** (`EgressDisabledError`) until an
> admin enables `allow_carrier_egress` on the company shipping profile
> (`PUT /admin/settings/shipping-profile`). This is the CUI / data-egress gate — those calls transmit
> the customer ship-to address to a third-party aggregator. `test-connection` is the only carrier
> round-trip exempt (it sends no customer data).
>
> **Idempotency.** `buy-label` / `buy-bol` pre-check for an already-purchased label/BOL and return the
> existing shipment with `already_purchased: true` (no provider call). A deterministic idempotency key
> (`sha256(company_id:shipment_id:rate_id)`) is persisted (partial-unique index) and sent to the
> provider as an `Idempotency-Key` header.
>
> **Freight is scaffolded, not functional on EasyPost.** `buy-bol` (and the underlying freight
> rate-shop) raise `NotSupportedError` on the EasyPost adapter → **HTTP 501**. EasyPost LTL is an
> Enterprise-gated feature with no public REST wire format; the freight path is real at the
> service/model/schema layers and waits on a future Zenkraft adapter. Parcel rate/label/track is fully
> implemented.
>
> **Carrier-error → HTTP mapping** (`_map_carrier_error`): `EgressDisabledError` → 409,
> `AddressInvalidError` → 422, `NotSupportedError` → 501, a `CarrierError` containing "not found" → 404,
> any other provider failure → 502. Provider internals and secrets are never surfaced.
>
> **Tracking is informational.** Webhook / poll tracking events update `tracking_status` and set
> `actual_delivery` on a `DELIVERED` event, but **never** auto-close the work order — `mark_shipped`
> remains the only WO-closing action.

> **Shipment-close is audited.** Marking a shipment shipped closes its work order
> (status → `CLOSED`); that terminal status change is recorded in the tamper-evident audit trail
> (`GET /audit/`), flushed so the audit row commits atomically with the closure.
>
> **`POST /shipping/{shipment_id}/ship` is RBAC-gated to Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Shipping.**
> Marking a shipment shipped is the terminal shipping action that **CLOSES the work order**, so it is
> restricted to the documented Shipping **"Complete"** role set
> (`require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR, SHIPPING])`) rather than any authenticated user. A
> non-privileged tenant user now gets **403**. See `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Shipping. (The two
> read CoC endpoints below stay open to any authenticated company user; issuing a CoC is
> Admin / Manager / Quality.)
>
> **Marking shipped decrements finished-goods inventory (G2).** `POST /shipping/{shipment_id}/ship`
> now writes the offsetting outbound stock movement for the goods leaving the building — the mirror of
> the Batch-6 finished-goods receipt on completion. It writes a `SHIP` `InventoryTransaction`
> (`quantity = -quantity_shipped`, `reference_type = "shipment"`) and decrements the finished-goods
> lot's on-hand / available (the lot is matched on `part_id` + finished-goods location +
> `work_order.lot_number`, exactly the row the receipt created). Both the SHIP transaction and its
> audit rows join the same unit of work as the SHIPPED status change + WO close, so they commit
> atomically. The decrement is **idempotent**: a re-submitted or concurrent double-ship (the shipment
> row is locked `FOR UPDATE` and a prior SHIP transaction for the shipment short-circuits) never
> double-decrements on-hand. **No new request/response field** — this is a side effect of marking
> shipped.
>
> **Over-ship and missing-FG-lot are warn-and-record, not blocking (G2).** Neither condition fails
> the ship — the ship/close still proceeds (mirrors the warn-and-record posture of the completion
> backflush-shortage and quality gates):
> - **Over-ship:** if cumulative `quantity_shipped` across the work order's non-cancelled shipments
>   exceeds what was produced (`WorkOrder.quantity_complete`), the ship is **allowed** but a
>   tamper-evident `audit_log` row (action `OVER_SHIP`) + a warning operational event record the
>   overage. There is no sales-order quantity to ship against; produced quantity is the ceiling.
> - **FG lot not found:** if no matching finished-goods lot row exists (the receipt was skipped, the
>   lot changed, or the stock was already moved), on-hand is **not** decremented and a tamper-evident
>   `audit_log` row (action `SHIP_FG_LOT_MISSING`) + a warning operational event record the
>   discrepancy; the ship/close still proceeds.

> **Certificate of Conformance (CoC) generation (G6-B).** A CoC is a real, per-shipment compliance
> artifact (previously just a `cert_of_conformance` boolean). It is a **DB frozen snapshot** — the
> `certificates_of_conformance` row stores the immutable certified facts at issue time and the PDF is
> rendered **deterministically on download** (there is no filesystem blob). CoC content is an AS9100D
> conformance statement + part/revision + WO# / customer-PO + quantity + lot/serial table +
> signature/issuer block. All three endpoints are **tenant-scoped** (a cross-tenant `shipment_id`
> returns **404**):
> - `POST /shipping/{shipment_id}/coc` — issue or return the existing CoC. **Idempotent**: at most one
>   CoC per shipment, DB-enforced (`uq_coc_company_shipment`); re-issuing returns the same CoC with no
>   second audit row. RBAC: **Admin / Manager / Quality** (quality artifact). First issue writes a
>   tamper-evident `log_create` audit row.
> - `GET /shipping/{shipment_id}/coc` — CoC metadata; **404** if none issued. Any authenticated company
>   user (read-broad / write-restricted, like the other shipping reads).
> - `GET /shipping/{shipment_id}/coc/pdf` — streams the rendered PDF (`application/pdf`,
>   `Content-Disposition: attachment`). Any authenticated company user.
>
> **Auto-issue on ship.** `POST /shipping/{shipment_id}/ship` auto-issues a CoC when one is
> **required** — required = the shipment's `cert_of_conformance` flag is set **OR** a company-scoped
> `Customer` matched by `work_order.customer_name` has `requires_coc` (which **defaults `True`**, so
> auto-issue fires for essentially every customer-matched shipment — the intended fail-safe).
> Auto-issue is **idempotent and best-effort**: a CoC failure never fails the ship — it records a
> `coc_generation_failed` warning operational event (mirrors the warn-and-record posture of the FG /
> over-ship guards). A successful auto-issue commits atomically with the ship and sets the shipment's
> `cert_of_conformance` flag.

### Reports

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/reports/production-summary` | Work orders by status, completions and on-time count, hours, produced / scrapped quantity and scrap rate over a rolling `days` window (1–365, default 30, counted back from now) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/quality-metrics` | NCR counts by status and source, receiving reject rate, over a rolling `days` window (default 30) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/inventory-value` | Value of the **company's own** on-hand stock at standard cost (`total_value`), its total quantity and distinct parts; customer- and supplier-owned stock is left out (see note) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/vendor-performance` | Per vendor: ordered / received quantity, fill and reject rates, PO count, over a rolling `days` window (default 90; `skip`, `limit` ≤ 500) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/work-center-utilization` | Per-work-center utilization over a rolling `days` window (default 30; `skip`, `limit` ≤ 500) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/daily-output` | Operations completed and quantity scrapped per **production day** for the last `days` (1–365, default 14) production days, the current one included; an operation counts on the production day its `actual_end` falls in (see "Production days in reports" below) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/work-order-costing` | Per work order: estimated vs actual hours and cost (`work_order_id`, else work orders created in a rolling `days` window, default 90) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/employee-time` | Time entries and operation completions per employee over an inclusive range of **production days** (`start_date`, default 7 days before the current production day; `end_date`, default the current one; `user_id`). Each entry carries `date` (its production day) and `shift_code` (see below) | Yes |
| GET | `/reports/ship-otd` | Ship-based OTD/OTIF detail report (`period` today/7d/30d/90d/ytd/custom + `start_date`/`end_date`) | Yes |

> **Production days in reports (P1.2, 2026-11-13).** `daily-output` and `employee-time` read
> production days on the company's production calendar (see [Production calendar &
> shifts](#production-calendar--shifts)): local midnight to local midnight when none is configured.
> Until 2026-11-13 both read **UTC** dates. `employee-time` includes a time entry when the production
> day it is **attributed** to (greatest shift overlap, ties to the outgoing shift; else the production
> day of its clock-in) lies in `start_date`..`end_date`, so every entry counts on **exactly one**
> production day; an open entry runs to now for attribution. A reversed range is **422**. A time-entry
> row's `date` is that production day and its `shift_code` that shift's code, `null` when it overlaps
> no defined shift. So a 01:30 Wednesday weld entry reads as Tuesday, `W2`, and a 04:55–15:30 Wednesday
> one as Wednesday, `W1` — in Wednesday's report only. **Changed 2026-11-13 (review fix):** the first
> P1 cut included an entry that clocked in **or out** inside the window, which put that 04:55 entry in
> Tuesday's report too (dated Wednesday, hours added to Tuesday's total); the pre-P1 report did the
> same across UTC midnight. An entry that crosses midnight with no calendar configured now counts on
> the local day it clocked in, and the operation it completed after midnight still shows in the next
> day's report as a completion row. A completion row's `date` is the production day of its
> `actual_end`, and its `shift_code` is the shift running at that instant. The rolling-`days` reports
> (`production-summary`, `quality-metrics`, `vendor-performance`, `work-center-utilization`,
> `work-order-costing`) count back from the current instant and have no day boundary.
>
> **Corrected 2026-11-13:** this table used to list `GET /reports/work-orders`, `/reports/production`,
> `/reports/quality` and `POST /reports/custom`, none of which exist. The custom-report runner is
> `POST /analytics/custom-report`.

> **Inventory value is the company's own stock (migration `129`, AS9100D 8.5.3).** Customer- and
> supplier-owned property held in the shop is physical stock, but not the company's inventory, so it
> is left out of every inventory value figure: all three figures of `GET /reports/inventory-value`,
> `summary.total_inventory_value` and each part's average inventory value (the turnover
> denominator) on `GET /analytics/inventory-turnover`, and the average inventory value behind the
> `inventory_turnover` KPI on `GET /analytics/kpis`. Physical on-hand quantities still include it
> (`GET /inventory/summary` reports it separately as `owned_by_others_on_hand`), and the inventory
> export keeps every row's `total_value` beside its `ownership`; the planning and reorder figures do
> not ([Planning and reorder count the company's stock only](#owned-stock-planning-and-reorder)). These
> figures and those readers share one clause, `owned_property_service.COMPANY_OWNED_ITEM_CLAUSES`. A
> company with no owned stock sees the same figures as before. See
> [Inventory → Customer- and supplier-owned property](#customer--and-supplier-owned-property).

> **`GET /reports/ship-otd` (Lean Phase 1).** The customer-experienced delivery report: measures
> `Shipment.ship_date` against the **promise** (`must_ship_by`, falling back to `due_date`), counting
> only real shipments (dated, not soft-deleted, not CANCELLED); multiple partial shipments roll up
> cumulatively, and the **full-ship date** is the shipment that crossed the ordered quantity.
> Returns: headline `otd_ship_pct` (**fulfillment-anchored** — of WOs whose full quantity finished
> shipping in the window, the share on/before promise) and `otif_pct` (**promise-anchored** — of WOs
> promised in the window, the share fully shipped **by** the promise date, so an open WO past promise
> counts as a miss immediately), both `null` on an empty denominator; per-WO `rows[]` (promise
> source/date, first/last/full ship dates, `on_time`, `days_late` — for an open WO past promise, days
> past so far); a `by_customer[]` rollup; and `promise_hygiene[]` — shipped/open WOs with **neither**
> promise field set (unmeasurable). These are the same legs as the `on_time_delivery_ship` / `otif`
> KPIs on `GET /analytics/kpis` (see Analytics).

| GET | `/analytics/cost-analysis` | Job cost analysis (estimated vs. actual) | Yes |

| GET | `/analytics/wip-aging` | WIP aging snapshot (open WOs, days since release / in current op) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/analytics/fpy` | First-pass yield / rolled throughput yield by part and work center | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| GET | `/analytics/scrap-pareto` | Scrap quantity/cost Pareto by reason code | Admin / Manager / Supervisor / Quality |
| GET | `/analytics/adoption` | Digital-adoption + hidden-factory metrics | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/analytics/predict/delivery/{work_order_id}` | Predicted completion date + per-operation forecast for one work order | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/analytics/predict/capacity` | Capacity utilization forecast by work center, by week | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |

| GET | `/analytics/inventory-turnover` | Inventory turnover: the ten lowest-turnover parts and `summary.total_inventory_value` / `avg_turnover` (`period` / `start_date` / `end_date`, `category`). Values count company-owned stock only (see [Reports](#reports)) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/analytics/data-sources` | Custom-report catalog: every data source and field (name, label, type, enum `options`) | Admin / Manager |

| GET | `/analytics/custom-report/templates` | List saved report templates: the caller's own plus every shared one | Yes |
| POST | `/analytics/custom-report/templates` | Save a report definition as a named template (validated, audited) | Admin / Manager |
| GET | `/analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}` | Get one saved template, with its `definition_errors` | Admin / Manager — own or shared (any for an Admin) |
| PATCH | `/analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}` | Change a template's name / description / sharing / definition (audited) | Admin / Manager — author or Admin |
| DELETE | `/analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}` | Delete a template (required audit row with a snapshot; 503 and nothing deleted if it cannot be saved) | Admin / Manager — author or Admin |
| POST | `/analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}/run` | Run a saved template (`?limit=`, 1–10,000, default 1,000) | Admin / Manager — own or shared (any for an Admin) |
| GET | `/analytics/custom-report/export` | Export a saved template's full result as CSV (`?template_id=`; csv only; audited; read-only / AI-external token 403) | Admin / Manager — own or shared (any for an Admin) |

> **Days in analytics (P1, 2026-11-13).** Every analytics range is a set of **company-local calendar
> days** (`Company.timezone`), and a point or bucket is dated in that same zone:
> `/analytics/production-trends` dates a RUN entry by the local date of its clock-in and a
> simplified-workflow completion by the local date of its `actual_end` (it used `func.date(...)`, the
> UTC date, until 2026-11-13, so evening work landed on the next day and a one-day range could return a
> point dated after its own end); `/analytics/adoption` puts a row in the ISO week of its local date.
> **Two bases share the KPI dashboard:** the OEE figures (headline, sparkline, `/analytics/oee`) read
> **production days** — the company's configured day start — while every other KPI (OTD, FPY, scrap,
> quotes, NCRs, turnover, flow, adoption) reads local **calendar** days. With no production calendar
> configured the two are identical. With Werco's 05:00 start they differ for 00:00–05:00: at 03:00 on a
> Wednesday, `period=today` is Tuesday's production day, so OEE counts Tuesday's 2nd shift through
> 05:00 Wednesday while the calendar-day KPIs count Tuesday 00:00–24:00. Completion-based **OTD** and
> the production-summary on-time count compare the company-local date of `actual_end` with `due_date`
> (a job finished at 19:00 CDT on its due date was counted late until 2026-11-13), and ship OTD,
> `/analytics/wip-aging`'s days-to-due and the shop-floor `due_today` filter use the company's calendar
> date, not the server's.
>
> **OEE inputs changed with the production days (2026-11-13), not only the day boundary.** The KPI
> sparkline is now exactly the per-day headline value, computed on the same inputs: (1) its ideal
> hours count **produced + scrapped** pieces (it counted produced only, so it read lower than the
> headline whenever there was scrap); (2) it honors `REQUIRE_APPROVED_LABOR_FOR_COST` (it ignored it);
> (3) the headline's ideal hours count **closed** entries only, like its staffed and run hours (open
> entries used to add ideal hours with no run time behind them). All three agree with the persisted
> `OEERecord` (`POST /oee/calculate`).
>
> **Flow & quality metrics (Lean Phase 1).** Five read-only, role-gated, tenant-scoped analytics
> endpoints. All but `/wip-aging` (a point-in-time snapshot) take the same window parameters as
> `/analytics/kpis`: `period` (`today` / `7d` / `30d` / `90d` / `ytd` / `custom`) plus
> `start_date` / `end_date` for `custom`. As throughout Analytics, uncomputable values are `null`
> ("n/a"), never a fake 0/100:
> - **`/flow`** — per completed WO: lead time (release → `actual_end`), release→first/last-ship days,
>   value-add RUN hours, and PCE (value-add ÷ lead time); summary adds median/avg lead time,
>   Little's Law WIP/throughput (the daily open-WO count runs from `released_at` to `actual_end` and
>   leaves out CANCELLED and DRAFT work orders — neither records when it left the floor, and a DRAFT
>   can carry a release stamp for a release that was put back), and per-work-center queue times (measured from `operation_ready`
>   events where available, predecessor-end → start as fallback, with `from_ready_events` counting
>   the former). **Queue time has a series break at 2026-08-11:** operations sharing a work center
>   now all become READY at work-order release rather than one at a time, so for those operations the
>   ready anchor means "released", not "the previous step finished", and measured queue time steps up
>   without the shop's flow having changed. Windows spanning that date are not comparable — see
>   [docs/LEAN_ROADMAP.md](LEAN_ROADMAP.md) → "Queue time — series break".
> - **`/wip-aging`** — every open released WO with days since release, the current operation and days
>   in it (since its `actual_start`, or since it became READY), and days to due (negative = past due).
> - **`/fpy`** — quantity-weighted first-pass yield (`(complete − reworked − scrapped) ÷ attempted`)
>   grouped by part and by work center; RTY (product of per-op FPYs) per part. Optional
>   `work_center_id` / `part_id` filters; RTY is omitted when `work_center_id` is set (it is a
>   full-route metric). Rework tracking feeds from produced quantity booked on REWORK time entries.
> - **`/scrap-pareto`** — scrap quantity and cost (quantity × `standard_cost` where available) bucketed
>   by scrap reason code with cumulative %, uncoded scrap in an `unspecified` bucket. Optional
>   `work_center_id` / `part_id` filters.
> - **`/adoption`** — the A0.1 paper-to-digital telemetry read side: digital completion % (live
>   kiosk/desktop/scanner vs. backfill/import vs. unknown channel), clock-in coverage, backfill rate,
>   a weekly trend, plus **hidden-factory** metrics — rework hours/quantity share, planned-vs-reactive
>   maintenance mix, and per-work-center MTBF/MTTR.
>
> **Provenance rule.** Labor/scrap booked through the `backfill` / `import` channels is **excluded**
> from the measured baselines (value-add hours, FPY-feeding rework, Pareto buckets, hidden-factory
> hours) and reported separately on each response (`excluded_backfill_import_*`), so migrated history
> can't masquerade as measured shop-floor data.
>
> **`GET /analytics/kpis` gained two ship-based delivery KPIs.** `on_time_delivery_ship`
> (fulfillment-anchored ship OTD) and `otif` (promise-anchored on-time-in-full) now ride the KPI
> dashboard alongside the existing completion-based `on_time_delivery`, as regular `KPIValue`s
> (value / prior / change / sparkline, nullable per the "n/a" rule below). Semantics and the shared
> promise precedence (`must_ship_by` || `due_date`) are documented under
> `GET /reports/ship-otd` (Reports). The fields are optional-with-default in the schema so cached
> consumers/fixtures keep validating; the live endpoint always populates both.

<a id="predictive-analytics"></a>
> **Predictive analytics (delivery / capacity / inventory demand).** Three read-only endpoints
> gated `require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR])`, served by `PredictionService`
> (`app/services/prediction_service.py`). All three are heuristic forecasts off live operational
> data — they write nothing: no ledger row, no audit row, no event.
> - **`GET /analytics/predict/delivery/{work_order_id}`** — no query params. Returns
>   `DeliveryPrediction`: the header (`work_order_number`, `part_number`, `quantity`, `due_date`),
>   nullable `predicted_completion`, `confidence` (scaled by how much historical data backs the
>   estimate), `on_time_probability` (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.95 by days of margin against `due_date`),
>   `bottleneck_work_center`, and `operations[]` — per routing step the `operation_name`,
>   `work_center_name`, nullable `predicted_start` / `predicted_end`, `queue_position` and `estimated_hours`.
>   Estimates are planned hours scaled by that work center's trailing-90-day actual-vs-planned ratio,
>   using its weekday calendar, dated closures/capacity overrides and queue hours. The target job
>   is excluded from its own queue. `materials`, `warnings` and `basis` explain the supply evidence
>   and assumptions: missing arrival evidence, unavailable calendar capacity or missing time estimates
>   produce unknown dates/probability rather than an unsupported promise. Known material supply
>   constrains the forecast. A job without defined requirements retains a clearly labeled capacity
>   estimate. See [planning and job history](ux-workflows/planning-job-history.md).
> - **`GET /analytics/predict/capacity`** — `weeks_ahead` (int, default `4`, `ge=1`, `le=12`).
>   Returns `CapacityForecastResponse`: `weeks[]` (each `week_start` / `week_end`, `work_centers[]`
>   with `committed_hours` / `available_hours` / `utilization_pct` / `is_overloaded`, plus
>   `total_committed` / `total_available` / `overall_utilization`) and `alerts[]` for week 0
>   overloads (`severity` `high` above 110% utilization, else `medium`). Committed hours are the
>   remaining hours on RELEASED/IN_PROGRESS work orders spread evenly across the window; available
>   hours sum the work center's actual calendar capacity across all seven dates in each window,
>   including dated overrides. The existing even-spread demand heuristic remains an estimate.
> - **`GET /analytics/predict/inventory-demand`** — no query params. Returns
>   `InventoryDemandResponse`: `predictions[]` (**capped at the 50 most urgent**) with `part_number`
>   / `part_name`, `current_stock`, `daily_usage_rate` (net 90-day issues less returns ÷ 90),
>   `predicted_stockout_date`, `days_until_stockout`, `open_po_quantity`, `next_po_due` and
>   `urgency` (`critical` ≤ 7 days, `warning` ≤ 14, else `ok`, de-escalated one step when an open PO
>   lands before the stockout date), plus `critical_count` / `warning_count`. Considers active,
>   non-deleted `purchased` / `raw_material` parts only. `current_stock` is the company's own
>   on-hand (active rows, any status): customer- and supplier-owned stock does not push a stockout
>   date out (see [Planning and reorder](#owned-stock-planning-and-reorder)).
>
> **Refusals on `/predict/delivery/{work_order_id}` (new).** A work order belonging to **another
> company** now returns **404 `{"detail": "Work order not found"}` — byte-identical to the response
> for an id that does not exist at all**, and identical for a soft-deleted work order. The refusal
> carries no identifier, so the status code cannot be used as an existence oracle (the #189
> convention). Previously this route looked the work order up **by primary key with no ownership
> check of any kind**, so a sequential-integer walk returned any tenant's header *and* its sequenced
> routing. The second refusal, 404 `{"detail": "Work order has no routing operations"}`, is now
> reachable only for a work order the caller owns, so keeping it distinct discloses nothing.
>
> <a id="predictive-analytics-behavior-change"></a>
> **⚠️ Behavior change on multi-company installs: these figures will DROP, and the old ones were
> wrong.** All three endpoints previously ran **entirely unscoped** — `PredictionService` was
> constructed with a session and no `company_id`, so every read underneath it (parts, inventory
> items, inventory transactions, work orders, work-order operations, work centers, purchase orders
> and PO lines) summed across **every tenant on the install**. Concretely, before this fix:
> `/predict/capacity` listed every tenant's machines by name and folded their open jobs into
> `committed_hours` / `overall_utilization`; `/predict/inventory-demand` rendered foreign part
> numbers and names into `predictions[]` and inflated `current_stock`, `daily_usage_rate` and
> `open_po_quantity` for shared part ids; and `/predict/delivery` reported `queue_position` counting
> other tenants' queued operations and `estimated_hours` steered by their efficiency ratios.
> **Anyone comparing a dashboard across this deploy should expect utilization, committed hours,
> queue positions, stock figures and part counts to fall, and in some cases for work centers or
> parts to disappear from the list entirely. That is the correction, not a regression — the smaller
> numbers are the first correct ones.** Single-company installs are unaffected, with one exception
> noted below.
>
> **Also corrected (single-tenant installs too): soft-deleted rows stopped counting.** Independent of
> tenancy, these reads did not filter `is_deleted` and so a caller's **own** deleted records were
> steering its own forecasts — a soft-deleted work order inflated its own queue depth (which
> multiplies into every predicted date) and its own `committed_hours`; a soft-deleted BOM kept
> generating component demand; a soft-deleted purchase order still counted as inbound supply, which
> suppresses a real stockout warning; and retired (`is_deleted`) parts were still being forecast and
> reordered. All are now excluded, so these figures can move on a single-company install as well.

<a id="custom-report-builder"></a>
> **Custom report builder (2026-11-16).** An ad-hoc query over **one** data source, run live or
> saved as a named template. One catalog in `app/services/report_builder.py` (`REPORT_SOURCES`)
> declares every data source and field: its column, label, type, enum options and any join it
> needs. The `GET /analytics/data-sources` body, validation (`definition_problems`) and execution are
> all derived from it, so the fields a client is shown and the fields the engine accepts cannot
> disagree. Template access and writes are in `app/services/report_template_service.py`. Every route
> is Admin / Manager except the template list (any signed-in role). The screen is Analytics →
> **Custom Reports** (below).
>
> **Catalog: `GET /analytics/data-sources`.** Keyed by `data_source` value; each entry is
> `{label, fields: [{name, label, type, options?}]}`. `type` is `string`, `number`, `date`, `datetime`
> or `enum`. It is derived from the column's SQLAlchemy type and decides the allowed operators and
> aggregates. `options` appears on enum fields only: the values a filter takes and a row shows. The
> list is complete (a field not in it is refused) and the same for every company. The sources are
> `work_orders`, `parts`, `inventory`, `quality` (NCRs), `purchasing` (purchase orders) and `quotes`.
> - **`production` is gone.** It never had a backing model, so every report on it answered 500. A
>   request naming it is now **422**, and the catalog leaves it out. The enum member stays so a stored
>   template that names it still lists.
> - **The old hand-written catalog was wrong in both directions.** It advertised two fields the
>   engine silently dropped and hid sixteen it supported. The two now work: `inventory.part_number`
>   and `purchasing.vendor_name`. Each is a LEFT OUTER JOIN to `parts` / `vendors` with the
>   active company in the ON clause, so a foreign row with a colliding id is never joined. The joined
>   row is deliberately **not** tombstone-filtered: a lot's part and a PO's vendor are historical
>   records that keep naming who they named (invariant 3). The sixteen are now listed:
>   `quantity_scrapped`, `customer_po` and `created_at` (work orders); `material_cost`, `labor_cost`,
>   `safety_stock` and `reorder_point` (parts); `quantity_available` and `status` (inventory);
>   `quantity_rejected`, `closed_date` and `actual_cost` (NCRs); `required_date` and `subtotal` (POs);
>   `subtotal` and `lead_time_days` (quotes).
> - **`estimated_hours` is not a work-order field.** It has no writer anywhere (structurally 0 in
>   every tenant), so it was dropped from the catalog (G3-content). Naming it is now a 422; before
>   this change it silently dropped out of the report.
>
> **The definition** is the body of `POST /analytics/custom-report` and the stored part of a template:
> `data_source`, `columns` (1–40), `filters` (at most 20), `group_by` (at most 10) and `sort` (at most
> 10). A run adds `limit`: 1–10,000, default 1,000. `null` is refused; it used to mean "no limit".
> **Unknown keys are refused at every level**, so a misspelled `agregate` is a 422, not a silently
> ignored key.
> - **Column** `{field, alias?, aggregate?}`. The output key is the alias, else the field; two columns
>   producing the same key are refused, and an alias is at most 100 characters and may contain neither
>   a NUL character nor an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (see below). `sum` and `avg` take
>   number fields; `min` and `max` take number, date, datetime and string fields; `count` takes any.
>   Once any column aggregates or `group_by` is set, every non-aggregated column must be in
>   `group_by`.
> - **Filter** `{field, operator, value, value2?}`. Operators by type: string `eq` / `ne` / `in` /
>   `like`; number `eq` / `ne` / `gt` / `gte` / `lt` / `lte` / `in` / `between`; date and datetime `eq` /
>   `ne` / `gt` / `gte` / `lt` / `lte` / `between`; enum `eq` / `ne` / `in`. Values are typed:
>   - a number is a JSON number (not a boolean, not a numeric string, finite); an integer must fit in
>     64 bits (−2^63 to 2^63−1);
>   - text is at most 500 characters, and no value (of any type, `in` items included) may contain a
>     NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate. JSON allows a lone `"\ud800"` escape, but no
>     response can carry it: a template that stored one answered 500 on every later read, the
>     company's whole template list included. The problem message says `a value cannot contain
>     characters that cannot be stored (an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate)` and does not quote the value;
>     the 422 entry's `input` still echoes the request body, with U+FFFD in place of each such
>     character;
>   - a date is `YYYY-MM-DD`;
>   - a datetime is ISO-8601 with at least hours and minutes. No zone means UTC, and a zone is
>     converted to UTC; an instant whose zone pushes it outside years 1-9999 in UTC is a 422 (`… is
>     outside the supported range of dates and times`);
>   - an enum value is one of the field's `options` — the lowercase value (`in_progress`), never the
>     member name (`IN_PROGRESS`).
>
>   `value: null` is allowed only with `eq` / `ne` and means IS NULL / IS NOT NULL. `in` takes a
>   non-empty list of at most 500 values, none of them null. `between` needs `value2`, is inclusive at
>   both ends, and treats `value2: 0` as a real bound. `like` is a case-insensitive "contains" in which
>   `%`, `_` and `\` match literally.
>
>   **`value2` must be `null` or one scalar** — text, a finite number or `true` / `false` — for
>   **every** operator, including those that never read it, because it is stored with the filter.
>   A list or object is a 422 (`value2 must be null or a single value (text, a number or
>   true/false), not a list or an object`). Text in it follows the text rules above (no NUL, no
>   unpaired surrogate, at most 500 characters), and `NaN` / `Infinity` is refused. It used to take any
>   JSON at all, so a deeply nested one could be saved and then fail every later read of the
>   template list. An unread scalar `value2`, such as a bound left behind when a filter is switched
>   from `between` to `eq`, is still accepted and ignored.
> - **Group by** `{field}`. `granularity` is not supported yet; setting it is a 422.
> - **Sort** `{field, direction}`. `field` is a catalog field or the output key of a selected column.
>   `direction` is `asc` or `desc` in any case, stored lowercase. A grouped report sorts by a
>   group-by field or one of its own columns.
>
> **One 422 lists every problem.** Every semantic rule runs in `definition_problems`, and a broken
> definition comes back as a single `detail` entry with `type: "report_definition"`. Its `msg` joins
> every problem with `; ` and `ctx.problems` carries the same problems as a list, for example
> `Column 1: "nope" is not a Work Orders field; Filter 1 (Status): operator "gt" does not apply to an
> enum field; use one of: eq, ne, in`. Shape errors — an unknown key, a list over its cap, a `limit`
> out of range, an unknown `data_source` — are FastAPI's ordinary per-field entries.
>
> **The result** of `POST /analytics/custom-report` and `POST /analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}/run`:
>
> ```json
> {
>   "columns": [
>     {"key": "status", "label": "Status", "type": "enum"},
>     {"key": "quantity_ordered", "label": "Sum of Qty Ordered", "type": "number"}
>   ],
>   "rows": [{"status": "in_progress", "quantity_ordered": 140}],
>   "row_count": 1,
>   "truncated": false,
>   "notes": []
> }
> ```
>
> - `columns[]` follows the selected columns in order. `key` is the row key (alias, else field).
>   `label` is the alias, else the catalog label, prefixed `Sum of` / `Average of` / `Count of` /
>   `Minimum of` / `Maximum of` when aggregated. `type` is the field's type, except that `sum`, `avg`
>   and `count` are always `number`.
> - `rows[]` are keyed by column key. An enum cell is its value, a datetime is UTC ISO-8601 with `Z`,
>   a date is `YYYY-MM-DD`, and floats and Postgres decimals are rounded to 2 places.
> - `row_count` is the number of rows returned. `truncated` is true exactly when more than `limit`
>   rows matched (the query fetches one extra row). An ungrouped report adds the base record's id as a
>   final sort key, so the first `limit` rows are deterministic.
> - `notes[]` entries are `{code, message, fields}`. There is one code today, `labor_not_tracked`.
>   When `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED` is off (the default) and a `work_orders` report selects
>   `actual_hours`, `actual_cost` or `estimated_cost`, those columns read a literal `0` that means
>   "not tracked", not a measured $0. The note names them in `fields`.
>
> **Scoping.** The base query is always restricted to the caller's active company before any
> caller-supplied filter, group-by or sort (G3-scope), and every join is company-scoped in its ON
> clause, so a report can never return another tenant's rows. **Soft-deleted base records are
> excluded** — work orders, parts, NCRs (voided ones included) and purchase orders. Inventory items
> and quotes have no soft delete. Running a report writes nothing.
>
> **Saved templates.** A template is a named definition, private to its author unless `is_shared`.
> - **Create** (`POST /analytics/custom-report/templates`). The body is the definition fields at the
>   top level plus `name` (1–255 characters, trimmed), `description` (optional, at most 2,000) and
>   `is_shared` (default `false`). It is validated by the same rules, with the same single 422. A
>   `name` or `description` holding a NUL or an unpaired surrogate is a 422 (`unstorable_text` /
>   `string_unicode`); it used to be a 500.
> - **Change** (`PATCH /analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}`). Send any of `name`,
>   `description` (`null` clears it), `is_shared` and `definition`. `definition` is the whole
>   `{data_source, columns, filters, group_by, sort}` object nested under that key; it replaces the
>   stored one and is validated like a new one. `name`, `is_shared` and `definition` may not be
>   `null`, and an empty body or an unknown key is a 422.
> - **Response** (`ReportTemplateResponse`, on every template verb but delete): `id`, `name`,
>   `description`, `data_source`, `columns`, `filters`, `group_by`, `sort`, `is_shared`, `created_by`,
>   `created_at`, plus two new fields, `updated_at` and `definition_errors`. The stored definition is
>   normalized: plain JSON, sort directions lowercased.
> - **Run** (`POST /analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}/run?limit=`). `limit` is 1–10,000,
>   default 1,000. It returns the same result shape as an ad-hoc run.
> - **Delete** (`DELETE /analytics/custom-report/templates/{template_id}`) answers
>   `{"message": "Template deleted"}`. It stays a physical delete: `ReportTemplate` is not
>   soft-deletable, and the audit row keeps a snapshot of what was removed. That audit row is
>   **required**: if it cannot be written the delete is rolled back and the answer is **503**
>   `The audit record for this delete could not be saved; the template was not deleted. Retry.` The
>   row is deleted (tenant-scoped) before the audit row is written, the same row-then-audit-chain
>   lock order as create and update; a delete that finds no row (a concurrent delete won) is the
>   same **404** as a missing template and writes no audit row.
>
> **Template access rule** (`report_template_service`):
>
> | Verb | Who | Otherwise |
> |---|---|---|
> | List | Any signed-in role; returns the caller's own templates plus every shared one, by name | — |
> | Get, run, export | Admin / Manager, and the template is the caller's own, shared, or the caller is an Admin (a superuser or Platform Admin counts as an Admin) | **403** `Access denied to this report` |
> | Change, delete | Admin / Manager, and the caller is the author or an Admin (a superuser or Platform Admin counts as an Admin) | **403** `Only the template's author or an admin can change or delete it` |
>
> A template in another company is **404** `Report template not found` on every verb, byte-identical
> to an id that does not exist, and never appears in the list. So a shared template can be run by
> every Admin / Manager in the company but changed only by its author or an Admin, and an Admin can
> open, run and export any template in the company. The read and change rules name the same Admin:
> until 2026-11-16 an Admin was refused a colleague's private template on read, yet could `PATCH` it
> and receive the whole definition back, so the refusal protected nothing. The list is unchanged —
> the caller's own plus every shared template, for every role — so an Admin opens a colleague's
> private template by id.
>
> **Stored templates are judged, never trusted.** Before this change templates were saved with type
> checks only, so a stored one can break a rule added since. Such a template still lists and opens,
> with `definition_errors` naming each problem. Running or exporting it answers **409**
> `Saved report "<name>" can no longer run: <problems>. Edit it and save it again.`, and a `PATCH` with
> a valid `definition` repairs it. `definition_errors` and the 409 come from the same validation, so
> they cannot disagree. Judging a stored definition never raises: an unexpected error while checking
> one is logged and reported as the single problem `The saved definition could not be checked; edit
> the report and save it again`, so one bad row can never fail the template list for the company.
> A stored definition holding an unpaired surrogate (saved before the refusal above existed) is
> rendered with U+FFFD in place of each such character, wherever it sits (a value, an alias, a key),
> and lists and opens with `The saved definition contains characters that cannot be stored (shown
> here as �); edit the report and save it again` first in `definition_errors`; running or exporting
> it is the **409**, since the definition that would run is not the one that was saved. A stored
> definition nested more than 32 levels deep (only an old `value2` could be; pydantic's serializer
> fails near 255, which 500'd the list) is treated the same way: everything past the bound is shown
> as `�`, and `The saved definition contains a value nested too deeply to show (shown here as �);
> edit the report and save it again` comes first in `definition_errors`. Every serialization of a
> stored definition goes through that rendering, the audit snapshots included, so a repair or
> delete never writes an audit row no audit-log read could render. The rendering walks are
> iterative, so no depth of stored JSON can make them fail.
>
> **Audit.** Create, change and delete each write a `report_template` audit row: `log_create`,
> `log_update` with old and new values, and a `DELETE` row with a snapshot of the deleted definition.
> Create and change are best-effort (the repo-wide `AuditService.log` contract), because a template
> is a saved query, not a quality record. **Delete is required** (`log_required`, the same fields
> `log_delete` writes): the delete is physical, so its snapshot is the only trace of the template,
> and a delete whose audit row cannot be saved is rolled back (**503**, above). Before this change,
> template create and delete wrote no audit row (and there was no update verb).
>
> **Export: `GET /analytics/custom-report/export?template_id=&format=csv`.** The caller must be able
> to read the template (own, shared, or any for an Admin).
> - **A read-only or AI-external API token is refused 403** `Read-only API token cannot download
>   files.` before anything is read — the template, the query, the row cap. It could never receive
>   the file, and the over-cap and empty-result 400s, which used to answer first, told it how many
>   rows a template matched.
> - **Every matching row is exported**, up to the shared bulk-export cap `MAX_EXPORT_ROWS` (10,000,
>   imported from `exports.py`). Over it the export is refused **400** `This export matches more than
>   10,000 rows. Add a filter, then export again.` rather than cut short — see
>   [Row cap on `/exports/*`](#row-cap-on-exports--refuses-at-10000-400). Before this change the export
>   ran with the run default and so stopped at 1,000 rows, with nothing in the file to say so.
> - An empty result is **400** `No data to export`; a template that can no longer run is **409**.
> - **`format` takes only `csv`** (OpenAPI `const: "csv"`). `xlsx` and `pdf` are a **422** at
>   validation. They used to be advertised in the parameter description and then answered 400
>   `Format … not yet supported`.
> - The header row is the column keys in column order. Cells and header are formula-neutralized; see
>   [Spreadsheet Exports](#spreadsheet-exports-csv--xlsx).
> - The file name is the template name, sent per RFC 6266 by
>   `export_safety.attachment_content_disposition`:
>   `attachment; filename="<ascii fallback>.csv"; filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded name>.csv`. The
>   fallback replaces non-ASCII, `"`, `/`, `\` and control characters with `_`. It used to be a bare
>   `filename=<name>.csv`, which broke on a space, a quote or a non-Latin-1 character.
> - A refusal (403, 404, 409, 422, the row cap, an empty result) writes no audit row. A successful
>   export still writes its `EXPORT` row (`resource_type` `custom_report`, the template as
>   `resource_id`, the stored columns and filters, never the rows) before the file streams.
>
> **Screen.** Analytics → **Custom Reports** (`/analytics/reports`) is a full builder. You pick a
> source, then columns and aggregates, typed filters, group by, sort and limit, and Run. The result
> renders as a table, plus a chart when the report is grouped. Saved templates open through
> `?template=<id>` (a reload or a shared link reopens the same one) and can be run, exported as CSV,
> edited, shared and deleted from the panel. The tab and the route require `analytics:export`
> (Admin, Manager and Platform Admin by default), which is the role set of the endpoints. Before
> this change every role saw the tab and then got 403s. See
> [RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md → Analytics](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#analytics).
>
> **⚠️ Contract change for API and MCP clients (2026-11-16).**
> - **`POST /analytics/custom-report` returns an object, not a bare array of row dicts.** A client
>   that read the array now reads `rows`. Through MCP, `run_custom_report`'s `structured_content` is
>   this object; before, the bare list arrived wrapped as `{"result": [...]}`
>   ([MCP.md §11](MCP.md#11-result-shapes-and-caps)).
> - **The `X-Report-Labor-Not-Tracked` and `X-Report-Labor-Note` response headers are gone.** The same
>   information is the `labor_not_tracked` entry in `notes`. Browsers could never read those headers:
>   they were not in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` (see [CORS](#cors)).
> - **Definitions that used to run with parts silently ignored are now 422s.** That covers an
>   unknown column, filter, group-by or sort field (an unknown filter field was dropped, so the
>   report returned unfiltered rows), an unknown operator, a wrongly typed value, `between` without
>   `value2`, `granularity`, an unknown key, a `limit` of `null` or above 10,000, and
>   `data_source: "production"`, which used to answer 500.
> - **Some filters now match what they say.** An enum filter binds the enum member, where the bare
>   string used to match nothing on most enum columns. `like` matches `%` and `_` literally.
>   `between` with `value2: 0` is applied instead of dropped.
> - **Soft-deleted work orders, parts, NCRs and purchase orders no longer appear.**
> - **The export takes csv only (422 otherwise)** and refuses over 10,000 rows (400) where it used to
>   stop at 1,000.

> **KPI values can be `null` ("n/a").** Each KPI on `GET /analytics/kpis` is a `KPIValue` whose
> **`value` (and `prior_value` / `change_pct`) are nullable**. A genuinely-uncomputable metric returns
> `null` rather than a misleading 0/100, and the frontend renders **"n/a"**:
> - **OEE** is `null` when the work center (or plant) has **no staffed (clocked) time** in the window —
>   there is no availability denominator, so it is uncomputable, not 0%.
> - **On-time delivery (OTD)** is `null` when **no work order with a due date completed** in the window
>   (empty denominator) — not a fabricated 100%.
>
> **OEE convention (`Availability × Performance × Quality`).** Computed per work center on the
> **staffed-time** basis, identical on this headline and on the persisted `OEERecord` (see OEE Tracking
> below): Availability = productive-run hours ÷ staffed (clocked) hours, productive run = (RUN+SETUP) −
> UNPLANNED downtime; Performance = ideal hours ÷ productive run, ideal hours = Σ((produced + scrapped)
> × routing `run_time_per_piece`) over RUN+REWORK (every piece run consumes a standard cycle, including
> scrap); Quality = good ÷ (good + scrapped) over RUN+REWORK.
>
> **OTD rule.** On-time = `actual_end.date() <= due_date`. A **COMPLETE work order with a null
> `actual_end` counts as NOT on time** (no verifiable completion date). The completed-set is
> tenant-scoped and soft-delete-filtered (`is_deleted == False`).

> **Cost-analysis labor/overhead is gated by `LABOR_COST_ROLLUP_ENABLED`.** `GET /analytics/cost-analysis`
> derives each job's labor and overhead from the work order's actual hours at the shared work-center
> rate — the **same** source the completion rollup uses, so the report and `WorkOrder.actual_cost` agree.
> When the flag is **off** (the default) the computed **labor and overhead legs report `$0`** (not
> tracked), uniformly across live- and reconcile-completed work orders. The **material leg is never
> gated** — it is real issued-material from inventory (the completion ISSUE transactions), so it stays
> accurate either way. The on-demand `POST /job-costs/{id}/calculate` recomputes job-cost labor from time
> entries regardless of the flag and is **tenant-scoped** (a job cost is looked up by id **and**
> company, closing a prior cross-tenant lookup).

### Production calendar & shifts

`app/api/endpoints/production_calendar.py`, mounted at `/production-calendar` (P1.2, migration
`120_production_calendar`). A **production day** is the shop's working day, not the calendar date: it
starts at the company's configured **production-day start** on the local clock (`Company.timezone`,
default America/Chicago) and runs to the same wall-clock time the next day; **a shift that runs past
midnight belongs to the day it started**. So with Werco's 05:00 start a weld entry at **01:30 Wednesday
is Tuesday's production day and Tuesday's 2nd shift**. A production day is 23 h / 25 h long across the
DST changes (boundaries are wall-clock times).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/production-calendar` | The calendar: `configured`, `version`, `timezone`, `production_day_start`, `patterns[]` (each with `work_center_ids` and `shifts[]`: `code`, `name`, `start`/`end` HH:MM, `start_minute`/`end_minute`, `ends_next_day`, `days` 0=Mon..6=Sun, `planned_minutes`, `is_active`), and `today` — the current production day's UTC window and every active shift on it as UTC instants (`Z`) | Yes |
| PUT | `/production-calendar` | Replace the **whole** calendar after a version check | **Admin** |
| GET | `/production-calendar/resolve` | Which production day and shift an instant (`at`, ISO-8601; offset-less = UTC; default now) belongs to at a `work_center_id` (omitted = the default pattern; another company's work center is **404**). Returns `production_day` with its UTC window, `shift` (the outgoing one in an overlap), `overlapping`, `pattern_id`, `configured` and `calendar_version`. An instant within a day of the ends of the datetime range is **422** `The instant is outside the supported range` | Yes |
| POST | `/production-calendar/working-calendars/sync` | Set each work center's weekly working hours from its shifts (`dry_run`, default `true`; `expected_version`) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |

**API tokens.** Both reads are open to every API token, read-only and AI-external ones included: they
are on the AI-external allowlist as reference data with no customer linkage, always served in full and
never ledgered (`resolve` takes `at` and `work_center_id` from such a token; see
[EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md → The AI-external allowlist](EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md#5-the-ai-external-allowlist)).
The `PUT` and the sync `POST`, a dry run included, refuse every read-only token **403** `Read-only API
token cannot modify data.`

**Unconfigured company (no calendar saved).** The production day is the **company-local calendar day**
(day start 00:00) and there are no shifts. This replaced the old **UTC-date** day boundaries of OEE,
the OEE cron, reports, downtime filters, job-cost labor dates and analytics on **2026-11-13** — for every
tenant, configured or not, a "day" is now a local day (or a production day), never a UTC date.
Historical `auto` OEE rows computed before that date stay as computed (UTC days); a re-run computes the
production day.

**Attribution rules.** An **instant** belongs to the production day it falls in; inside two
overlapping shifts (the rest-of-shop 15:30–16:00 hand-off) it belongs to the **outgoing** (earlier-start)
shift — `resolve` returns it as `shift` and lists both in `overlapping`. An **interval** (a time entry,
a downtime event) belongs to the shift it overlaps **most** (a tie goes to the outgoing shift) and to
that shift's production day; one that overlaps no shift belongs to the production day of its start. So
an early **04:55 weld clock-in** that runs into the 05:00 1st shift counts on that day's 1st shift, not
the previous production day. A work center belongs to at most one **pattern**; one in no pattern (and an
entry with no work center) uses the company's **default** pattern — at most one, and possibly none, in
which case such a work center has no shifts.

**However long it runs, an interval counts on exactly one production day.** Greatest overlap can put a
long interval on a later production day than the one it started on — a weld clock-in at 16:00 Monday that
is not clocked out until 16:00 Tuesday overlaps Tuesday's W1 (10.5 h) more than Monday's W2 (10 h), so it
is **Tuesday's**; a rest-of-shop breakdown from 16:00 Monday to 10:00 Wednesday is Tuesday's S1. Every
reader that attributes — OEE and its cron, the analytics OEE figures, the wallboard, the employee-time
report — reads every interval that **overlaps** the requested days, back as far as attribution can
reach (two production days before the first one), so such an interval is counted on its attributed day,
including in a single-day report or a range that starts on that day. Until 2026-11-15 these reads only
looked 12 hours before the day start, and an interval like those two was counted on **no** day at all;
before 2026-11-13 it counted on the UTC date it started.

**Boundaries across DST.** The production day of an instant is the day whose window contains it, so
the attribution and every SQL day filter always agree. A day start that names a wall time a DST change
skips (02:00–02:59 on the spring-forward Sunday in a US zone) resolves with the pre-change offset, and
one that repeats (01:00–01:59 on the fall-back Sunday) at its first occurrence. Werco's 05:00 start is
unaffected.

**History is re-read under the current calendar.** Persisted `OEERecord`s keep the values they were
computed with, but every read that attributes on the fly — the analytics OEE figures, the wallboard,
the employee-time report, the downtime filters, job-cost recompute — buckets past data under the
calendar as it is **now**. So changing the day start, or a shift's times, days or planned minutes,
re-buckets history on those reads, and a past day's `/analytics/oee` can stop matching its stored
`/oee` record. Only a referenced shift's removal and `code` change are refused; the required audit row
(the whole before/after document) is the record of what the calendar was. To keep a referenced
shift's history unambiguous, retire it and add a new shift rather than re-timing it.

**Who reads production days.** OEE records and `POST /oee/calculate` (`record_date` is a production
day), the nightly OEE cron, the wallboard **today** pulse, the shop-floor dashboard `completed_today`
(its ETag folds in the production day and calendar version), `GET /reports/daily-output` and
`GET /reports/employee-time` (each entry's `date` is its production day, plus `shift_code`), the
downtime `date_from`/`date_to` filters, job-cost labor `entry_date`, the analytics OEE figures, and
every analytics `period`'s "today". **Due-today / overdue / lateness stay on the company calendar
date** — they compare calendar due dates.

**The ERP's own OEE convention is unchanged.** Availability stays productive run ÷ **staffed (clocked)**
time; BREAK entries are not newly excluded and a shift's `planned_minutes` is **not** the availability
denominator. `planned_minutes` (planned production time, breaks and lunch excluded) is exposed so a
consumer can compute planned-time availability itself.

**`PUT /production-calendar`** (Admin only). Send the whole document with `expected_version` as read
(`0` before the first save) — a stale version is **409** (`This production calendar changed. Reload it
before saving.`). It is validated as a set before anything is written (**422**): `production_day_start`
and every `start`/`end` are `HH:MM`; an `end` at or before its `start` ends the next day; every shift
must start at or after the production-day start and end by the next day's start (so it belongs to the
day it starts on); `planned_minutes` ≤ the shift's length; the **active** shifts of one pattern that
start on one weekday plan at most **1440 minutes** together (shifts may overlap — parallel crews — but the
sync writes that sum as the work center's hours for the day, and a working calendar holds 0–24 h; added
2026-11-15); at most one `is_default` pattern (none is allowed: then a work center in no pattern has no
shifts); a work center in at most one pattern (listed twice in the same pattern it is one membership); unique pattern names and shift codes (case-insensitive); work centers
must be this company's; an `id` that names no existing pattern or shift is 422 (omit it to create one);
a pattern name or shift code may not start with `~` (reserved for the save's own temporary renames).
Limits: 20 patterns, 12 shifts per pattern, 500 work centers per pattern, `planned_minutes` 1–1440.
Existing patterns and shifts keep their `id`; **anything omitted is removed —
except a shift an OEE record references**, which must be retired with `is_active: false` (removing it
is 422) and whose `code` can never change (422). Retired shifts stay in the document and on historical
records but are no longer attributed. An identical document is a no-op (no version bump). A save writes
one **required** `audit_log` row (`resource_type` `production_calendar`, the whole before/after
document) in the same transaction — **503**, nothing saved, when it cannot. A save that collides with a
concurrent write to a row it changes (an OEE record that started using a shift this save removes) is
**409** `The production calendar could not be saved because a record it changes was changed at the same
time …` — the version-check text is reserved for a real version race. Every successful save (a no-op
included) broadcasts `dashboard_update` with `event: "production_calendar_updated"` to the company's
sockets; a sync commit broadcasts `event: "working_calendar_updated"` once per written work center.
Saving does **not** change working calendars; run the sync.

**Werco's configuration (worked example).** Not seeded by the migration — an Admin applies it once
(replace the `work_center_ids` with the ids of WLD-01 … WLD-06), then runs the sync dry run and commit:

```json
PUT /api/v1/production-calendar
{
  "expected_version": 0,
  "production_day_start": "05:00",
  "patterns": [
    {
      "name": "Weld shop",
      "is_default": false,
      "work_center_ids": [101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106],
      "shifts": [
        {"code": "W1", "name": "Weld 1st", "start": "05:00", "end": "15:30", "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], "planned_minutes": 600},
        {"code": "W2", "name": "Weld 2nd", "start": "15:30", "end": "02:00", "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], "planned_minutes": 600}
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Rest of shop",
      "is_default": true,
      "work_center_ids": [],
      "shifts": [
        {"code": "S1", "name": "1st shift", "start": "07:30", "end": "16:00", "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], "planned_minutes": 480},
        {"code": "S2", "name": "2nd shift", "start": "15:30", "end": "00:00", "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], "planned_minutes": 480}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**`POST /production-calendar/working-calendars/sync`** (Admin / Manager / Supervisor — the roles of
`PUT /scheduling/work-centers/{id}/calendar`). For every **active** work center covered by a pattern
(its own, or the default), the new Mon..Sun `weekly_hours` are the sum of `planned_minutes` ÷ 60 of the
active shifts **starting** each weekday — Werco weld `[20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 0, 0]`, rest of shop
`[16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 0, 0]`. `dry_run=true` (the default) writes nothing and returns, per work center,
`current_version`, `current_weekly_hours`, `new_weekly_hours`, `overrides_kept` and `changed` (a work
center with no saved calendar, `current_version` 0, is always a change) plus the production calendar's
`calendar_version`. A work center whose pattern has **no active shift** (an empty pattern, or one whose
shifts are all retired) is not covered — it is left out of the rows and never written, so a pattern
cannot zero a work center's scheduling capacity. A derived day of more than **24 hours** — only possible
for a calendar saved before the 1440-minute rule above, or written around it — is **422** on the dry run
and the commit alike, naming the work centers and their patterns, and nothing is written; the shared
writer refuses any weekly hours outside 0–24 for every caller, so the sync can never store a calendar
the scheduling editor's own `PUT` would refuse. `dry_run=false` (pass that `calendar_version` back as
`expected_version`: a different calendar version is **409**; omitting it skips the check) takes the
production calendar's own lock first — a concurrent `PUT /production-calendar` waits, so the hours and
the audit rows' `production_calendar_version` come from one calendar version — and writes every
changed work center
through the scheduling calendar's own writer (`working_calendar_service.save_working_calendar`): dated
overrides are **kept**, `version` is bumped, and one **required** `working_calendar` audit row is written
per work center (`extra_data.source` = `production_calendar_sync`; **503**, nothing saved, when one
cannot). **This moves every scheduling projection, capacity heat map and delivery prediction** for
those work centers (a center with no saved calendar was planned at its `capacity_hours_per_day`, 8 h
when unset, every day, weekends included) — review the dry run first. In the app the editor and the
sync are on Admin Settings → **Production Calendar** (`/admin/settings?tab=calendar`, Admin only; a
pattern the Admin adds there starts **not** default, and its **Default pattern** checkbox makes it the
one default or, unchecked, leaves the calendar with none — so configuring the weld shop first never
hands its shifts to every other work center); a
Manager or Supervisor runs the sync through this route or the MCP tool
`sync_working_calendars_from_shifts`.

### OEE Tracking

OEE = **Availability × Performance × Quality** per work center. **Reads** (dashboards/trends) are open
to any authenticated user in the tenant so the shop floor can view them; **writes** (auto-calculate,
records, targets) require **Admin / Manager / Supervisor**.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/oee/dashboard` | OEE per work center, plant-wide OEE, targets (`period` 7d/30d/90d/365d, or explicit `date_from`/`date_to` which take precedence) | Yes |
| GET | `/oee/trends` | OEE time-series for charts (`work_center_id`, `period`, or explicit `date_from`/`date_to`) | Yes |
| GET | `/oee/six-big-losses/{work_center_id}` | Six-big-losses breakdown | Yes |
| GET | `/oee/records` | List OEE records (filters: WC, date range, `shift` label, `shift_id`) | Yes |
| GET | `/oee/records/{record_id}` | Get one OEE record | Yes |
| POST | `/oee/calculate/{work_center_id}` | Auto-calculate the production-day (or `shift_id`) OEE record from data | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| POST | `/oee/records` | Create an OEE record (manual inputs) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| PUT | `/oee/records/{record_id}` | Update + recalculate an OEE record | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| DELETE | `/oee/records/{record_id}` | Delete an OEE record | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| GET | `/oee/targets` | List OEE targets | Yes |
| POST | `/oee/targets` | Create/update a work center's OEE target | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| PUT | `/oee/targets/{target_id}` | Update an OEE target | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| DELETE | `/oee/targets/{target_id}` | Delete an OEE target | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |

> **RBAC split (read-broad / write-restricted).** The write/mutation endpoints depend on
> `require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR])` (`OEE_WRITE_ROLES` in `app/api/endpoints/oee.py`); they
> were previously open to any authenticated user. Read endpoints depend on `get_current_user` only, so
> operators/viewers can still load dashboards. Superuser / Platform Admin bypass role checks, as
> elsewhere. See `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → OEE.
>
> **OEE writes are audited.** All OEE record/target mutations — `POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}`,
> `POST/PUT/DELETE /oee/records`, and `POST/PUT/DELETE /oee/targets` — now write a tamper-evident
> `audit_log` row (`AuditService` `log_create` / `log_update` / `log_delete`, resource types
> `oee_record` / `oee_target`). The audit row is flushed and logged **before** the terminal commit, so
> it commits atomically with the record/target. The auto-calc upsert writes one representative row per
> call. (These were RBAC-gated but unaudited prior to 2026-06-09.)

> **`POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}` (auto-calculate).** Builds (or upserts, per work center +
> date + shift) a real `OEERecord` for `record_date` — a **production day** (default: the current one;
> see Production calendar & shifts) — from the **closed** `TimeEntry` rows and reported `DowntimeEvent`
> rows **attributed** to that production day (greatest shift overlap, ties to the outgoing shift), plus
> the routing standard cycle time — on the **staffed-time** convention so it agrees with the
> `/analytics/kpis` headline. With `shift_id` only what is attributed to that shift counts, and the
> record carries `shift_id` and `shift` = the shift's code. Every entry a shift-scoped record counts is
> also in that day's whole-day record; an entry that overlaps no defined shift counts only in the
> whole-day record, so the shift records can add up to less than it. A legacy `shift` text resolves only when it equals a defined code (see "Shifts
> are defined shifts" below). The metric is unchanged:
> - **Availability** = productive-run minutes ÷ **staffed (clocked)** minutes at the WC; productive run
>   = (RUN+SETUP) minutes − **UNPLANNED** `DowntimeEvent` minutes. (Returns/stores 0 availability when
>   there is no staffed time for that WC/day.)
> - **Performance** = ideal hours ÷ productive run; ideal hours = Σ((`quantity_produced` +
>   `quantity_scrapped`) × `WorkOrderOperation.run_time_per_piece`) over RUN+REWORK — derived from the
>   routing, not a hardcoded cycle. Every piece run (including scrap) consumes a standard cycle.
> - **Quality** = good ÷ (good + scrapped); good = Σ `quantity_produced`, scrapped =
>   Σ `quantity_scrapped` over RUN+REWORK.
>
> This endpoint previously referenced `TimeEntry.start_time` / `end_time` (which do not exist) and
> returned **500** on every call; it now uses `clock_in` / `clock_out`. All queries are tenant-scoped;
> a foreign `work_center_id` returns **404**. The calculation itself lives in
> `app/services/oee_service.py` (`compute_oee_for_work_center`) — the nightly auto-calc cron runs the
> **same code** (below), so a manual trigger and the cron can never disagree on the math.

> **Shifts are defined shifts (migration 120).** `OEERecord.shift_id` references a shift of the
> production calendar; `shift` stays as the **label snapshot** (the code). Writes (`POST`/`PUT
> /oee/records`, `POST /oee/calculate`) take `shift_id` — a shift that is not this company's is **404**,
> one that is retired or not in the work center's pattern **422** (a record may keep its own retired
> shift). The legacy `shift` text is accepted only when it equals a defined code (it resolves to that
> shift); **any other text is 422**; blank means no shift. Pre-120 free-text labels (`1st`, `Day`) were
> **not** backfilled and stay readable as labels with `shift_id: null`; a `PUT` that sends a record's
> own legacy label back unchanged (with no `shift_id`) is not a shift change and is accepted, leaving
> the label as it is, so a client can echo the record to edit its other fields. A `record_date` at the
> ends of the date range (`9999-12-31`) is **422** on `POST /oee/calculate`. Responses add `shift_id` and
> `shift_name`. `GET /oee/dashboard`, `/oee/trends` and `/oee/six-big-losses` periods count back from the
> current production day.
>
> **One OEE record per (work center, date, shift) — duplicates are 409 (Lean Phase 1).** A unique
> index (`uq_oee_company_wc_date_shift`, migration `063`) enforces at most one `OEERecord` per
> company + work center + `record_date` + shift, where a **`null` shift and an empty-string shift are
> the same "no shift" key**. `POST /oee/records` for an existing key — and a `PUT /oee/records/{id}`
> whose shift change collides with an existing record — return **409 Conflict** (`"An OEE record
> already exists for this work center, date, and shift. Update the existing record instead …"`) instead
> of silently creating a double-counting duplicate. `POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}` still
> **upserts** (overwrites the existing record for the key); only a lost create race surfaces as 409.
>
> **`calculation_source` — manual vs. auto (Lean Phase 1).** Every OEE record response now carries
> `calculation_source`: **`manual`** (hand-entered via `POST /oee/records`, or the on-demand
> `POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}` trigger — a human asked for it; all pre-existing rows
> backfill to it) or **`auto`** (minted only by the nightly ARQ cron, `run_oee_auto_calc_job` at
> **02:30 UTC**, which computes each company's **previous production day** — `current_production_day
> − 1` on that company's calendar, never the container's `date.today()` — as a whole-day record per
> active work center; with a 05:00 day start, Monday's production day closes Tuesday 05:00 and is
> computed Tuesday ~20:30 Central). The cron writes whole-day records only; per-shift records come from
> `POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}?shift_id=`. The cron **never overwrites a `manual` record** — a hand-entered record for that WC/day
> (any shift) is authoritative and the cron skips the WC; `auto` records **are** recomputed by
> re-runs (idempotent refresh). Idle work centers (no closed clocked entry and no unplanned downtime
> that day) are skipped entirely — no staffed time is uncomputable, not an all-zero measurement.
> Cron-written records are audited with the system as actor. See `docs/DOCKER_PRODUCTION.md` →
> Background Jobs.

### Downtime Tracking

`app/api/endpoints/downtime.py`, mounted at `/downtime`. An event is reported against a work center
(optionally a work order) and resolved when the machine runs again; **UNPLANNED** event minutes are
the availability input to `POST /oee/calculate/{work_center_id}` above. The `date_from` / `date_to`
filters on the list, `/summary` and `/by-work-center` are inclusive **production days** (events that
started from the production-day start of `date_from` to the start of the production day after
`date_to`; local midnights when no production calendar is configured); a reversed range is **422**.
These lists put an event on the production day it **started**, while OEE attributes it like a time
entry — to the shift it overlaps most — so an event that straddles the day start (a weld stop from
04:50 to 06:50) is listed under the earlier day's `/downtime/summary` but counts against the later
day's OEE.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/downtime/` | List events (`work_center_id`, `category`, `planned_type`, `date_from` / `date_to`, `active_only`; `skip`, `limit` `1 … 5000`) | Yes |
| GET | `/downtime/active` | Unresolved events | Yes |
| GET | `/downtime/summary` | Resolved events: total / planned / unplanned hours, by category, top 15 reasons | Yes |
| GET | `/downtime/by-work-center` | Resolved-event hours per work center | Yes |
| GET | `/downtime/reason-codes` | Reason-code vocabulary (`category`, `active_only`) | Yes |
| GET | `/downtime/{id}` | One event | Yes |
| POST | `/downtime/` | Report (start) an event. **409** when a maintenance work order already holds the machine down (its downtime event is open) — see the note below | Any role except Viewer |
| POST | `/downtime/{id}/resolve` | Resolve: sets `end_time` (default now) and `duration_minutes` | Any role except Viewer |
| PUT | `/downtime/{id}` | Correct an event after the fact | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| POST | `/downtime/reason-codes` | Create a reason code | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |
| PUT | `/downtime/reason-codes/{id}` | Edit a reason code (retire with `is_active: false`) | Admin / Manager / Supervisor |

There is no delete endpoint.

> ⚠️ **Every event read returned 500, and so did create — after committing.** The `reporter` /
> `resolver` objects in `DowntimeEventResponse` declared a required `username`, but `User` has no such
> column and `reported_by` is NOT NULL, so every event failed response validation: list, get and
> active were 500s, and create, update and resolve were 500s *after* their change had committed.
> `reporter.username`
> and `resolver.username` are now optional and **always `null`** (the page's TypeScript type now says
> `username?: string | null`; nothing renders it). Read `full_name`.

> **`work_order.wo_number` now carries the number.** The nested `work_order` object read `wo_number`
> off a `WorkOrder` whose column is `work_order_number`, so it serialized `null` on every event
> (fixed 2026-11-11 with a validation alias; the wire name is unchanged). Clients should still link by
> `work_order_id` and treat the number as optional, since an API deployed before the fix sends `null`.

> **Tenancy: the work center and work order are validated, and a legacy cross-tenant link no longer
> renders.** `work_center_id` and `work_order_id` on create and on `PUT` must belong to the active
> company — a flat **404** (`"Work center not found"` / `"Work order not found"`), never 403 — and a
> soft-deleted work order is refused the same way. On `PUT` only a reference that **changes** is
> validated: re-sending the work order the event already names (a client that `PUT`s the whole object
