> back to fix `category`) is not a new selection, so it still saves after that job was soft-deleted —
> the historical record keeps naming what it named (invariant 3). The work center need not be active: downtime is
> what you record against a machine that is down. Unvalidated, the write doubled as a read, because
> the response rendered the foreign machine's name straight back. A row written before this guard is
> owned by the caller and passes every `company_id` filter, so event reads now load `work_center` /
> `work_order` under tenant loader criteria: a foreign relation reads as `null`, while
> `work_center_id` stays visible so the row can be corrected. `GET /downtime/by-work-center` filters
> the joined work center by company too, so such a row drops out of that grouping (its minutes still
> count in `/summary`). Another tenant's event is **404** on get, `PUT` and resolve, with nothing
> written. See the pre-deploy detection SQL in `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Downtime.

> **RBAC was added; there was none.** Every handler was a bare `get_current_user`, so a Viewer could
> start, correct and close the events OEE availability is computed from. Reporting (create / resolve)
> stays open to every tenant role except **Viewer**; correcting an event (`PUT`) and managing reason
> codes match the OEE write roles (Admin / Manager / Supervisor), because both rewrite OEE inputs after
> the fact. Reads stay open. See `docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md` → Downtime.

> **Every state change writes a tamper-evident `audit_log` row** (the router wrote none before):
> `downtime_event` `log_create` on create, `log_update` on `PUT`, and `log_status_change` (`active` →
> `resolved`, with `end_time`, `duration_minutes` and `resolution` in `extra_data`) on resolve;
> `downtime_reason_code` `log_create` / `log_update`. The `downtime_started` / `downtime_resolved`
> operational events are unchanged. `PUT` and resolve row-lock the event (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE OF
> downtime_events` on Postgres), so two simultaneous resolves cannot both pass the "not yet resolved"
> check. `PUT /downtime/{id}` applies an explicit allowlist
> (`work_center_id`, `work_order_id`, `category`, `planned_type`, `reason_code`, `description`,
> `resolution`) rather than a blind `setattr`; an explicit `null` on `work_center_id`, `category` or
> `planned_type` (NOT NULL columns) is **422**. A reason-code edit onto a code the tenant already has
> is **400** `"Reason code already exists"`. Reason codes are unique per company (migration `116`),
> so another tenant's identical code is accepted — see Calibration → `equipment_id` codes.

> **Maintenance work orders open and close events too (migration `124`).** Starting a work-center
> maintenance work order with `requires_shutdown` opens an event only when the machine has none open
> (it adopts an operator's open event, or shares one another shutdown work order holds), and completing
> or cancelling it resolves the event, hands it to a work order still holding the machine down, or —
> for an adopted event on a cancel — hands it back to the machine still open — see Maintenance →
> *Maintenance work order → downtime event*. Such an event carries `maintenance_work_order_id` in
> `DowntimeEventResponse` (`null` on every other event); `PUT /downtime/{id}` cannot change it (it is
> not in the allowlist). It can still be resolved here like any other event; the maintenance work
> order then has nothing left to resolve and, on complete, records the resolved minutes. Create and
> resolve here run through the same `app/services/downtime_service.py` helpers. One create rule is new:
> `POST /downtime/` refuses **409** a report on a machine a maintenance work order is holding down
> (*"{machine} is already down for maintenance work order {MWO} (downtime event DT-{id} is open), so
> this stoppage is already being recorded. …"*) — a second open event would count the stoppage twice.

### Users (Admin)

> **Department is a pick list (2026-11-23).** `department` on `POST /users/`, `PUT /users/{id}`,
> `POST /users/{id}/approve`, `POST /auth/register` and the user import must be one of Purchasing,
> Inventory, Sales, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Production, Other (any case or spacing; the
> canonical spelling is stored) or blank -- else **422** *"Department must be one of: Purchasing,
> Inventory, Sales, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Production, Other (or left blank)."* Notifications
> match departments by exact name, which is why. A `PUT` that re-sends a user's existing legacy value
> unchanged is accepted; `GET /users/departments` lists those values for correction. No migration.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/users/` | List all users | Admin / Manager |
| POST | `/users/` | Create user | Admin |
| POST | `/auth/register` | Alternate tenant-user creation path with the same role policy | Admin |
| POST | `/users/import-csv` | Import CSV/XLSX users; existing dry-run and per-row error contracts apply. A `department` not on the pick list is that row's error | Admin |
| GET | `/users/departments` | The fixed Department pick list and every user whose stored Department is not on it: `{"departments": ["Purchasing", "Inventory", "Sales", "Quality", "Maintenance", "Shipping", "Production", "Other"], "unlisted": [{"id", "name", "employee_id", "is_active", "department"}]}`. Writes nothing | Admin |
| PUT | `/users/{id}` | Update user. `is_active: false` also revokes every live API token the user holds (reason `user deactivated`, audited) — see [API tokens](#api-tokens-bots-and-mcp-clients) — and the user's export authorization (one `EXPORT_AUTHORIZATION_REVOKE` row). A role change into Admin, Manager or Quality from any other role clears the user's floor PIN and, if they had one, requires a new one from an Admin (see the floor PIN note below) | Admin |
| POST | `/users/{id}/approve` | Approve a pending tenant account with a tenant role. Approving into Admin, Manager or Quality clears any floor PIN the account carried and, if it had one, requires a new one from an Admin | Admin |
| POST | `/users/{id}/reset-password` | Reset another account's password | Admin |
| POST | `/users/{id}/activate` | Reactivate an account, without restoring revoked API tokens | Admin |
| DELETE | `/users/{id}` | Deactivate user (sets `is_active=false`; cannot deactivate yourself). Revokes every live API token the user holds in the same transaction (reason `user deactivated`, one `API_TOKEN_REVOKED` audit trail each); the response carries `api_tokens_revoked`. Also revokes the user's export authorization (one `EXPORT_AUTHORIZATION_REVOKE` row, reason `user deactivated`; `export_authorization_revoked` in the response). Reactivation (`POST /users/{id}/activate`) restores the account, never a token or an export authorization | Admin |
| POST | `/users/{id}/unlock` | Clear failed-login lockout (not a floor-PIN lock — see `POST /users/{user_id}/floor-pin/unlock`) | Admin |
| PUT | `/users/{user_id}/floor-pin` | Set or reset the user's floor PIN for badge sign-on. Body `{"pin"}` → the user record. Also clears any PIN lock and the wrong-PIN count. See the floor PIN note below | Admin; a Manager for Operator / Supervisor / Shipping / Viewer accounts only. Signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |
| DELETE | `/users/{user_id}/floor-pin` | Clear the user's floor PIN and any PIN lock → the user record. Idempotent | Admin; a Manager for Operator / Supervisor / Shipping / Viewer accounts only. Signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |
| POST | `/users/{user_id}/floor-pin/unlock` | Lift a floor-PIN lock early (every lock also expires on its own) and reset the wrong-PIN count, keeping the PIN → the user record. Idempotent | Admin; a Manager for Operator / Supervisor / Shipping / Viewer accounts only. Signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |
| PUT | `/users/{id}/export-authorization` | Body `{"export_authorized": bool, "reason"}`; grant or revoke the only thing that opens an `export_controlled` document. Refuses any API token **403**; not an MCP tool | Admin |
| GET | `/users/mention-search` | People to @mention in a comment: active members of the active company by name, `{id, display_name}` only (never email, role or phone). Documented under [Comments and watchers](#comments-and-watchers) | Any signed-in member of the company (a read-only API token is **403**: `Users` tag) |

> **User writes are Admin-only; the list read is Admin / Manager.** `GET /users/` (and
> `GET /users/{id}`) are `require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER])`; `POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE` are
> `require_role([ADMIN])`, except the three floor-PIN routes (Admin, or a Manager within a role
> scope, below). The shared tenant-account policy covers **both** create routes,
> update, approval, and CSV/XLSX import. `role = platform_admin` returns **400** on create/update/
> approval and a per-row error on import, even for a platform caller. Tenant Admin remains an
> assignable role. Creation derives the active company server-side and forces `is_superuser=false`;
> extra body/import fields cannot grant platform authority or choose another company. On
> `PUT /users/{id}`, changing one's own role remains **400** (`"You cannot change your own role"`).
>
> **Existing platform accounts are protected too.** Update, approval, password reset,
> activation, deactivation and unlock of a stored Platform Admin or superuser require a stored
> platform principal (**403** for a tenant Admin); foreign-company target ids remain **404**.
> An Admin-held API token does not gain platform authority.
>
> Creation, update, approval, password reset, activation, deactivation and unlock require audit
> persistence in the same transaction (**503**, `"Unable to save audit record"`, with rollback
> on audit loss). Deactivation includes the companion API-token revocation rows in that guarantee.
> CSV/XLSX import preserves its per-row transaction/error result: a failed row creates no account,
> while previously successful rows remain committed. `/auth/register` records the initiating Admin
> as actor and the new account as target. Unchanged account updates and unlocks with no lock state
> do not add audit rows. Passwords
> and hashes are never included. Other self-service/auth audit paths retain their existing
> behavior; this is not a global replacement of best-effort logging. See
> [docs/RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#users).
>
> **`POST /users/{id}/unlock` — the admin remedy for the failed-login lockout.** After 5 failed
> logins the auth endpoints set `locked_until` 30 minutes out and refuse further attempts with
> `"Account is locked. Please contact administrator."`; unlock resets `failed_login_attempts` to 0
> and clears `locked_until` so the user can log in immediately. Tenant-scoped (an id in another
> company is **404**) and **idempotent**: unlocking a user with no lock state returns **200** and
> writes **no** audit row. The audit row is truthful about the prior state: clearing a lock still
> **in force** (`locked_until` in the future) records a `STATUS_CHANGE` (`locked` → `unlocked`)
> with the prior `failed_login_attempts` / `locked_until` in `extra_data`; clearing only
> **residual** state (an expired lock, or failed attempts that never reached 5) records an
> `UPDATE` of the two fields instead — no lockout status actually changed.
> To let the admin UI surface the lock, `locked_until` is exposed on the **inline user-management
> `UserResponse`** (`app/api/endpoints/users.py`) only — every route serializing it is self-scoped
> (`GET /users/me`) or Admin/Manager-gated; general user serialization
> (`app.schemas.user.UserResponse`, the per-domain summaries) still omits lockout state.
>
> **`PUT /users/{id}/export-authorization` — who may open export-controlled documents**
> (AS9100D 7.5.3.1, migration `131`). An export-authorized user may open `export_controlled`
> documents of their **own** company; nobody else may, whatever their role, Admin, superuser and
> Platform Admin included, and a platform account's grant never carries into a tenant it switches
> into (see
> [Documents → Restricted and export-controlled documents](#restricted-and-export-controlled-documents-as9100d-7531)).
> Body `{"export_authorized": true|false, "reason": "..."}`; the reason is required (1–2000
> characters, not blank).
>
> - Admin only. Any API token, whatever its role or scope, is refused **403** before anything is
>   read, and the route is not an MCP tool, so a person's own JWT cannot reach it through an agent.
> - The target must be in the active company (**404** otherwise), and a stored Platform Admin or
>   superuser target needs a platform principal (**403**), as on `PUT /users/{id}`.
> - **409** when the user is already in the requested state, judged on the row-locked user, so two
>   concurrent grants (or a grant racing a revoke) serialize.
> - A grant stamps `export_authorized_at` / `export_authorized_by`; a revoke clears both. An Admin
>   may grant their own authorization; it is audited like any other grant.
> - A required audit row (`EXPORT_AUTHORIZATION_GRANT` or `EXPORT_AUTHORIZATION_REVOKE`, resource
>   `user`) with the old and new value and the reason, in the same transaction (**503**, nothing
>   saved, if it cannot be written). A revoke's row also keeps the grant it ended
>   (`revoked_grant`: when and by whom).
>
> The flag is not on the create, update or import bodies; this verb and deactivation are its only
> writers. The management `UserResponse` (list, detail, `/users/me` and the write responses) carries
> `export_authorized`, `export_authorized_at` and `export_authorized_by`. A new user, and every user
> after the migration, starts unauthorized.
>
> **Deactivation revokes it.** Both deactivation verbs (`DELETE /users/{id}` and `PUT /users/{id}`
> with `is_active: false`) clear the flag and its stamps in the same transaction, with a companion
> required `EXPORT_AUTHORIZATION_REVOKE` row (reason `user deactivated`, `source: deactivation`,
> `revoked_grant`), like the API-token sweep. `DELETE /users/{id}` reports it as
> `export_authorization_revoked`. Reactivation restores the account and no authorization: an Admin
> grants it again, with a reason.

> **Floor PIN — `PUT` / `DELETE /users/{user_id}/floor-pin`, `POST /users/{user_id}/floor-pin/unlock`
> (AS9100D 8.5.2, migration `130`).** The second factor on badge sign-on
> ([Badge sign-on and the floor PIN](#badge-sign-on-and-the-floor-pin-as9100d-852)). All three are
> checked in this order: the role gate (`require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER])`; Superuser / Platform Admin
> pass as everywhere); **any API token 403** with `"A floor PIN, and the company's badge-sign-in PIN
> policy, are set by a person signed in to the app, not an API token: credential administration is a
> person's act."` before anything is read; the target in the active company (**404** otherwise); a
> stored Platform Admin / superuser target needs a platform principal (**403**, as for password
> reset and unlock); and **a Manager may manage PINs only for Operator, Supervisor, Shipping and
> Viewer accounts** (**403** `"A Manager can manage floor PINs only for Operator, Supervisor, Shipping
> and Viewer accounts. Ask an Admin to manage this account's PIN."`). A badge plus a PIN the caller
> chose is a sign-on, so an Admin's, a Manager's (their own included) or a Quality user's PIN needs
> an Admin. Together with the promotion rule and the session binding below, nobody below Admin can
> take over an identity that approves, dispositions or signs off quality. See
> [RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md → Users](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#users).
>
> - **PIN rules** (`app/core/floor_pin.py::validate_floor_pin`), each a **422** whose `detail` is
>   the rule's plain text and never the PIN: digits only, 4 to 6 long (`"A floor PIN must be 4 to 6
>   digits, with no letters, spaces or symbols."`); not one digit repeated (`"A floor PIN cannot be
>   the same digit repeated."`); not a straight run up or down such as 1234 or 4321 (`"A floor PIN
>   cannot be a straight run of digits counting up or down."`); not the user's own employee-ID
>   digits or their badge's last 4, 5 or 6 digits (`"A floor PIN cannot be the user's own employee
>   ID or the last digits of their badge."`).
> - **`PUT`** stores a bcrypt hash, stamps a new `floor_pin_set_at`, and clears the wrong-PIN count,
>   any PIN lock and the `floor_pin_reset_required` flag. Required audit row
>   `FLOOR_PIN_SET` (`resource_type=user`; `extra_data`: `source: "admin_set"`,
>   `replaced_existing_pin`, `cleared_pin_lockout`, `cleared_pin_reset_required`), never the PIN or its hash; **503** `"Unable to save audit
>   record"` and nothing saved if it cannot be written. The new set time **ends every
>   `["badge", "pin"]` session of that user** at its next request or refresh (**401**
>   `floor_pin_reauth_required`): they verified the old PIN.
> - **`DELETE`** clears the hash, the set date, the count, any lock and the reset flag. From then
>   on the badge signs in without a PIN, unless the company requires one (then **403**
>   `floor_pin_not_set` until a new PIN is set); on a promoted user that is an explicit decision to
>   allow badge-only sign-on. It ends the user's badge + PIN sessions the same way. Required audit
>   row `FLOOR_PIN_CLEARED` (`had_pin`, `cleared_pin_lockout`, `cleared_pin_reset_required`). A user with no PIN and no lock or reset state is returned
>   unchanged, with no row.
> - **`POST …/floor-pin/unlock`** lifts a lock in force (`floor_pin_locked_until` in the future,
>   any tier) early and resets the wrong-PIN count, keeping the PIN, so the person can sign in with
>   it at once; sessions that verified it carry on. Every lock also expires on its own; the unlock is
>   how an Admin answers a `floor_pin.lockout` alert sooner. Required audit row `FLOOR_PIN_UNLOCKED`
>   (`source: "admin_unlock"`, the prior `floor_pin_locked_until` and `floor_pin_failed_attempts`;
>   **503**, nothing saved, if it cannot be written). With no lock in force it answers **200** with
>   the user record and writes nothing (the count is left as it is).
> - **Response fields.** The inline user-management `UserResponse` (every `/users` route that
>   returns a user record, `GET /users/me` included) carries `has_floor_pin` (bool),
>   `floor_pin_set_at`, `floor_pin_locked_until` (UTC `Z`; a future value means a lock in force, and
>   is always its end) and `floor_pin_reset_required` (bool; a promotion cleared the PIN). Never the
>   PIN or its hash. The Users page shows them as the **Floor PIN** column for Admin and Manager:
>   *New PIN needed (role changed)*, *Locked* with its end time, *Set* with the date, or *Not set*.
>   Above the table it lists every floor PIN currently locked, each with its end time and the way to
>   unlock it (the `floor_pin.lockout` alert lands there). The Manage action opens the set / reset /
>   clear dialog, which carries **Unlock** while the PIN is locked; on a row the caller may not
>   manage, the action is replaced by *Admin only* (or *Platform admin only*).
> - **A promotion clears the PIN and requires a new one.** A role change into Admin, Manager or
>   Quality from any other role, on `PUT /users/{id}` or `POST /users/{id}/approve`, clears the
>   user's floor PIN (hash, set date, wrong-PIN count and any lock) in the same transaction, and
>   that route's required audit row carries `extra_data.floor_pin_cleared_on_promotion: true`. If the
>   user **had** a PIN it also sets `floor_pin_reset_required` (marked `floor_pin_reset_required:
>   true` on the same row): both badge routes then answer **403** `floor_pin_reset_required`
>   ("Your role changed. Ask an Admin to set a new floor PIN."), **whatever the company policy**,
>   until an Admin sets a new PIN or clears it, so the promotion never downgrades the badge to
>   badge-only. The user's existing badge + PIN sessions end at their next request, since the PIN
>   they verified is gone. A PIN a Manager chose for a floor account therefore never survives into a
>   judgment role, as a PIN or as a session. A move between those three roles, a demotion and a
>   move between floor roles keep the PIN.

> **Password-strength policy — enforced server-side on every password-set path.** A password set
> through `POST /users/` (create), `POST /users/{id}/reset-password`, or the self-service
> `POST /users/change-password` must satisfy exactly **two** rules: it must be **≥ 12 characters**,
> and it must not contain a **common weak substring** (case-insensitive) from the blocklist in
> `_COMMON_PASSWORD_PATTERNS` — keyboard walks, perennial top-100 passwords, digit runs, and the
> shop's own name (`werco`, `wercomfg`). A violation returns **422**; the blocklist message is
> `"Password contains a common word or pattern that is too easy to guess"`. There are **no
> character-class (composition) requirements** — the uppercase / lowercase / digit / special-character
> rules were removed on 2026-07-29 per NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2 (length + blocklist over composition),
> and the blocklist was expanded from 6 entries to ~37 in the same change. A passphrase such as
> `correct horse battery staple` is now accepted, where the old rules rejected it. The 12-character
> minimum is unchanged and is additionally enforced as `Field(min_length=12)` on the request schemas.
> The **same policy** — the shared `validate_password_strength` (`app/schemas/user.py`) —
> also governs `POST /auth/register` (admin create), public self-registration
> `POST /auth/register-public`. Both company-creation routes were **removed** on 2026-11-23: the
> unauthenticated self-registration route `POST /companies/register` (now 404) and platform-admin
> `POST /platform/companies` (now 405), so no first-admin `admin_password` path remains. The user CSV import
> (`POST /users/import-csv`) applies the same check to **user-supplied** passwords **per row** (a weak
> password fails only that row, `reason` = `"Weak password: …"`); operator **auto-generated**
> passwords (for badge/employee-ID logins) satisfy the policy by construction and are **exempt**.

> **Changing your own password — `POST /users/change-password`** (body `current_password`,
> `new_password`; any signed-in person, on My Settings → Password). People only: every API token
> and every crew-station badge or station token is refused **403** `PASSWORD_CHANGE_PEOPLE_ONLY`
> before the body's passwords are read, and the route is not an MCP tool (`EXCLUDED_OPERATIONS`).
> **400** `Current password is incorrect`; **422** on the policy above. The new hash,
> `password_changed_at` (also stamped by the admin `POST /users/{id}/reset-password`) and the
> `PASSWORD_CHANGE` audit row (`extra_data.source = "self_service"`, no password or hash) commit
> as one transaction: an audit write that fails rolls the change back (**503**
> `Unable to save audit record`). The change does **not** end other signed-in sessions:
> `POST /auth/refresh` does not read `password_changed_at`, so another session keeps refreshing
> until it signs out or sits unused for the 7-day idle window.

### User self-service (My Settings)

Self-scoped profile + notification settings for the signed-in user. **No role gate beyond
authentication** — every route reads/writes only `current_user` and never accepts a user id, so no
caller can reach another user's phone or preferences. Backing UI: **My Settings** (`/settings`, all
roles). See [docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md](NOTIFICATIONS.md#sms-channel-twilio).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/users/me` | Current user's own profile (the one general route exposing `phone`) | Any authenticated user (self) |
| PUT | `/users/me/phone` | Set or clear your own phone number (stored E.164, audited) | Any authenticated user (self) |
| GET | `/users/me/notification-preferences` | Your **effective** per-event channel matrix | Any authenticated user (self) |
| PUT | `/users/me/notification-preferences` | Save your **SMS** opt-ins (audited) | Any authenticated user (self) |
| POST | `/users/me/test-sms` | Send a test SMS to your own number — **`3/minute` per IP + `3/hour` per user** | Any authenticated user (self) |
| POST | `/users/change-password` | Change your own password (My Settings → Password). Required audit; does not end other sessions — see [Changing your own password](#users-admin) above | Any signed-in person (self). Every API token and badge / station token **403**; not an MCP tool |

> **`PUT /users/me/phone`** — body `{ "phone": "512-555-0100" }` (or `{ "phone": null }` / `""` to
> clear); `phone` is `max_length` 32. The number is parsed against `SMS_DEFAULT_REGION` (default
> `US`) and **normalized to E.164** before storage, so the SMS transport never has to guess a
> country code. An unparseable/invalid number returns **400** (`"Invalid phone number: …"`) rather
> than being stored and failing later at send time. Returns the full `UserResponse`. The change is
> written to the tamper-evident audit log (`extra_data.source = "self_service"`) — the phone is the
> destination of every SMS alert, so a silent redirect would be an audit gap. A no-op change
> (same number) short-circuits without an audit row. The **admin** paths `POST /users/` and
> `PUT /users/{id}` accept and normalize `phone` the same way (it was previously a phantom schema
> field that was silently dropped).
>
> **`GET /users/me/notification-preferences`** returns the channel map the dispatcher **would apply
> right now** — catalog defaults where the user has saved nothing, plus any mandatory channel forced
> on — resolved through the dispatcher's own `channels_from_pref`, so the settings UI can never
> disagree with what actually gets sent. It is **read-only and non-creating**: a user who has never
> saved preferences gets defaults and **no** `NotificationPreference` row is written.
>
> **What makes that a mechanism rather than a promise:** one shared resolver, with every input it
> needs passed in rather than defaulted. `channels_from_pref` takes an `email_deliverable` flag — the
> dispatcher forces `in_app` on beside a **mandatory `email`** channel when the recipient's address
> is an undeliverable placeholder (see [docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md](NOTIFICATIONS.md#channels)) — and this
> endpoint threads `email_deliverable_for_user(current_user)` into it.
> `_effective_preferences(pref, user)` takes the user as a **required** parameter for exactly that
> reason: left at the resolver's `True` default the screen rendered a hypothetical recipient with a
> working mailbox, so a badge-only user who muted `account.locked` was shown `['email']` while the
> dispatcher resolved `['email', 'in_app']` and filed an in-app row. Same function, same inputs, both
> sides.
> ```json
> {
>   "preferences": {
>     "wo.blocker_created": { "digest": false, "email": true, "in_app": true, "sms": false }
>   },
>   "has_saved_preferences": false,
>   "phone": "+15125550100",
>   "sms_egress_enabled": false,
>   "sms_configured": true
> }
> ```
> `sms_egress_enabled` (the company kill switch) / `sms_configured` (server-side Twilio config) /
> `phone` are what the UI uses to explain why an SMS toggle would currently be inert.
>
> **`PUT /users/me/notification-preferences`** — body
> `{ "preferences": { "<event_key>": { "sms": true }, … } }`, max 200 events. **Scope: the `sms`
> channel only.** Both models are `extra="forbid"`, so a payload carrying `in_app` / `email` /
> `digest` fails loudly with **422** instead of silently dropping channels this endpoint does not
> yet own (the full matrix is PR 3). Errors: an unknown `event_key` → **400**
> (`"Unknown notification event(s): …"`); enabling `sms` on an event that is not `sms_eligible` →
> **400** (`"SMS is not available for event(s): …"`). Events the user has never touched are seeded
> from catalog defaults before the `sms` bit is applied, and the stored row keeps the full
> `{in_app, email, sms, digest}` shape per event. The mandatory channel is **not** baked into the
> stored row — the dispatcher re-applies it at send time. Audited as a
> `notification_preference` update. Returns the same response shape as the `GET`.
>
> **`POST /users/me/test-sms`** — no body. Sends `Werco: test message - SMS alerts are configured
> for your account.` to **`current_user.phone`**; the destination can never be supplied by the
> caller, so this cannot be used to message an arbitrary number. It runs through the same
> `sms_service` path as real notifications (so the `allow_sms_egress` kill switch is enforced
> fail-closed) and writes a `notification_logs` row (`event_type = "sms.test"`) **before** the
> outbound call, so the attempt is recorded even if the process dies mid-flight.
>
> Bounded **twice**, because it is the one authenticated route that spends carrier money per call:
> **`3/minute` per IP** (`ENDPOINT_RATE_LIMITS` in `main.py`) and **`3/hour` per user**
> (`SMS_TEST_HOURLY_CAP_PER_USER`, `reserve_test_sms_quota`). The per-IP limiter alone is not
> sufficient — it keys on address, so one account multiplies it by rotating egress IPs, and it is
> disabled entirely wherever `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false`. The per-user budget is separate from
> `SMS_HOURLY_CAP_PER_USER`, so testing never consumes the critical-alert allowance.
>
> Any phone number appearing in a provider/validation error is **masked** before it is written to
> `notification_logs.error` (`***0134`), because that field is served by
> `GET /notifications/logs` to roles that cannot see `phone`. The HTTP `detail` returned to the
> caller is unmasked — they own the number.
>
> | Status | When |
> |---|---|
> | **200** `{ status, sid, provider_status, detail }` | Sent (`status = "sent"`), **or** Twilio unconfigured on the server (`status = "skipped"`, `detail` explains) |
> | **400** | No phone on file; company SMS egress disabled; the stored number is invalid |
> | **429** | Per-user hourly test budget exhausted (`3/hour`) |
> | **503** | The quota backend (Redis) is unavailable — refuses rather than sending unmetered, and deliberately does *not* report this as a limit the user hit |
> | **502** | Provider rejected the message, or the provider was unreachable |

### Personal dashboard layout

Which widgets the signed-in user's dashboard (`/`) shows, in what order and, for panels, at what
width — saved **per user, per active company**. Presentation only: a layout grants nothing, and
every endpoint a widget reads enforces its own authorization. **No role gate**: like
`/users/me/*`, the routes read and write only the caller's own row and never accept a user id.
Backing UI: Dashboard → **Customize** ([docs/DASHBOARD.md → Customizing the dashboard](DASHBOARD.md#customizing-the-dashboard)).
Source: `app/api/endpoints/dashboard_layouts.py`, `app/services/dashboard_layout_service.py`,
`app/schemas/dashboard_layout.py`; table `dashboard_layouts` (migration 118).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/dashboard/layout` | Your saved layout for the active company, or `layout: null` for the default. Never creates a row | Any authenticated user (self); kiosk badge tokens are refused by their path fence |
| PUT | `/dashboard/layout` | Replace your layout (version compare-and-swap, required audit) | Interactive person in a writable company (self) |
| POST | `/dashboard/layout/reset` | Return to the default, keeping the row and its audit history | Interactive person in a writable company (self) |

All three return the same body:

```json
{
  "company_id": 1,
  "version": 3,
  "layout": {
    "format_version": 1,
    "widgets": [
      { "id": "attention", "size": null },
      { "id": "kpi.overdue", "size": null },
      { "id": "capacity_overview", "size": "wide" },
      { "id": "quality_pulse", "size": "half" }
    ]
  },
  "updated_at": "2026-11-11T15:04:05Z",
  "can_edit": true
}
```

- `layout: null` is the stock default. With no saved row the answer is `version: 0`,
  `layout: null`, `updated_at: null`.
- `widgets` is in render order; `size` `null` means the widget's own default width.
- `can_edit` says whether **this session** may save (see Credentials below).

**`PUT /dashboard/layout`** — body `{ "expected_company_id": 1, "expected_version": 3, "layout":
{ "format_version": 1, "widgets": [ { "id": "kpi.overdue" }, { "id": "presence", "size": "full" } ] } }`.
**`POST /dashboard/layout/reset`** — body `{ "expected_company_id": 1, "expected_version": 3 }`.
Input is strict (**422**): every object is `extra="forbid"` (a `layout` sent to reset is refused);
`expected_company_id` must be > 0 and `expected_version` ≥ 0 (0 = first save); `layout.widgets` is
**required**, so `layout: {}` is a 422 while `widgets: []` saves a deliberately **empty** dashboard;
at most 64 entries, ids unique; `id` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]{0,63}$`; `size` is `null` or matches
`^[a-z][a-z_]{0,23}$`; `format_version` may be omitted and must otherwise be `1`.

**Shape, not membership.** The server accepts any well-formed id and size. The widget catalog and
the width vocabulary belong to the SPA, which deploys separately from the API: the SPA ignores an id
it does not know (and drops it on its next save) and renders an unknown width at the widget's
default.

**Write semantics.**

- **Check order:** `expected_company_id` ≠ the active company → **409** → credential and company
  check → **403** → a per-user advisory lock and row lock → `expected_version` ≠ the current version
  (0 with no row) → **409** → no-op check → write.
- **Compare-and-swap.** The first save creates version 1; every real change increments it. Send the
  version from the last response, and after an uncertain response reload rather than overwrite. On
  PostgreSQL the per-user advisory lock serializes two first saves, so the second sees version 1 and
  gets the stale-version **409**; the unique (company, user) key is the backstop, and a save it
  refuses answers the same **409**.
- **No-op.** A current-version `PUT` whose layout is identical to the stored JSON (the raw row, not
  its normalized view), a reset with no saved row, and a reset of a row already at the default write
  nothing — no version bump, no audit row — and return the current state. The version check still
  applies to them.
- **Reset is the only way back to the default.** It stores the empty object (served as
  `layout: null`) and increments the version; it does not delete the row. No `PUT` can produce the
  default.
- **Required audit.** Each real change writes one audit row in the same transaction: resource type
  `dashboard_layout`, action `CREATE` for the first save and `UPDATE` afterwards (reset included),
  identifier `Employee <user id> dashboard layout`, `old_values` `{version, layout}` (the stored JSON
  verbatim) on `UPDATE`, `new_values` `{version, layout}` (`{}` for a reset), and `extra_data`
  `{source: "dashboard_layout", reset_to_default: true|false}`. If the audit row cannot be written
  the change rolls back and the caller gets **503**.
- **Stored rows are read leniently and never cause a 500.** Every response reads the stored row
  through one normalizer: a non-object root, a `format_version` other than the integer 1, or a
  missing or non-list `widgets` serves the default (and logs a warning); an entry with an invalid id
  is dropped and an invalid size becomes `null`; duplicates keep the first; at most 64 are kept; a
  non-empty stored list from which nothing survives serves the default, while a stored empty list
  stays an empty dashboard. Writes compare and audit the **raw** stored JSON, so a row written by
  another schema can always be saved over or reset.

**Credentials.**

| Caller | GET | PUT / reset |
|---|---|---|
| A person's own session (access JWT), any role, in an active company they belong to | 200, `can_edit: true` | Allowed |
| Platform Admin or superuser in a writable switched company | 200, `can_edit: true` | Allowed (their own row in that company) |
| Long-lived API token (including through the MCP door) | 200, `can_edit: false` | **403** `Save your dashboard layout from an interactive account in a writable company.` |
| Read-only company context | 200, `can_edit: false` | **403** from the read-only fence, `Read-only company context cannot modify data` |
| Kiosk badge token (`scope="kiosk"`) | **403** (path fence) | **403** (path fence) |

The three routes are also MCP tools — `get_my_dashboard_layout`, `save_my_dashboard_layout` and
`reset_my_dashboard_layout` — and run as the caller, so an agent on an API token can read the layout
but not change it.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| **200** | Read; saved; reset; or a no-op |
| **401** | Not authenticated |
| **403** | The session may not save (table above), or a kiosk badge token on any verb |
| **409** | `Active company changed. Reopen the dashboard in the intended company.` — `expected_company_id` is not the active company. `Your dashboard layout changed in another tab. Reload it before saving.` — stale `expected_version`, or a lost first-save race |
| **422** | Invalid body (rules above) |
| **503** | `Your dashboard layout could not be saved because its audit record failed; nothing was changed. Retry.` |

**Deploy skew.** The SPA (Vercel) and the API (Railway) deploy independently. An SPA that reaches an
API without these routes gets **404** (or 405), renders the default dashboard and hides Customize; an
older SPA never calls them. Adding a widget to the SPA needs no API change. Migration 118 adds the
table and no environment variable.

### Admin Settings (Admin)

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/admin/settings/audit-log` | Settings/quote-config change history (filterable, up to 1yr) | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/email-recipients` | Email types, selections, missing defaults and the company's user directory. Each event also carries who it **actually reaches** today: `audience_source` (`selected` = the saved or shipped list, exclusive; `automatic` = the catalog's roles or departments with each person's own email choice applied), `reaches_user_ids` (deliverable addresses only), `depends_on_record` (the event also reaches people derived from the record, e.g. its creator) and `reaches_nobody` | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/email-recipients/{event_key}` | Set one email type's recipients (`{"user_ids": [...]}`; `null` restores the default). **400** on an unknown email type, or on a user who is not an active user of this company with a deliverable address | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/work-center-rates` | Work centers with their hourly rates (`include_inactive` default false) | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/work-center-rates/{work_center_id}` | Set a work center's hourly (labor costing) rate. **404** on another company's work center | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/work-center-types` | Allowed work-center types, plus the ones in use | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/work-center-types` | Replace the allowed work-center types. **400** if it would remove a type still in use | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/role-permissions` | Every role's effective permissions (company override or default), plus the permission catalog | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/role-permissions/{role}` | One role's effective permissions and `is_customized` | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/role-permissions/{role}` | Replace a role's permissions with a company override (body: JSON array of permission keys). **400** on an unknown role or permission; **503** if its required audit row cannot be written (see note) | Admin |
| POST | `/admin/settings/role-permissions/{role}/reset` | Drop the company override so the role reverts to its defaults; a role with no override is a no-op. **503** as above | Admin |

> **Settings-audit tenancy:** `GET /admin/settings/audit-log` reads the `SettingsAuditLog` trail
> (admin / quote-config changes) and is **scoped to the caller's active company**
> (`get_current_company_id`). Writes to this trail are tagged with that same active company, so a
> platform admin's changes attribute to the company they have switched into — matching the
> `/audit/*` (`AuditLog`) attribution. This is a separate trail from `/audit/*` and is **not** part
> of the tamper-evident hash chain: it is the Admin page's settings-history display table, a plain
> mutable tenant table.
>
> **Admin-settings writes are on the tamper-evident chain too (2026-11-05).** Every write that adds a
> `SettingsAuditLog` row now also writes the authoritative `audit_log` row (`GET /audit/`) in the same
> transaction:
>
> | Write | `audit_log` row | Failure posture |
> |---|---|---|
> | `PUT /role-permissions/{role}`, `POST /role-permissions/{role}/reset` | `role_permission` UPDATE, identifier = the role; old/new `permissions` + `is_customized`; `extra_data` `action` (`update` / `reset`), `granted`, `revoked` | **Required** — `log_required` inside `atomic_security_write`. If the audit row cannot be written the RBAC change is rolled back and the caller gets **503** `"Unable to save audit record"`, the same posture as account administration |
> | `PUT /work-center-rates/{work_center_id}` | `work_center` UPDATE (the resource type `PUT /work-centers/{id}` writes), identifier = the work-center code, `extra_data.source = "admin_settings"` | Best-effort |
> | `PUT /email-recipients/{event_key}` | `notification_email_recipients` UPDATE, identifier = the event key; old/new `user_ids` are the **effective** audience before and after (a `null` request records the default it restores, never `null`) + `uses_default` (a default audience is not an explicit selection). A save that changes neither writes no row, here or in the settings history | Best-effort |
> | `PUT /work-center-types` | `work_center_types` UPDATE; old/new `types` | Best-effort |
>
> Refusals (bad role, unknown permission, foreign work center or user, unknown email type, removing an
> in-use type) write neither row. A first customization of a role's permissions now records the new
> override's real id in both records; the settings history used to log `entity_id` `0` for it.

> **`POST /admin/settings/seed-database` ships no default credentials (Admin-only).** The one-time
> bootstrap seed **no-ops once any user exists** (returns `{"status": "already_seeded"}`); on an
> empty instance it creates the initial admin + sample users with **strong, per-user passwords
> generated at runtime** (policy-compliant by construction) and returns them **once** in the response
> `credentials` map for the calling admin to distribute and rotate. No `admin123` / `password123` or
> other hardcoded/default password is used anywhere on this path.

### Company (self-service)

The active company's own profile and self-managed settings. Mounted under `/companies`.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/companies/me` | Get the active company (includes `allow_ai_egress`, `allow_sms_egress`, `require_floor_pin`, and `user_count`) | Any authenticated user |
| PUT | `/companies/me` | Update the active company's settings | Admin |
| PUT | `/companies/me/ai-egress` | Toggle the company's **AI document-extraction egress kill switch** (`allow_ai_egress`), which also gates every AI-external API token | Admin, signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |
| PUT | `/companies/me/sms-egress` | Toggle the company's **notification-SMS egress kill switch** (`allow_sms_egress`) | Admin, signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |
| PUT | `/companies/me/floor-pin-policy` | Turn the company's **"require a PIN for badge sign-in"** policy (`require_floor_pin`) on or off | Admin, signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |

> **`allow_ai_egress` is the AI-egress CUI kill switch (default OFF).** It gates **all** outbound
> AI document-extraction egress to the Anthropic API (the AI analogue of `allow_carrier_egress` /
> `allow_print_egress`), enforced fail-closed at the shared LLM client. `PUT /companies/me/ai-egress`
> takes `{ "allow_ai_egress": boolean }` and returns the updated `CompanyResponse`; the flip is
> recorded on the tamper-evident audit trail as both a field update and an
> `ai_egress_enabled` / `ai_egress_disabled` **status change**, both **required** evidence in the
> flip's own transaction: if either row cannot be written the flip is rolled back and the answer
> is **503** `"The audit record for this AI egress change could not be saved; nothing was changed.
> Retry."`. Sending the value the company already has writes nothing. While OFF, AI features (PO/quote,
> BOM, QMS, routing, laser-nest PDF extraction, Copilot, NL search) **degrade gracefully** — no
> request leaves the boundary (laser-nest extraction falls back to filename-only). It is also the
> per-company switch for applying AI recommendations (owner ruling 3, 2026-11-05): while OFF,
> `POST /ai/recommendations/{id}/apply` is refused **403** and nothing an AI recommendation proposes
> is applied — see [AI Recommendations](#ai-recommendations-action-inbox). It also gates the
> **AI-external API token**, the credential an outside AI connector such as Claude holds
> (Claude-plugin brief P0.3, 2026-11-13). While it is OFF, such a token is refused **403** on every
> API route and at the MCP door, `initialize` and `tools/list` included. Turning it ON therefore
> also opens that connector: do it only once the empowered official has cleared it
> ([docs/EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md](EXPORT_CONTROL_AI_EGRESS.md)). A new company row
> (only the empty-install bootstrap creates one) starts **OFF**; existing companies were grandfathered **ON**. The toggle is **Admin-only**
> (`require_role([ADMIN])`), matching the sibling `allow_carrier_egress` / `allow_print_egress`
> controls. It is exposed in the UI at
> **Admin Settings → AI Privacy** (`/admin/settings?tab=aiprivacy`) — interactive for Admin
> (enabling egress requires explicit confirmation), read-only for other roles. See
> [docs/AI_QUOTING_AGENT_RUNBOOK.md](AI_QUOTING_AGENT_RUNBOOK.md).

> **`allow_sms_egress` is the notification-SMS CUI kill switch (default OFF).** It gates **all**
> outbound notification SMS to Twilio, which sits outside the CUI boundary.
> `PUT /companies/me/sms-egress` takes `{ "allow_sms_egress": boolean }` and returns the updated
> `CompanyResponse`. **Admin-only** (`require_role([ADMIN])`), matching the sibling
> `allow_ai_egress` / `allow_carrier_egress` / `allow_print_egress` controls, and it only ever
> mutates the caller's **own active company** (`get_current_company_id`; never taken from the
> request body). **Double-audited**: the flip writes both a field-level update **and** an
> `sms_egress_enabled` / `sms_egress_disabled` status change on the tamper-evident trail. Every
> company is created **OFF**; while OFF the SMS transport denies **fail-closed** on every send —
> including messages already queued in ARQ — and nothing (not even the destination number) leaves
> the boundary. Turning it on is necessary but not sufficient: SMS also requires server-side Twilio
> configuration and a per-user opt-in with a saved phone number. Exposed in the UI at
> **Admin Settings → SMS Privacy** (`/admin/settings?tab=smsprivacy`). See
> [docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md](NOTIFICATIONS.md#sms-channel-twilio).

> **`require_floor_pin` is the badge sign-in PIN policy (default OFF; AS9100D 8.5.2, migration
> `130`).** On, a badge / employee-ID sign-on (`POST /auth/employee-login` and the crew-station
> badge mint) by a user with **no** floor PIN is refused **403** `floor_pin_not_set`; a user who has a
> PIN is challenged for it either way, and password sign-in is unaffected (see
> [Badge sign-on and the floor PIN](#badge-sign-on-and-the-floor-pin-as9100d-852)).
> `PUT /companies/me/floor-pin-policy` takes `{ "require_floor_pin": boolean }` and returns the
> company record (`CompanyResponse`) plus **`users_without_pin`**: how many **active badge users**
> of the company have no floor PIN, that is active accounts with a non-empty `employee_id`, platform
> accounts (superuser / Platform Admin) excluded. Turning the policy on while that number is above
> zero is allowed; set those people's PINs first (`PUT /users/{user_id}/floor-pin`). **Admin-only**
> (`require_role([ADMIN])`), and it only ever changes the caller's **own active company**. Any API
> token is refused **403** with `"A floor PIN, and the company's badge-sign-in PIN policy, are set by
> a person signed in to the app, not an API token: credential administration is a person's act."`
> before anything is read, and the route is not an MCP tool. A real flip writes two **required**
> audit rows in its own transaction, an `UPDATE` of `require_floor_pin` (old / new) and a
> `STATUS_CHANGE` `floor_pin_optional` ↔ `floor_pin_required`; if either cannot be written the flip
> is rolled back and the answer is **503** `"The audit record for this badge sign-in PIN policy
> change could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry."`. Sending the value the company already
> has writes nothing and still returns the count. Turning it on also ends badge-only sessions at
> their next refresh (`floor_pin_reauth_required`), but not badge sessions signed in before
> migration `130`, which carry no `amr`; rotate `REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY` before the first turn-on
> (see [Badge sign-on and the floor PIN](#badge-sign-on-and-the-floor-pin-as9100d-852)). Exposed in the UI at **Admin Settings → Badge
> Sign-in** (`/admin/settings?tab=floorpin`): interactive for Admin (turning it on asks first and
> shows the count), read-only for other roles.

#### Egress kill switches are a person's judgment

> The four routes that flip a company egress kill switch — `PUT /companies/me/ai-egress`,
> `PUT /companies/me/sms-egress`, `PUT /admin/settings/shipping-profile` (`allow_carrier_egress`)
> and `PUT /receiving/print-profile` (`allow_print_egress`) — refuse **any** API token, whatever
> its role or scope, with **403** `"A company egress kill switch (AI, SMS, carrier or label-print egress) is turned on or off by an Admin signed in to the app, not an API token: opening or closing data egress is a person's judgment."`, before reading or writing anything (lead decision,
> Claude-plugin brief build 2026-11-15; `app.core.credentials.API_TOKEN_EGRESS_SWITCH`). A
> read-only token meets the read-only gate's `"Read-only API token cannot modify data."` first.
> The two profile routes are refused whole, since each is its switch's only writer. None of the
> four is an MCP tool (`catalog.EXCLUDED_OPERATIONS`), so an agent holding a person's own JWT
> cannot reach them either; the profile `GET`s stay tools. An Admin signed in to the app is
> unchanged. See [RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md → Credential policy for judgment writes](RBAC_PERMISSIONS.md#credential-policy-for-judgment-writes).

### Company onboarding and platform administration

There is **no public company self-registration**. Werco is the only company on this system
(owner decision 2026-11-23), so the former unauthenticated `POST /companies/register` route, its
`CompanyRegister` request schema, its rate-limit entry and the SPA page `/register-company` were
deleted; the path now answers **404** and is absent from OpenAPI and the MCP catalog.

There is **no platform-admin company creation** either (owner decision 2026-11-23, "Delete it
too"). `POST /platform/companies`, its `CompanyCreate` request schema and
`services/company_onboarding.py` (`onboard_company`) were deleted, along with the Platform Overview
**Add Company** button and the `create_company` MCP tool. A `POST` to that path now answers **405**;
`GET /platform/companies` at the same path still lists companies, and every other `/platform` route
(get, update, users, dashboard, overview) and platform-admin company context switching are unchanged.

The **only** code path that constructs a `Company` row is the empty-install first-user bootstrap
in `POST /auth/register-public` (documented under Authentication): only when the install has
**zero users**, it creates the `werco` company (or reuses it if it already exists) and makes the
registrant an active **Platform Admin with superuser authority**. Once any user exists, the same
route only creates an inactive VIEWER in the Werco company, pending approval.
`backend/tests/test_company_creation_doors_guard.py` pins that single door and fails CI on a new one.

`PUT /platform/companies/{company_id}` requires platform authority and records changed fields,
including activation/deactivation, in a required `UPDATE` audit row scoped to the **target company**.
Mutation and audit commit together (**503** and rollback on audit loss); unchanged values do not
produce a fictitious update. A missing company is **404**, and an ordinary tenant Admin is **403**.
The stored-platform-only inactive-company recovery exception permits this control-plane route,
while ordinary tenant-data routes and WebSockets still require an active company. A switched
read-only context still cannot mutate companies; logout/switch provide the existing exit path.

### Carrier Integrations (Admin)

Per-company carrier-aggregator credentials + ship-from / egress profile for the multi-carrier
shipping integration. All routes are mounted under `/admin/settings` and gated to **Admin**. See
[docs/SHIPPING_CARRIER_INTEGRATION.md](SHIPPING_CARRIER_INTEGRATION.md).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts` | List the company's carrier accounts (secrets masked) | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts/{id}` | Get one carrier account (secrets masked) | Admin |
| POST | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts` | Create a carrier account (api key / webhook secret encrypted at rest) | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts/{id}` | Update a carrier account; sending `api_key` / `webhook_secret` rotates the stored secret | Admin |
| DELETE | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts/{id}` | **Soft-delete** a carrier account (never physical — purchased labels/BOLs reference it) | Admin |
| POST | `/admin/settings/carrier-accounts/{id}/test-connection` | Validate the stored credential (the **only** carrier call exempt from the egress kill switch — sends no customer data) | Admin |
| GET | `/admin/settings/shipping-profile` | Get the company shipping profile (ship-from origin + egress flag); **404** until created | Admin |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/shipping-profile` | Create / update the shipping profile, including the `allow_carrier_egress` kill switch | Admin, signed in (any API token **403**; not an MCP tool) |

> **Secrets are write-only.** `api_key` and `webhook_secret` are accepted on create/update,
> **Fernet-encrypted** before storage, and **never returned** — read responses expose only
> `api_key_last4` and `has_webhook_secret`, and secrets never appear in audit / event payloads.
> Create / update / delete are audited; an update flags `api_key_rotated` / `webhook_secret_rotated`
> rather than recording the value.
>
> **`allow_carrier_egress` is the CUI kill switch (default OFF).** A new profile is created with
> egress **disabled**; it flips only when an admin sets it on `PUT /shipping-profile`, and that toggle
> is recorded as a **status change** on the tamper-evident audit trail. The route is the switch's
> only writer, so the **whole** route refuses any API token **403** before reading or writing
> anything, and it is not an MCP tool — see
> [Egress kill switches are a person's judgment](#egress-kill-switches-are-a-persons-judgment). While OFF, every
> customer-data-bearing carrier call (`/shipping/validate-address`, `/rate-shop`, `/buy-label`,
> `/buy-bol`, `/schedule-pickup`, `/void-label`, `/refund`) is blocked with **409**.

### Operational Events

The durable, tenant-scoped operational event stream (`operational_events`) that feeds real-time AI
context, the notification outbox, and a few floor reads. Telemetry, not audit data: nothing here
writes to the `audit_log` hash chain. Both routes scope to the caller's active company
(`get_current_company_id`).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/operational-events/` | Read the stream, newest first; filters `source_module`, `event_type`, `work_order_id`, `limit` (1–250, default 100). The raw store: deliberately **not** bounded by `occurred_at` (below) | Yes |
| POST | `/operational-events/` | Record a **custom** event as context for AI assistants (`event_type`, `source_module`, optional `entity_type` / `entity_id` / `work_order_id` / `operation_id` / `severity` / `event_payload` / `occurred_at`). A future `occurred_at` is stored as now. A `work_order_id` or `operation_id` that is not this company's is **404**. **400** for any event type the system records itself (below). Never sends a notification | Yes |

> **Server-recorded event types are refused (400).** A client-posted row is indistinguishable from
> one the server wrote, so `operational_events.SERVER_ONLY_EVENT_TYPES` refuses the union of:
> - **every notification source type** — each key of `notification_catalog.SOURCE_EVENT_TYPE_TO_KEY`
>   (work order released / started / completed / closed, operation completed / ready / hold, NCR /
>   CAR / FAI, receipts, shipments, purchase orders, downtime, backflush and material shortages,
>   dispatch order changes, …). Derived, so a newly cataloged type is refused with no route change.
>   `emit` tags those rows for the outbox, so a posted one used to fan real in-app / email / SMS
>   notifications out to other users, and any signed-in principal (OPERATOR, VIEWER, an API token)
>   could post one.
> - **`READER_TRUSTED_EVENT_TYPES`** — the types a reader selects by name and presents as fact:
>   `dispatch_order_changed` (the RUN NEXT banner, `dispatch_service.latest_dispatch_notices`),
>   `operation_hold` (who / when held, `operation_hold_view`), `operation_ready` (the flow-metrics
>   queue-time anchor), `operation_completed` (the adoption-metrics digital-completion share), and
>   `ncr_updated` / `fai_updated` (quality rows on the work-order timeline). Listed on their own so a
>   type dropped from the catalog stays refused while a reader still trusts it.
>
> Matched after trimming, case-insensitively. Nothing is written and no notification is queued; the
> attempt is logged at WARNING (`operational event post refused …` with company, user and type). Exact
> detail: `Event type '{event_type}' is recorded by the system itself and cannot be posted. Perform the
> action through its own screen or endpoint; the system records the event when it happens.` — for
> `dispatch_order_changed` followed by ` To change a machine's run order, use the Dispatch Board.` To
> make one of these events happen, call the endpoint that performs the action. **Adding a reader that
> filters `OperationalEvent.event_type` on a server-written type means adding that type to
> `READER_TRUSTED_EVENT_TYPES`** — `tests/api/test_operational_event_forgery.py` scans `app/` and fails
> on a filter naming a type missing from that set. A custom type (e.g. `agent_observation`) still
> records and never notifies: only cataloged types are tagged for the outbox, and all are refused. The
> generated MCP tool `record_operational_event` is this route and carries the same refusal.
>
> **`occurred_at` is clamped.** A value later than the server's now is stored as now; a past value is
> kept (normalized to UTC, same instant, and stored naive like every server-written row); omitted, the
> server stamps it. An instant outside the representable range (e.g. `0001-01-01T00:00:00+05:00`) is
> **422**. The readers that trust
> `occurred_at` also ignore rows dated after now, whoever wrote them — hold context, the AI work-order
> context (the copilot's `recent_events`), the timeline's quality telemetry, adoption metrics and flow
> metrics — and adoption metrics treats a non-object payload as an unreported source rather than
> failing. `GET /operational-events/` is deliberately **not** bounded: it is the raw store, so a bad
> row stays visible to whoever investigates it. The dispatch-notice reader is bounded on both sides —
> see "Floor dispatch notices" under Shop Floor.

### AI Usage Telemetry

Read-only cost/latency observability over the per-call LLM usage ledger (`ai_usage_events` — one
row per Anthropic API call, written by the shared client `app/services/llm_client.py`). Aggregates
are **scoped to the caller's active company** (`get_current_company_id`).

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| GET | `/ai-usage/summary` | Per-task and per-model AI usage aggregates over a trailing window | Admin / Manager |

**Query parameters:** `days` — aggregation window in days, integer `1`–`365` (default `30`).

**Response shape:** `{ window_days, since, totals, by_task[], by_model[] }`. `totals` and each
`by_task` / `by_model` row carry the same aggregate fields: `calls`, `input_tokens`,
`output_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `estimated_cost_usd` (nullable —
`null` when the bucket has no priced calls; models missing from the price table in
`llm_client.MODEL_PRICING_USD_PER_MTOK` record cost as `NULL`), `avg_latency_ms` (nullable), and
`error_rate` (failed calls / total calls, `0.0`–`1.0`). `by_task` rows add `task` (e.g.
`po_extraction`, `routing_generation`); `by_model` rows add `model` (the exact model id used).

> **Telemetry, not audit data.** `ai_usage_events` rows record task, model/tier, prompt version,
> token counts, estimated USD cost, latency, and success/error per LLM call. They are operational
> telemetry — not on the tamper-evident `audit_log` hash chain — and the endpoint is read-only
> (no `AuditService` involvement).
>
> **UI surface / dormant Manager allowance.** The endpoint backs the **Admin Settings → AI Usage &
> Cost** tab (`/admin/settings?tab=aiusage`). The server allows **Admin and Manager**
> (`require_role([ADMIN, MANAGER])`), but the only consuming UI today is the AdminRoute-gated
> Admin Settings page, so Managers can currently exercise the allowance only via direct API calls.

<a id="werco-copilot-read-only-ai-chat"></a>

### Hank (AI shop teammate)

Ask-anything chat over the caller's **own company's** ERP data, answered via Claude tool-use
against existing read paths (`app/api/endpoints/copilot.py` + `app/services/copilot_service.py`).
Surfaced in the app as **Hank**, named after the shop's yellow Labrador (header button /
`Ctrl+.`); not available on the `/kiosk` or `/wallboard` screens. Page-aware starter questions
help employees investigate the current job, stock, or purchasing records. Chat can also save
an audited proposal for employee review; it cannot execute that proposal. The panel's separate
**Upload PDF** form uses the existing document upload route.
See [Hank](HANK.md) for the employee workflows and their boundaries. Route names,
`Copilot*` contracts, OpenAPI tag, model configuration, and telemetry identifiers stay stable.

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Auth Required |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| POST | `/copilot/chat` | One chat turn — SSE stream by default; `?stream=false` for plain JSON | Yes (any authenticated user) |
| GET | `/hank/briefing` | Live, deterministic, role-ordered shift briefing; no LLM or database writes | Yes; effective view permissions gate each source |
| GET | `/hank/capabilities` | Active company, reviewed-action `allowed_kinds`/`can_write`, and separate `can_watch` capability | Yes |
| GET | `/hank/tasks` | Own saved proposals/receipts/watches; `limit` 1–100 (default 25), optional positive `before_id`, optional exact `status` | Yes; kind-specific current view gates |
| GET | `/hank/tasks/{id}` | Own saved task under the same credential | Yes; kind-specific current view gates |
| POST | `/hank/tasks` | Save and audit a task preview; does not execute the business action | Yes; action-specific role and effective permissions |
| POST | `/hank/tasks/{id}/execute` | Execute the reviewed task and save its receipt atomically | Yes; same actor/credential and current action authority |
| POST | `/hank/tasks/{id}/cancel` | Cancel an unexecuted proposal | Yes; same actor/credential and current action authority |
| POST | `/hank/watches` | Explicitly save a personal work-order follow-up in `watching` state | Interactive user; effective `work_orders:view`, writable company context |
| POST | `/hank/watches/{id}/{action}` | `check`, `snooze` (one hour), `resume`, or `cancel` a saved follow-up | Same company/owner, interactive user and current watch authority |
| GET | `/hank/preferences` | Own saved choices or typed defaults; no write on read | Yes; current company/user |
| PUT | `/hank/preferences` | Explicitly replace typed personal choices using the current version | Interactive user in writable company context |
| POST | `/hank/preferences/reset` | Restore typed defaults while retaining task and audit history | Interactive user in writable company context |
| POST | `/hank/intake` | Durably upload 1–5 PDF/DOCX/XLSX/XLS files and enqueue extraction; multipart `expected_company_id`, UUID `request_key`, `files` | Interactive Admin/Manager/Quality; writable company |
| GET | `/hank/intake` | Own batches, newest first; `limit` 1–50 (default 20), optional `before_id` | Same company/owner and current document role |
| GET | `/hank/intake/{batch_id}` | Recover all files in an owned batch | Same company/owner and current document role |
| GET | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}` | Recover one file's analysis, plan or receipt | Same company/owner and current document role |
| GET | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/source` | Size/hash-verified source bytes with native MIME; PDF inline, Office attachment; private/no-store | Same company/owner and current document role |
| GET | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/source-preview` | Bounded native text `{format, units, labels, warnings}`; no model call; private/no-store | Same company/owner and current document role |
| GET | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/purchase-order-draft` | Deterministic supplier-PO suggestions from saved extraction; no model call or writes | Same company/owner and current document role plus purchasing-task authority |
| GET | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/receiving-draft` | Deterministic receiving suggestions from saved extraction; optional positive `purchase_order_id`; no model call or writes | Same company/owner and current document role plus receiving-task authority |
| POST | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/plan` | Save reviewed filing choices and source fingerprints | Same authority plus selected-source view permissions |
| POST | `/hank/intake/files/{file_id}/{action}` | `execute`, `retry`, or `cancel` with expected company/version | Current interactive write authority; receipt release additionally requires receiving view/create |
| GET | `/hank/work-orders/{id}/readiness` | Recorded material, blocker, instruction, traveler and quality gaps; never production authorization | `work_orders:view`; additional sources separately gated |
| GET | `/hank/work-orders/{id}/knowledge` | Released document links and bounded prior-run notes | `work_orders:view` |
| GET | `/hank/work-orders/{id}/shipping-packet` | Existing shipment, packing-slip and released-document evidence | `work_orders:view` + `shipping:view` |
| GET | `/hank/purchase-orders/{id}/impact` | Outstanding supply, same-part alternatives, potential jobs and unsent follow-up draft | `purchasing:view`; stock/jobs separately gated |
| GET | `/hank/trace/{kind}/{value}` | `lot` or `serial` recorded genealogy, value up to 100 characters | Inventory, quality, work-order and purchasing view permissions |
| GET | `/hank/handoff-people` | Up to 100 eligible same-company recipients; optional `q` up to 100 characters | Interactive `work_orders:view` |
| GET/POST | `/hank/handoffs` | List participant handoffs or explicitly send one | Interactive `work_orders:view`; writes require writable company |
| GET | `/hank/handoffs/{id}` | Sender/recipient-only saved handoff | Same-company participant and current access |
| POST | `/hank/handoffs/{id}/{action}` | Recipient `acknowledge`/`complete`, sender `cancel`; expected company/version | Authorized participant in writable company |
| POST | `/hank/handoffs/{id}/attachments` | Multipart PNG/JPEG evidence: expected company/version, UUID `request_key`, `file` | Participant; active handoff and live job |
| GET | `/hank/handoffs/{id}/attachments/{attachment_id}` | Verified private photo bytes | Same-company participant and current access |
| GET/POST | `/hank/routines` | List approved routines/templates or create a draft | Interactive work-order access; create requires Admin/Manager/Supervisor |
| GET/PUT | `/hank/routines/{id}` | Read a routine or edit it back into draft | Draft/archive visibility and editing require routine-management authority |
| POST | `/hank/routines/{id}/{action}` | `approve`, `archive`, or `start` a reviewed current version | Approve: Admin/Manager; archive: Admin/Manager/Supervisor; start: interactive current access |
| GET | `/hank/routine-runs` | Own runs; `limit` 1–100 (default 20), optional `before_id` | Interactive current work-order/context access |
| GET | `/hank/routine-runs/{id}` | Own snapshotted routine and recorded step evidence | Same company/owner and current context access |
| POST | `/hank/routine-runs/{id}/{action}` | `advance` one step with evidence or `cancel`; expected company/version | Own run in writable company; each business action retains its own authority |
| GET | `/hank/work-queue` | Combined own tasks/intake/runs and participant handoffs; optional exact state filter | Interactive work-order access; each source retains its current read gates |

**Document intake.** Each PDF, DOCX, XLSX or XLS file is at most 10 MB; a batch is
at most 25 MB. PDFs allow 25 pages. Office files allow 25 evidence sections,
120,000 text characters and 2,000 populated rows; workbooks allow 10,000 populated
cells and 200 columns per sheet. Expansion and subprocess resource limits reject
oversized or unsupported files without silently truncating them. Macros, encrypted
files, embedded executable objects, unresolved Word tracked revisions, populated
hidden spreadsheet content and external workbook links are unsupported.
Formulas are never evaluated, and cached formula values remain uncertain.
Upload request keys are company-scoped and bound to actor plus exact
filename/hash inputs. Extraction uses the shared, company-egress-gated model
client with `hank_document_intake` prompt 1.2.1. A request-driven ARQ job claims
and commits before parsing/model work, then reloads current authority and saves
its result with required audit. Parsing runs in a resource-bounded subprocess;
no database transaction stays open during file or model I/O.

Extraction suggests one of `purchase_order`, `vendor_quote`, `packing_slip`,
`material_certificate`, `drawing`, or `other`, with bounded header fields, up to
50 lines, confidence, source/excerpt evidence, warnings and permission-filtered
exact identifier matches. Scanned-page evidence remains uncertain when native
text cannot verify it. Drawings expose title-block metadata, not interpreted
manufacturing requirements. Duplicate warnings cover same-company files
submitted through intake; other employees' private file IDs are not returned.
`analysis.has_duplicates` signals matching content even when both duplicate ID
lists are empty because the matching intake is private. Clients use this flag to
offer explicit duplicate acknowledgement before saving a filing plan. An extraction
that hits the output limit or reports `has_more_lines` is rejected as incomplete.

File states are `queued`, `analyzing`, `awaiting_review`, `planned`, `completed`,
`failed`, and `cancelled`. File responses contain source identity, status/version,
analysis, plan, result, safe error text and UTC timestamps. `source_format` is
`pdf`, `docx`, `xlsx` or `xls`; `source_labels` names native evidence sections.
Evidence `page` is the one-based PDF page or Office section; optional `locator`
identifies a paragraph/table row or worksheet row. `analysis`/`plan`/`result`
can be null. Batch responses contain `{id, company_id, request_key, created_at, files[]}`;
lists contain `{batches[], has_more, next_before_id}`. The source route verifies
saved size/hash before returning original bytes (409 on changed evidence). Clients
must fetch with authentication and may use a PDF blob URL with `#page=N` for review.
Office clients render escaped source-preview text and download the original separately.

**Import an existing supplier PO.** The purchase-order draft supplies printed
identifiers, dates, exact vendor/part candidates and all extracted lines. It creates
no records. Submit reviewed values through the existing `draft_purchase_order`
task with `source_intake_file_id`, `source_intake_version`, the original `po_number`,
optional `order_date`, and `ready_for_receiving`. Each line must include its unique
zero-based `source_line_index` and reviewed `unit_of_measure` matching the chosen
part's stocking unit. Every source line must be represented exactly once; missing,
ambiguous and unsupported units/prices require employee correction.

Execution preserves the printed PO number, original file and reviewed dates.
`ready_for_receiving=true` additionally requires Admin/Manager approval authority
and records the existing PO as `sent`, so the current Receiving open-PO list includes
its lines. This performs no supplier dispatch, receipt, inspection or inventory
update. Otherwise the PO remains draft. An existing number (including case variants
and deleted orders), previously imported identical bytes, changed source version or
changed vendor/part snapshot blocks creation. Required audits, PO creation and task
receipt commit atomically; task replay returns the existing result. Legacy tasks
without source fields retain their draft-only behavior.

Plan requests are `{expected_company_id, expected_version, plan}`. `plan` includes
title, document type, revision, optional description and selected part/job/vendor/
PO/receipt IDs, corrected `reviewed_fields`, `acknowledge_duplicate`, and
`filing_mode` (`draft` or `release_receipt_certificate`). The first mode creates
a draft with optional part/job/vendor links and retained PO/receipt provenance.
The second requires a PDF and explicitly releases a certificate for the selected receipt's exact
part/supplier and fills its empty certificate slot; it never replaces a prior
certificate or changes inspection/accepted quantities. Execution rechecks source
fingerprints and concurrent duplicate filing, then commits document, optional
receipt linkage, required audits and intake result atomically. Completed execution
replays its receipt. Intake-linked documents and source bytes cannot be deleted
through Documents. Retry requeues queued/failed files or analyzing work older than
15 minutes. Late results cannot overwrite a cancelled/newer version. Upload and
filing uncertainty is recovered by the same request key or saved file ID.

**Operational reports.** Every report returns `{company_id, checked_at, title,
summary, checks[], coverage_notes[], draft_text}`. Checks distinguish recorded
facts, attention, unknown coverage and information. Readiness requires work-order
view; material coverage additionally requires inventory and purchasing view,
and quality exceptions require quality view. Purchasing impact identifies direct
material/BOM demand only; downstream jobs require work-order, BOM and inventory
view. Same-part stock excludes held/expired/unavailable quantities. Supplier
messages are returned as drafts only. Knowledge links up to 50 released documents,
five completed prior runs and five notes per run; it does not read those file
contents. These routes do not reconcile job state or write records.
Trace identifiers are URL-encoded as one value; encoded slashes in recorded lot
or serial numbers remain part of the identifier. The 100-character value bound
and source permissions still apply.

**Handoffs, routines and queue.** Handoff creation includes a UUID request key,
expected company, work order, recipient, summary and optional completed/remaining
work, problems, quantity and up to ten document IDs. Lists accept `direction`
(`all`, `sent`, `received`), exact status, `limit` and `before_id`. New and changed
handoffs send private participant in-app notices, never email/SMS. Up to ten
verified PNG/JPEG photos (10 MB/20 megapixels each) can be added while active;
photo replay keys preserve uncertain saves. Document and photo references do not
constitute quality approval.

Routines contain 1–12 ordered typed steps. Editing an approved routine returns it
to draft; each run retains the approved version's snapshot. `start` includes a
request key, expected company/version and optional work-order/PO context.
`advance` carries expected company/version and a review note or the required
completed `task_id`, `intake_file_id` or `handoff_id`; evidence must belong to the
employee/participants, correct context and current permissions. Checklists record
employee statements, not automatic business execution. Routines seed no approved
procedures and cannot grant authority. The queue filters each source before its
50-row bound, returns `{checked_at, items[], truncated}`, and supports `working`,
`waiting_on_you`, `waiting_on_other`, and `finished`; use source inboxes for more
history. This expansion requires migration110, with no new environment variable
or scheduled cron. Intake requires a matching enqueue-driven worker.

**Reviewed task contract.** `POST /hank/tasks` accepts
`{ expected_company_id, request_key, kind, input }`. `request_key` is normalized to a canonical
UUID. The eight `kind` values are listed below; each input is
validated against its specific schema and undeclared fields are rejected. The task stores
immutable input/preview evidence and fingerprints of the source plan. There is a cap of 100
proposals awaiting review per actor/credential. Creating a proposal requires the same
authority as its eventual action:

| Kind | Required input | Authority / result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repeat_job` | `source_work_order_id`, positive `quantity_ordered`, optional `due_date` | Admin/Manager/Supervisor plus effective `work_orders:view` and `work_orders:create`; creates a **draft** through the existing duplicate service |
| `draft_purchase_order` | `vendor_id`, 1–50 `lines` with `part_id`, positive `quantity_ordered`, nonnegative `unit_price`; optional PO dates/address/method/notes and line date/notes; source imports additionally require the source/version, printed number, line indices and stocking units described above | Admin/Manager/Supervisor plus effective `purchasing:view` and `purchasing:create`; normally creates a **draft**. A reviewed existing-document import can record **sent** for Receiving with Admin/Manager and `purchasing:approve`; never emails a vendor or receives material |
| `attach_document` | `document_id`, `work_order_id` | Admin/Manager/Quality plus effective `work_orders:view`; links an existing PDF using the document workflow, without approving its contents. A document the user may not open is **404**; from Hank chat an `export_controlled` one is too. Execution raises the document to `export_controlled` when the work order's customer is export-controlled (Documents → "Restricted and export-controlled documents") |
